articles.title: Ver Defensa y Justicia vs. Independiente gratis por Fútbol Libre y Roja Directa: el error que puede exponer tus datos personales
articles.text:
La expectativa por el partido entre Defensa y Justicia e Independiente, correspondiente a la fecha 15 del Torneo Clausura 2026 del fútbol argentino, puede llevar a muchos hinchas a buscar transmisiones gratuitas en internet. Sin embargo, ingresar a páginas como Fútbol Libre y Roja Directa o descargar aplicaciones como Xuper TV puede poner en riesgo la información personal almacenada en celulares, computadoras y televisores inteligentes.
El encuentro se disputará este lunes 2 de noviembre, desde las 19:00 en Argentina, en el estadio Norberto Tomaghello, ubicado en Florencio Varela. En Perú y Colombia comenzará a las 17:00, mientras que en México será a las 16:00 y en España a las 23:00. La transmisión oficial en Argentina está disponible a través de TNT Sports Premium.
El problema de recurrir a enlaces no oficiales no se limita a la posibilidad de encontrar una señal interrumpida o de mala calidad. Algunas páginas utilizan anuncios engañosos, ventanas emergentes y falsas actualizaciones para inducir a los usuarios a descargar archivos o entregar permisos que no necesitan para reproducir un partido.
Dónde ver Defensa y Justicia vs. Independiente
El encuentro corresponde a la jornada 15 del Torneo Clausura y será importante para ambos equipos en la recta final de la fase regular. El árbitro designado es Sebastián Martínez y el estadio Norberto Tomaghello será el escenario del compromiso.
En cuanto a las señales oficiales, la transmisión para Argentina estará a cargo de TNT Sports Premium, mientras que en Perú y otros países de Latinoamérica las opciones incluyen Disney+ Premium y Fanatiz, según el territorio.
La búsqueda de alternativas gratuitas puede llevar a los hinchas a páginas que utilizan nombres conocidos para atraer visitantes. El riesgo está en que no todos los enlaces conducen a un reproductor: algunos redirigen a sitios publicitarios, solicitan datos personales o muestran botones falsos de descarga.
El error de instalar aplicaciones para ver fútbol gratis
Uno de los principales peligros aparece cuando una página solicita descargar un archivo APK para acceder a la transmisión. Este formato permite instalar aplicaciones en dispositivos Android, pero hacerlo desde sitios desconocidos implica evitar los controles de seguridad de las tiendas oficiales.
El Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad de España (Incibe) advierte que las aplicaciones pueden solicitar permisos que no guardan relación con su función. Entre los más delicados están el acceso a contactos, mensajes, notificaciones y servicios de accesibilidad.
Una aplicación destinada a reproducir Defensa y Justicia vs. Independiente no necesita consultar los mensajes privados, acceder a la cámara o controlar otras funciones del teléfono. Si exige esas autorizaciones, el usuario debería desconfiar y evitar la instalación.
También hay que prestar atención a las extensiones que prometen eliminar anuncios, desbloquear señales o mejorar la calidad del video. Algunas pueden registrar la actividad de navegación, insertar publicidad o redirigir a páginas fraudulentas.
Cómo pueden robar contraseñas y datos bancarios
Entre las amenazas asociadas a las aplicaciones maliciosas se encuentra el keylogger, un programa que registra las pulsaciones realizadas en el teclado o la pantalla. De esta manera, puede capturar nombres de usuario, contraseñas y otros datos que una persona introduce al utilizar sus servicios digitales.
El acceso a los mensajes SMS también representa un problema. Algunas entidades financieras utilizan códigos temporales para verificar operaciones, recuperar cuentas o confirmar el ingreso desde un dispositivo nuevo. Si una aplicación consigue leer esas notificaciones, podría facilitar el acceso de terceros a información sensible.
Otra modalidad es el phishing, que consiste en engañar a una persona mediante páginas que imitan servicios legítimos para conseguir sus credenciales. Durante la búsqueda de una transmisión deportiva pueden aparecer ventanas que simulan alertas de seguridad o solicitan datos de tarjetas bancarias para habilitar un supuesto acceso gratuito.
David González Cuautle, investigador de ESET Latinoamérica, ha advertido sobre los riesgos de conceder permisos especiales y críticos a aplicaciones de streaming que no necesitan esas funciones.
Qué señales indican que un dispositivo podría estar comprometido
El peligro de ingresar a estos sitios no necesariamente termina cuando finaliza el partido. Una aplicación maliciosa puede permanecer activa en segundo plano y continuar recopilando información o mostrando publicidad sin que el propietario lo advierta.
Entre las señales que pueden alertar sobre un problema se encuentran:
- Aparición de anuncios que no desaparecen.
- Aplicaciones desconocidas instaladas en el teléfono.
- Cambios inesperados en la pantalla de inicio.
- Mayor consumo de batería y datos móviles.
- Disminución del rendimiento del dispositivo.
- Redirecciones automáticas hacia páginas desconocidas.
Estos comportamientos no confirman por sí solos una infección, pero justifican revisar las aplicaciones instaladas y los permisos concedidos.
Si el usuario descargó un archivo sospechoso para intentar ver el encuentro entre Defensa y Justicia e Independiente, conviene desinstalarlo, ejecutar un análisis de seguridad y cambiar las contraseñas de las cuentas que pudieron quedar expuestas. También es recomendable revisar los movimientos bancarios si se introdujeron datos financieros.
La posibilidad de ver un partido sin pagar una suscripción puede resultar atractiva, especialmente cuando se trata de un encuentro importante del fútbol argentino. Sin embargo, instalar aplicaciones desconocidas o entregar permisos innecesarios puede convertir una búsqueda deportiva en un problema de seguridad digital que afecte información personal y otros dispositivos conectados a la misma red.

articles.title: Cette entreprise qui traque les pirates de cryptomonnaies se fait elle-même pirater
articles.text:
C'est le comble. Une entreprise qui traque les pirates, se fait elle-même pirater. Alors, quels risques pour la sécurité de vos données et surtout, de votre argent ? Pour l'heure, les données volées semblent essentiellement être des informations des clients Chainalysis.
La société d'analyse de blockchains Chainalysis a annoncé vendredi avoir subi un incident de cybersécurité ayant entraîné une fuite de données. Si cet incident n'a pas de lien avec le piratage de Binance, il est d'autant plus dramatique que l'entreprise est spécialisée dans les transactions en cryptomonnaies et la lutte contre la criminalité financière.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Des accès détectés en octobre
Selon Chainalysis, des attaquants extérieurs ont utilisé en octobre des « techniques agentiques offensives » pour accéder à ses systèmes et à certains de ses outils internes. La nature des techniques employées n'a pas encore été dévoilée par l'entreprise.
Les pirates ont pu consulter certaines données relatives aux utilisateurs de la plateforme : identifiants clients, noms complets, adresses e-mail et intitulés de rôle au sein de leur entreprise ou organisation.
L'entreprise indique en revanche ne disposer, à ce stade, d'aucun élément laissant penser que d'autres informations ont été touchées.
« Sur la base des éléments dont nous disposons à ce jour, nous n'avons trouvé aucun indice que ces incidents aient abouti à un accès non autorisé aux contenus d'enquête (graphes, notes ou dossiers), aux résultats de transactions ou de requêtes, aux mots de passe en clair, aux secrets d'authentification multifacteur ou aux jetons de session des utilisateurs », a déclaré Chainalysis.
Chainalysis prend des mesures
Chainalysis a envoyé un message d'alerte aux clients concernés. Elle leur demande de rester attentifs à toute demande inattendue de réinitialisation de mot de passe ou d'authentification, et leur recommande d'activer l'authentification à deux facteurs sur leur compte s'ils ne l'ont pas déjà fait.
Mais voilà, Chainalysis n'a pas des clients comme les autres. Parmi ces derniers figurent des banques, plateformes de cryptomonnaies, des forces de l'ordre et agences gouvernementales dans divers pays du monde. L'accès non autorisé à leurs noms et coordonnées les expose davantage à ces types d'attaques.
L'entreprise a par ailleurs fait appel à des experts en cybersécurité indépendants. Ils doivent l'aider dans l'enquête, examiner la sécurité de la plateforme, repérer d'éventuelles vulnérabilités et renforcer ses défenses.
Dans son message aux clients touchés, Chainalysis précise :
« Nous sommes en train de déterminer quels enregistrements concernant votre organisation ont été consultés et nous vous transmettrons un détail complet dès que cette analyse sera terminée. »
Un acteur des enquêtes sur la criminalité crypto
Les blockchains comme celle du Bitcoin enregistrent publiquement toutes les transactions, puis les chiffrent. Chainalysis regroupe des adresses en ensembles, les rattache à des entités réelles (plateformes d'échange, marchés du darknet, groupes sous sanctions) et signale les flux jugés à risque.
L'entreprise participe actuellement aux investigations sur les mouvements de fonds issus du piratage de Binance survenu la semaine dernière, attribué au groupe de cybercriminels nord-coréen TraderTraitor. Elle a décrit ce qu'observent ses enquêteurs : « des schémas de blanchiment jamais vus auparavant » avec les fonds dérobés.
« Des milliers de transactions en peu de temps laissent penser que les attaquants recourent à l'automatisation pour brouiller la piste des fonds. Plutôt que de simplement les transférer, ils les font circuler à plusieurs reprises entre des adresses, en renvoyant souvent des fonds vers des adresses utilisées plus tôt dans la séquence », a ajouté Chainalysis.
Source : Help Net Security

articles.title: ASUS XG Core Radeon RX 9060 XT LP Heavily Downclocked to Meet 75 W Power Limit
articles.text:
Monday, November 2nd 2026
ASUS XG Core Radeon RX 9060 XT LP Heavily Downclocked to Meet 75 W Power Limit
According to the latest update on the ASUS page, the official specifications for the PCIe slot-powered 75 W ASUS XG Core Radeon RX 9060 XT LP differ significantly from those of the regular desktop card. As an external graphics solution, the XG Core powers the GPU through the PCIe slot without needing external GPU PCIe power connectors. The XG Core operates at a default game clock of 1,010 MHz and can boost up to 1,600 MHz. In OC mode, these figures increase modestly to 1,030 MHz and 1,620 MHz, respectively, which is not very noticeable. This contrasts sharply with the standard Radeon RX 9060 XT LP edition, which has a base frequency of 1,380 MHz—nearly 37% higher—and a boost frequency of up to 3,040 MHz, which is nearly double.
The differences in frequency also correlate with power consumption. The Navi 44 XTLP in the XG Core solution is rated for just 75 W, while the desktop GPU is designed for a 140 W power draw and requires an external GPU power connector. The entire XG Core unit, including its USB4 controller, is capped at 75 W. This aggressive power limit necessitates lower clock speeds to maintain stability and thermal performance within its compact chassis, which measures roughly 114 × 117 × 39 mm. The device connects to host systems via USB4 and provides limited display outputs, making it a portable graphics dock suitable for mini-PCs, notebooks, and handhelds.ASUS first showcased the XG Core at Gamescom 2026 as a more compact, less gaming-focused alternative to its ROG XG Mobile eGPU lineup. The product is designed for both gaming and local AI workloads, with the updated listing highlighting 406.3 AI TOPS. The newly published clock data clearly illustrates that there must be a performance trade-off to deliver desktop-class RDNA 4 silicon in a USB4-powered external form factor that consumes only half the power of a typical discrete RX 9060 XT GPU version.
Sources:
				ASUS, 				via Uniko's Hardware			
	
	
	
		
	
		
6 Comments on ASUS XG Core Radeon RX 9060 XT LP Heavily Downclocked to Meet 75 W Power Limit
Regardless, Navi44 is one of the most efficient GPUs on the market at the moment, I bet this thing performs surprisingly well for how constrained it is.
They'll offer you a Zenbook 14 with a U9 285H but then kneecap it at 45-65w in the bios so it never melts the laptop.
- 75W TGP, lower than the LP's 140W
- Only USB4 40Gbps. They could've gone with USB4 80Gbps (but they probably did not want to license TB5 or buy JHL9480 as there still is no ASMedia/VIA solution yet)
- Missing one DisplayPort connector. RX 9060 XT supports DisplayPort and one HDMI output simultaneously
There are a couple of good things about it:
- Seems to runs off USB-C power itself, this is most likely the reason why they had to further limit it to PCIe slot power:
- This may be the most compact eGPU solution outside of boutique OEMs. The dimensions are quite small compared to others: 144 x 117 x 39 mm
If this is more than $500 (proper MSRP, not based off current memory pricing) for what it is, then this may not be a good buy. articles.title: India shines in Apple’s record September quarter
articles.text:
India shines in Apple’s record September quarter
Apple achieved an all-time revenue record in India during CEO John Ternus’s debut quarter, as global revenue reached $114.48 billion despite unprecedented memory cost inflation.
India emerged as a stellar growth market for Apple in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, registering an all-time company revenue record in the country.
“We also set September quarter revenue records in both developed and emerging markets, in addition to an all-time record in India,” Apple Chief Executive Officer John Ternus said.
The performance in India was propelled by a September quarter record for iPhone upgraders, with Worldpanel survey data ranking iPhone among the top-selling smartphone models in the country.
Mac sales also set an all-time revenue record in India, driven by demand for the new MacBook Neo and MacBook Pro.
Furthermore, Apple launched Apple Pay in India in this quarter in partnership with Axis Bank, extending digital payments to one of the world’s largest consumer markets.
“We are optimistic about the long-term future of our services business,” Apple Chief Financial Officer Kevan Parekh noted.
Global financials
Moving to global business, Apple generated quarterly total revenue from operations of $114.48 billion, an 11.72% YoY increase compared to $102.47 billion in Q4 FY25.
For the full fiscal year FY26, total revenue reached an all-time record of $478.83 billion, up 15.06% YoY from $416.16 billion, while full-year net profit reached $132.18 billion, up 18% YoY.
Quarterly revenue comprised two distinct streams: Products revenue of $82.90 billion (72.42% of total) and Services revenue of $31.57 billion (27.58% of total).
Across product categories, iPhone generated $57.58 billion (50.30% of total revenue), growing 17.46% YoY due to global upgrader records and demand for iPhone 18 Pro and the foldable iPhone Duo.
Services achieved an all-time record of $31.57 billion, rising 9.82% YoY on record cloud, video, and payment revenues, with paid subscriptions topping 1.5 billion.
Mac revenue jumped 23.68% YoY to $10.79 billion due to strong MacBook Neo adoption and global market share gains. Conversely, Wearables, Home and Accessories fell 7.91% YoY to $8.30 billion against tough prior-year comparisons, while iPad revenue declined 10.40% YoY to $6.23 billion due to supply constraints.
Apple’s profit after tax rose 11.81% YoY to $30.71 billion, compared to $27.47 billion in Q4 FY25, assisted by a $0.05 per share tariff refund benefit.
On a full-year basis, EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation), which measures operational cash profit, reached $171.49 billion, delivering an EBITDA margin of 35.81% on $478.83 billion in revenue.
Expense drivers
Managing total operations required $59.66 billion in total cost of sales, up 10.22% YoY. Total operating expenses jumped 20.58% YoY to $19.19 billion.
Research and Development (R&D) represented the largest cost centre at $11.73 billion (61.13% of total operating expenses), surging 32.30% YoY from $8.87 billion as Apple accelerated investments in generative artificial intelligence (AI), such as Siri AI, and custom silicon.
Meanwhile, Apple’s active installed base stood over 2.5 billion devices, with $28.10 billion in quarterly operating cash flow, and $137 billion in cash reserves.
However, unprecedented memory cost inflation compressed profit margins, while supply limits on advanced nodes, cutting-edge semiconductor manufacturing chips, restricted device availability.
“What we are seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented. And as we said earlier in the September quarter, we did see higher memory costs as compared to the June quarter, which were partly offset by the benefit of carrying inventory and lower costs on certain non-memory components,” Ternus explained.
Supply chain bottlenecks also hampered shipments.
“The Q4 constraints were primarily driven by the availability of the advanced nodes our SoCs are produced on. But as we have transitioned more of our lineup to the latest 2-nanometer technology nodes, our constraints on advanced nodes are easing,” Apple Chief Operating Officer Sabih Khan said, detailing these operational challenges.

articles.title: Ce robot maçon débarque en France et promet de monter les murs d'une maison en 3 jours
articles.text:
Vedette du salon Batimat il y a un mois, l’australien Hadrian X résume dix ans de robots maçons restés, pour la France, des animaux de salon. Fin octobre, le WLTR, développé par le groupe tchèque GreenBuild avec le fabricant de matériaux Wienerberger et KM Robotics, est passé aux travaux pratiques : une semaine d’essais grandeur nature sur Scale One, la plateforme que Bouygues Construction vient d’inaugurer à Chilly-Mazarin, dans l’Essonne. Un premier chantier en conditions réelles pourrait suivre dès début 2027.
Un maçon de 2,5 tonnes piloté à la tablette
La machine tient de l’imprimante grand format qui aurait troqué l’encre contre la terre cuite. Son bras saisit deux briques à la fois sur leur palette, les encolle de deux cordons de mousse en guise de mortier, puis les aligne au millimètre en suivant le plan numérique du bâtiment. Un opérateur surveille l’ensemble sur sa tablette, pendant qu’un aide gère l’approvisionnement et les finitions.
Sur le papier, la cadence grimpe jusqu’à 10 m² de mur par heure, 7,5 m² en moyenne, pour des parois qui culminent à 3,50 m. Le bras soulève surtout sans sourciller des blocs de 52 kg, la part du métier qui abîme le plus sûrement les dos, le tout pour 1,5 kW, la consommation d’une bouilloire. Il réclame en échange du courant triphasé, une arrivée d’eau, un espace dégagé le long du mur et des briques à son format, une gamme Porotherm dessinée pour sa pince.
Le premier essai hors de Tchéquie date de fin 2024, avec environ 300 m² de murs montés en six jours sur un entrepôt autrichien. Une douzaine d’exemplaires tournent depuis en Europe centrale, de la Tchéquie à la Pologne, plus de 40 000 m² au compteur, et les gammes de blocs compatibles sortent d’usines d’une demi-douzaine de pays, Royaume-Uni compris. À Budapest, l’un d’eux a signé le gros œuvre d’une maison de 100 m² en moins de trois jours, une première résidentielle pour la Hongrie.
Cinq maçons remplacés ? Le chantier dit plutôt un
L’équivalent d’une équipe de cinq personnes : la promesse figure en toutes lettres dans l’argumentaire du fabricant. À Kladno, près de Prague, le groupe de construction PORR fait travailler un WLTR depuis 2025 sur un ensemble de 371 logements. Son bilan d’étape, publié cet été, retient une productivité comparable à celle d’un seul maçon expérimenté, avec deux personnes mobilisées en continu autour de la machine. Au rang des avantages tout de même : la qualité d’exécution ne bouge pas du premier au dernier rang de briques. Découpes, ouvertures et ancrages demeurent du ressort de l’équipe, et le patron du groupe, Karl-Heinz Strauss, préfère prévenir que construire « est et restera une affaire d’humains ».
Lire aussi : Construire une maison en deux jours : le robot maçon face au mur de la réalité
En France, la construction alignait cette année 143 000 projets de recrutement, dont 65 % jugés difficiles à pourvoir, un record, et les maçons figurent parmi les profils les plus recherchés. Le secteur peine donc à recruter, ce qui laisse de la latitude pour une machine qui absorbe le port des charges les plus lourdes, même au rythme d’un seul maçon. Les majors françaises ne partent d’ailleurs pas de zéro : Bouygues Construction expérimente déjà des robots de perçage pour limiter la pénibilité sur ses chantiers.

articles.title: Malgré la flambée du prix des carburants, 57 % des automobilistes français refusent toujours de passer à l’électrique
articles.text:
Prix de l’essence et du gazole : pourquoi les Français préfèrent moins rouler plutôt que passer à l’électrique
Face à l’envolée du prix des carburants, les automobilistes français limitent leurs trajets et traquent les stations les moins chères, mais boudent toujours la voiture électrique.
En deux ans, les tarifs à la pompe se sont envolés dans l’Hexagone. On pourrait logiquement penser que cette pression financière sur le budget des ménages accélère l’abandon des moteurs thermiques au profit de véhicules électriques. Pourtant, une récente enquête montre que face à un plein toujours plus cher, les conducteurs français adaptent leurs déplacements quotidiens mais rechignent encore à changer de motorisation.
Les conducteurs français préfèrent lever le pied plutôt que de passer à la voiture électrique
Pour réaliser son étude en septembre 2026, DiscoverCars, comparateur de locations en ligne, a croisé les réponses de 1 110 clients internationaux avec les données publiques de l’Insee pour la France. Selon l’institut statistique, le sans plomb 95-E10 a augmenté de 16 % depuis septembre 2024 pour atteindre 2,01 € en août 2026, tandis que le gazole a bondi de 31 % à 2,21 €, avant de culminer à 2,41 € en septembre.
Une hausse qui pèse lourdement sur le portefeuille : remplir les 35 litres d’une citadine coûtait jusqu’à 77,35 € en gazole en août, et 143,65 € pour les 65 litres d’un SUV. Sans surprise, 31 % des répondants français se disent “beaucoup” touchés dans leur budget, contre 21 % dans le monde.
Malgré tout, cette flambée ne suffit pas à déclencher un basculement massif vers les motorisations électrifiées. Pendant que 47 % du panel mondial roule à l’essence et 28 % au gazole, 57 % des sondés français n’envisagent pas de passer à une voiture hybride ou électrique pour le moment, un taux supérieur à la moyenne internationale (52 %). À l’échelle mondiale, seuls 8 % songent à l’électrique et 15 % à l’hybride, tandis que 7 % déclarent avoir déjà franchi le pas.
Au lieu d’abandonner le thermique, la majorité des conducteurs interrogés dans le monde (51 %) déclarent avoir adapté leurs habitudes, une tendance encore plus marquée chez les Français. Près de la moitié comparent les prix des stations (48 %) et évitent les trajets inutiles (47 %), tandis que 38 % utilisent moins leur voiture et 25 % marchent davantage sur les courts trajets. Seuls 21 % d’entre eux affirment n’avoir rien changé au volant depuis la hausse des prix des carburants (contre 30 % dans le monde).
Cette frilosité envers l’électrification, exprimée par la clientèle de DiscoverCars, contraste toutefois avec le marché français du neuf où la voiture électrique a établi un record à 41,6 % des ventes en septembre 2026 (65 247 immatriculations, +107,5 % sur un an). Un paradoxe qui s’explique par le fait que les acheteurs de voitures neuves ne reflètent pas le budget de l’ensemble des automobilistes, pour qui le coût d’achat initial et les contraintes de recharge restent des freins majeurs malgré la flambée à la pompe.

articles.title: Rettung für das Stromnetz? „Ohne die Transformatoren gibt es eigentlich kein Stromnetz“
articles.text:
Neue Generation: Diese Halbleiter-Technik soll den größten Engpass im Stromnetz lösen
Transformatoren sind ein zentraler, aber fast unsichtbarer Bestandteil unseres Stromnetzes: Die Großgeräte tragen dazu bei, Strom effizient über lange Entfernungen zu transportieren. Die Technik ist komplex und schwer zu bauen – immer noch. Da sich ihr grundlegendes Design seit etwa einem Jahrhundert kaum verändert hat, wären sie eigentlich reif für eine Modernisierung, doch die schien lange nicht zu passieren. Das ändert sich jetzt: Während die Welt darum kämpft, den steigenden Strombedarf von Elektrofahrzeugen, Rechenzentren und anderen Bereichen zu decken, suchen Forscher:innen und Unternehmen nach Möglichkeiten, Transformatoren umzukrempeln. Und es gibt erste Erfolge: Neue Halbleiter-gestützte Varianten der Technik könnten dazu beitragen, Versorgungsengpässe teilweise zu lindern und sicherzustellen, dass das Stromnetz dem wachsenden Nachfragedruck standhalten kann.

articles.title: PapApp Luján: la aplicación gratuita que permite orientarse sin Internet durante la visita del papa León XIV
articles.text:
La llegada del papa León XIV a Luján volverá a concentrar a miles de personas en una ciudad donde la conectividad suele resentirse en las jornadas de mayor convocatoria. Frente a ese escenario, una aplicación gratuita propone mapas, recorridos y puntos de interés que pueden consultarse sin señal de celular, con información para orientarse entre los accesos, los servicios previstos y las zonas de estacionamiento.
La herramienta, llamada PapApp Luján, fue desarrollada por Juan Segundo Addamo y Simón Forteza, alumnos de cuarto año de Ingeniería Informática de la Universidad Argentina de la Empresa (UADE) y oriundos de Luján.
Los dos conocen el movimiento que generan las peregrinaciones y la visita papal, por lo que pensaron la aplicación como una respuesta a una dificultad que se repite cuando la cantidad de teléfonos supera la capacidad de la red. “La señal se va a saturar completamente”, afirmó Forteza en Infobae Al Amanecer.
Con ese problema como punto de partida, PapApp Luján reunirá en un mismo mapa la ubicación de escenarios, puestos médicos, zonas de hidratación, pantallas gigantes, estacionamientos, puntos de encuentro y carpas de comunión, entre otros servicios.
La información estará ordenada por categorías para que cada persona pueda identificar lo que necesita sin navegar entre datos innecesarios. “Como 25 capas”, describió Forteza al explicar la cantidad de niveles informativos que incorporaron al sistema.
Uno de los recursos apunta a resolver una de las situaciones habituales de las grandes concentraciones: encontrar el vehículo después de varias horas y tras recorrer una ciudad desconocida o colmada.
La aplicación permitirá guardar el punto donde se dejó estacionado el auto y, más tarde, elegir la función “volver a mi auto” para recibir una guía peatonal hasta ese lugar. Al comparar esa función con las plataformas de navegación, Forteza resumió la diferencia central: “Es un Waze que funciona sin Internet”.
El funcionamiento sin conexión no elimina por completo la necesidad de prepararse antes de viajar. Los usuarios deberán descargar PapApp Luján desde las tiendas oficiales y abrirla con internet antes del evento, para que el teléfono incorpore los mapas, los recorridos y el resto de los datos.
Una vez completada esa instancia, la información queda guardada en el dispositivo y puede consultarse incluso si no hay cobertura o si el equipo está en modo avión. “Todo corre local en tu celular”, explicó Forteza.
Esa modalidad también forma parte de las recomendaciones de Addamo y Forteza para quienes asistan a la jornada. Sugieren descargar la aplicación y actualizar sus contenidos con anticipación, tanto para evitar depender de los datos móviles como para cuidar la batería durante el recorrido.
Después de hacerlo, plantean que el modo avión puede ser útil cuando la señal sea débil o inexistente. “Nosotros decimos que lo usen en modo avión para guardar la batería del celular”, señaló Forteza.
La decisión de que los datos queden almacenados en cada teléfono busca, además, que la plataforma no dependa de consultas permanentes a un servidor mientras transcurra el evento.
Según sus creadores, esa arquitectura permitiría que la aplicación siga disponible aunque una gran cantidad de personas la use al mismo tiempo, aunque existe una etapa inicial de descarga desde la nube.
“La aplicación se la pueden bajar las siete mil millones de personas que están en el planeta. No colapsa porque al ser 100% local no puede colapsar”, afirmó Forteza.
El proyecto comenzó hace dos meses, mientras ambos estudiantes cursaban en la UADE y reunían la información necesaria sobre los servicios, los accesos y los caminos previstos para la visita a Luján.
La idea surgió en una conversación familiar y avanzó a partir de una necesidad concreta: ofrecer una alternativa para quienes lleguen a la ciudad y pierdan la posibilidad de usar las aplicaciones habituales de navegación. “Arrancó de cero hace dos meses”, contó Forteza.
Además del mapa visible para los usuarios, Addamo y Forteza crearon un sistema propio para cargar y actualizar los datos con mayor rapidez. Ese trabajo incluye los recorridos de peregrinación, los ingresos a Luján y los trayectos sugeridos para quienes dejen sus vehículos en zonas periféricas y continúen a pie.
El desarrollo atravesó las revisiones de las tiendas oficiales, donde una versión fue rechazada por una captura de pantalla incorrecta antes de quedar disponible en ambas plataformas.
“Te pueden rechazar por código o por parte de información que uno sube”, explicó Forteza. Las novedades sobre el uso de la aplicación y la información difundida por el municipio también se publican en la cuenta de Instagram de PapApp Luján.

articles.title: Piratage de Binance : le FBI confirme que la Corée du Nord est derrière le casse
articles.text:
Le FBI vient d’attribuer officiellement à des pirates nord-coréens le vol record de 6,3 milliards de dollars en cryptomonnaies sur Binance. Les enquêteurs ont également identifié des centaines d’adresses utilisées pour déplacer le butin et tentent désormais d’empêcher son blanchiment.
Les soupçons pesaient déjà sur la Corée du Nord depuis le piratage de Binance, le 29 octobre dernier. La société d’analyse blockchain TRM Labs avait rapidement désigné TraderTraitor, un groupe de cybercriminels soutenu par Pyongyang, comme responsable de l’attaque. Le FBI vient de confirmer cette information dans une alerte publiée le 31 octobre, tout en appelant les acteurs du secteur à coopérer pour empêcher les pirates de blanchir les milliards dérobés.
TraderTraitor, déjà impliqué dans plusieurs vols majeurs de cryptomonnaies
Pour rappel, l’attaque du 29 octobre a permis aux pirates de détourner environ 6,3 milliards de dollars en cryptomonnaies depuis plusieurs portefeuilles de Binance, établissant un nouveau record. Les premières investigations de la plateforme avaient révélé la compromission possible de l’ordinateur d’un ingénieur DevOps, qui aurait permis aux attaquants d’accéder à un conteneur de service et de déclencher des retraits non autorisés. Binance a depuis découvert d’autres points de compromission, sans avoir encore établi l’ensemble du déroulement de l'intrusion.
Dans son avis de sécurité, le FBI attribue désormais formellement l’opération à TraderTraitor, un groupe nord-coréen associé à l’écosystème Lazarus. Les autorités américaines lui imputaient déjà plusieurs vols majeurs de cryptomonnaies, dont les 308 millions de dollars dérobés à DMM Bitcoin en mai 2024 et le piratage de Bybit, qui avait rapporté près de 1,5 milliard de dollars aux attaquants en février 2025.
Ces précédentes opérations avaient mis en évidence le recours à l’ingénierie sociale pour compromettre des employés ou des développeurs disposant d’accès sensibles. Le FBI ne détaille toutefois pas les éléments ayant permis d’attribuer la nouvelle attaque à TraderTraitor, ni la méthode employée pour pénétrer dans l’infrastructure de Binance.
Des centaines d’adresses identifiées pour tenter de bloquer le blanchiment
L’enquête se concentre désormais sur les déplacements des fonds volés. Selon le FBI, les pirates ont commencé à convertir une partie de leur butin en ether (ETH), une cryptomonnaie qu’ils pourraient ensuite faire transiter par des services de finance décentralisée (DeFi) et des plateformes d’échange instantané. Une succession d’opérations qui pourrait compliquer le suivi des fonds et réduire les possibilités de les geler.
Pour entraver ces transferts, le FBI a publié une liste de 628 adresses associées à l’attaque, dont 608 sur Ethereum, 19 sur Bitcoin et une sur Solana. Aux côtés du Secret Service et du service d’enquêtes criminelles de l’administration fiscale américaine (IRS-CI), l’agence demande aux plateformes d’échange, aux opérateurs de nœuds blockchain, aux services DeFi et aux autres prestataires du secteur de bloquer les transactions impliquant ces adresses ou les fonds qui en proviennent.
Des mesures de gel avaient d’ailleurs déjà été prises avant cette alerte. Dès le 30 octobre, Binance indiquait avoir obtenu, avec l’aide de ses partenaires, le gel d’environ 3 milliards de dollars d’actifs dérobés.
En attendant de savoir quelle proportion de ces fonds gelés pourra effectivement être récupérée, Binance poursuit la reconstitution de ses réserves. Dans un communiqué du 1er novembre, la plateforme a fait savoir qu’elle avait remplacé environ 95 % des actifs dérobés grâce à ses propres ressources financières, sans avoir récupéré cette proportion du butin auprès des pirates. Les 5 % manquants correspondent à des cryptomonnaies moins liquides, que l’entreprise continue de racheter.
Cette reconstitution s’accompagne d’une reprise progressive des retraits, engagée le 1er novembre après plusieurs jours de suspension. Depuis le 2 novembre, les utilisateurs peuvent également vérifier la couverture intégrale de leurs soldes pour les dix principales cryptomonnaies concernées, grâce à une preuve cryptographique des réserves publiée par Binance. La plateforme prévoit d’élargir les retraits à de nouveaux actifs le 3 novembre et s’engage à prendre intégralement en charge les pertes liées au piratage, tandis que les enquêteurs poursuivent la traque des fonds détournés.

articles.title: How Xatoms is using AI to solve the global water crisis - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
How Xatoms is using AI to solve the global water crisis
Every September, Climate Week and Global Citizen Week in New York bring together policymakers, investors and innovators focused on the world’s most pressing problems.
It’s also when Cisco Systems Inc. and Global Citizen recognize the winner of the Global Citizen Prize: Cisco Youth Leadership Award. Cisco and Global Citizen created the award in 2018 to honor a young leader who uses technology to help end extreme poverty, and this year’s recipient may have the most compelling story yet.
Diana Virgovicova (pictured) is the founder and CEO of Xatoms (pronounced “X-Atoms”), a Toronto-based company that uses artificial intelligence and quantum chemistry to design sunlight-activated materials that break down pollutants in water. The award comes with a $250,000 grant, and Xatoms was chosen from more than 2,000 applications.
Most of the AI conversation at Climate Week focused on what AI takes from the planet: power, land and, increasingly, water. Xatoms offers a positive counterpoint, a case study in AI giving back.
A personal mission, not a market opportunity
Most founders find a market. Virgovicova found a problem the hard way. She grew up in a village of about 800 people in Slovakia, surrounded by farms that used heavy amounts of pesticides. “I got sick when I was 14 years old,” she told me. “I was diagnosed with ovarian cancer because of the water I drank.”
After her diagnosis, she persuaded her mother to go backpacking across Asia. On trains in India, she heard from women facing the same thing. “I learned that there is a girl in Slovakia who got sick. There is a girl in India who’s getting infections. There is a girl in Africa who has to spend long hours every single day searching for clean water,” she said. “So, we need to find a solution, and it is affecting mainly women across the globe.”
Globally, women and girls spend 250 million hours a day collecting water, more than three times the time men and boys spend. “While boys go to school, the girls are responsible for bringing a bucket of water home, and they start missing school very early on,” Virgovicova explained. “It’s an educational, economic and health problem.”
And it’s growing. “We have 2 billion people that don’t have access to clean drinking water, and this number is actually growing because of flooding, climate change,” she said.
Going after the contaminants everyone ignores
One of the more interesting aspects of Xatoms is where it chose to play. Many water treatment efforts target bacteria such as E. coli because the effects are immediate. Xatoms goes after the harder problem: complex industrial pollutants such as pesticides, pharmaceuticals, forever chemicals and heavy metals.
“I think we are forgetting about these complex contaminants because they don’t make us sick tomorrow. They make us sick in 10 years,” she said. “They give us chronic diseases. They cause infertility.” She made a point I hadn’t considered: Scientific progress is making it worse.
“We are able to create better antibiotics, but these better antibiotics are more complex, thus more difficult to destroy in water,” she said. That’s a second-order problem traditional treatment wasn’t built for, and exactly where advanced computational design has an edge.
Quantum chemistry plus AI equals speed
At 17, while working with a university professor in Slovakia, Virgovicova used quantum chemistry software to design a new molecule that harnesses sunlight to break down water pollutants. That work earned her a Diploma of Excellence from the Swedish Royal Family and a full scholarship to the University of Toronto.
“What is so exciting about this science is that we can use computers to design new materials, and we don’t have to create them in the lab,” she said. “We can see these materials, how they react, and what their properties are before we even synthesize them.”
Quantum chemistry gets far fewer headlines than quantum computing, so I asked her to explain it. “Quantum helps us understand these molecules at a fundamental level, including how the atoms within the molecule interact,” she said. “When we know these fundamental properties, we can understand what makes each molecule good at something, and that helps us design an even better molecule, a better material.”
The output is a photocatalyst powder. “Initially, it was a molecule in a computer, but we were able to synthesize it in a lab,” Virgovicova said. “We put this photocatalytic powder into water. It splits water into OH radicals, and the OH radicals then destroy contaminants.”
Because it’s a catalyst, it isn’t consumed, so a small amount can treat “hundreds of gallons,” she said. Earlier photocatalysts required ultraviolet light; her design works with visible light, such as sunlight or LEDs, eliminating the need for expensive UV reactors.
AI is the accelerant. “It would take a decade if we did it without AI,” she said. “We can do it in 30 days.” That’s the real story for business leaders. Materials discovery has historically been slow, expensive and lab-bound, and Xatoms has transformed it into a computational pipeline.
AI that helps solve AI’s water problem
Here’s where it matters for technology buyers. Data centers consume enormous volumes of water for cooling, and the AI buildout is making that worse. I asked Virgovicova whether Xatoms can flip the script. “There are a lot of problems with contaminants within the data center,” she said. “The data center water needs to be completely clean for cooling,” she said. “We are able to use this catalyst to help reuse the water in data centers.”
This is an underappreciated opportunity. Hyperscalers and neoclouds face mounting pressure over water use, and the industry’s response has largely focused on cooling design. Reuse through improved treatment is a different and more planet-friendly solution.
Not one-size-fits-all
Xatoms works with Indigenous communities in Canada under longstanding boil-water advisories, as well as in Kenya and South Africa. Virgovicova told me the footprint now includes Japan and Azerbaijan. Every engagement is customized.
“We collect a water sample. Recently, we shipped the sample from Azerbaijan all the way to Canada,” she said. “We identify the contaminant and then determine which of these 88 options would be the best.”
Customers define the outcome. “Some of them want to take yellow water and decolorize it. Some of them have a specific contaminant in mind that they want to remove or reduce,” she said.
Next up are Turkey, where co-founder Kerem Topal Ismail Oglou grew up, and the broader Middle East, driven by textile manufacturing and oil and gas. She also met South Africa’s water minister during Climate Week ahead of a trip to Cape Town.
Being named a global winner of the World Economic Forum’s Water Resilience Challenge opened doors with large enterprises. “We had the chance to interact with some of the biggest Fortune 500 companies, which helped us create pilots and partnerships,” she said.
Water is chronically underfunded
The Cisco grant is moving directly into execution. “We have more than six major projects coming up, so we need help with lab work,” she said. “We need to figure out the best way to manufacture more materials.” The goal is to “commercialize this technology as fast as we can.”
When I joked that billionaires are hunting for water on Mars while we haven’t solved it here, she pointed out a funding gap. “About 3% of climate VC funding goes to water only,” she said. Water underpins industry, agriculture and now AI infrastructure, yet it remains capital-starved.
Advice for the next generation
Virgovicova mentors young founders, especially women in science and climate, and her advice is very direct. “There’s always going to be skepticism in every single room you go into at first,” she said. “It’s very important that you know how to present yourself and that you’re confident. You can really prove everyone wrong as long as you know your stuff.” With women still scarce among Fortune 500 CEOs, she added, “If I can do it, you can do it as well.”
Her favorite piece of advice: “If you focus on watering your grass, you don’t care about someone’s grass being greener.” And the AI myth she wants gone? “That it’s going to destroy the world. I think it’s a tool for improving the world.”
Final thoughts
Cisco uses this award to make a point it rarely gets credit for: technology’s value is measured by what it does for people. Xatoms applies two of the decade’s most hyped technologies, AI and quantum, to a tangible, urgent problem.
For technology leaders, there are three key takeaways. First, AI’s biggest payoff may come from scientific discovery, where compressing a decade of work into 30 days can reshape an entire industry’s economics. Second, AI’s water problem has solutions beyond cooling design, and data center builders should be evaluating treatment and reuse partners now. Third, water deserves far more capital than it receives.
In 10 years, Virgovicova wants Xatoms to be “a global leader in discovery of these materials,” with solutions for many toxic contaminants worldwide. Given how far she has come from a village of 800 people, I wouldn’t bet against her.

articles.title: Google vai anunciar Googlebooks que funcionam como tablets • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Google vai anunciar Googlebooks que funcionam como tablets
Próximo formato da categoria Googlebook deve contar com teclado destacável, fazendo os modelos da linha funcionarem como tablet.
Os Googlebooks foram anunciados como laptops sofisticados, que combinam recursos do Android e do Chrome S. Mas, e se eles também pudessem funcionar como tablets? Bom, modelos que trazem essa característica podem virar realidade em um futuro não muito distante.
Durante o evento Android Dev Summit 2026, realizado no último fim de semana, o Google deu a entender que o próximo formato da linha Googlebook consistirá em laptops que trazem teclado destacável ou removível. Isso significa que esses modelos poderão ser usados como tablet.
Não chega a ser uma surpresa. Basta levarmos em conta que o Acer Googlebook 14, que faz parte da primeira leva de Googlebooks, permite que a tela seja girada em 360 graus, o que o transforma em um laptop “2 em 1”. Nessas circunstâncias, o modelo funciona como tablet, mas com a desvantagem de ter um teclado “pendurado” na traseira.
Um teclado destacável faz o equipamento funcionar, efetivamente, como tablet, tornando a experiência do usuário mais flexível, por assim dizer.
Provavelmente, sim. Tablets Android estão há anos no mercado, mas, até hoje, determinados aplicativos funcionam neles sem aproveitar todo o potencial de uma tela maior. Já o Googlebook OS (o sistema operacional da categoria) teria mais potencial para combinar a experiência de desktop, que é o seu foco principal, à praticidade dos tablets.
É claro que, para isso, o Google precisará fazer um bom trabalho de adaptação. Nesse sentido, consideremos que o Googlebook OS já permite que aplicativos funcionem em tela cheia e com orientação retrato, mas algumas partes do sistema, como a tela inicial, ainda não suportam essa combinação de modos.
Ainda não há data de lançamento para os Googlebooks com teclado destacável, mas um vazamento do Android Headlines feito em julho sugere que o primeiro modelo a contar com essa característica será lançado pela Lenovo. Fiquemos de olho.

articles.title: Apple Watch's AI features for rewinding and recapping conversations begin beta testing | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Apple’s AI-powered “Audio Intelligence” technology for the Apple Watch is now rolling out into beta testing, initially for developers in the iOS 27.3 update, after first being announced at the company’s Surprise and Shine hardware event in September. The technology includes a set of four opt-in AI features that allow Apple Watch Series 12 wearers to detect important sounds, identify songs, catch up on conversations, and take notes.
The sound recognition feature will help deaf and hard-of-hearing users identify important sounds like sirens, alarms, or doorbells from their watch, while the song recognition feature taps into Apple’s Shazam app to detect music playing in the background and identify the song name and artist.
However, the more potentially controversial features are those that listen to human conversations: Live Rewind and Siri Recaps.
Given the backlash to AI recording devices, like Meta’s AI glasses and other AI wearables, Apple has attempted to carve out a space where the features can be useful to Apple Watch owners, while still respecting the privacy of those around them.
With Live Rewind, the idea is to let you go back in time to see what someone just said, in case you missed it. For instance, if someone was giving you verbal directions or reading a long list of specials at a restaurant, you could double-press on the Watch’s digital crown to see what was said in the last 15 seconds as a text snippet displayed on the watch face. You can either view this snippet and then do nothing, and it will disappear permanently. Or you can save it to the standalone Siri app that shipped with iOS 27 for later access, which might be helpful if you’re trying to remember someone’s name or take a quick note from a fast-paced presentation.
Apple says that users will also be able to tap an “Ask Siri” option that appears below the text snippet if they have questions about something that was said — like a technical term they don’t understand, or perhaps some sauce option the waiter mentioned that they’re unfamiliar with, among other things.
When you double-press the digital crown, an audible chime appears and an animation displays on the watch. This is meant to signal to people through the combination of the gesture, sound, and the visual display that you’ve recorded something that was said.
These snippets will be deleted automatically after 30 seconds if you don’t save them.
The other option, Siri Recaps, takes this ambient listening technology even further by allowing Apple Watch owners to take high-level notes of their conversations.
Importantly, Apple says it’s not identifying speakers, saving the raw audio, or providing word-for-word transcriptions. Instead, the feature summarizes a conversation with a short sentence and some bullet points that identify key points. For instance, depending on the topic, the bullet points might include things like important dates or deadlines, pricing or payment plan information, and other factual information.
Apple suggested the feature could be used in scenarios like work meetings, parent-teacher conferences, personal training sessions, or other places where you may need to remember what tasks you have to complete or things that were said. Essentially, it’s supposed to mimic a user’s ability to jot down their own notes — without adding emotion or tone.
This could be helpful particularly at times when you aren’t able to write up your own notes, either because your hands are full or you’re trying to concentrate on whatever’s being said at the time. The recaps won’t record conversations when you’re listening to music with your headphones or using their noise cancellation features.
At the end of the day, you’re prompted to review your saved Siri Recaps when the feature is enabled, and then choose which, if any, you want to save. These notes can be saved to your Notes app or even exported to your Journal app, if they’re more personal in nature. If you do nothing, the recaps will delete themselves within seven days.
This reminder to review the Siri Recaps you’ve recorded also appears when you first unlock your Apple Watch in the morning, too.
Users can opt to enable the Siri Recaps manually, or they can configure a schedule, such as only having the recapping take place while at work, or making sure that they never run at night. Even if they’re running on a schedule, you can still turn off the recapping feature at any time from the Control Center.
Apple notes that Siri Recaps has been designed to omit sensitive information like government-assigned identifiers, financial and authentication data, certain personal identifiers, and any language that would promote self-harm.
The Audio Intelligence features for the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 rely on a combination of Apple’s hardware, software, and services. This includes the S11 chip, built-in microphone, and the Apple Intelligence models that run on the iPhone, as well as Apple’s Private Cloud Compute.
The always-on processor includes a secure enclave — a hardware-protected memory space that can’t be accessed by the rest of the operating system — where a dedicated audio buffer processes the raw audio. This allows the audio to be processed without it actually being accessible to anyone, including Apple. The audio is only accessible to the paired iPhone through a secure pairing mechanism between it and the watch.
To work, lightweight AI models on the S11 chip on the Apple Watch detect if there’s a conversation happening that the wearer is a part of, which is then transferred to the secure enclave on the iPhone. On-device processing on the iPhone turns the audio into condensed text, meaning the text of the conversation with the filler words removed. This condensed text is then encrypted and sent to Apple’s Private Cloud Compute (PCC) to create the recap of the conversation that is sent back to the phone. (The recap and any summarizations used to create it are deleted from PCC immediately afterwards).
The recaps you can then access on your iPhone are only accessible to you, not to Apple. And they’re encrypted when they’re synced between your multiple Apple devices.
Similarly, Apple Watch transfers audio to the iPhone for processing to create the 15-second snippets for Live Rewind.
Apple says none of these features should impact the battery life of your watch or phone. The features will later roll out to the public beta for broader testing before becoming publicly available to all.

articles.title: Google kills off Jules, its AI coding agent which promised to do all the jobs you didn't want to
articles.text:
Google kills off Jules, its AI coding agent which promised to do all the jobs you didn't want to
Google's agentic coding platform shuttered after less than two years
- Google confirms it will move away from Jules, which launched in 2025
- Users have until November 11 2027 to finish projects, then it'll be read-only
- 'Learnings' gained from the 'experiment' will inform Antigravity project
It feels like just months since Google launched its AI coding agent, Jules, but the tech giant is now shuttering the project as it looks to consolidate its agentic AI efforts.
The company confirmed in an X post that "Jules will be winding down" while it "focus[es] on [the] unified experience" that is Antigravity.
While Jules itself as a product will be shuttered, with Google describing it as an "experiment to learn how asynchronous coding agents can help developers ship faster," many of the tools it offered will live on under Google's Antigravity project.
Google shutters Jules AI coding agent
Users now have until November 11 2027 to finished their ongoing Jules sessions, after which it will operate in read-only mode for existing projects. The company has also introduced an export process to help developers move out of the platform.
"You can now export everything Jules knows about your work into a local folder: account settings, environment variables, scheduled tasks, connected repositories, memories, setup scripts, and every session, including its prompt, plan, full activity log, and code patches," a more detailed announcement confirms.
The decision may not come as a surprise to all – the platform didn't seem especially popular among developers. "Could've just emailed the 3 people this affects," one comment on X reads.
Google never shared details of how popular Jules was, but it did boast of thousands of developers testing it during the beta phase. Still, Jules will have likely faced stiff competition from OpenAI's Codex and Claude Code, as well as GitHub Copilot and a long list of others.

articles.title: Gamer's Asus TUF monitor blocks bullet fired through wall during Call of Duty session — says 280Hz monitor is 'the best $280 I ever spent'
articles.text:
Gamer's Asus TUF monitor blocks bullet fired through wall during Call of Duty session — says 280Hz monitor is 'the best $280 I ever spent'
It goes without saying, but don't try this at home, kids.
A Redditor by the name of /u/antisocialnae describes their Asus TUF VG258QM 280Hz gaming monitor as "the best $280 [they] ever spent" after it blocked a bullet that passed through the wall of their home, nearly striking them directly as they were playing some "late-night Call of Duty." Asus has responded to the post with a promise to investigate, though no confirmation of a replacement monitor just yet.
It probably doesn't need explaining that the only reason the plastic-and-plastic monitor was able to stop a bullet is that it had already passed through the exterior wall of the home, and that monitors are generally not ideal for sheltering from gunfire.
But even still, it's a wonderful tale, especially given the TUF branding of the display. TUF technically stands for "The Ultimate Force", but most TUF gear is actually subjected to U.S. Department of Defense MIL-STD-810H testing protocols, including shock & drop tests, vibration tests, high-and-low temperature tests, humidity, sand and dust ingress, and more. That sand and dust ingress protection could be important given the sheetrock powder all over the back of his rig.
What Asus doesn't test for is bullet ingress, which would be quite a thing. While it wouldn't actually be that hard to build, it's difficult to imagine the circumstances where someone would specifically select for that when buying a display.
While these events don't seem to be all that common, we've previously covered a couple, including an event where a user's gaming PC deflected a bullet that came through the wall earlier this year. A few years ago, another user's Razer headset deflected a bullet, almost assuredly saving their life. For their part, /u/antisocialnae says that they've been meaning to buy a new display anyway, so this makes the perfect excuse. For now, they apparently have two other Asus monitors to game on.
Incredibly, the monitor actually still works aside from the damaged portion of the LCD. It makes a decent advertisement for Asus TUF monitors, which mostly miss our selections of the best gaming monitors — beaten by pricier rivals — not because of any problems with the quality. In fact, our last TUF Gaming monitor review scored very well and earned itself an Editor's Choice award. Of course, we also don't test for bullet ingress.

articles.title: The Power of Dual-Phase DrMOS Technology in AI Systems - EE Times
articles.text:
Background and Industry Evolution
As AI systems continue to push boundaries, current demands are rapidly increasing. Next-generation AI systems face a critical layout bottleneck caused by escalating current demands that now frequently reach the 1000A to 2000A threshold per socket.
To supply this immense demand for low-voltage power stably while minimizing ripple, voltage regulator module (VRM) architectures are forced to aggressively scale up their phase counts in order to distribute large currents across components to prevent overheating, reduce the output ripple, and improve transient response. This means that new VRMs often require 16, 24, or even more phases. This surging power requirement comes at a time when AI systems-on-chip (SoCs) and application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) are expanding significantly, delivering higher computing density, but also consuming more board space while overall board size remains strictly fixed. This creates a critical physical squeeze, leaving power designers tasked with delivering vastly more current through a crowded network of phases within a restricted footprint.
Due to these demands, adopting high-density, space-saving components like dual-phase DrMOS is no longer just an optimization strategy — it’s become an absolute necessity to overcome space constraints and power tension.
Today’s DrMOS
DrMOS evolution has been driven by continuous need to maximize power density through packaging innovation. The technology reached a critical milestone in the 5mmx6mm era around 2017, where advanced silicon and thermal enhancements successfully pushed current from 70A to 90A within the same footprint. To further optimize space, the industry transitioned to the 4mmx6mm 90A generation in 2021 by shaving 1mm off the package width while maintaining the full 90A output. This has become the current mainstream standard for packing high-current phases closer to the CPU.
The latest processors demand unprecedented power, and future trends are rapidly shifting toward dual-phase integration, such as 5mmx5mm dual (60A + 60A) and 6mmx6mm dual (90A + 90A) — which compress two phases into a single package to maximize current density and save critical PCB space.
Key Advantages of Dual DrMOS
Dual DrMOS solutions provide three main advantages: higher power density, low input voltage options, and flexible package options.
Higher Power Density
Dual-phase DrMOS support unprecedented power density, which is critical for modern voltage regulator module designs in high-performance computing applications. They achieve this by delivering higher current output (90A per phase) within a constrained footprint, optimizing space efficiency compared to deploying two individual single-phase DrMOS components.
Utilizing dual DrMOS enables a higher degree of integration, effectively saving critical board space while maintaining high output power (POUT) for high-density designs. By integrating two phases into a single package, dual DrMOS significantly reduce overall component count and required PCB real estate, leading to a more compact, efficient layout (see Figure 1). This helps save cost and PCB space.
16V and 8V Input Voltage Options
In addition to a standard 16V version (MP87595), we are excited to introduce a new low-voltage version. The MP87597 is an 8V dual-phase DrMOS that offers superior power conversion efficiency and significantly higher power density compared to a traditional 4mmx6mm DrMOS. Utilizing a lower input voltage significantly enhances power conversion efficiency by reducing switching losses and optimizing the duty cycle for low-voltage core rails.
Within the same 6mmx6mm package, MPS’s low-voltage process provides a specific on resistance (RDS(ON)), enabling the seamless integration of dual-phase functionality onto a single die without compromising efficiency.
Under the same test conditions, our solution demonstrates a 2% efficiency gain compared to traditional high-voltage process dual DrMOS (see Figure 2).
Exposed Top and Standard Overmolding Package Options
Dual DrMOS solutions include both traditional overmolding package and exposed top package options (see Figure 3 and Figure 4).
Exposed top package design significantly enhances thermal performance by providing a direct low thermal-resistance path from the silicon to the ambient environment or to an external heatsink. The exposed top allows for the attachment of a dedicated heatsink or thermal interface material directly on top of the DrMOS. Creating a secondary cooling path complements the traditional path through the PCB.
This structure allows heat to be dissipated more efficiently from the top of the component, preventing heat accumulation on the PCB and enabling higher power density in compact system designs.
MPS’s Dual DrMOS Family: MP87595 and MP87597
MPS’s growing DrMOS family includes the MP87595 and MP87597, both of which offer high-density power solutions that help overcome the space constraints faced by modern AI systems.
The MP87595 is a dual output Intelli-PhaseTM with a wide 3V to 16V input voltage (VIN) range. It can handle a maximum continuous current per phase of up to 90A, and features Accu-SenseTM current-sensing. It is available in an LGA-40 (6mmx6mm) package with an exposed top, which contributes to high thermal resistance (0.2°C/W for ΘJT and 0.8°C/W for ΘJB when exposed).
The MP87597 offers the same package size and key features with an even higher current capability, up to 100A and up to 8V VIN. Leveraging MPS’s low-voltage process, the MP87597 also achieves improved efficiency gain.
Conclusion
Dual-phase DrMOS technology offers the potential to overcome the power bottleneck and board size restrictions in AI systems by maximizing power density. Both the MP87595 and MP87597 provide the necessary advantages of dual DrMOS solutions that will enable the next generation of AI computing. To learn more, explore MPS’s robust Intelli-PhaseTM DrMOS solutions.

articles.title: ‘Is Sam Altman going to break into my house and steal my RAM?’ — why the AI boom could keep memory prices high until 2030
articles.text:
‘Is Sam Altman going to break into my house and steal my RAM?’ — no, but the AI memory crisis could be about to get a whole lot worse
Your RAM is safe in your PC, for now
Sam Altman has been making headlines for his claims that consumers don’t deserve DRAM because it is only utilized “5% of the time.” In his opinion, DRAM supplies should be prioritized for data centers where its utility can be maximized powering cloud environments.
Altman’s perspective is like a utilitarian's fantasy. Humanity’s endurance of short-term pain - by handing over every bit of DRAM we have - will lead to a morally right outcome in the form of a world powered by time-saving, efficiency-increasing, productivity-boosting AI.
Sounds great if you’re the head of an AI company, but less so if you just want memory to be affordable again.
But what the OpenAI head seems to forget is that the DRAM shortage is part of a crisis he had a hand in creating. When OpenAI’s Stargate datacenter buildout was announced in early 2025, it was predicted that the project would require 40% of the world’s global supply. Supply issues were compounded as leading producers of memory entered a production turndown just a few years before to help stabilize pricing.
Will Sam Altman break into your house to steal your RAM?
The good news is that there is little Sam Altman himself can do to take your RAM off you. One reddit user asked Google AI the question we’ve all been thinking: “Is Sam Altman going to break into my house and steal my RAM?”
Google reassured the user with, “No, Sam Altman is not going to break into your house to physically steal your RAM.” So at least there's that.
But given how constrained the current memory supply is, there are a few ways that AI and other future tech could make the whole situation worse.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The worst could still be yet to come
One of the world’s leading memory manufacturers, SK Hynix, has predicted that the supply shortage could “persist through 2030,” making any hopes of a return to affordable pricing in the next few years a distant dream.
With OpenAI and Anthropic both set to hit the public market within that window, there is a lot of uncertainty over how the memory giants that control around 90% of the world’s supply will shift production.
Given the difference in revenue between the consumer memory market and the AI market, it wouldn’t be surprising to see a significant production swing towards the high-bandwidth memory required for AI inference and training.
This could be compounded by AI’s effect on the job market, with numerous firms enacting hiring freezes as AI strategies help cut out repetitive rote work. Higher unemployment and a lack of open positions could further reduce the demand for consumer memory, swinging production further in favor of AI.
But other emerging industries are also looking to take a bite out of the memory market.
Robots and autonomous vehicles are coming for your RAM
There has been a recent explosion in the robotics industry: from humanoid bots competing in their very own Olympics, to warehouses staffed by fleets of micro-bots. As AI improves and converges with the robotics industry to produce bots with near-human fine motor control, numerous industries spanning manufacturing, hospitality and logistics could buy robots in place of humans.
After all, a robot can work around the clock, doesn’t need to rest, and doesn’t have any rights to be violated with unsafe working conditions or excessive hours. The same goes for an autonomous taxi or cargo truck.
But they will need memory to run their little AI brains. And serving the corporate overlords is much more important (and much more profitable) than expanding memory production for the consumer market, so don’t expect things to improve any time soon.

articles.title: Apple finally has a touchscreen MacBook. Why now?
articles.text:
Apple finally has a touchscreen MacBook. Why now?
The Windows world has had touch for over a decade. Is Apple getting in the right way?
Last week, Apple finally brought two new display technologies to the MacBook Pro: OLED and touch. For the former, it was just a matter of time; Apple has been using OLED in the iPhone and Apple Watch for years, and also just brought it to the iPad Mini. But touch has never felt like a sure thing. While many of Apple's most successful products have relied on touch: the iPhone, the iPad, the Apple Watch, and some late-stage iPods all featured touchscreens. But until now, it never made its way to Apple's laptops.
Former Apple CEO Steve Jobs' words are infamous: "It's ergonomically terrible," he said of touchscreen laptops in 2010, describing how "your arm wants to fall off" due to fatigue. "Touch surfaces want to be horizontal," he added.
Since then, touchscreens have become ubiquitous on Windows PCs and Chromebooks. Outside of the Touch Bar, which was ultimately reversed because Mac users were not fans, Apple hasn't had a real touchscreen on the Mac.
That changed, as the company announced 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros with "PROLED XDR" displays with, yes, touch support. The devices are also lighter than existing MacBook Pros, have updated speaker systems, and, yes, are more expensive.
Apple eschewed touch on its laptops for years. But it seems, however, that at least some Mac owners disagreed.
"Apple tends not to move to a new technology until it can bring to market a differentiated product," Tom Mainelli, group vice president of device and consumer research at IDC, told Tom's Hardware. "Based on all the demos they are showing here in LA, the drive for 'why now' is because they see a desire for touch from creators who use the Mac."
He added: "The more business-focused answer is the company is creating further segmentation in a mature market, offering a new, more premium tier to its pro lineup."
Years and years of touch
There's one last uphill climb that the touchscreen on the new MacBook Pro faces: the price. After all, the touchscreen is debuting on just the new, redesigned 14- and 16-inch models.
In time, touch will likely fall down the stack, to the cheaper MacBook Pro models, the MacBook Air, and possibly even the Neo. You may see a touch iMac at some point. That will take time. After all, the Mac is just getting OLED, too. That means it's unlikely we'll see mass adoption of touch on the Mac anytime soon. It still has to reach the most popular devices, and even then, it has to coexist with the old standbys, keyboard and mouse.
You could trace the touchscreen laptop back to 2008's HP TouchSmart tx2, which had a swiveling screen. The real touch revolution started around two other releases: The Microsoft Surface Laptop RT and the release of Windows 8 in 2012, which had a touch-forward interface and led to a flood of touch laptops.
Windows 10 came and went with more touchscreens, and by the time of Windows 11's release in 2021, touchscreens largely became the default for Windows laptops. On all but the cheapest devices, I tend to assume a Windows notebook has a touchscreen.
On Chromebooks, the 2013 Chromebook Pixel was considered premium because of its touchscreen. In 2019, I reviewed the Samsung Chromebook Pro and Plus, as Google first experimented with Android apps in Chrome. I remember sitting there poking and prodding the device, thinking that "if Android apps are going to be on Chromebooks, every single one needs a touchscreen." I was seven years too early.
When Apple introduced the MacBook Neo earlier this year, it shocked the industry on price and performance. But it did cut some features, like a backlit keyboard. But some companies that made competitors, such as Dell with its XPS 13, made a point to add that not only did it have a backlit keyboard — it had a touchscreen. (HP also kept the touchscreen with its OmniBook 5. Acer did away with it on the Swift Air 14).
In an interview with Steven Levy at Wired, Apple's chief hardware officer Johny Srouji said that "Ten years is a very very long time," and said that a lot has changed, from display technology to custom silicon to software architecture, which now "met our bar." In the same interview, Apple's senior vice president of worldwide marketing, Greg Joswiak, explained that most creatives have an iPhone or iPad and find it natural: "There’s a generation of young creators and young people using our MacBook Pros that expect to touch."
Touch still has yet to prove itself
This might betray my age, but in general, outside of tablets and 2-in-1 laptops, I don't make a ton of use of touchscreens on computers. It hasn't bothered me once in the past five years that my personal MacBook Pro doesn't have a touchscreen. In general, I agree with Jobs; The ergonomics aren't great.
There are other reasons you might skip a touchscreen. For a long time, they were thought of as battery hogs. The digitizer can add extra weight or cost. And operating systems haven't been designed with touch in mind.
Windows 11 was supposed to be more designed for touchscreens, having taken cues from the unreleased Windows 10X, designed for touchscreens and foldables. But Windows is Windows, and the underlying OS still feels best with a keyboard and mouse.
One of the best operating systems I've seen for touch is Googlebook OS, if only because it's so based on Android 17 that some parts make more sense with a finger than a keyboard and mouse.
For macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple has added system gesture APIs to make apps more likely to support touch. Apple says its own apps are ready, and in its press release, listed a number of other apps like the Microsoft Office suite, Zoom, Notion, Da Vinci Resolve, Adobe Lightroom, Blender, and Algoriddim DJay Paro.
But it also didn't remove the keyboard and touchpad. It's a Mac with a touchscreen, but not touch-first.
For creative professionals who need true accuracy, specialty tablets that work as peripherals will still be king.
When the price is right
There's one last uphill climb that the touchscreen on the new MacBook Pro faces: the price. After all, the touchscreen is debuting on just the new, redesigned 14- and 16-inch models, starting at $2,899 for the 14-incher and $3,399 for the 16-inch models, respectively.
In time, touch will likely fall down the stack to the cheaper Pros, the MacBook Air, and possibly even the Neo. You may see a touch iMac at some point. That will take time. After all, the Mac is just getting OLED, too.
That means it's unlikely we'll see mass adoption of touch on the Mac anytime soon. It still has to reach the most popular devices, and even then, it has to coexist with the old standbys, keyboard and mouse.
Andrew E. Freedman is a senior editor at Tom's Hardware focusing on laptops, desktops and gaming. He also keeps up with the latest news. A lover of all things gaming and tech, his previous work has shown up in Tom's Guide, Laptop Mag, Kotaku, PCMag and Complex, among others.
