articles.title: BIWIN to Show Storage Solutions for AI and the Edge at electronica 2026 - EE Times
articles.text:
Gear up for the AI era. From 122.88 TB enterprise SSDs to integrated embedded memory and Mini SSDs, BIWIN will showcase storage solutions built specifically for a new generation of electronic systems.
BIWIN, a leading provider of memory and storage solutions, will exhibit at electronica 2026, November 10-13 at Trade Fair Center Messe München in Germany– showing the range of BIWIN technologies for AI infrastructure, industrial edge computing, intelligent vehicles, embedded devices, and compact PCs.
BIWIN develops storage for systems with very different demands, from data centers processing AI workloads to wearables with limited board space to industry 5.0 platforms running 24/7. Its in-house capabilities span hardware, firmware, storage algorithms, packaging, testing, and manufacturing, supporting product development across a wide range of applications.
From AI Infrastructure to the Edge
BIWIN’s PCIe 5.0 enterprise SSD portfolio is built around solutions for the different workloads and deployment priorities found across modern data infrastructure.
The SP509/SP519 series comprises high-performance, highly reliable PCIe Gen5 x4 enterprise SSDs optimized for the demanding I/O requirements of AI training and inference. The series delivers sequential read/write speeds of up to 14,700/9,000 MB/s and 4K random read/write performance of up to 3,200K/800K IOPS. The SP5002 leverages high-density QLC NAND technology to deliver up to 61.44 TB in EDSFF form factors, making it ideal for data lakes, cloud infrastructure, and high-density storage. The SP5010, a 2.5-inch U.2 PCIe Gen5 x4 enterprise SSD, offers up to 122.88 TB per drive, combining exceptional storage density and sequential throughput with reduced power consumption, rack footprint, and data center TCO. Designed for hyperscale environments, the SP506/SP516 series of 2.5-inch U.2 PCIe Gen5 x4 enterprise SSDs combines PCIe 5.0 performance with OCP 2.0 compliance and high performance-per-watt efficiency.
Rather than applying one enterprise SSD design across every workload, BIWIN develops SSD solutions around different priorities in endurance, density, power efficiency, interoperability, and latency.
For highly integrated devices in the AI era, the design priorities must change. The BIWIN ePoP5X combines LPDDR5X memory and eMMC storage in a compact Package-on-Package solution, reducing the PCB space required for separate components. It gives designers of next-gen industrial devices, AI glasses, and other space-constrained devices more flexibility to accommodate more memory and storage within increasingly compact hardware.
BIWIN applies its storage engineering across both ends of the computing spectrum, from scaling data infrastructure to fitting more capability into increasingly compact AI edge devices.
Industrial Storage Built for Continuous Workloads
The BIWIN TGS601 Industrial SSD is engineered for sustained, always-on workloads in industrial and edge systems.
At its core is Win-REC, BIWIN’s proprietary intelligent write algorithm developed for continuous video recording. A single TGS601 can support recording from up to 24 simultaneous video streams while maintaining consistent write performance, helping reduce frame drops and recording interruptions in surveillance and other video-intensive deployments.
Wide-temperature operation from -40°C to 85°C, full-capacity onboard DRAM, hardware-based power-loss protection, and multi-layer data protection further support deployment in autonomous security systems, intelligent transportation, in-vehicle surveillance, edge computing, industrial servers, and other demanding environments.
With the TGS601, BIWIN brings workload-specific optimization into the drive itself, targeting the sustained write behavior and operating conditions that define industrial storage in the field. The BIWIN TGS601 provides the high-capacity buffer for Edge AI perception engines and the ruggedized, fail-safe platform needed for Physical AI control loops.
Automotive Storage for Data-Driven Vehicles
BIWIN’s automotive storage portfolio covers the growing data requirements of intelligent cockpits, infotainment, navigation, digital instrument clusters, T-BOX modules, and domain controllers.
The TAU208 UFS 3.1 combines automotive-grade reliability with intelligent power and storage management. Its Deep Sleep mechanism can reduce sleep-mode power consumption by up to 95%, while Performance Throttling Notification and Error History logging provide additional capabilities for managing storage within vehicle systems.
The TAE308 eMMC 5.1 extends the portfolio with an embedded solution built around BIWIN’s self-developed controller. AEC-Q100 Grade 2 qualification and operation from -40°C to 105°C support reliable deployment across demanding automotive environments.
Together, TAU208 and TAE308 give automotive platform developers storage options for different performance and integration requirements as vehicle architectures become more centralized, connected, and software-defined.
Compact Storage for New Device Designs
The BIWIN BL130 Mini SSD brings PCIe Gen4 storage into an ultra-compact removable form factor.
With sequential read speeds up to 3,700 MB/s and capacities up to 2 TB, the BL130 gives OEMs a way to bring SSD-class storage into handheld gaming devices, compact PCs, smart cameras, edge AI platforms, and other systems where internal space is limited.
Its smaller footprint opens valuable room inside the device, giving product designers greater flexibility over system layout while making thinner, more integrated designs possible without sacrificing removable storage.
BIWIN approaches miniaturization from multiple directions across its portfolio. The BL130 reduces the footprint of removable high-performance storage, while ePoP5X combines memory and storage within a single package. Both address physical integration as part of storage engineering.
Storage Designed Around the Application
BIWIN’s products at electronica 2026 address storage challenges at very different scales. The SP5002 brings higher density to data infrastructure with capacities up to 61.44 TB, while the TGS601 uses BIWIN’s Win-REC algorithm to handle sustained multi-channel video recording. For space-constrained hardware, ePoP5X integrates memory and storage in a single package, and the BL130 brings removable PCIe storage into a much smaller footprint.
The differences go beyond form factor or performance. BIWIN develops each solution around how and where the storage will be used, with product architecture and firmware shaped by the demands of the target system.
Visit BIWIN at electronica 2026
Meet BIWIN at electronica 2026 to see the latest enterprise, embedded, industrial, automotive, and PC OEM storage technologies and speak with the team about platform requirements and storage development.
Booth: Hall C6, Booth 140
Date: November 10-13, 2026

For more information, please visit the BIWIN website.

BIWIN Storage Technology Co., Ltd. Recognized globally across enterprise, data center, automotive, industrial, and consumer markets, BIWIN is distinguished by its robust in-house R&D capabilities spanning hardware, software, firmware, storage algorithms, and advanced packaging and testing.
BIWIN’s comprehensive product portfolio encompasses PCIe NVMe SSDs, SATA SSDs, enterprise SSDs, DRAM modules, embedded storage solutions (ePoP/eMMC/UFS), automotive and industrial-grade storage solutions, portable SSDs, memory cards, and USB flash drives.

articles.title: Why AI-powered intelligence is every winning brand’s secret sauce
articles.text:
Why AI-powered intelligence is every winning brand’s secret sauce
As AI reshapes ecommerce, brands are shifting focus from customer acquisition to intelligent fulfilment, inventory management and customer experience. This article explores how AI and agentic systems enable smarter, faster operational decisions.
For years, the playbook for building a winning consumer brand was simple: a compelling product, a strong brand identity, and smart customer acquisition. Those fundamentals still hold, but they no longer decide who wins.
Today's battle is fought in fragments of attention, where brands have seconds to convert interest into a purchase. And the moment “Buy Now” is clicked, a second, harder battle begins: fast fulfilment, a seamless delivery experience, and effortless handling of queries and returns - the moments that actually earn loyalty.
Amid endless channels and ever-shifting marketing strategies, the real differentiator has moved downstream: it's the intelligence behind every operational decision made after the click.
Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming this intelligence layer. No longer limited to chatbots or content generation, AI is transforming how brands forecast demand, allocate inventory, orchestrate fulfilment, engage customers, and optimise operations in real time.
This shift comes at a time when commerce itself has grown far more complex. Consumers now discover, evaluate, and buy across a maze of touchpoints - brand websites, marketplaces, quick commerce, social commerce, and physical stores - often within a single purchase journey. Powering every one of those purchases is a complex web of inventory nodes, warehouses, logistics partners, and engagement systems that must move in perfect synchronisation.
For brands, this translates into a flood of operational data. Every inventory movement, customer interaction, order update, warehouse scan, and delivery milestone becomes a signal that can influence the next business decision. What begins as a simple online business quickly turns into a web of real-time, interconnected decisions - each one shaping the customer experience.
Until a few years ago, brands and marketplaces operated on Systems of Record - a single source of operational truth that captured transactions and helped manage inventory. Ecommerce enablement SaaS platforms turned these Systems of Insight - real-time dashboards and analytics that let businesses move from reactive to data-driven decision-making.
The next phase of this evolution is now underway. Building on this rich data and technology-enabled processes, these Systems of Record and Insight are becoming Systems of Intelligence - where AI is not just analysing information, but actively framing recommendations and executing decisions across business operations.
Consider a fashion retailer during a festive sale. Thousands of orders may arrive simultaneously across its website, marketplaces, and quick commerce platforms. Instead of relying on manual rules or static workflows, AI can continuously evaluate inventory availability, warehouse capacity, delivery timelines, shipping costs, and customer location before automatically routing each order through the most efficient fulfilment path. It can also spot that a fast-moving product is about to run out in one city while stock sits healthy elsewhere and line up a transfer before availability ever becomes the customer's problem.
This matters even more in an omnichannel world, where customers expect availability wherever and however they shop. Delivering on that promise takes more than inventory visibility - it demands continuous coordination across allocation, order orchestration, warehouse operations, logistics, and customer communication. AI makes that coordination possible at a scale and speed manual decision-making simply can't match.
The next frontier here is Agentic AI. Unlike traditional automation, which follows predefined workflows, Agentic AI can reason across multiple variables, recommend the next best course of action, and autonomously execute routine operational decisions within business-defined guardrails. Whether prioritising high-value orders during peak demand, responding to supply chain disruptions, or flagging fulfilment bottlenecks before they bite, these systems move beyond supporting human decisions to actively driving them.
This marks a fundamental shift in how brands approach growth. Acquiring customers remains critical, but sustainable growth increasingly depends on what happens after demand is generated. Rather than adding operational headcount every time order volumes spike, businesses are investing in intelligent platforms that let them scale without proportionately scaling complexity. The goal is no longer simply to process more orders - it's to make better operational decisions, faster and more consistently.
Ecommerce enablement platforms, with deep data and operational ties into brands, are already building this future. AI-first SaaS tools are no longer just software - they're becoming operational partners, continuously improving how the business runs.
Tomorrow's market leaders won't necessarily be the brands with the biggest marketing budgets. They'll be the brands whose technology lets them operate smarter, adapt faster, and make better decisions every single day. Their competitive advantage will increasingly come from the intelligence behind every business decision they make.
(Kapil Makhija is the MD & CEO of Unicommerce eSolutions Limited)

articles.title: « Soyez prudent ! » : Amazon aurait annulé des commandes de cartes graphiques à cause de la crise de la mémoire
articles.text:
Le géant du e-commerce Amazon annulerait-il des commandes de particuliers en raison de la crise mondiale de la mémoire ? C’est en tout cas ce que laissent penser les témoignages d’un utilisateur de X et de Tim Sweeney, fondateur et PDG d’Epic Games.
Des commandes de matériel informatique annulées
Sur le réseau social X, un utilisateur baptisé Nicksaraev explique avoir passé sur Amazon quatre commandes distinctes de DGX Spark, soit un mini-superordinateur dédié à l’intelligence artificielle. Jusque-là, rien d’anormal. Seulement voilà, Nicksaraev assure, captures d’écran à l’appui, qu’Amazon a annulé ses commandes, mais aussi fermé son compte. Dans un mail, le géant du e-commerce lui explique avoir pris cette décision après avoir effectué une analyse approfondie de son compte, sans donner plus de précisions.
Nicksaraev assure ne jamais avoir connu de problème de ce type auparavant et en arrive à une conclusion : « Peu importe les efforts que je déploie, Amazon ne me laisse pas acheter le DGX Spark ». Il avertit ensuite : « Acheter même de modestes quantités de calcul vous place immédiatement sur une liste de surveillance. Soyez prudent ! ». Précisons que Nicksaraev explique avoir besoin de ces DGX Spark pour configurer « des modèles locaux pour un projet » et qu’il ne fait pas de revente.
De son côté, Tim Sweeney, fondateur et PDG d’Epic Games, semble avoir connu une mésaventure similaire. Son compte Amazon n’a pas été fermé, mais ses commandes de deux GPU Nvidia ont été annulées. En réponse au post de Nicksaraev, il explique : « Intéressant. Amazon n’a pas suspendu mon compte, mais a continué d’accepter toutes mes commandes habituelles avant de les annuler juste avant leur date de livraison, après que j’ai essayé d’acheter deux cartes graphiques Nvidia. Plutôt étrange ».
Sam Altman veut que votre RAM soit dans ses datacenters
Nous vous en parlions récemment, Sam Altman a déclaré : « c’est en fait assez terrible que tout le monde ait un tas de DRAM, dont l’offre mondiale est limitée, posé dans son propre ordinateur et utilisé 5 % du temps ». En d’autres termes, la RAM présente sur votre ordinateur devrait être dans les datacenters d’OpenAI.
Il est tout de même difficile de ne pas faire de lien entre ces propos de Sam Altman et les étranges annulations de commandes Amazon rapportées par Tim Sweeney et Nicksaraev. La crise de la mémoire est-elle devenue si grave qu’il faudrait désormais réserver les stocks aux grandes entreprises plutôt qu’aux particuliers ? En soi, c’est déjà le cas depuis un moment, mais il semble que cette tendance s’intensifie encore davantage.

articles.title: Android Auto ne se connecte plus avec certains Samsung Galaxy sous One UI 9
articles.text:
Votre smartphone Samsung ne se connecte plus à Android Auto en voiture ? C'est sans doute normal. Google semble être en train d'identifier le problème, un correctif devrait être apporté dans les jours à venir.
Certains propriétaires de smartphones Samsung Galaxy signalent des problèmes avec Android Auto depuis quelques jours. L'arrivée de ces soucis coïncide avec le passage à One UI 9, la nouvelle version de la surcouche de Samsung, basée sur Android 17. Si Google a pris connaissance de ces signalements, l'origine du problème n'est pas encore indiquée.
Des connexions qui échouent, ou se coupent
Les utilisateurs concernés décrivent deux types de problèmes. D'une part, Android Auto qui refuserait catégoriquement de se connecter au système du véhicule, et d'autre part, des déconnexions répétées en cours d'utilisation. Le problème ne semble pas être lié à un seul modèle de smartphone Samsung, mais ne semble pas être généralisé non plus. Sur les forums communautaires de Samsung, un propriétaire explique qu'Android Auto a cessé de fonctionner après la mise à jour vers One UI 9.
Toutefois, sur Reddit, si d'autres utilisateurs font état de problèmes semblables, pour certains, Android Auto fonctionne sans aucun problème chez eux.
La dernière mise à jour en cause ? Google enquête
Pour étayer ce souci en rapport potentiel avec One UI 9, un propriétaire de Galaxy S25 Edge a tenté de connecter son véhicule à Android Auto avec deux Samsung Galaxy restés sous One UI 8.5, sans difficulté. En revanche, après la mise à jour d'un Galaxy S24 Ultra sous One UI 9, les problèmes ont commencé. Si ce problème isolé ne suffit pas à lui seul à expliquer une panne massive, Google a répondu à la plainte d'un utilisateur de Galaxy A55 pour le même problème.
Le groupe a confirmé que l'équipe d'Android Auto avait bien reçu le signalement et l'avait transmis en interne.
Google n'a toutefois pas encore indiqué si l'enquête interne pour identifier le problème était terminée et si One UI 9 était la cause du problème.
- Interface simplifiée et claire
- Intégration fluide des apps mobiles
- Commandes vocales efficaces
Un sentiment de déjà-vu
Android Auto a déjà rencontré des problèmes similaires. Des déconnexions intempestives en mode sans-fil avaient déjà été signalées, notamment sur le Galaxy A55, bien avant la mise à jour vers One UI 9. Reste-t-il encore à savoir si c'est un ancien problème qui refait surface, ou si c'est une conséquence directe de la dernière mise à jour de Samsung.
Les utilisateurs doivent en attendant continuer à chercher une solution par eux-mêmes, en attendant un correctif de la part de Google, et une potentielle mise à jour transmise à Samsung.
Source : AndroidAuthority

articles.title: Hace 50 años, Viking 2 grabó dos misteriosas señales. Hoy unos científicos apuntan a la grabación más antigua de un terremoto marciano
articles.text:
En 1975, la NASA envió a Marte las sondas Viking 1 y Viking 2 con el objetivo de buscar posibles signos de vida. Para saber si es o fue en algún momento un planeta habitable, era importante estudiar tanto su composición geológica como la posible aparición de terremotos. Para esto último, ambas sondas contaban con un sismómetro. Sin embargo, la primera lo desplegó mal y la segunda captó demasiadas interferencias como para determinar si realmente se estaban detectando terremotos. Era muy difícil analizar sus señales de forma fiable, así que estas cayeron en el olvido. Ahora, 50 años después, un equipo de científicos chinos ha decidido rescatarlas y ha encontrado la que podría ser la grabación más antigua existente de un terremoto marciano.
El problema de Viking 2. El sismómetro de Viking 2 estaba montado directamente sobre el módulo de aterrizaje. Este se movía por efecto del viento, transmitiendo las vibraciones al sismómetro como si de una vela se tratase. Por lo tanto, era imposible determinar si las señales que captaba procedían del suelo o del viento. Además, el único contacto de Viking con el suelo eran sus patas. Eran estas las que transmitían las vibraciones hacia el sismómetro, por lo que podrían generarse muchas interferencias por el camino.
La NASA aprendió de sus errores. En 2018, la NASA envió a Marte la sonda InSight. De nuevo, dotaron a un módulo de aterrizaje de un sismómetro, pero en este caso había una gran diferencia. Y es que el vehículo disponía de un brazo robótico que, una vez en el planeta rojo, sacó hacia fuera el sismómetro y lo colocó directamente sobre el suelo. Así, las vibraciones que captaba serían mayormente subterráneas, sin tantas interferencias del viento.
Más de mil terremotos. Entre 2018 y 2022, InSight detectó 1.319 terremotos, demostrando que el planeta rojo tiene más actividad sísmica de lo que se pensaba. Si el sismómetro de las sondas Viking hubiese funcionado mejor, quizás habría detectado algunos. Ahora bien, ¿realmente habría que dar por perdidas las grabaciones de Viking 2?
Sol 80. Los días marcianos se conocen como soles. Viking 2 realizó dos grabaciones sospechosas, una en el Sol 53 y otra en el Sol 80. La primera se terminó catalogando como una racha de viento, pero la segunda en su día se vio como buena candidata a albergar un terremoto. Desgraciadamente, había demasiadas dudas a causa de las interferencias. Medio siglo después, los autores del estudio que se acaba de publicar pensaron que se podrían volver a estudiar teniendo en cuenta todo lo aprendido con InSight. Las analizaron minuciosamente y vieron que en la grabación del Sol 80 había algo muy parecido tanto a los terremotos de California como a los martemotos detectados por InSight.
La vibración se parecía; pero, además, se había detectado de madrugada, cuando los vientos suelen ser menos intensos, y justo 20 minutos después de un periodo de vientos débiles. Era poco probable que fuese una interferencia del viento marciano.
Otras opciones. En realidad, no se puede descartar que la grabación se corresponda con otro tipo de evento, como el impacto de un meteorito. De hecho, nunca lo sabremos con seguridad. Pero sí que es cierto que estos científicos han hecho bien en rescatar la grabación, pues podría albergar la señal del terremoto marciano más antiguo que se ha grabado jamás. Aunque no lo sepamos con seguridad, la incertidumbre es una parte importante de la investigación del espacio, por lo que sigue siendo interesante.

articles.title: ChatGPT gratis responde más corto y adula menos, pero cometió más errores en las pruebas de OpenAI
articles.text:
OpenAI actualizó en pasados días el modelo que ChatGPT usa en su versión gratuita para que dé respuestas más breves y con menos lenguaje complaciente. Según el informe de seguridad que la empresa publicó ese día, la versión nueva comete más errores factuales que la anterior en las seis métricas que OpenAI midió.
El cambio alcanza a los usuarios del plan gratuito, a los del plan Go y a quienes usan ChatGPT sin iniciar sesión, según las notas de versiones de la empresa. En los planes Plus y Pro, el modelo principal no cambia: la versión actualizada solo aparece como respaldo cuando el usuario agota su límite de mensajes con GPT-6.
El modelo se llama GPT-6 Luna. OpenAI lo llevó a ChatGPT el 7 de octubre de 2026 para los planes gratuito y Go, junto con una función que permite respuestas con elementos visuales e interactivos. Los planes de pago usan otro modelo, GPT-6 Sol, que esta actualización no modifica.
El documento, un anexo a la tarjeta del sistema de GPT-6 Luna (el informe técnico que la empresa publica con cada modelo), afirma que la versión del 29 de octubre de 2026 muestra tasas de error factual más altas que la del 7 de octubre de 2026 en las seis métricas. Mantiene, sin embargo, tasas menores que GPT-5.6 Luna, el modelo de agosto.
Respuestas 12% más cortas y menor puntaje en salud
OpenAI muestra esos errores solo en un gráfico, sin cifras en el texto. Las tablas del anexo sí detallan los resultados en HealthBench, el conjunto de preguntas de salud con el que la empresa evalúa sus modelos. La longitud media de las respuestas bajó de 3.361 a 2.970 caracteres, cerca de un 12%.
El puntaje de HealthBench, ajustado por longitud, pasó de 50,4 a 48,2 sobre 100. En la variante HealthBench Hard, con preguntas más difíciles, cayó de 27,2 a 22,8. En HealthBench Consensus bajó de 95,0 a 93,3, y en HealthBench Professional, de 48,2 a 47,4.
En MentalHealthBench, la prueba de OpenAI sobre situaciones de salud mental, el puntaje general bajó de 51,73 a 48,68. La tabla del anexo indica un error estándar de unos 0,97 puntos para la versión nueva.
Mixed, un sitio especializado en IA, señaló que la nota de OpenAI no incluye conversaciones de ejemplo ni resultados comparativos sobre la reducción del tono halagador. La nota tampoco promete que todas las respuestas sean breves ni que desaparezcan los errores.
El anexo clasifica a la versión actualizada con capacidad alta en ciberseguridad y en biología y química, según el marco de preparación de la empresa. Usa las mismas salvaguardas que la versión del 7 de octubre de 2026.
La adulación ya había obligado a OpenAI a retroceder
No es la primera vez que OpenAI corrige el tono de ChatGPT. En abril de 2025, la empresa retiró una actualización de GPT-4o que reconoció como muy aduladora. El director ejecutivo, Sam Altman, admitió entonces que el modelo era adulador, según la BBC.
Usuarios habían difundido capturas en las que el chatbot elogiaba lo que le escribieran. Una persona contó en Reddit que ChatGPT respaldó su decisión de dejar un medicamento. La empresa decía entonces que 500 millones de personas usaban ChatGPT cada semana.
OpenAI explicó entonces que había dado mucho peso a las valoraciones inmediatas de los usuarios, como los pulgares hacia arriba, y que el modelo derivó hacia respuestas de apoyo poco sinceras. Prometió reforzar las pruebas y dar más control sobre el comportamiento del chatbot.
OpenAI no publicó en el texto del anexo las cifras exactas de error factual de la versión del 29 de octubre: solo las muestra en un gráfico, con tasas más altas que las de la versión del 7 de octubre y más bajas que las del modelo de agosto.

articles.title: IA faz demanda por fitas magnéticas voltar a crescer • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
IA faz demanda por fitas magnéticas voltar a crescer
Fujifilm investirá R$ 344 milhões para quintuplicar a produção de fitas magnéticas. Mídias são usadas por data centers para guardar grandes volumes de dados.
A expansão da inteligência artificial está aumentando a demanda por uma série de outras tecnologias, incluindo fitas magnéticas para armazenamento: a Fujifilm anunciou um investimento de cerca de 10 bilhões de ienes (aproximadamente R$ 344 milhões) para ampliar a produção desse tipo de mídia no Japão.
Com o aporte, a fabricante pretende quintuplicar a capacidade de produção de fitas LTO (Linear Tape-Open) até 2028, tomando como referência o volume do ano fiscal de 2025, de acordo com o ArsTechnica. O investimento mira, principalmente, a demanda de data centers e provedores de computação em nuvem por armazenamento de grandes volumes de dados.
Segundo a Fujifilm, será o maior aporte individual já feito pela companhia em instalações destinadas à produção dessas fitas. Um dos focos deve ser a fabricação LTO Ultrium10, geração mais recente da família de fitas da empresa.
Apesar de terem praticamente desaparecido do uso doméstico, as fitas magnéticas continuam sendo utilizadas em ambientes corporativos para arquivamento e backup de dados.
Atualmente, esses sistemas costumam ser usados em equipamentos para servidores e racks, por exemplo, além de bibliotecas automatizadas e produções audiovisuais. Já são comercializados cartuchos compatíveis com LTO-10, capazes de armazenar até 40 TB nativos ou 100 TB comprimidos.
A principal vantagem é o custo de armazenamento de grandes volumes por longos períodos. Para situações em que as informações não precisam ser acessadas constantemente, as fitas podem sair mais baratas do que manter os mesmos dados em HDDs ou SSDs — que têm ficado cada vez mais caros nos últimos meses pela crise do setor de chips de memória, também por causa da IA.
A Fujifilm atua nesse mercado desde a década de 1950 e passou a comercializar fitas da família LTO nos anos 2000. Em 2011, a companhia começou a usar partículas magnéticas de ferrita de bário na fabricação das mídias, lembra o ArsTechnica. A combinação dessas partículas com ferrita de estrôncio, que forma o LTO Ultrium10, chegou em 2025.
Outro motivo para o uso de fitas, segundo a empresa, é a possibilidade de manter cópias de dados fisicamente desconectadas da rede. Os cartuchos podem ser removidos dos leitores e armazenados separadamente, criando o chamado air-gap.
Essa característica pode ser útil em estratégias de backup contra ransomware, evitando que ataques em servidores comprometam os dados na fita.

articles.title: Robotics startup Tutor Intelligence nabs $75M investment - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Robotics startup Tutor Intelligence nabs $75M investment
Warehouse automation provider Tutor Intelligence Inc. today announced that it has raised $75 million in funding.
Andreessen Horowitz led the Series A investment. It was joined by Union Square Ventures and Neo, which led Tutor’s previous two rounds.
The merchandise that a warehouse processes often arrives on pallets, flat wood structures capable of holding up to several tons. Tutor sells a mobile robotic arm called Cassie that can take packages off a pallet and place them in containers. It’s also capable of performing the opposite operation.
Cassie can process up to 18 items per minute depending on the package type. Its robotic arm is equipped with a vacuum gripper designed to pick up more than 50 pounds. The arm is mounted on a four-wheeled platform that enables Cassie to autonomously travel between different sections of a warehouse.
Automating pallet processing is challenging because the merchandise that a warehouse receives changes over time. Historically, adapting a robotic arm’s workflow to a new item involved manual coding. Cassie uses built-in artificial intelligence models to learn how to pick up new package types automatically.
Tutor also ships its AI models with a second wheeled robot called Sonny. It uses a pair of robotic arms to take items off warehouse shelves and place them in packages. The robot finds the needed items using an array of time-of-flight and stereo cameras. Both camera varieties collect depth data, which makes it easier to determine the distance of an object.
Tutor plans to apply Sonny to additional use cases in the future. In particular, it sees industrial companies using the system to assemble products and perform equipment maintenance. Tutor teaches Sonny’s AI models new tasks in a facility that hosts more than 100 robots. Human experts demonstrate how to perform a task using a remotely controlled robot and the AI models learn by imitation.
“Sonny’s manufacturability at scale makes it an ideal robot not just for most handwork in manufacturing and logistics, but for arbitrary business-critical applications across the physical economy,” Tutor co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Josh Gruenstein wrote in a blog post. “Data collected by our Sonny fleet trains our largest and most capable robot foundation models at the frontier of rate and reliability.”
Tutor sells its robots under a usage-based pricing model. It removes the need for customers to make a large upfront purchase, which lowers the entry barrier. The company disclosed today that the number of facilities where its robots are used has nearly quadrupled over the past year.
Tutor will use its newly raised funding to enhance its AI models and speed up robot production.

articles.title: Marvell Acquires Lumentum for $115 Billion All-Stock Deal
articles.text:
Monday, November 2nd 2026
Marvell Acquires Lumentum for $115 Billion All-Stock Deal
Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MRVL) and Lumentum (NASDAQ: LITE) today announced that they have entered into a definitive agreement for Marvell to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction. Under the terms of the agreement, Lumentum stockholders will receive a fixed exchange ratio of 4.500 shares of Marvell common stock for each share of Lumentum common stock they own. The transaction has an implied enterprise value of $115 billion for Lumentum, representing approximately $1,132 per share of Lumentum common stock and a premium of approximately 23.9% based on each company's unaffected closing share price as of October 28, 2026, the last trading day before market speculation regarding a potential transaction began. Post-closing, current Marvell stockholders will own approximately 67% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis, while Lumentum stockholders will own approximately 33%.
The AI infrastructure industry is at an inflection point. Rapidly growing bandwidth requirements and the physical limitations of copper-based connectivity are accelerating the transition toward optical technologies. As AI infrastructure scales to increasingly complex architectures, particularly scale-up and scale-in, the industry is shifting from discrete, modular components toward highly integrated optical solutions that require much closer co-design of electrical and optical technologies to deliver greater bandwidth, performance and energy efficiency.The combination brings together best-in-breed technology to meet this need, joining Marvell's strengths in electrical and optical interconnect, network switching, custom XPU and XPU attach and advanced semiconductor technologies with Lumentum's expertise in high-performance lasers, optical transceivers, optical circuit switching (OCS) and specialized compound semiconductor manufacturing. Following closing, the combined company is expected to offer a highly complementary portfolio spanning leading-edge CMOS, silicon photonics, compound semiconductors, advanced packaging and manufacturing capabilities. The combination is intended to enable deeper integration and co-design across the electrical and optical signal chain, positioning Marvell to deliver highly optimized connectivity solutions across a wide range of distances, from distributed data centers to connections within advanced semiconductor packages.
"AI infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental architectural shift toward optical connectivity, creating an opportunity that comes along once in a generation," said Matt Murphy, Chairman and CEO of Marvell. "The companies that move first and help define this transition will set the standard for decades to come. By bringing together two leaders with highly complementary technologies, exceptional talent and specialized manufacturing capabilities, we intend to help shape the next era of AI connectivity and create exceptional stockholder value."
"Joining Marvell creates a company uniquely positioned to capitalize on a market opportunity of $550 billion and generate significant, sustainable stockholder value," said Michael Hurlston, President and CEO of Lumentum. "Surging AI data traffic requires rapid hardware innovation, and this combination enhances our ability to deliver next-generation solutions at scale. Together with Marvell, we will meet our customers' complete interconnect needs, spanning scale-across and scale-out today to scale-up and scale-in domains tomorrow. By offering extreme co-design around our customers' demanding requirements, we will help them achieve faster time to market, accelerated innovation cycles and category-defining performance."
Compelling Strategic and Financial Rationale
The combination is expected to deliver substantial strategic and financial benefits:
- Creates a category leader in AI connectivity: Combining Marvell's electrical and optical interconnect, switching and custom silicon technologies with Lumentum's high-performance lasers, optical transceivers and OCS capabilities will create a comprehensive connectivity portfolio spanning scale-across, scale-out, scale-up and scale-in. Upon closing, the combined company anticipates being positioned to address customer connectivity requirements across a broad range of distances and topologies, from distributed data centers to advanced semiconductor packages.
- Enables end-to-end extreme co-design and accelerates customer innovation: As AI infrastructure becomes increasingly complex, customers require higher levels of integration and optimization across digital, analog and optical technologies. By bringing together complementary technologies and engineering expertise across the signal chain, the combined company expects to be positioned to develop highly-optimized, pre-validated optical solutions designed to improve bandwidth, performance and power efficiency, accelerate customer time to market and support high-volume production.
- Combines highly specialized manufacturing capabilities and enhances R&D resources: Lumentum brings advanced compound semiconductor manufacturing and process technologies, including indium phosphide (InP), as well as high-speed and high-power laser capabilities. After closing, the combined company plans to bring together leading-edge semiconductor design, advanced packaging and specialized manufacturing capabilities to enable deeper heterogeneous integration, strengthen strategic supply and accelerate the development of next-generation optical technologies.
- Creates significant long-term stockholder value: The combination brings together two of the fastest-growing companies enabling AI infrastructure and expands the combined company's total addressable market to $550 billion and enhances the combined company's ability to serve customers in emerging scale-up and scale-in markets. The transaction is expected to enhance the combined company's long-term revenue growth, non-GAAP gross margin and non-GAAP operating margin profile, provide line of sight to more than $1 billion in annual run-rate cost synergies and is expected to be accretive to Marvell non-GAAP earnings per share in year one post-close.
Transaction Structure and Terms
Under the terms of the agreement, which has been unanimously approved by the boards of directors of both companies, Lumentum stockholders will receive a fixed exchange ratio of 4.500 shares of Marvell common stock for each share of Lumentum common stock held at the time of closing, implying pro forma ownership of approximately 33% of the combined company for Lumentum stockholders on a fully diluted basis.
Following closing, Matt Murphy will continue as Chairman and CEO of the combined company. As part of the transaction, three members of Lumentum's Board of Directors, including Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston, will join Marvell's Board, which currently consists of seven directors.
The transaction is expected to close in the first half of calendar year 2028, subject to approval by Marvell and Lumentum stockholders, receipt of regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions.

articles.title: Google takes Dreambeans to India in bid to bring AI-generated personal stories to the masses | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google has launched its experimental AI app Dreambeans in India, its first market outside the U.S., as the company looks to tap the world’s second-largest internet market to bring personalized visual stories drawn from users’ digital activity to a broader audience.
On Monday, Google expanded Dreambeans, available on Android and iOS, to India with support for 13 local languages, including Hindi, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, and Bengali, alongside English. The launch comes less than two months after Google made the app available to all eligible U.S. users aged 18 and older.
Introduced in June, Google’s Dreambeans uses information from connected Google services, including Calendar, Gemini, Gmail, Photos, Search, and YouTube, to proactively generate personalized, illustrated stories about users’ interests and everyday lives, without requiring them to enter a prompt. The app initially featured static, AI-generated illustrations, but Google recently added a feature that uses its Veo video-generation model to even animate images in select stories.
Google said it chose India as Dreambeans’ first international market because of strong interest from Indian users seeking access to the app and the widespread use of its services in the country. India stood out for its high overlap of users across Gemini, Gmail, and Google Photos, Google product manager Gozde Oznur said during a press briefing.
Dreambeans has recorded nearly 55,000 downloads in the U.S. since its June debut, according to estimates from market intelligence firm Sensor Tower shared with TechCrunch. About 63% of those downloads came in September, when Google opened the app to all eligible U.S. users aged 18 and older. However, downloads dropped 84% month over month to about 5,500 in October.
In the first 30 days after Google opened Dreambeans to all eligible U.S. users, the app recorded an estimated 29,000 downloads, compared with 7.4 million for Meta’s Muse, 2.8 million for ChatGPT, 362,000 for Grok Bot, and 155,000 for Claude during their respective first 30 days after launch, Sensor Tower estimates show. However, unlike those general-purpose AI apps, Dreambeans focuses on generating personalized stories instead of responding to a broad range of user queries.
Even though Dreambeans supports many widely spoken Indian languages, users can select only one language at a time for their generated stories. The app can draw on information across Google services in multiple languages, but it cannot currently generate stories that mix languages, Oznur said during the briefing.
That could limit Dreambeans’ appeal in India, where many people regularly switch between languages, including Hindi and English, often mixing the two in what is commonly known as Hinglish.
Dreambeans’ dependence on information from users’ Google accounts also raises questions about privacy and data access. The app uses Google’s Personal Intelligence technology to draw on connected services and personalize its AI-generated stories. Those services can contain sensitive personal information that some users may not want to share with an AI app just to receive personalized content.
Users can choose which Google services to connect to Dreambeans and disconnect them at any time, Oznur said. They can also delete their Dreambeans data from within the app. Moreover, Oznur asserted that information deleted from the underlying connected services is also removed from Dreambeans’ personalization system.
Users, Oznur said, can tell Dreambeans to avoid certain subjects, including business-related information, and the app will try to adjust its stories accordingly. She added that Dreambeans is available only to personal Gmail account holders, not enterprise users, and that generated stories are visible only to the account holder.
Dreambeans’ proactive approach also carries the risk of surfacing memories that users may find upsetting. Oznur acknowledged that Dreambeans could generate stories involving people who have died, for instance. She said users can tell the app to stop showing certain subjects, comparing the feature to controls in Google Photos that let users limit which memories appear.
Oznur told reporters that Google is exploring ways to make Dreambeans more actionable, moving beyond personalized stories and recommendations to help users act on the app’s suggestions.

articles.title: Nvidia Brev security breach may have exposed SSH keys used to access customer VMs — investigation finds unauthorized activity spanning 16 days, but no evidence of misuse
articles.text:
Nvidia Brev security breach may have exposed SSH keys used to access customer VMs — investigation finds unauthorized activity spanning 16 days, but no evidence of misuse
Nvidia replaces potentially exposed SSH keys after detecting unauthorized activity on its Brev cloud platform
Hackers have struck Nvidia again, this time targeting its BREV cloud development platform, with users reporting unauthorized activity between October 4 and October 20. According to a notification sent to affected customers, some accounts may have been exposed. The company said it had investigated the incident and identified unidentified activity on the platform, adding that information stored on the platform may have been exposed to malicious actors. The said information included the SHH key set up by Brev.
The company has already replaced the affected SHH keys and updated customer machines with new ones but says they found no evidence of improper use. “We are writing to inform you that Nvidia Corporation has experienced a security incident that may have affected the security of your data," the notification reads. “Our analysis determined that your information from our Brev network may have been affected. This SSH key has since been rotated, and your instances have been updated with the replacement key.”
However, the company fell short of explaining how the attackers gained access, or whether anyone attempted to use the compromised data. Moreover, it has not disclosed whether customer data or workloads were accessed. SSH is a protocol used to establish a secure connection between ‘virtual machines’ or remote computers working together. Developers or system administrators can use it to manage remote servers, transfer files, and execute commands without needing physical access to the machine—much like AnyDesk or TeamViewer, but now for developers. Brev uses SSH keys to help customers access these services in the cloud, meaning if attackers access these keys, they could potentially take control of a virtual machine, depending on its specific permissions and other security controls.
The incident comes as several firms hosting AI development services and cloud infrastructure grapple with mounting security incidents involving customer credentials. On October 30, cybersecurity firm Wiz released a blog dubbed ‘Black October’ for AI developer platforms. The firm identified at least nine platforms that have had security incidents during the month, including Zeabur, Fireworks AI, Lightning AI, Opencode, Warp, Northflank, among others. As per the firm, the incidents were recurrent, with researchers noting that “all public reports highlight targeted exploitation, explicitly hunting stored environment variables, with a focus on those granted AI access.” Wiz further shared two cases involving compromised Amazon Bedrock credentials where, in one, attackers generated about 800,000 API calls over 30 hours while another key was used to make roughly 1.7 million calls over 13 hours. The combined usage came to a staggering $100,000 at list prices.
Such incidents are not just restricted to Nvidia, with major US banks including JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley and Bank of America restricting Agents from accessing customer accounts earlier this month. Their primary concern is that automated assistants could veer off set instructions and initiate unauthorized approvals. Similarly, the CyberCartel hacking group has previously used Anthropic’s AI tool Claude and Grok’s XAI to conduct attacks on more than 400 Latin American institutions, mostly targeting banks and mobile payments services after attackers obtained customer login credentials. China-linked attackers have also been accused of using AI agents in a ConnectWise supply chain attack that left about 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants exposed, with some attacks reportedly reaching privileged access in under three hours.
Though updating compromised software may not be enough to eliminate an attacker’s access, Bradford Regeski, a threat intelligence analyst at RH-ISAC, has recommended extensive checks for customers in SHH-related incidents, asking users to “Isolate hosts that installed the compromised extension during the exposure window,” remove unauthorized SSH keys and persistence mechanisms, and rotate credentials and sessions.

articles.text:
Vor Mega-Börsengang: Was trotz Umsatzexplosion gegen Anthropic sprechen könnte
Läuft alles, wie seit Monaten von manchen Börsianer:innen erwartet, könnte in den kommenden Tagen der größte Börsengang aller Zeiten über die Bühne gehen. KI-Anbieter Anthropic soll dabei eine Bewertung von rund zwei Billionen Dollar anstreben. Doch zuletzt hat sich die Hype-Stimmung rund um die KI-Branche deutlich abgekühlt. Und auch die neuesten Zahlen von Anthropic bieten durchaus Potenzial für Zweifel.
Anthropic: Umsatz bremst sich ein
Zwar hat der Claude-Entwickler für das abgelaufene dritte Quartal 2026 einmal mehr ein rekordverdächtiges Umsatzplus gemeldet. Gegenüber dem Vorjahresquartal stieg der Umsatz um 1.127 Prozent auf 16,96 Milliarden Dollar. Doch zuletzt hat sich das Umsatzwachstum damit stark eingebremst, wie CNBC schreibt. Nach 132 Prozent und 144 Prozent in den ersten beiden Quartalen kletterte der Q3-Umsatz gegenüber dem Vorquartal „nur“ um 47 Prozent.
Darüber hinaus musste Anthropic im abgelaufenen Dreimonatszeitraum einen Verlust von 23,29 Milliarden Dollar hinnehmen. In den neun Monaten des Jahres 2026 summierte sich das Minus damit auf 104 Milliarden Dollar. Auch wenn ein Großteil davon aus Neubewertungen von Wandelanleihen und Derivaten stammt – im dritten Quartal blieb auch unter dem Strich ein operativer Verlust von 567 Millionen Dollar. Im Quartal zuvor hatte noch ein Gewinn von 974 Millionen Dollar zu Buche gestanden.
895 Milliarden Dollar an Verpflichtungen
Ebenfalls auf die Stimmung potenzieller Investor:innen drücken dürfte die Offenlegung des Umfangs von Kaufverpflichtungen und Mietverträgen sein, die vor allem für den Ausbau von Rechenleistung und Infrastruktur gedacht sind. Diese Verpflichtungen belaufen sich nämlich auf gut 895 Milliarden Dollar. Der Großteil dieser geplanten Ausgaben soll schon in den kommenden fünf Jahren anfallen.
Darüber hinaus wies Anthropic in der aktuellen Mitteilung auf Risiken für seine vertraglich vereinbarten Rechenkapazitäten hin. Möglich sei, dass die Partner keine Finanzierung für den Kauf von KI-Chips erhalten. Die kreditfinanzierte Expansion der KI-Branche und die zugleich ausbleibenden Anzeichen für den massiven Investitionen entsprechende Einnahmen hatten dafür gesorgt, dass die Aktien großer Tech-Firmen zuletzt kräftig nachgaben.
IPO-Preisspanne noch nicht bekannt
Geht es um die mögliche Preisspanne für die im Rahmen des IPO auszugebenden Aktien, hält sich Anthropic weiter bedeckt. Bloomberg zufolge rechnen Investor:innen mittlerweile eher mit 1,4 bis 1,5 Billionen Dollar statt der zwei Billionen Dollar, die zuvor im Raum gestanden hatten. Doch auch damit würde das KI-Unternehmen den Börsengang von SpaceX deutlich übertreffen, der 86,2 Milliarden Dollar eingebracht hatte und als bisher größter IPO gilt.

articles.title: Elon Musk throttled Grok Bot after its usage costs became ‘unsustainably high' — as ChatGPT users call OpenAI's new limits the 'end of an era'
articles.text:
Elon Musk says Grok Bot was throttled because costs were ‘unsustainably high’ — as users call the move a ‘rug pull’
The increasing costs of AI
- Grok Bot users recently found they were hitting their usage limits very fast
- That’s because Elon Musk decided to throttle Grok Bot usage limits
- The X owner said Grok Bot costs were "unsustainably high"
If you noticed that you burned through your Grok Bot usage much faster than usual in recent days, there’s a reason for that: Elon Musk intentionally limited users’ AI agent allowances in the face of “unsustainably high costs.” And as you’d expect, a lot of people are unhappy with that.
The revelation came about after an X user pinged platform owner Musk, asking for a Grok Bot reset after they surprisingly hit their 100% usage limit, four days before it was due to reset. They additionally commented that “Normally I don’t even reach 100%.”
Musk then replied to the post, stating: “The cost of serving Grok Bot was unsustainably high relative to revenue.”
Many X users seemed irked by the situation, with several saying that their Grok Bot usage had hit the 100% limit while they were sleeping and not using any AI agents. Users claimed their usage had suddenly gone from 50% to 100%, 35% to 78%, and 70% to 100%, all supposedly without using Grok Bot at all.
Unsustainable costs
Elon Musk’s comments come amid broader scrutiny of the financial sustainability of many AI products. Tech stocks — including those of many leading AI firms — fell sharply last week as investors grew concerned over the profitability of the industry, with Google revealing that its own AI summaries have hurt its search advertising revenue.
Concerns have also been raised in recent months over the finances involved in many AI companies’ offerings. For instance, users of AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude Code can often spend many times more in tokens than they’re actually paying in monthly subscriptions, leading to questions over how sustainable many AI business models really are and whether things will need to be adjusted in the near future.
This changing landscape hasn’t gone down well with many users, of course. One thread on Reddit dubbed Musk’s about-face an “indirect rug pull” of Grok Bot, with features and usage limited in a bid to cut costs.

But it’s unlikely that AI producers will be able to subsidize their products’ costs to users forever. Usage limits will necessarily need to tighten (as OpenAI quietly announced recently, much to the frustration of users) and prices will need to increase for these business models to make sense. So don’t be surprised if Grok Bot’s lower cap is just the first of many big changes looming on the horizon.

articles.text:
MobiKwik reports Rs 11.83 Cr profit in Q2; Indian female workforce growth lacks quality jobs
MobiKwik’s revenue rose 9.4% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 295.70 crore. The company attributed the quarter’s performance to higher gross merchandise value (GMV) growth and improved margins.
Dear Reader,
Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani has emerged as the world's biggest billionaire wealth gainer, adding over $6 billion to his fortune in a single day, as shares of his flagship company surged following a stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings performance.
According to Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires list, Ambani's wealth increased by 7.85%, or $6.3 billion, making him the biggest gainer globally in the latest update to the ranking on November 2.
ICYMI: The gap between economic superpowers, the US and China, versus the rest of the world is striking. The US economy is bigger than the combined GDP of Germany, Japan, the UK, India, and France.
In other news, ValueQuest Tristar Fund, an India-focused private equity fund, has secured over Rs 2,100 crore in investor commitments within 15 months of its first close, surpassing both its base target and the full greenshoe option. The fund targets advanced manufacturing sectors, including aerospace, defence, precision engineering, and the energy transition. It has so far invested in four companies: Hi-Q Electronics, Rangsons Aerospace, Waaree Energy Storage Solutions, and Trusted Aerospace & Engineers (TASE Global).
Meanwhile, PRISM, parent entity of hospitality chain OYO, has posted a consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 353 crore in the first quarter ended June, registering 17% growth from Rs 301 crore in the year-ago period. The quarterly profit included a deferred-tax credit of approximately Rs 244 crore, according to the company's audited financials.

- Indian female workforce growth lacks quality jobs

News
MobiKwik reports Rs 11.83 Cr profit in Q2
Fintech company MobiKwik reported a net profit in the second quarter of FY27, compared with a loss in the year-ago period, marking its fourth consecutive profitable quarter and its highest-ever quarterly profit. It saw a net profit of Rs 11.83 crore for the July-September quarter, against a loss of Rs 28.61 crore in Q2 FY26.
Key takeaways:
- MobiKwik’s revenue rose 9.4% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 295.70 crore. The company attributed the quarter’s performance to higher gross merchandise value (GMV) growth and improved margins.
- According to MobiKwik, its payment business recorded a 35% year-on-year (YoY) growth in gross merchandise value (GMV) to Rs 59,677 crore in Q2 FY27.
- The company’s registered user base increased to 196.3 million in Q2 FY27, compared with 183.5 million in the corresponding quarter last fiscal.

Social impact
Indian female workforce growth lacks quality jobs
Women in India are working more but they remain tied to agriculture and other lower-productivity activities, while the disproportionate burden of unpaid domestic and care work continues to constrain their economic opportunities.
A new report, The Participation Paradox: Women’s Work and Time-Use in India, 2017-18 to 2025, examines this disconnect.
Key takeaways:
- Between 2017-18 and 2025, the number of women in the workforce nearly doubled, from 104 million to 201 million. The female worker population ratio also rose from 22% to 38%.
- However, the rise in numbers tells a more complicated story. Much of the increase was driven by rural women entering agriculture, taking up own-account work, and engaging in unpaid family work.
- In 2025, 60% of women outside the labour force cited childcare or personal household commitments as their primary reason for not working.

S'il se paie le luxe d'être un peu plus fin et plus léger que son prédécesseur et ose enfin le pari d'une batterie au silicium-carbone, il apporte peu de nouveautés matérielles à sa série. Dans l'ensemble donc, le smartphone est réussi, mais peine à se distinguer d'un Z Flip 7 qui reste d'actualité.

articles.title: Meta travaille sur un robot humanoïde qui fait le ménage à votre place
articles.text:
Depuis maintenant un moment, nous savons que Meta travaille sur l’élaboration de robots humanoïdes. L’entreprise américaine se concentre toutefois sur les logiciels et l’intelligence artificielle permettant de faire fonctionner les robots, plutôt que sur leur matériel. En mai dernier, Meta a d’ailleurs racheté Assured Robot Intelligence (ARI), une start-up spécialisée dans le développement de modèles d’intelligence artificielle destinés aux robots humanoïdes. Nous apprenons aujourd’hui que l’entreprise de Mark Zuckerberg travaille sur un nouveau robot destiné à la maison.
Meta travail sur un robot destiné à effectuer des tâches ménagères
Comme le rapporte le média The Information, Meta travaille sur un robot humanoïde dont la fonction est de réaliser des tâches ménagères (plier des vêtements, faire le lit, ranger la vaisselle, etc.). Baptisé en interne Max, ce robot aurait été construit en seulement trois mois avec l’aide de l’entreprise chinoise Fourier Intelligence, qui se serait donc occupée de l’aspect matériel du processus de fabrication.
Max pèserait environ 48 kg et mesurerait environ 1,5 mètre. Il présenterait au niveau du visage un écran capable d’afficher des expressions faciales et intégrerait un haut-parleur afin de communiquer avec son propriétaire. Bien entendu, il possèderait de petites mains pour saisir des objets. Dans ses entrailles, nous retrouverions des puces Nvidia Jetson Thor qui lui permettent de fonctionner.
Meta travaillerait par ailleurs déjà sur un second prototype, baptisé logiquement Max 2. Des améliorations au niveau de son torse et de ses mains auraient été apportées, tandis qu’un projecteur et des capteurs supplémentaires auraient été ajoutés afin de faciliter la montée et la descente des escaliers. Pour l’instant, Meta ne prévoirait toutefois pas de commercialiser Max et Max 2 auprès du grand public. Les deux robots seraient plutôt destinés à des usages expérimentaux dans des domiciles privés. Quoi qu’il en soit, le secteur de l’aide à domicile grâce à la robotique devrait donc bientôt accueillir un nouvel acteur.
Un nouveau concurrent dans le secteur des robots domestiques
En septembre dernier, l’entreprise Figure a déployé ses robots Figure 03, dotés du modèle Helix 2.5, dans 30 appartements de San Francisco. Leurs objectifs ? Ranger des pièces, plier des serviettes et faire le lit. Les résultats ont été mitigés, mais ces essais ont tout de même annoncé de sérieux progrès dans ce domaine spécifique.
De son côté, Elon Musk vise fin 2027 pour déployer son robot humanoïde Optimus dans certains foyers. Le milliardaire sud-africain vise même une production en série de son robot, mais cela implique inévitablement un compromis. Le robot Max de Meta arrivera-t-il à mieux s’occuper d’une maison que Figure 03 et Optimus ? Seul l’avenir nous le dira.

articles.title: El nuevo cuello de botella de la IA no son los chips ni la energía: es el dinero barato
articles.text:
Los inversores se han vuelto mucho más exigentes a la hora de prestar dinero a la IA, según el WSJ. Las más afectadas son empresas como CoreWeave, Nebius y Nscale, que se endeudan para construir centros de datos y alquilar su potencia de cálculo.
Llevan varias semanas casi sin poder vender bonos, una de sus grandes vías para conseguir dinero.
El contraste. Dos casos enseñan lo rápido que ha cambiado todo:
- QTS. Este operador de centros de datos estudiaba hace seis meses pedir 800 millones de dólares. Ahora busca casi el mismo préstamo, pero le costará entre 4 y 6 millones más de intereses al año.
- CoreWeave. A principios de año logró vender deuda pagando un 9,75% de interés. Quien compra hoy esos bonos exige una rentabilidad superior al 15%.
Por qué es importante. No credit, no party. Que no haya party significa que los centros de datos van a tardar más en llegar. Hock Tan, el CEO de Broadcom, ya avisó en octubre de que el dinero podía convertirse en un freno mayor que la falta de chips o de electricidad. Y ya era decir.
Nscale de hecho ya lo está notando. Optó por retrasar a diciembre su salida a bolsa porque quienes podrían financiar su centro de datos para Anthropic están pidiendo condiciones más duras.
Entre líneas. Nadie puede decir que no hayamos recibido avisos desde hace un año. A finales de 2025, Deutsche Bank y Morgan Stanley ya buscaban cómo protegerse de la deuda que ellos mismos habían dado para construir centros de datos. Ahora ese recelo ha llegado a todo el mercado.
Los inversores temen, según el WSJ, que las protestas vecinales retrasen las obras y que los beneficios de la IA tarden más de lo prometido. También creen tener ya demasiado dinero metido en el sector.
- Tener un gran cliente tampoco basta. QTS ha construido un centro de datos para Microsoft, y su deuda ligada a ese proyecto se ha encarecido desde abril, mientras la de Microsoft apenas ha cambiado.
- El mercado ya distingue entre prestarle a Microsoft y prestarle a quien le alquila un edificio a Microsoft.
Sí, pero. Tampoco es que el dinero se haya terminado. Hasta septiembre, las empresas de IA habían captado 466.000 millones de dólares en deuda, más de cuatro veces lo de hace un año, según Morgan Stanley. Y los chips siguen escaseando: el CEO de Broadcom cree que el problema podría no aliviarse hasta 2028 o 2029. Otras voces apuntan a 2030.
Así que no es que falte dinero, en todo caso lo que falta es dinero barato, sobre todo para quien no gana lo suficiente como para pagarse las obras.
Y ahora qué. El presidente de EQT ha encontrado en Semafor una estupenda palabra para los anuncios gigantes que nunca se concretan: “bragawatts”. Historia.
Firmar megavatios es muy fácil, entregarlos conectados, no tanto; y pagarlos ahora, desde luego, aún menos.

articles.title: Dario Gil, director de investigación de IBM: “Ni 1.000 millones de supercomputadoras podrán igualar la capacidad de un ordenador cuántico”
articles.text:
Las supercomputadoras actuales tienen una enorme capacidad de procesamiento, pero existe una tecnología que podría dejarlas atrás: la computación cuántica. Esta nueva generación de máquinas promete resolver problemas que hoy están fuera del alcance de los equipos más potentes.
Dario Gil, director de investigación de IBM, sostiene que ni siquiera 1.000 millones de supercomputadoras actuales conectadas entre sí podrían realizar determinados cálculos que sí están al alcance de un ordenador cuántico. Su afirmación pone en perspectiva la diferencia entre la informática tradicional y una nueva generación de máquinas que promete transformar la manera en que se procesan los datos.
La computación cuántica no busca simplemente fabricar equipos más rápidos que los actuales. Su principal diferencia está en la forma en que procesa la información. Mientras los ordenadores convencionales trabajan con bits que representan valores de cero o uno, los sistemas cuánticos utilizan cúbits, capaces de aprovechar propiedades de la física cuántica para representar y procesar información de otra manera.
Por qué un ordenador cuántico puede superar a miles de millones de supercomputadoras
La principal diferencia entre ambas tecnologías se encuentra en sus principios de funcionamiento. Los superordenadores tradicionales realizan operaciones mediante procesadores que ejecutan instrucciones utilizando bits. Aunque pueden trabajar con miles de procesadores simultáneamente, siguen dependiendo de las reglas de la informática clásica.
Los ordenadores cuánticos, en cambio, utilizan fenómenos como la superposición y el entrelazamiento cuántico. La primera propiedad permite que un cúbit represente una combinación de estados, mientras que la segunda establece relaciones entre diferentes cúbits, incluso cuando se encuentran separados.
Estas características permiten abordar determinados problemas matemáticos y científicos mediante métodos que no están disponibles para las computadoras convencionales.
Esto no significa que un ordenador cuántico sea superior para cualquier actividad. Una computadora tradicional continúa siendo más adecuada para tareas cotidianas, como navegar por internet, editar documentos, reproducir videos o ejecutar programas convencionales.
La ventaja cuántica aparece cuando se enfrentan problemas específicos que requieren explorar enormes cantidades de posibilidades. Entre ellos figuran algunas simulaciones moleculares, investigaciones sobre nuevos materiales y determinados desafíos de optimización.
La carrera por desarrollar computadoras cuánticas más potentes
IBM es una de las compañías que lidera la investigación en este campo. La empresa tecnológica trabaja en el desarrollo de procesadores cuánticos y herramientas que permitan aprovechar esta capacidad para resolver problemas científicos e industriales.
El desafío no consiste únicamente en aumentar la cantidad de cúbits de un procesador. También es necesario reducir los errores que aparecen durante las operaciones, mantener la estabilidad de los sistemas y conseguir que las máquinas puedan ejecutar cálculos complejos de manera confiable.
Los cúbits son extremadamente sensibles a las condiciones del entorno. Pequeñas alteraciones pueden provocar que pierdan sus propiedades cuánticas, un fenómeno conocido como decoherencia. Por eso, construir ordenadores capaces de mantener operaciones estables durante períodos prolongados representa uno de los principales obstáculos de esta tecnología.
En paralelo, diferentes países y compañías están invirtiendo en infraestructuras para acelerar su desarrollo. China también impulsa proyectos de investigación y programas tecnológicos destinados a fortalecer sus capacidades en computación avanzada.
Qué cambiará con la llegada de la computación cuántica
Las aplicaciones potenciales de esta tecnología abarcan sectores como la medicina, la industria farmacéutica, la energía y las finanzas. Una de las posibilidades más relevantes es acelerar la simulación del comportamiento de moléculas, lo que podría facilitar la investigación de nuevos medicamentos y materiales.
También podría ayudar a resolver determinados problemas de optimización relacionados con rutas de transporte, cadenas de suministro y consumo energético.
Otro ámbito de interés es la seguridad informática. El desarrollo de computadoras cuánticas suficientemente avanzadas podría comprometer algunos sistemas de cifrado utilizados actualmente para proteger información bancaria, comunicaciones y datos personales. Por ese motivo, investigadores y empresas trabajan en métodos de criptografía poscuántica.

articles.title: Apple's stock drops as new CEO John Ternus delivers his first earnings call - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Apple’s stock drops as new CEO John Ternus delivers his first earnings call
Apple Inc. just delivered its first earnings call since new Chief Executive John Ternus took over the company from Tim Cook on Sept. 1, and the results beat expectations on the top and bottom lines. But the company missed expectations on iPhone sales and offered disappointing guidance going forward, and the stock fell in late trading.
The company reported fourth-quarter earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of $2.10 per share, comfortably ahead of Wall Street’s target of $1.99 per share. Revenue for the period rose 12%, to $114.48 billion, easing past the $113.39 billion analyst forecast. All told, its net income came to $30.71 billion at the end of the quarter, up from just $27.46 billion one year earlier.
When Ternus (pictured) stepped up to relieve Cook in the CEO’s chair a couple of months ago, he realized he was stepping into a job with sky-high expectations, following in the footsteps of two of the most successful company leaders in American history. Steve Jobs was credited with revolutionizing consumer devices, while Cook took the company to spectacular new heights thanks to his operational expertise, establishing it as one of the world’s most iconic brands.
The weight of expectations is reflected by Apple’s enormous valuation. According to Oppenheimer analyst Martin Yang, the iPhone maker is trading at about 36 times next year’s expected earnings. That represents a premium compared with the rest of the technology market, even though its earnings are only expected to grow 1% this year, slower than many of its peers.
Nonetheless, investors have piled into Apple because it’s something of an outlier in the artificial intelligence boom. While its rivals are all spending hundreds of billions of dollars on building data centers, Apple has remained extremely capital-efficient, pouring cash into share buybacks and dividends for shareholders. That has given the company a strong margin for safety, but its position could still be threatened if Ternus can’t find a way to speed up Apple’s innovation engine.
The company has already been criticized for its lackluster performance in AI. Its long-awaited Siri AI chatbot finally arrived during the past quarter, but it came across as stale the moment it arrived. By the time it had launched, it had already been surpassed by autonomous AI agents such as Dots and Muse that can perform multistep tasks on behalf of users, while Siri is still fumbling around with answering questions.
Analysts wanted to know if Apple is planning to offer more AI features through subscriptions or services, but Ternus declined to reveal what the company’s future plans are. But he insisted that Apple has “lots of opportunities” for monetization in future. “One example is the hardware side, right?” he said. “It offers a compelling reason for upgrading or switching.”
Jacob Bourne of Emarketer told SiliconANGLE that Apple’s stock premium is likely linked to the growing concerns some investors have over the enormous cost and uncertain returns of the AI boom, which is being driven by all of Apple’s big tech peers. “Its tepid approach to AI infrastructure spending has helped to preserve its cash flow, and through strategic partnerships Apple may be able to strengthen its AI capabilities without taking on the same financial risks as its peers,” Bourne said. “But Apple faces its own challenges as AI-enabled devices such as smart glasses could eventually challenge the iPhone’s central role in iOS. Apple’s long-term advantage will hinge on combining its hardware strengths with compelling AI capabilities in a way that preserves its reputation.”
In the meantime, the pressure is on for Apple to give consumers more reasons to buy its expensive devices, especially as the costs of those products have been getting higher. Today’s report was the first full quarter of higher-priced Apple products following a price hike in June that stemmed from the rising cost of memory supplies and other components.
The price of most iPhone handsets was hiked by around $100, but consumers didn’t appear to punish Apple. On the contrary, iPhone revenue was a bright spot, reaching $57.58 billion in the quarter, up 17% from a year earlier and above the $56.54 billion consensus estimate. That’s despite the quarter including only eight days of new iPhone 18 Pro sales and none of the new flagship device, the iPhone Duo.
Apple needed a good quarter from the iPhone because its main growth engine, the services business, is slowing. Revenue there came to $31.57 billion, just below the Street’s forecast of $31.58 billion, growing less than 10% during the quarter, its slowest rate of growth since September 2022. The business includes revenue from a wide range of products and services, such as iCloud storage, AppleCare warranties, App Store fees and licensing revenue from Google LLC for putting its search engine as the default option in the Safari browser.
“We saw strong performance in many service categories, with all-time records in video, cloud services, payment services and advertising, and a September quarter record in music,” Tetanus told analysts.
Apple saw a better performance in its Mac computer division, with sales of $10.79 billion comfortably topping the Street’s forecast of $9.61 billion. The unit’s revenue grew almost 24% on an annual basis, following the launch of new Mac Studio and Mac Mini laptops in August.
The iPad division was a disaster, however, as sales declined more than 10% from the previous year to $6.3 billion, trailing the Street’s forecast of $6.7 billion. Last month saw the launch of a new iPad Mini model, following the debut of the updated iPad Air back in March, but despite those releases, there has been no flagship model launching this year, and that appears to have hurt the business’ performance. When asked about the miss, Ternus blamed supply constraints and a difficult comparison with last year as the main reasons for its disappointing performance.
The disappointing performance of Apple’s services and iPad units was compounded by what was seen as weak guidance for the current quarter, which includes the peak Christmas sales period. Apple Chief Financial Officer Kevan Parekh didn’t offer concrete numbers, but said the company expects its revenue to grow by between 7% and 10% in the quarter. Wall Street analysts are looking for higher growth of 11.4%, however. Parekh also revealed that Apple is forecasting its gross margin to fall between 45% and 46%, declining from the fourth quarter.
Apple’s stock fell almost 3% on today’s report, but it’s still up more than 24% in the year to date compared with a gain of just over 10% for the broader S&P 500 index.

articles.title: Encore sur Windows 10 ? Si jamais vous changez d'avis, vous pouvez désormais passer directement à Windows 11 26H2
articles.text:
Windows 11 26H2 est désormais proposé aux PC encore équipés de Windows 10. Une possibilité réservée aux machines compatibles, qui nécessite toutefois une mise à niveau complète du système, plus longue qu'une simple mise à jour d'activation.
Déployé progressivement depuis le 29 septembre, Windows 11 26H2 était accessible depuis le 21 octobre à tous les ordinateurs exécutant Windows 11 24H2 ou 25H2. Une semaine plus tard, Microsoft a annoncé l'extension de son déploiement à l'ensemble des appareils éligibles. D'après les observations de Neowin, cette ouverture concerne également les machines encore sur Windows 10, qui peuvent passer directement à 26H2 sans installer de version intermédiaire de Windows 11.
Une migration directe, mais pas une mise à jour express
Si vous avez finalement décidé de quitter Windows 10, commencez par vérifier si votre PC peut bénéficier de cette migration. Pour cela, rendez-vous dans Paramètres > Mise à jour et sécurité > Windows Update, puis lancez une recherche de mises à jour. Si Windows 11 26H2 n'apparaît pas, vous pouvez vérifier la compatibilité de votre ordinateur à l'aide de l'application Contrôle d'intégrité du PC, puis, si votre configuration le permet, passer par l'Assistant d'installation officiel de Microsoft.
Attention toutefois, la procédure diffère de celle proposée aux PC déjà équipés de Windows 11 24H2 ou 25H2. Sur ces versions, Microsoft distribue 26H2 sous la forme d'un petit paquet d'activation, qui débloque les composants déjà présents sur le système. Depuis Windows 10, il faut en revanche télécharger et installer Windows 11 dans son intégralité. L'opération prend donc davantage de temps et nécessite plusieurs redémarrages.
On rappellera enfn que cette extension du déploiement ne change rien aux exigences matérielles de Windows 11. Les ordinateurs doivent toujours disposer d'un processeur compatible, d'une puce TPM 2.0 et satisfaire aux autres critères imposés par Microsoft. Les PC qui ne remplissent pas ces conditions restent donc officiellement exclus de la migration, à moins de recourir à des outils comme Rufus ou Ventoy, qui permettent en partie de contourner de ces restrictions.

Galaxy Buds 4 Pro recebe 36% OFF na Black November do Magalu
Galaxy Buds 4 Pro traz ANC de cinco níveis e áudio superior; fones da Samsung saem por um dos menores preços que vimos com a entrada do mês da Black Friday
O Galaxy Buds 4 está saindo por apenas R$ 1.349,10 no Pix no Magazine Luiza, um desconto de 36% obre o preço original de R$ 2.099. A oferta do início da Black November na loja é uma boa oportunidade para quem procura um fone premium da Samsung com cancelamento de ruído, graves e agudos nítidos, e integração com IA.
O Galaxy Buds 4 Pro é equipado com ANC com cinco níveis de ajuste, permitindo que você ajuste a intensidade do cancelamento de ruído à sua necessidade. Para chamadas, os seis microfones integrados com detecção de voz garantem que sua voz saia clara e sem ruídos de vento para quem está do outro lado da linha. E a conectividade Bluetooth 6.1 dos fones da Samsung garante uma conexão extremamente estável e rápida com seus aparelhos.
Sobre a bateria, a autonomia é de até 30 horas com o ANC desligado, ou 26 horas com ele ativado. Com essas características, o Galaxy Buds 4 em oferta no mês da Black Friday no Magalu é uma ótima opção de compra pelo preço de R$ 1.349,10 no Pix; aproveite antes que acabe.
Este é o nome que damos para o mês da Black Friday, que acontece na última sexta-feira do mês de novembro, e é a principal época para promoções no varejo. Como grande parte dos lojistas, incluindo a Magalu, começam a distribuir cupons e descontos bem antes da data, a Black November ganhou esse nome.
