articles.title: Refrigerator cyberattack spreads to many European countries, spoiling food worth thousands
articles.text:
What we know so far: Last month's cyberattack on French grocery store refrigerators became an expensive reminder of the risks of relying on the Internet of Things for critical infrastructure. New attacks this week show that several European countries face the same vulnerabilities, with lax security practices and obsolete systems the likely culprits.
A cyberattack on internet-connected refrigeration systems ruined food at grocery stores in at least seven European countries on Monday, with one Belgian Delhaize store estimating its losses at €100,000. The attack mirrors the one that hit French grocers in mid-October, exposing gaping security holes.
Grocery stores and chains in Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Belgium, Sweden, Finland, and Estonia reported that refrigerators had been set to defrost, in some cases raising temperatures to 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit), spoiling food and leaving many shelves empty. The French attack set cooling systems to the same temperature and caused damages estimated in the tens of millions of euros.
An ICA store manager in Stockholm told Reuters on Monday that employees didn't notice the attack, which hit at 2am local time, until hours later, by which point "everything" was destroyed. Other targeted businesses include Delhaize in Belgium and Luxembourg, Carrefour and De Laet & Van Haver in Belgium, Coop in Sweden, and more.
It remains unclear who was responsible for the attacks. No one has claimed responsibility, and at least some affected stores have security vulnerabilities so deep that practically anyone could have accessed their systems.
The refrigerators attacked in France were operated by Danfoss, and the incident came two months after security researchers at Claroty warned of multiple vulnerabilities in the company's controllers. Danfoss also supplied the affected units in at least some of Monday's attacks, though Belgian installer Sabcobel, which operates Delhaize's refrigeration, was also involved.
Security researcher Kevin Beaumont says several thousand Danfoss management systems are directly reachable from the internet with essentially nonexistent login security. In his words, the username is "admin" and the password changes daily to the current date. Claroty's research points to a hidden daily code derived from the date that bypasses the real password, a flaw Danfoss has since patched.
Furthermore, many affected systems were running outdated firmware, and some can't receive patches at all because they are end-of-life, a common risk with IoT devices. Shodan.io shows thousands of exposed Danfoss units, more than half in France, with others in South Africa and elsewhere.
Whether a sophisticated state actor or a bored individual was behind the attacks, they serve as another lesson in IoT pitfalls. Some also fear that similar incidents could form part of a broader effort to destabilize a country's infrastructure.

articles.title: Apple may try to increase revenue by doing...something with third-party AI apps | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Apple’s services business remains at record levels, but it’s facing growing pressure. The central part of that business, Apple’s App Store, has faced regulatory pressure and a slump in mobile gaming, which have hurt services growth.
However, on Monday’s earnings call, Apple signaled that it may look to boost services revenue through third-party apps. What does that mean, exactly? Unfortunately, it’s not entirely clear.
When discussing how AI could potentially “contribute to revenue growth over time,” Kevan Parekh, Apple’s chief financial officer, said: “On the product side, you know, we feel AI offers a compelling reason for customers to upgrade and switch in order to get the latest capabilities, and we also feel there’s opportunities across third-party apps and partnerships as well as first-party opportunities.”
Parekh did not elaborate on what sorts of opportunities might be available via third-party apps. However, Reuters reported Monday that investors are wondering whether Apple could profit by distributing third-party AI agents through the App Store and taking a cut of the revenue they generate.
Regulatory and legal changes have cut into App Store commission revenue in some markets, even as Apple’s services business as a whole continues to grow. Third-party estimates in August, for example, suggested the company had seen an 18% drop in U.S. commission revenue, with declines also in Brazil and Japan after those countries introduced new regulations. Apple has traditionally controlled payments within its app marketplace tightly, taking a cut of all App Store transactions. But a lawsuit by Epic Games ultimately forced the company to allow apps to redirect users to outside payment systems. Other legal challenges throughout the world have further hampered the business.
During the earnings call, Parekh referenced Apple’s App Store woes and returned to the idea that the company’s service business could expand into new territory.
“We’ve also seen some factors that impacted the performance of the App Store, and during the September quarter, the performance on the App Store was similar to the prior year, and we had a record number of paid subscriptions with double-digit growth for third-party apps on the App Store,” Parekh said. “At the same time, we did see some headwinds in mobile gaming that we’ve talked about before, and expect to see those continue into the summer quarter.”
Parekh added: “As we move ahead, we expect services growth to to be between 8 to 9% [in the December quarter]. This outlook contemplates our best estimates on sequential headwinds, primarily from third-party licensing and the additional half percentage point of foreign exchange I just mentioned.”
TechCrunch has reached out to Apple for more information and will update this story if it responds.

articles.title: Raspberry Pi 5 16 GB Hits $385 Following Latest Price Hikes
articles.text:
Monday, November 2nd 2026
Raspberry Pi 5 16 GB Hits $385 Following Latest Price Hikes
Raspberry Pi has raised prices again, and this time the 16 GB Raspberry Pi 5 takes the hit. CEO Eben Upton announced in a blog post that the 16 GB model goes up by $80 to $385, more than triple the $120 it launched at in January 2025. The 16 GB Compute Module 5 variants are also going up by $40, with updated prices listed in the product brief on the Compute Module 5 page. This follows the October 1 increase, when the 2 GB Pi 4 and Pi 5 each went up by $12.50. Compared to today's hike, that one was minor. Upton blames a lack of alternative supply for 16 GB DRAM, made worse by other ongoing component shortages. 
Upton encouraged customers to make sure they are not paying for more memory than they need. He pointed out that lower-density variants or older Raspberry Pi models could be a solution. Also, underlined developers to optimize memory use in their applications. He closes the post by saying the current memory situation is difficult but temporary. Raspberry Pi Foundation intends to roll the increases back once memory costs start to decrease.Remember, just two weeks ago, Dell's CEO said he doesn't think the memory shortage is anywhere near over, it could get worse in 2027. Since SK hynix expects that memory demand will outpace supply even in 2030, there's little chance that Raspberry Pi prices to get lowered. However, there is one bit of good news. The Raspberry Pi 500+, the 16 GB all-in-one computer built into a mechanical keyboard, stays at its current price of $410. At least for the moment.

articles.title: Gefängnis: KI soll Gewaltrisiko vorhersagen können
articles.text:
Fast wie in Minority Report: KI soll Gewaltrisiko von Häftlingen vorhersagen
In Steven Spielbergs Science-Fiction-Thriller Minority Report sehen sogenannte Precogs dank hellseherischer Fähigkeiten Morde voraus, die erst in der Zukunft stattfänden. Die Namen von Tätern und Opfern sind ebenso bekannt wie der Zeitpunkt der Gewalttaten – die potenziellen Täter werden aus dem Verkehr gezogen.
KI zur besseren Risikoeinschätzung
Letztlich stellt sich aber heraus, dass das System Fehler hat, da die Precogs auch Situationen vorhersehen, in denen ein Mord wahrscheinlich ist, aber nicht stattfindet. Ein neues KI-System, das die Justizvollzugsbehörde des US-Bundesstaates Michigan einsetzen will, erinnert im Kern an Spielbergs filmische Zukunftsvision, wenn das Ganze in der Realität auch weniger drastisch ausfallen dürfte.
Konkret geht es um eine KI-gestützte Software, die in Gefängnissen in Michigan künftig vorhersagen soll, welche Gefangene eine potenzielle Gefahr darstellen könnten. Diese Risikoeinschätzung dient dazu, die Häftlinge in eine von insgesamt fünf verschiedenen Sicherheitsstufen einzuordnen, wie Futurism berichtet.
Mehr Sicherheit für Beschäftigte und Insassen
Die Gefängnisbehörde erhofft sich dadurch eine um 30 Prozent genauere Vorhersage als mit den aktuellen Verfahren. Ein entsprechendes Pilotprojekt soll Anfang September 2026 in mehreren Männergefängnissen starten, wie die Behörde mitteilte. Ziel ist demnach, die zuletzt stark gestiegene Zahl von Angriffen auf Beschäftigte sowie Gewalt zwischen Inhaftierten zu senken.
Das Programm hat die Behörde zusammen mit der aus Google hervorgegangenen gemeinnützigen Organisation Recidiviz entwickelt. „Ich bin zuversichtlich, dass wir mit diesem Pilotprojekt und der Nutzung wissenschaftlich fundierter sowie historischer Daten ein dynamisches und objektives Instrument entwickelt haben, das die Sicherheit unserer Einrichtungen stärken wird“, erklärte die Direktorin Heidi E. Washington.
Allerdings erklärte Washington nicht, welche Daten die KI erhält. Das wiederum ist aber mitentscheidend dafür, wie korrekt das System arbeitet. Und davon hängt viel ab. Je nach Einstufung erhalten die Gefangenen während ihres Aufenthalts unterschiedliche Programme oder Ressourcen. Zudem entscheidet sich dadurch, mit wem sie untergebracht werden.
Negative Folgen durch Vorurteile möglich
Macht die KI hier Fehler, etwa durch nicht korrigierte Vorurteile, kann das zu strengeren Haftbedingungen und einer möglicherweise schlechteren Vorbereitung für die Zeit nach der Haft führen. Bei einem ähnlichen Programm zur Risikobewertung im US-Bundesstaat Louisiana sollen die zur Einstufung verwendeten Daten rassistische und sozioökonomische Biases enthalten haben, wie eine Untersuchung von Propublica zeigte. Mit negativen Folgen für das Strafvollzugssystem.

articles.title: AI model gets a 32-bit RISC-V CPU compiled directly into its weights, then runs DOOM on it — experimental AI model can run Doom and C code using its own weights as RAM
articles.text:
AI model gets a 32-bit RISC-V CPU compiled directly into its weights, then runs DOOM on it — experimental AI model can run Doom and C code using its own weights as RAM
Project takes a stock Qwen 3.5 4B and compiles a RISC-V CPU into its weights.
AI engineer Divyansh Agrawal has revealed the Qwenputer. Described in its most basic terms, Qwenputer is an experimental blend of the stock Qwen 3.5 4B AI LLM with a 32-bit RISC-V CPU compiled and inserted directly into its weights. In use, Qwenputer can run processor arithmetic operations – or even run C and MicroPython code on its built-in CPU, eschewing any external runtime or tool use. Moreover, it can run Doom, albeit very slowly. You can see the Qwenputer running Doom on its RISC-V CPU by expanding the tweet below.
The implementation of Qwenputer raises some interesting concepts and solutions. For example, the developer used Qwen’s Gated DeltaNet (GND) state as RAM, which Agrawal reckons is “a pretty neat trick.” They admit that using these ‘fast weights’ as RAM isn’t an original concept, but modifying Qwen 3.5 this way does seem to be a first.
Unlike traditional LLM creation, adding a ‘CPU’ doesn’t involve training. This RISC-V CPU implementation “is 11 transformer layers in front of Qwen's own, and none of their weights are learned: a compiler computes every one,” it is explained. Agrawal boasts that Qwenputer’s built-in CPU “passes the official riscv-tests, its programs match qemu, and it has run 18 million instructions free-running without a single error.”
The developer stresses that Qwen makes use of this ‘CPU’ to send instructions and read them back with no external tool or runtime calls. In practice, it works as intended. Use of the CPU inside Qwenputer provides exact calculations, overcoming the arithmetic weaknesses of many LLMs. Moreover, users can run code on the CPU inside the LLM, with C and MicroPython compatibility.
Not content with wedging a CPU into an LLM, Agrawal decided to also give it a filesystem. They describe this extension of the model as relatively trivial, since RAM is already in place. Indeed, the filesystem storage also uses the DeltaNet state. There are 1,024 slots holding up to 512 files. Moreover, this storage is persistent if you save the state at the end of a conversation with the LLM.
Due to its expanded resource use, Qwenputer has basically doubled the size of the underlying Qwen 3.5 4B LLM to almost 19GB. Thus, Agrawal recommends a workstation with 24GB of VRAM or more for testing Qwenputer in its current version. Efforts are being made to streamline coding in Qwenputer, as well as make it run faster.
The project is experimental. One gets the impression that Agrawal built Qwenputer primarily as an experiment to explore what is possible, rather than to solve a specific problem. Nevertheless, the creation of this custom LLM raises some interesting concepts and makes the mind wander regarding potential practical applications.

articles.title: GCHQ has apparently lost thousands of storage devices in recent years — and has no idea where any of them are
articles.text:
GCHQ has apparently lost thousands of storage devices in recent years — and has no idea where any of them are
GCHQ slated for having 'thousands' of unaccountable storage drives
- 'Thousands' of GCHQ storage devices are missing or unaccounted for
- Most are likely protected by encryption or PIN access
- Watchdog is 'concerned' and 'disappointed'
The UK's intelligence and cybersecurity agency, GCHQ, has been slammed by its very own watchdog after failing to account for thousands of missing storage devices.
The 2025 Investigatory Powers Commissioner's Office (IPCO) report ultimately concluded GCHQ has failed to establish the location or status of thousands of removable storage devices such as USB sticks, external hard drives and memory cards.
While the exact number of devices is unconfirmed, the IPCO report does confirm the estimate to be "in the thousands" – and that's a GCHQ estimate, not a third-party estimate.
GCHQ has seemingly lost thousands of USBs, external drives, memory cards
"There is a programme of further work to locate and account for as many of these devices as possible," the report adds, noting that "GCHQ will be able to report how many devices have been confirmed as lost."
Nevertheless, the IPCO expressed disappointment at how long investigations and remedial action had taken – the problems were actually first brought to the watchdog's attention years ago, so it's not a newly discovered issue. "We remain very concerned about this issue and are disappointed with the time it has taken GCHQ to investigate."
The issue was already raised in the IPCO's 2024 report, when the watchdog confirmed that it has asked GCHQ and MI5 to "review their internal allocation and audit of removable media" the year prior.
Back then, it was already acknowledged that many of the missing devices were either encrypted or required a PIN to access, however given the intense sensitivity of many of these artefacts, significant risk could still be on the cards.

articles.title: Customers withdraw $3.6B after largest theft in Binance's history
articles.text:
Customers withdraw $3.6B after largest theft in Binance's history
According to media reports, customers withdrew $3.6 billion of assets from Binance as it reopened on Sunday following the theft.
Binance witnessed a massive increase in outflows, with customers withdrawing $3.6 billion from the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange after the largest theft in its history, which has been linked to North Korea.
According to media reports, customers withdrew $3.6 billion of assets from Binance as it reopened on Sunday following the theft of $6.3 billion on Thursday.
The company had suspended all transactions following the incident.
"Binance began restoring withdrawals in phases at 06:00 UTC on November 1, 2026," the company posted on X on Sunday, three days after it froze assets in the wake of the theft.
"By 12:36 UTC, withdrawals had resumed for all 15 networks and assets in the initial phase. After an initial spike, withdrawal volumes have declined and are stabilising as expected, while deposit volumes have remained substantial," it said.
According to Binance, customers deposited $1.01 billion and withdrew about $4.649 billion in assets. Most of those transactions occurred in the first few hours after trading was restored, it added.
The outflow of $3.64 billion represents 2.1% of $171 billion in total assets under its management, the company said on Sunday.
"Our team continues testing rigorously the remaining networks and assets. We know how important safe and reliable access to your funds is and will share details of the next phase as soon as we can. Rest assured that market conditions are stable,” Binance said in a post on X.
The company said that it would cover all losses that occurred during the hack and that it had worked with other cryptocurrency firms to freeze about USD 3 billion in stolen assets, according to a The New York Times report.
The paper said that the cybersecurity analysts and the FBI have attributed the theft to North Korea, which has targeted cryptocurrency companies for years, taking advantage of vulnerabilities in their infrastructure to steal assets.
"The hackers may have used artificial intelligence technology to accelerate their attack, according to the crypto analytics firm Chainalysis, which said that the attackers processed 'thousands of transactions in a short period'," the NYT report said.
Changpeng Zhao, a co-founder of Binance, said, "Trust isn’t earned by what you say in good times. It’s earned by what you do in hard times."
According to the NYT, he also warned customers to beware of online scammers making bogus offers of compensation.""

articles.title: Ce nettoyeur de sol a un bouton pour chauffer et frotter les taches
articles.text:
Tineco S9 Artist Boost Steam : un jet de vapeur à la demande pour les taches qui s'accrochent
Vapeur de rien
Le Floor One S9 Artist Boost Steam associe aspiration, lavage et vapeur déclenchable d'une pression. Tineco y ajoute un rouleau qui inverse sa rotation pour frotter les traces récalcitrantes. Prix conseillé de cet aspirateur laveur : 699 €.
Les aspirateurs laveurs savent ramasser les miettes et récupérer une boisson renversée, mais les résidus séchés peuvent réclamer quelques allers-retours supplémentaires. Avec le Floor One S9 Artist Boost Steam, Tineco propose de déclencher ponctuellement un jet de vapeur tout en renforçant le frottement du rouleau.
Une pression active simultanément la projection de vapeur BoostSteam et le système ReverseScrub qui inverse le sens de rotation du rouleau. Le but est d'associer chaleur et action mécanique pour décoller les salissures sèches, collantes ou grasses, sans interrompre le ménage pour sortir un autre appareil.
Comptez environ 20 secondes de chauffe initiale, puis un réchauffage d'environ 5 secondes pour les projections suivantes. Attention toutefois au chiffre de 230 °C mis en avant qui correspond à la température de chauffe interne. La vapeur atteint quant à elle 99 °C en sortie..
À plat, mais toujours au travail
Le S9 Artist Boost Steam aspire et lave simultanément, avec une dépression de 25 kPa. Le capteur adapte automatiquement l'aspiration et le débit d'eau aux salissures détectées. Le rouleau est rincé en continu à l'eau propre, tandis que les résidus sont récupérés dans un réservoir distinct.
L'appareil peut aussi se coucher à 180°, avec une hauteur minimale de 13 cm, pour passer sous les meubles. Une assistance au déplacement, un éclairage LED et une tête conçue pour nettoyer près des bords sur trois côtés complètent l'équipement.
Un peigne et un racloir sont chargés de limiter l'enroulement des cheveux et des poils autour de la brosse. Après utilisation, un cycle d'autonettoyage à l'eau chauffée rince le circuit.
Le Tineco Floor One S9 Artist Boost Steam est commercialisé sur la boutique de la marque et sur Amazon au prix public conseillé de 699 €.

articles.title: Anthropic le ordenó a Claude no recrear videojuegos de otras empresas y ya hay desarrolladores bloqueados
articles.text:
Anthropic añadió a Claude Code, su asistente de programación, una instrucción que le prohíbe construir la recreación de un videojuego existente, aunque se le cambie el nombre. La empresa confirmó el cambio el 30 de octubre de 2026 y lo justificó por el uso de su IA para infringir propiedad intelectual.
La regla fue detectada por un usuario de X llamado Chasm, que dijo que se activó alrededor del 27 de octubre. Aparece bajo el nombre interno “tengu_heron_brook”. Su texto indica que Claude debe construir juegos originales, de un género o basados en diseños y materiales del propio usuario, pero no recreaciones de un juego específico.
Addy Osmani, integrante del grupo técnico de Anthropic, la explicó en X. “Agregamos dos oraciones al prompt de Claude Code en Opus 5.5 para evitar que recree el juego específico de otra persona, porque usar Claude para infringir propiedad intelectual va contra nuestra política de uso”.
Osmani agregó que los juegos originales, de género y los hechos con diseños propios “deberían seguir funcionando”. Pidió además que quien reciba una negativa sobre algo propio se lo comunique. Anthropic dijo que seguirá ajustando la medida para encontrar el equilibrio.
En qué versión de Claude está la regla de no recrear videojuegos
El sitio web XDA Developers verificó por su cuenta que la instrucción está en la versión 2.1.314 de Claude Code. También halló un mecanismo separado para aplicarla solo al modelo Opus 5.5, lo que sugiere que no se trata únicamente de una prueba limitada a un grupo de usuarios.
En sus pruebas, XDA pidió a Opus 5.5 y a su antecesor, Opus 5, recrear Pokémon Diamond. Ambos se negaron al inicio. Opus 5.5 explicó que sus instrucciones de sesión lo prohibían, con una redacción cercana a la hallada en el programa. XDA aclaró que lo que un modelo dice sobre sus propias instrucciones no siempre es fiable.
Según XDA, la regla no prohíbe de forma expresa la descompilación, es decir, convertir un juego terminado de nuevo en código, ni la recompilación estática, que lo traduce para otra plataforma. Tampoco está claro qué tipo de desarrollo considera Anthropic una recreación ni si la medida se extenderá a todos sus modelos.
Por qué las restricciones de Claude generan problemas a desarrolladores
Tom’s Hardware señaló de una serie de reclamos en el repositorio público de Claude Code en GitHub, donde usuarios dicen que el asistente se niega a hacer tareas habituales en juegos. Entre ellas, replicar una mecánica o corregir un juego de tablero. El medio admite que algunos reclamos pueden venir de usuarios con malas intenciones.
Uno de ellos es el dueño de Conflict Simulations LLC, que crea versiones digitales de juegos de guerra de mesa para clientes que poseen el juego físico. Escribió el 30 de octubre de 2026 que una regla general contra los juegos no distingue entre piratería y un trabajo profesional encargado por el dueño del juego. XDA no pudo reproducir esos rechazos.
El contexto es una oleada de clones hechos con IA. Según PC Gamer, varios estudios cancelaron pruebas públicas de sus juegos por temor a que el código de la demo se usara para copiarlos. Game Developer cita el caso de Digital Sun Games, que canceló la prueba de su próximo título, ReVamp.
Expertos advierten que la regla podría frenar solo a los copiadores menos esforzados, porque las limitaciones de seguridad de la IA se han esquivado con trucos de redacción. También señala que el programa no puede comprobar si el usuario es dueño de una idea o de unos materiales, y que quienes clonan juegos pueden recurrir a modelos de código abierto sin esas restricciones.
Valve, la empresa que opera la tienda Steam, reconoció el problema sin prohibir las herramientas de IA. Su directivo Tom Giardino dijo en un evento para desarrolladores que no quieren “ser guardianes” que digan qué herramientas usar.

articles.title: « On s’est trompés de bouton » : LFI assure avoir voté par erreur la taxe au gigaoctet
articles.text:
Ce vendredi 30 octobre, le député Laurent Lhardit a déposé l’amendement I-1358, qui propose une taxe de 0,055 euro par gigaoctet, susceptible de faire exploser le prix du streaming. Le député socialiste estime que cette taxe pourrait générer 10 milliards d’euros de recettes par an, à la charge des fournisseurs de contenus. Autant dire que cet amendement a été largement décrié, notamment par Xavier Niel, fondateur de Free, qui a qualifié les auteurs de cette taxe d’« ignares incompétents ». Pour rappel, le texte a été adopté par 11 voix contre 10. Parmi ces 11 voix favorables figuraient 5 députés PS, deux députés Les Écologistes, 2 députés du groupe de la Gauche démocrate et républicaine (GDR) et deux députés LFI. Justement, Éric Coquerel, membre de La France insoumise et ayant voté en faveur de cette taxe, a annoncé que les deux votes de son groupe étaient « une erreur » technique.
La France Insoumise s’est trompée de bouton lors des votes
Sur X, Éric Coquerel, membre de La France insoumise, a expliqué que son vote, ainsi que celui de son collègue, étaient « une erreur ». Une erreur, non pas de jugement, mais technique. Il explique : « On votait très rapidement une série d’amendements de taxation sur les Gafam et on est deux parmi les LFI à s’être trompés de bouton sur cet amendement qui fait payer les utilisateurs au lieu des plateformes ». Éric Coquerel et son partenaire se seraient donc trompés de bouton lors du vote. Ils auraient par ailleurs demandé à ce que leur vote soit corrigé, mais cela ne changera pas le résultat du scrutin, les votes étant définitivement clôturés. Il s’agit donc d’une modification purement symbolique.
 Salut @fitetok Je te réponds clairement : c’est une erreur. On votait très rapidement une série d’amendements de taxation sur les Gafam et on est deux parmi les LFI à s’être trompés de bouton sur cet amendement qui fait payer les utilisateurs au lieu des plateformes. On a…
— Eric Coquerel (@ericcoquerel) October 31, 2026
Autant dire que cette défense ne semble pas vraiment convaincre l’opinion publique. En effet, au-delà du fait de s’être prétendument trompé de bouton lors des votes, Éric Coquerel avait cosigné en 2024 une proposition de taxe des GAFAM semblable à celle d’octobre 2026, tout en étant bien plus importante.
Éric Coquerel avait voté en 2024 pour une taxation des GAFAM bien plus sévère
En octobre 2024, la députée insoumise Marianne Maximi a déposé l’amendement I-2475 au budget 2025. Ce texte, cosigné par Éric Coquerel, proposait une « contribution à l’emploi de réseaux physiques à des fins numériques » de 100 € par térabit, soit 80 centimes par gigaoctet. L’amendement actuel propose une contribution de 0,055 € par gigaoctet, soit près de 15 fois moins que celle proposée dans l’amendement d’octobre 2024. Par ailleurs, contrairement au texte de 2024, l’amendement de Laurent Lhardit prévoit un plafonnement de la taxe, fixé à 15 % du chiffre d’affaires réalisé en France par l’émetteur ou à 2 % de son chiffre d’affaires global.
Dans tous les cas, erreur ou non, les votes des deux membres de La France insoumise ont bien été enregistrés en faveur d’une taxe de 0,055 euro par gigaoctet.

articles.title: La taxe au gigaoctet a été votée à une voix près : deux députés LFI disent s'être trompés de bouton
articles.text:
Adoptée vendredi dernier à une seule voix de majorité, la taxe sur les gigaoctets téléchargés connaît un rebondissement assez improbable. Deux députés de La France insoumise auraient voté favorablement par erreur, alors que leurs voix ont précisément permis au texte de passer.
Il aura suffi de deux mauvais boutons pour faire adopter une taxe susceptible de rapporter dix milliards d’euros par an. C’est en tout cas l’explication avancée par Éric Coquerel, président de la commission des finances de l’Assemblée nationale, après le vote particulièrement serré du 30 octobre. Alors que les députés venaient d’approuver une nouvelle contribution de 5,5 centimes sur chaque gigaoctet transmis aux internautes français, l’élu insoumis assure désormais qu’il n’avait aucune intention de soutenir cette mesure. Une justification qui soulève quelques questions, d’autant qu'il avait défendu une proposition comparable par le passé.
Deux votes qui auraient dû être des abstentions
Vendredi 30 octobre, l’Assemblée nationale a adopté l’amendement du député socialiste Laurent Lhardit par 11 voix contre 10, avec 14 abstentions. Parmi les onze élus favorables figuraient deux députés de La France insoumise : Éric Coquerel et Abdelkader Lahmar, député du Rhone.
Seulement voilà, Éric Coquerel affirme désormais qu’il s’agissait d’une erreur de manipulation. Dans une réponse publiée sur X, le président de la commission des finances explique que les députés votaient dans la précipitation une série d’amendements fiscaux visant les géants du numérique. Deux membres de LFI, dont lui-même, auraient alors appuyé sur le mauvais bouton.
Le député précise avoir demandé une rectification de son vote, qu'il souhaitait transformer en abstention. Une démarche qui ne change toutefois pas le résultat officiel du scrutin : sans ces deux voix, l’amendement aurait été rejeté par 10 voix contre 9. Deux erreurs revendiquées par Éric Coquerel qui auraient donc suffi à faire basculer le vote.
Le président de la commission des finances justifie également son opposition au texte en estimant qu'il ferait payer les internautes plutôt que les grandes plateformes. Une interprétation qui mérite d’être nuancée : l'amendement adopté désigne bien les fournisseurs de contenus comme redevables de la contribution, et non directement les particuliers. Cela n’empêcherait toutefois pas Netflix, Google ou d’autres entreprises concernées de répercuter une partie de ce coût sur leurs services et leurs abonnements.
Le texte avait d'ailleurs suscité une vive réaction dans le secteur des télécoms. Xavier Niel, fondateur de Free, s'en était pris aux députés ayant adopté la mesure, les qualifiant d'« ignares incompétents ». Une sortie particulièrement mordante, alors que l'on apprend désormais que deux des onze votes favorables auraient été enregistrés par erreur.
Un revirement étonnant, alors que LFI défendait une taxe similaire en 2024
L’explication d’Éric Coquerel surprend d’autant plus qu’il avait cosigné, en octobre 2024, un amendement de la députée insoumise Marianne Maximi proposant une contribution assez comparable.
À l’époque, le groupe souhaitait instaurer une taxe de 100 euros par térabit de données transmises, soit l’équivalent de 80 centimes par gigaoctet. Un montant près de quinze fois supérieur aux 5,5 centimes adoptés vendredi dernier. Le texte avait finalement été retiré avant son examen.
Ce précédent ne démontre évidemment pas que le vote du 30 octobre était volontaire, mais il apporte un éclairage intéressant sur les positions défendues par le député ces dernières années.
Pour autant, la taxe au gigaoctet est encore loin d’entrer en vigueur. Les députés doivent se prononcer sur l’ensemble du volet recettes du budget 2027. Si celui-ci est rejeté, les amendements adoptés jusqu’ici, dont la taxe sur les données, tomberont avec lui.
Le gouvernement s’est par ailleurs opposé à cette proposition, qui devrait encore franchir plusieurs étapes parlementaires avant de pouvoir devenir une loi. Éric Coquerel anticipe lui-même un rejet du budget, ce qui rendrait finalement son erreur de vote sans conséquence sur le texte définitif.

articles.title: Spam-Anrufe erkennen und blockieren: Diese Apps und Funktionen helfen dir sofort
articles.text:
Spam-Anrufe erkennen und blockieren: Diese Apps und Funktionen helfen dir sofort
Jeden Monat werden Hunderttausende Spam-Anrufe getätigt. Das geht aus einer Untersuchung von Clever Dialer hervor. Allein im April 2026 wurden mehr als 585.000 Spam-Anrufe registriert. Im Schnitt wurden die Betroffenen dabei mehr als viermal von den betrügerischen Anrufer:innen genervt. Die häufigste Masche besteht darin, den Angerufenen einen Gewinn bei einem Gewinnspiel vorzugaukeln – und darüber sensible Daten abzufragen.
Andere Betrüger:innen setzen die Angerufenen hingegen unter Druck, dass sie noch Schulden offen hätten. Sie verlangen, dass die Rechnung schnellstmöglich beglichen wird. Wer darauf hereinfällt, bleibt meist auf den horrenden Kosten sitzen. Damit das nicht passiert, haben viele Smartphones mittlerweile integrierte Spam-Schutzmechanismen. Wie du sie aktivieren kannst, liest du in dem jeweiligen Abschnitt zu einzelnen Smartphone-Marken und Betriebssystemen.
Android: Neuer Schutz für Banken-Scam
Android bekommt in Kürze einen allgemeinen Schutz vor Spam-Anrufen, wie Endgadget berichtet. Der Nachteil dabei: Das Feature wird wohl nur bei betrügerischen Anrufer:innen greifen, die sich als Mitarbeiter:innen von Banken ausgeben wollen. Sobald Google das Feature unter Android ausrollt, soll das Betriebssystem im Hintergrund mit deiner installierten Banking-App kommunizieren, sobald ein Anruf mit der Nummer einer unterstützten Bank eintrudelt.
Die Banking-Apps können deinem Android-Smartphone dann zurückmelden, ob es sich um einen echten Anruf handelt oder aktuell gar keine Anrufe an dich geplant sind. Damit will Google gegen Spoofing vorgehen, bei dem die Betrüger:innen die Nummer der jeweiligen Institute nachahmen. In letzterem Fall legt das Android-Smartphone automatisch auf, bevor du den Anruf annehmen kannst. So soll sichergestellt werden, dass du nicht um deine Daten oder dein Geld gebracht wirst.
Ein noch größerer Nachteil ist, dass Google mit den entsprechenden Banken Partnerschaften schließen muss, damit das Feature funktioniert. Zum Launch sind das lediglich Revolut, Itaú und die Nubank. Weitere Banken sollen folgen. Glücklicherweise musst du aber nicht auf einen effektiven Spam-Anruffilter verzichten, wenn deine Bank nicht unterstützt wird. Denn andere Hersteller – und sogar Google selbst – haben schon andere Spam-Schutzmechanismen in ihren Geräten integriert.
Spam-Anrufe mit Samsung-Smartphone unterbinden
Um Spam-Anrufe zu erkennen und schnellstmöglich wieder abzuwimmeln, hat Samsung die „Smart Call“-Funktion auf seinen Smartphones integriert. Das Feature scannt jede Nummer, die anruft, und überprüft diese in einer Datenbank. Sollte die Nummer in der Vergangenheit schon aufgefallen sein oder ungewöhnliche Merkmale beinhalten, wird sie für dich gekennzeichnet: entweder als Spamverdacht oder als potenzieller Betrugsanruf.
Statt den Anruf anzunehmen oder aufzulegen, kannst du in diesem Fall einfach vom unteren Bildschirmrand nach oben wischen und dann aus zwei Optionen wählen: „Nummer blockieren“ und „Nummer melden“. Über erstere Option stellst du sicher, dass dich die Nummer nicht noch einmal anrufen kann. Über die zweite Option hilfst du Samsung dabei, besagte Nummer auch bei anderen Anrufer:innen als Spam zu markieren.
Um Smart Call zu aktivieren, öffnest du die Telefon-App auf deinem Samsung-Smartphone und tippst auf das Dreipunktemenü am rechten Bildschirmrand. Wähle anschließend „Einstellungen“ aus. Im Normalfall sollte die Option „Anrufer-ID und Spam-Schutz“ aktiviert sein. Ist das nicht der Fall, aktiviere den Schieberegler, um künftig vor Spam-Anrufen gewappnet zu sein.
Pixel-Smartphones übernehmen Spam-Anrufe
Android-Entwickler Google bietet auf seinen Pixel-Smartphones auch einen allgemeinen Schutz vor Spam-Anrufen. Dabei handelt es sich um die Funktion „Anruf-Filter“. In den USA können Pixel-Smartphones automatisch verdächtige Anrufe annehmen und für dich beantworten. In Deutschland ist die Funktion immerhin händisch aktivierbar.
Bekommst du auf deinem Pixel-Smartphone einen Anruf, dessen Nummer dir verdächtig vorkommt, wähle „Anruf prüfen“ als Option aus. Im Hintergrund nimmt ein Anrufassistent für dich ab und fragt Anrufer:innen, was sie von dir möchten. Erhält der Assistent eine Antwort, wird sie als Transkript an dich weitergeleitet. Sollte es sich um Spam handeln, kannst du direkt „Als Spam melden“ auswählen. Der Assistent wimmelt die Anrufer:innen dann ab und sagt ihnen, dass sie dich nicht mehr kontaktieren sollen.
Um die Option zu aktivieren, musst du in die Telefon-App wechseln und dort das Dreipunktemenü aufrufen. Unter „Einstellungen“ findest du den Menüpunkt „Spam und Anruf-Filter“. Sobald das Feature aktiviert ist, musst du einer kurzen Anleitung folgen, um die Einrichtung abzuschließen. Sollte der Anruf-Filter nicht als Option in den Einstellungen auftauchen, ist er laut Googles Support-Dokument nicht für dein Gerät verfügbar.
iPhones gegen Spam-Anrufe wappnen
Apple bietet auf seinen iPhones eine Reihe von Anti-Spam-Maßnahmen. Zunächst kannst du die Anrufidentifizierung aktivieren. Dadurch wird jede anrufende Nummer gescannt – entweder über eine Dritt-App, deinen Mobilfunkanbieter oder Apple Business Connect. Ist die Nummer verdächtig, wird dir das entsprechend angezeigt. Die Option findest du in den „Einstellungen“ unter „Apps“ und schließlich „Telefon“. Tippe dort auf „Anrufe blockieren u. identifizieren“. Dort kannst du dann wählen, wer Anrufe scannen soll.
Noch komfortabler wird es mit dem „Anruffilter“. Über dieses Feature nimmt Sir Anrufe entgegen, ohne dass du davon gestört wirst. Der Sprachassistent fragt den Grund des Anrufs und den Namen der Anrufer:innen ab, bevor diese Informationen an dich weitergeleitet werden. Im Anschluss kannst du entscheiden, wie du mit dem Anruf verfahren möchtest. Die Option findest du ebenfalls in den Einstellungen der Telefon-App. Wähle dort „Nach Grund des Anrufs fragen“ bei „Anruffilter“ aus.
Zu guter Letzt kannst du Spam-Anrufe und unbekannte Nummern automatisch stummschalten und in gesonderte Anruflisten umleiten lassen. Das geht in der Telefon-App mit der Einstellung „Unbekannte Nummern“ und „Spam“. Sobald ein Anruf die Kritierien erfüllt, wird er dir nicht weitergeleitet, sondern läuft stumm im Hintergrund ab. Als Spam eingestufte Anrufe werden zuvor noch an deine Voicemail weitergeleitet.
Alternative: Apps gegen Spam-Anrufe
Neben den Lösungen der einzelnen Hersteller gibt es auch mehrere Apps, die Anrufer:innen für dich identifizieren und dir so Spam-Probleme frühzeitig ersparen. Die bekanntesten sind dabei das schon erwähnte Clever Dialer (für Android und iOS) oder Tellows (für Android und iOS). Beide Apps setzen auf Meldungen der Community. Wird eine Nummer von anderen User:innen als unseriös eingestuft, wird sie für dich bei einem Anruf als Spam markiert. In den Apps kannst du dann noch nachvollziehen, ob es sich etwa um Werbeanrufe oder betrügerischen Spam gehandelt haben könnte. Über beide Apps kannst du die Nummer auch auf deinem Smartphone blockieren.
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 13.05.2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.

articles.title: Most users can now upgrade to Windows 11 26H2, even from Windows 10
articles.text:
TL;DR: A few weeks into the rollout, Microsoft has confirmed that all eligible Windows users can now get the latest OS build on their compatible systems. There are no earth-shattering changes this time, but the extra security bonus should be enticing enough for most people.
Microsoft recently updated its official guidance on installing the latest version of Windows 11. Windows 11, version 26H2 is now available to all eligible devices, including those running the 25H2 and 24H2 releases and, well, most everything else a reasonably modern PC can run. The upgrade process also supports the latest Windows 10 version enrolled in the extended support program.
Windows 10 reached its scheduled end of life in 2025, but Microsoft has repeatedly extended the window for customers who want to hang on a bit longer. The highlander of operating systems can now receive free, officially sanctioned security updates for home users until October 2027. After that, 0patch micropatching solution should keep the system safe for many years to come.
Either way, Microsoft has now confirmed that up-to-date Windows 10 builds can still get the latest Windows edition for free. The company initially extended the offer to earlier Windows 10 versions as well, but that option is long gone. Windows 11 and 10 share a common licensing structure, which should help with installing the latest OS build in a variety of usage scenarios.
Windows 10 remains a massively popular OS, and many people are likely clinging to the tried-and-tested platform to avoid whatever Microsoft is up to with Windows 11. Enterprise organizations, however, might find the free upgrade option enticing enough to finally pull the plug on the platform that let every PC user forget about the Windows 8.x fiasco.
Officially known as the Windows 11 2026 Update, Windows 11 26H2 was released on September 29, 2026, for both x86-64 and Arm CPU architectures. Microsoft described the new build as a predictable, low-disruption update, with greater stability and compatibility than previous releases. In fact, 26H2 simply enables and switches on dormant features that were already present in earlier versions.
Microsoft has been working hard to improve performance and reliability in Windows 11, but AI-assisted vulnerability discovery has turned software security upside down. The company is now being forced to ship massive bug-fix packages covering thousands of security flaws found by both Microsoft's own AI and third parties.

articles.title: Rack-scale AI: How Dell and AMD are building platforms - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Rack-scale AI: How Dell and AMD are building infrastructure
Dell Technologies Inc. and its partner Advanced Micro Devices Inc. face similar competitive pressures. Both tech powerhouses operate in a business climate where success is now measured across central processing units, graphics processing units, rack-scale systems, memory capacity, network bandwidth and tokens per dollar.
The pressure to compete across those measures underscores what theCUBE Research has termed “Engineering Velocity.” Since the Dell Technologies World event in May, AMD and Dell have not slowed their pace of collaborations and announcements.
AMD and Dell are working to build enterprise AI infrastructure that can keep pace with changing workloads and customer requirements.
“In AI infrastructure, the winner may not be the company with the best benchmark on keynote day,” said theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante. “It will more likely be the company whose engineering system learns, validates and improves the entire platform faster than anyone else.”
This feature is part of SiliconANGLE Media’s exploration of the architectural shifts powering continuous, production-grade AI. Be sure to check out theCUBE’s “Dell AI Data Platform Event: From Ambition to AI at Scale” and its past coverage of this year’s Dell Technologies World. (* Disclosure below.)
Rack-scale consolidation
A cornerstone of the Dell and AMD relationship is the server giant’s PowerEdge portfolio. Dell expanded its PowerEdge server line in May and has followed that up with additional details surrounding the integration of AMD processors.
The two companies have pursued a strategy designed to facilitate server consolidation as agentic AI drives a surge in demand for general-purpose compute. Agents rely heavily on CPUs, yet data centers don’t have a lot of extra room to add servers in rooms already stacked with GPUs.
Systems powered by AMD processors will deliver 70% gen-over-gen performance gains and can fold 13 servers from Dell’s 14th PowerEdge generation into one, according to Pradyumna Narendra, product planner and senior consultant at Dell.
“For every 10 to 13 servers you replace, you get so much of that productivity gain back because now you can do that with one server,” he told theCUBE. “When you expand that across data centers, that’s like an accelerating effect that you get to capitalize from.”
Dell and AMD must also accommodate a wealth of AI use cases and the accompanying demand for compute. Dell’s three-rack-unit server requires less power for cooling than a two-unit equivalent, allowing customers to pack more computing power into each rack, according to Narendra.
“By deploying servers that are slightly larger in package, you deliver more density at a rack level, which seems sometimes counterintuitive,” he explained. “As AI accelerates, inferencing and agentic AI around it will accelerate and grow faster. As these use cases scale out, you get exponential growth in the need for compute.”
Modular deployment and validation
Beyond server consolidation, Dell and AMD have been steadily enhancing a modular solution to simplify AI deployment and scaling: the Dell AI Platform with AMD.
The on-premises enterprise AI solution integrates AMD Instinct accelerators and EPYC processors with Dell PowerEdge servers, PowerSwitch networking and PowerScale storage for model training, fine-tuning and high-throughput inference. The platform is designed to let customers begin with configurations that meet current workloads and expand compute and GPU density over time, without rearchitecting.
“What we’re finding is customers want modular solutions. They want to think about [solutions] across the whole platform,” said Varun Chhabra, senior vice president of product marketing and infrastructure solutions group at Dell, in a discussion with theCUBE. “Compute, storage, networking [and] GPU. The software framework on top of it, the models: Have they all been tested? Have they all been validated?”
Dell has integrated the AMD ROCm software stack into the platform to support training, fine-tuning and serving large language models on-premises. The modular platform lets customers begin with smaller deployments and expand on the same infrastructure, according to Chhabra.
“You can start small with these composable units of storage, compute, networking, pre-integrated with AMD Instinct and EPYC CPUs with the ROCm software as well as the open ecosystem that sits on top of it,” he said. “We test it, we validate it, and the customers can use it and once they start seeing value in it, they know they can scale in a modular way with the same frameworks.”
Leveraging benefits of PCIe
Dell announced support for AMD Instinct MI350P PCI Express GPUs in its PowerEdge XE7745 and R7725 servers beginning in July, giving enterprises another option for scaling agentic and generative AI deployments. It also represents an important boost in memory bandwidth which matters in time-to-first-token latency.
The MI350P offers 144 gigabytes of HBM3E memory, which can be a key differentiator for inference performance, according to Mike Darby, senior manager of business development, Instinct Data Center GPUs, at AMD, during an appearance on theCUBE.
“It’s a lot of memory, but it’s also HBM3E, so [it has] an amazing amount of bandwidth,” he said. “The main use case being inference: It’s all about that latency, time to first token [and] the user experience, so that your attention span doesn’t move somewhere else while you’re waiting for your response.”
AMD and Dell’s collaboration on PCIe integration has another angle worth watching. AMD’s PCIe-based GPU supports air-cooled deployments, providing users with a path to deploy AI within existing data center infrastructure.
As the tech industry has encountered resistance in recent months to the buildout of large data centers across the U.S., concerns have centered on the environmental impact and use of water-based cooling systems. Separately, Dell found that, as it deployed its next-generation PowerEdge servers, some enterprise customers were still not prepared to adopt liquid cooling within data centers.
“Working with Dell, we added a PCI card to our air-coolable roadmap for GPU Instinct so that it fit in more Dell PowerEdge servers that go to the broader enterprise,” said Robert Hormuth, corporate vice president of architecture and strategy for the Data Center Solutions Group at AMD, during a conversation with theCUBE. “Not everybody is adopting direct liquid cooling.”
Collaboration in an open market
Dell’s work with AMD this year has extended beyond joint product announcements. In June, the two companies announced a partnership with the University of Cambridge to establish a Sovereign AI Innovation Lab (SAIL) in the United Kingdom.
The collaboration is designed to help advance the next generation of AI infrastructure and AI-powered scientific breakthroughs. It builds on Cambridge’s expanded AI research infrastructure, including the Zenith AI supercomputer, powered by fifth-generation AMD EPYC processors and AMD Instinct MI355X GPU accelerators integrated into Dell infrastructure.
Dell and AMD have also collaborated in recent months on a telecom initiative with AT&T Inc. Telecom data is a heavy lift when it comes to AI, with AT&T having processed over one trillion tokens to train models. AMD has provided the high-performance hardware foundation for both training and inference workloads involving the OTel 2.0 models developed through the Open Telco AI initiative.
Dell integrated this technology with AI-optimized servers for telecom environments to create a production-grade foundation for operators across data-intensive, real-world network environments. OTel 2.0’s training infrastructure uses Dell’s PowerEdge XE9785 server configured with eight MI355X GPUs.
The alliance between Dell and AMD highlights a key development in the growing AI infrastructure market: There are plenty of opportunities for competition. Both Dell and AMD appear committed to building portfolios that offer enterprise choices in AI processing solutions.
“AMD didn’t present its new products … as ‘respectable alternatives,’” Vellante said. “It claimed outright leadership across CPUs, GPUs, rack-scale performance, memory capacity, network bandwidth and tokens per dollar. It extended the argument across enterprise AI, robotics, ultra-low-latency inference and a rapidly expanding partner ecosystem.”
(* Disclosure: TheCUBE is a paid media partner for the Dell AI Data Platform Event. Neither Dell, the sponsor of theCUBE’s event coverage, nor other sponsors have editorial control over content on theCUBE or SiliconANGLE.)

articles.title: Microsoft explica por que o Windows 11 não deixa arrastar a Barra de Tarefas • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Microsoft explica por que o Windows 11 não deixa arrastar a Barra de Tarefas
A Barra de Tarefas do Windows 11 voltou a ser móvel, mas não via mouse, como no Windows 10. A Microsoft finalmente contou o porquê.
Neste ano, a Barra de Tarefas do Windows 11 voltou a ser móvel, ou seja, você pode posicioná-la nas laterais ou na parte superior da tela. Mas, para isso, é preciso fazer um ajuste na área de configurações do sistema. Não é possível mover a Barra de Tarefas com um simples arrastar do mouse. A Microsoft finalmente explicou o porquê.
Se você ainda usa o Windows 10, faça o teste: clique com o botão esquerdo do mouse em uma área livre da Barra de Tarefas e a arraste para os lados ou para cima. O componente será reposicionado de acordo com esse movimento, muito facilmente. O Windows 11, por outro lado, impede a movimentação da barra com o mouse.
Falha de projeto? Preguiça? Dificuldade técnica? Não. De acordo com Diego Baca, vice-presidente de design do Windows, essa limitação existe para evitar que a Barra de Tarefas seja reposicionada acidentalmente no Windows 11.
Curiosamente, a explicação, que é reproduzida integralmente abaixo, foi dada via X quando Baca respondeu a uma chamada do Windows Central que comenta sobre o retorno da Barra de Tarefas móvel ao Windows 11, mas com um apontamento que diz “você ainda precisa de um aplicativo de terceiros para arrastar a barra de tarefas”:
Eu acho que manchetes como essa são desnecessariamente negativas. Em vez de dizer “você ainda precisa” de um aplicativo de terceiros, por que não dizer “você também pode usar” um? Isso transmite a mesma informação sem enquadrar tudo como uma falha.
Em nossa pesquisa, arrastar a Barra de Tarefas para reposicioná-la pode levar a movimentos acidentais, o que é um dos motivos pelos quais a opção “Bloquear a barra de tarefas” existe em versões anteriores do Windows. Também descobrimos que alterar a posição da Barra de Tarefas não é algo que as pessoas façam com frequência.
Acreditamos que fornecer uma configuração facilmente acessível, a apenas um clique com o botão direito de distância, é uma experiência mais intencional e previsível. É uma decisão de design deliberada, não uma capacidade ausente.
Diego Baca, vice-presidente de design do Windows
Isso significa que, provavelmente, versões futuras do Windows 11 não permitirão que a Barra de Tarefas seja movida com o mouse. Para reposicioná-la, continuará sendo necessário acessar a área de configurações.
O caminho é este: Configurações / Personalização / Barra de Tarefas / Comportamento da Barra de Tarefas / Posição da Barra de Tarefas. Por fim, escolha o local onde a barra deve ficar.

articles.title: Qualcomm Validates HBC Silicon, Samples Appear in First Half of 2027
articles.text:
Monday, November 2nd 2026
Qualcomm Validates HBC Silicon, Samples Appear in First Half of 2027
Qualcomm has officially validated its High Bandwidth Compute (HBC) concept, which the company showcased this summer. Instead of using traditional HBM and compute dies, Qualcomm has developed a technology that stacks multiple LPDDR layers and embeds a base die that serves as a compute engine for AI inference. In Qualcomm's San Diego lab, the first-generation HBC has achieved silicon validation with full read-write and near-memory computation capabilities. HBC utilizes LPDDR memory, stacking it across multiple layers in a 3D vertical space and interconnecting them with through-silicon vias (TSVs). This approach provides better energy efficiency than traditional HBM, which stacks regular DDR in vertical layers, as the low-power DDR (LPDDR) chips consume less power while delivering similar bandwidth and capacity.
Qualcomm has successfully stacked multiple LPDDR layers on top of each other, with the base of the HBC being a compute die that performs near-memory computation and offloads processing to near-memory dies. This technique is similar to what HBM4 memory currently does, with the base die being a logic die to better integrate compute solutions for packet tracing and data preparation for entering and exiting HBM. However, Qualcomm aims to achieve higher efficiency and more optimized data movement, with a 6x increase in bandwidth per watt compared to the current HBM specification. The goal is to have compute directly under these memory stacks so that data travels only a few microns instead of a few centimeters.HBC Gen 1 achieved 133 TB/s of total memory bandwidth on the AI250 accelerator card, an 18x increase over the LPDDR5X currently used in the AI200 card from Qualcomm. This is a total accelerator memory bandwidth number, not a per-HBC module bandwidth. The company also claims there is a viable roadmap for using HBC across many Qualcomm AI accelerators, with HBC Gen 1 set to ship with the AI250 AI accelerator in the first half of 2027.

articles.title: Ukraine’s new pocket-sized gadget turns Russian drones’ cameras against them | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Ukrainian drone teams have a new way to spy on the drones that spy on them. A Kyiv equipment startup called CODE380 has been gaining attention for a pocket-sized receiver, the D·Vision SDR, that picks up live camera video from many Russian drones and shows it on a screen.
Those drones send their video over the air without any scrambling, so anyone with the right receiver can watch along. A Ukrainian unit can see where a drone is heading and what its pilot is aiming at before it hits.
According to Defense News, the device is light, at about 10 ounces, which is less than half the weight of competing Ukrainian models, one of which weighs a couple of pounds.
It also listens on the radio channels Russia’s newer Molniya drones started using for video in June. Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov, a radio specialist who advises Ukraine’s president, said in a June Facebook post cited by Defense News that “most detectors don’t see these frequencies, or see them poorly.” He warned that putting too much trust in a detector could prove fatal.
Beskrestnov has also warned that digital video could one day replace analog, which would blind receivers like this one. The New York Times reported in August that some Molniyas are AI-guided, using Nvidia chips and emitting no signals.

articles.title: Siri AI, « une IA que personne ne remarque » : le nouveau patron d'Apple reste serein malgré les retards
articles.text:
Dans un entretien publié ce week-end, John Ternus a résumé sa doctrine d’une formule : Apple ne veut pas « livrer de l’IA pour l’IA ». Le successeur de Tim Cook, aux commandes depuis le 1er septembre, assure « vraiment aimer » la position actuelle de l’entreprise, longtemps critiquée pour ses retards sur l’intelligence artificielle. Cette ligne, il la tenait déjà en avril, bien avant sa prise de fonction.
La même partition depuis avril
Mi-avril, celui qui dirigeait encore l’ingénierie matérielle décrivait la course à l’IA comme « un marathon, pas un sprint » ; le 21, lors d’une réunion interne, il expliquait qu’Apple ne livre pas « de la technologie pour la technologie ». Tim Cook, lui, promettait le 1er août 2025 un engagement total : « Apple doit le faire. Apple le fera. » Le premier mémo du nouveau directeur général aux équipes annonçait, lui, un lancement d’ampleur, sans plus de précision.
Interrogé sur les agents conversationnels qui pourraient un jour remplacer les applications, l’intéressé a défendu le modèle maison : « la création de produits est une chose profondément humaine et personnelle ». Apple compte « absolument tirer parti de l’IA », au point que « les gens n’auront pas à se demander si c’est l’IA qui a permis cela ou un logiciel plus traditionnel ». Dans cette vision, l’IA réussie ressemble à la correction automatique du clavier : invisible tant qu’elle fonctionne, remarquée seulement quand elle se trompe.
Un calme que la France observe de loin
Présenté à la WWDC le 9 juin, le nouveau Siri dopé à l’IA est déployé depuis le 14 septembre avec iOS 27, en version bêta et en anglais uniquement. Promise dès 2024 puis repoussée officiellement au printemps 2025, la refonte doit permettre à l’assistant de comprendre le contexte personnel de l’utilisateur, d’agir dans les applications et de tenir compte de ce qui s’affiche à l’écran. Les iPhone et iPad de l’Union européenne en sont privés depuis le premier jour, au nom d’une lecture du règlement sur les marchés numériques, le DMA, que la firme juge « extrême ». Ouvrir ces capacités aux assistants concurrents reviendrait, à l’en croire, à exposer les données des utilisateurs sans garde-fous suffisants.
L’entreprise affirme avoir proposé à la Commission européenne un dispositif de contrôle baptisé « Trusted System Agent », assorti d’un déploiement étalé sur 18 mois, sans la convaincre. Le Mac et le Vision Pro, eux, y ont droit dans l’UE, signe que le blocage tient au statut d’iOS dans le règlement européen davantage qu’à la technique.
La mise à jour iOS 27.2, diffusée le 26 octobre, a ajouté le français à l’assistant tout en laissant le verrou en place pour l’Hexagone sur iPhone. Aucun calendrier n’existe officiellement pour iOS et iPadOS dans l’UE, l’entreprise disant seulement « espérer » y amener un jour Siri AI. Une échéance circule, mars 2027 au plus tôt, qu’aucune annonce officielle n’étaye pour l’instant.

articles.title: Quick Share peut simplifier le transfert des photos vers un PC sur Android
articles.text:
Les capacités de stockage de nos smartphones incitent les utilisateurs à prendre des photos et des vidéos, sans se soucier de l’espace disponible. Mais lorsque la mémoire vient à manquer, plusieurs solutions s’offrent à eux : transférer leurs fichiers vers un service cloud ou les déplacer directement vers un PC pour libérer de l’espace.
Une manipulation qui peut rapidement être ralentie par le fait de devoir brancher un câble USB ou avoir recours à un cloud pour seulement effectuer le transfert.
Une situation que Google pourrait bientôt chercher à simplifier. La dernière version des services Google Play (v26.43) évoque l’arrivée d’une fonctionnalité de sauvegarde automatique des photos et vidéos d’Android vers Windows, qui s’appuierait sur Quick Share.
Un transfert simplifié
Les équipes d’Android Authority ont repéré une nouvelle fonctionnalité dans la section « Connectivité des appareils » : la « sauvegarde automatique ». Une fois activée sur le smartphone, il faudra également lancer Quick Share sur le PC et garder les deux appareils à proximité. Lorsque la connexion sera établie, Quick Share pourra transférer automatiquement les photos et vidéos du smartphone vers le PC, sans câble ni cloud.
Dans ses premières analyses, Android Authority évoquait une possible exclusion des smartphones et PC Samsung de cette fonctionnalité. Toutefois, les notes de mise à jour des services Google Play ne font aucune mention d’une telle restriction. Il faudra donc attendre d’en savoir davantage pour confirmer si les appareils du constructeur coréen seront concernés.
Cette nouveauté commence à être déployée progressivement auprès des utilisateurs Android.

articles.title: Google data center wins approval in Minnesota after protests delay council vote twice — 200-acre project moves forward despite opposition from local residents, tech giant scales down project and drops $80 million tax break request
articles.text:
Google data center wins approval in Minnesota after protests delay council vote twice — 200-acre project moves forward despite opposition from local residents, tech giant scales down project and drops $80 million tax break request
Google secures approval for its Minnesota data center despite local protests, lawsuits, and power supply concerns
Google has secured approval for a proposed data center in Hermantown, Minnesota, following a unanimous vote by the city council, MPR News reports. The decision, reached on Friday, October 30, clears a major hurdle for the company following at least two postponed meetings and hours of public opposition, though the project still faces lawsuits and a separate inquiry into its electricity supply. The proposed development could cover just over 200 acres in a rural residential area outside Duluth with three data center buildings spanning approximately 1.66 million square feet.
The council approved a development agreement, a special use permit, and provisions for decommissioning the site if construction is abandoned or the facility eventually closes. The meeting, which was capped at 85 people and offered a livestream, ended shortly before midnight, with some criticizing the attendance restriction. Council member John Geisler, however, clarified the move, noting that the decision concerned local land use application rather than the wide debate over artificial intelligence or big technology companies.
“What we've done tonight is not about AI. It's not about big tech. It's not about software. It's about a project here in Hermantown, a land use application, and agreements that are associated with that,” Geissler said.
The approval comes at a hefty price for Google, with the company being forced to make several changes during the approval process. The company changed its initial plan of putting up four buildings to three, capped their height at 33 feet, and agreed to monitor nearby private wells —but each building would still be larger than six football fields. Google also agreed to withdraw an earlier request for up to $80 million in property tax breaks. The revised arrangement is now expected to generate about $3 million in annual property tax for the city, with a separate decommissioning agreement valued at $210 million in place.
Supporters point to those provisions as evidence that Google had responded to local concerns. Opponents, however, argue that the changes did not address the important questions of whether such a colossal development belongs in the area. The dispute echoes other data center battles within local communities, with Alabama residents being unable to halt a 50MW Bitcoin mining facility in August, despite local moratoriums, exposing gaps in the state's zoning rules. In September, a proposal for a 1,300-acre data center in Pennsylvania by NorthPoint Development also faced resistance despite its developer offering $10,000 to thousands of nearby households. Key issues raised mostly by residents in both cases have been about noise and water consumption by such facilities and property values.
It’s important to note, however, that Hermantown’s vote does not mean Google can immediately begin construction. Three lawsuits filed by The Minnesota Center for Environmental Advocacy and Stop the Hermantown Data Center challenge the city’s zoning process and ownership of the land, and are also demanding the project’s environmental review. The project’s environmental needs are also another pain point, given it requires about 500 megawatts, comparable to the combined demands of homes in Minneapolis, St. Paul, Duluth, and Rochester, as per the Citizens Utility Board of Minnesota. Google still needs approval from the Minnesota Public Utilities Commission on power consumption, despite its agreement with Minnesota Power.
The scale of demand is a recurring point of friction in data center proposals. Last year, the OpenAI Stargate facility in Michigan received approval for a 1.4-gigawatt power supply — construction, however, started in June 2026 despite objections from local residents. Google is also pursuing a separate data center project near Pine Island, close to Rochester. That proposal is now subject to a more extensive environmental review following a legal settlement.

No, because the distinction matters. One makes for good ragebait. The other tends to be ignored, because peeps generally have an aversion to math.
Arguments favor emotions over logic, because people are emotional creatures. You bring up numbers, and peoples' eyes glaze over. Saying "we are paying Google $80M" or "data centers are taking our water and raising our utility bills" gets their proper attention.
BTW, the tax breaks aren't $80M. That's just for the city rebate on property tax, spread over 28 years. The larger tax break is the state sales & use tax, which can amount to $20M/yr, is still in play, and presumably already granted given the go-ahead.
If anyone wants the particular on Google's tax burden for this particular example in Hermantown, Minnesota, I invite you to query your online chatbot. Edit: Per Meta's Muse Spark,
Total tax break requested:
. City property tax: $80M nominal / $33.5M present value
. State sales/use on IT: ~$400-700M over 20-35 years on our $2B build assumptions
. State sales/use on electricity: ~$50M over 20 years if it had stayed exempt
= ~$530M to $830M lifetime nominal — but only the $80M was ever in a city document.
Total actually granted going forward after the withdrawal and the new state laws:
. City property tax abatement: $0
. State sales/use on IT equipment: partial — likely the first tranche pre-July 2026 still exempt, all future refresh fully taxable
. State sales/use on electricity: $0
. State annual fee owed by Google: ~$5M/year
That's why the city could announce "Google will pay full taxes" and be technically true for property tax, while the much larger state exemption that dwarfs the $80M was quietly grandfathered and then repealed for everyone else next year. Reply

The numbers may not be correct, but they should be in the ballpark. It's a fair chunk of change per year, in the tens of millions. If assuming a 20-year life span, then hundreds of millions. It's not (just) about jobs.
Edit: Per Meta's Muse Spark,
Total tax break requested:
. City property tax: $80M nominal / $33.5M present value
. State sales/use on IT: ~$400-700M over 20-35 years on our $2B build assumptions
. State sales/use on electricity: ~$50M over 20 years if it had stayed exempt
= ~$530M to $830M lifetime nominal — but only the $80M was ever in a city document.
Total actually granted going forward after the withdrawal and the new state laws:
. City property tax abatement: $0
. State sales/use on IT equipment: partial — likely the first tranche pre-July 2026 still exempt, all future refresh fully taxable
. State sales/use on electricity: $0
. State annual fee owed by Google: ~$5M/year
That's why the city could announce "Google will pay full taxes" and be technically true for property tax, while the much larger state exemption that dwarfs the $80M was quietly grandfathered and then repealed for everyone else next year.That's a whole lot of words just to defend systematic corruption and piecemeal, selectively chosen deals that benefits massive shareholder corporations. At the expense of local competition who never win these deals. Along with higher local utility rates, among other barmohls cost disease, cost inflation, issues as well.
Unless the tax break comes with a proportional, direct equity ownership of the property in question by the municipality or state, it should never be granted. This guarantees that regardless of the economic situation of the property, such as running lean on zero local jobs (and thus zero tax burden), it still has value to the community in the equity of the property. If the property is still making money without producing any taxable jobs, or enough of them, the community still stands to benefit from its equity ownership.
Anything else is just selective corruption for these massive corporations. Did we not learn this exact lesson from the massive mall subsidies people gave out 40 years ago? That lead to completely worthless buildings that are actively being demolished? Oh sure, 10-20% grew into their areas, but was it worth the other 80% wastes of space? While those construction companies that built them ran home with the hundreds of millions in tax breaks for the worthless property? Cool investment. Not.
This is all just a grift and it doesn't matter that's it's not money being directly given to these companies, because in a roundabout way it is. They are using more out of local services than any of their tax burden pays for. They are placed favorably against local businesses and residents and keeps those residents uncompetitive against these companies that can get massive property tax breaks, while no other local residents can. Reply
- bill001g This is fairly standard corruption you see. Many times they state stuff like x years of tax abatements and rebate of other taxes like sales taxes. They try to say it will cause great economic growth to other business that will make up for it. Nobody bothers to check years down the road if it turned out to not be true....and what can you possibly do if you prove they knowing lied. Because of the cost to run and get elected for city console or mayor only the guys who own very large business in the city tend to run. You seldom see them run on platforms of controlling city spending, all talk about economic growth.Reply
