articles.title: 200 Gigabyte und mehr: Mit diesen externen Speicherlösungen rüstest du deine Konsole für den Download von GTA 6 auf
articles.text:
200 Gigabyte und mehr? So rüstest du deine Konsole für den Download von GTA 6 auf
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Am 19. November 2026 erscheint GTA 6. Fans der Reihe mussten sich lange gedulden, denn die Veröffentlichung des Vorgängers liegt mehr als 13 Jahre zurück. Während die Vorfreude steigt, machen neue Details allerdings klar, dass das Spiel die bisherige Hardware an ihre Grenzen bringen könnte – auch beim Speicherplatz. Wir erklären dir, wie groß der Download des langersehnten Spiels ausfallen könnte und mit welchen externen Festplatten du deine Konsole aufrüstest.
Externer Konsolenspeicher: Das musst du beachten
Mehrere Medien, darunter Yahoo Tech, berichten, dass der Download von GTA 6 über 200 Gigabyte groß sein soll. Grund dafür könnten das aufwendige Design und das immersive Spielerlebnis sein. Rockstar Games hat den Umfang bisher zwar nicht offiziell bestätigt, aber auch frühere Titel brauchten viel Platz. So kam beispielsweise Red Dead Redemption 2 auf rund 125 Gigabyte. Der interne Speicher von Playstation- und Xbox-Konsolen ist allerdings begrenzt. Oft startet er bei einem Terabyte, die kompaktere Xbox Series S gibt es sogar mit nur 512 Gigabyte. Der tatsächlich freie Speicher fällt noch geringer aus, weil die Konsole einen Teil für das Betriebssystem und weitere Systemfunktionen reserviert. Wenn du ein Spiel wie GTA 6 installieren willst, wird es also schnell eng.
Unter den Pioneers Picks stellen wir dir regelmäßig weitere praktische Tools und Gadgets vor.
Die gute Nachricht ist, dass du deine Konsole um eine externe Festplatte oder SSD erweitern kannst. Dabei gibt es aber einiges zu beachten. Anders als bei älteren Konsolen kannst du Spiele für die Playstation 5 nämlich nicht direkt auf einem externen USB-Speicher zocken. Der Grund: Diese bieten nicht die nötige Geschwindigkeit. Zum Spielen müssen die Games also zuerst auf den internen Speicher der Konsole kopiert werden. Eine externe Festplatte oder SSD dient bei der Playstation 5 daher eher als Archiv für Spiele, die du länger nicht gezockt hast, und schafft Platz auf der internen Festplatte.
Externe Speichererweiterungskarte für die Xbox
Auch bei der Xbox hängt die Nutzung eines externen Speichers von der Konsolengeneration ab. Bei älteren Modellen kannst du direkt von einer externen Festplatte oder SSD spielen. Bei der Xbox Series X und Series S geht das nicht. Eine Ausnahme bildet die externe Speichererweiterungskarte: Sie wurde in Zusammenarbeit mit Xbox entwickelt und bietet ein nahtloses Spielerlebnis, weil du hier Games direkt von der Karte starten und spielen kannst. Sie ist so konzipiert, dass sie die gleiche Speicherleistung wie die interne SSD bietet. Laut Herstellerangaben sorgt eine Übertragungsrate von 3.000 Megabyte pro Sekunde für schnelle Ladezeiten und geringe Latenzen. Du steckst die Karte auf der Rückseite der Xbox direkt in den dafür vorgesehenen Steckplatz. Das Modell von Seagate ist mit einem oder zwei Terabyte erhältlich. Bei Amazon kostet es ab 282,99 Euro.
Game Drive von Seagate für Xbox und Playstation 5
Sony bietet selbst einige externe Speicheroptionen an, die auf die Playstation 5 optimiert sind. Eine davon ist der Game Drive von Seagate. Der Durchmesser des Geräts beträgt 2,5 Zoll. Das Design ist der Konsole angepasst – inklusive Logo. Die externe Festplatte ist mit zwei oder fünf Terabyte erhältlich und bietet somit ausreichend Platz, um ältere Spiele zu archivieren oder überall hin mitzunehmen. Du schließt sie per USB-3.0-Schnittstelle direkt an die Konsole an. Ein erneutes Herunterladen entfällt somit. Bei Amazon kostet die kleinere Variante aktuell 150,99 Euro. Das gleiche Modell gibt es auch für die Xbox mit der klassischen schwarzen Optik der Microsoft-Konsole. Es ist mit zwei, acht und 20 Terabyte verfügbar, der Preis startet bei 128,99 Euro.
- Seagate Game Drive für Playstation 5 bei Amazon*
- Seagate Game Drive für Xbox Series X und Series S bei Amazon*
Externe SSD von Sandisk für deine Playstation 5
Auch Sandisk bietet externen Speicher, der offiziell für die Playstation 5 lizenziert ist. Die SSD misst ebenfalls 2,5 Zoll und orientiert sich mit ihrer weißen Farbe am Design der Sony-Konsole. Laut Hersteller bietet sie eine hohe Geschwindigkeit von bis zu 1.000 Megabyte pro Sekunde, um Spiele schnell vom externen SSD-Archiv auf den internen Speicher der Playstation 5 zu übertragen. Zudem ist sie besonders robust: Sie bietet IP65-Schutz und ist fallsicher aus bis zu drei Metern Höhe. Wie die Seagate-Festplatte schließt du die SSD per USB an die Konsole an. Das Modell gibt es mit einem oder zwei Terabyte Speicherplatz. Bei Amazon kostet es ab 200,99 Euro. Laut etablierten Preisvergleichsportalen ist das aktuell das günstigste Angebot. Trotzdem kann es sich lohnen, mit dem Kauf noch etwas zu warten, denn bis vor Kurzem war die SSD schon ab 179 Euro erhältlich.

articles.title: Apple préparerait un grand renouvellement de ses iPad en 2027, mais tous n'auront pas droit aux mêmes nouveautés
articles.text:
Apple aurait prévu de renouveler trois familles d’iPad au cours du premier semestre 2027, avec des évolutions importantes pour certains modèles. Écran OLED, processeurs plus rapides et refroidissement amélioré seraient au programme, mais les nouveautés ne devraient pas être réparties équitablement entre les différentes tablettes.
Apple vient à peine de présenter son nouvel iPad mini OLED que les regards se tournent déjà vers les autres tablettes de la marque. Et l’année prochaine pourrait être particulièrement chargée. Selon Mark Gurman, Apple préparerait une nouvelle vague de lancements au premier semestre 2027, avec des mises à jour de l’iPad classique, de l'iPad Air et de l'iPad Pro. Si plusieurs caractéristiques ont déjà fait l’objet de rumeurs, ce calendrier laisse entrevoir un renouvellement presque complet de la gamme en quelques mois.
L’iPad Air se rapprocherait encore un peu plus du Pro
Dans sa dernière newsletter Power On, publiée par Bloomberg, Mark Gurman évoque notamment l’arrivée d’un iPad Air équipé d'un écran OLED au premier semestre 2027.
Cette évolution était attendue depuis plusieurs mois. Elle permettrait à la tablette intermédiaire d’Apple d’abandonner enfin sa dalle LCD, alors que l’iPad Pro utilise déjà l’OLED depuis 2024 et que le nouvel iPad mini vient lui aussi d’adopter cette technologie.
Le changement devrait se traduire par des noirs plus profonds et un meilleur contraste, particulièrement appréciables pour regarder des films, consulter des photos ou travailler sur des contenus visuels.
Cela ne signifie pas pour autant que l'iPad Air récupérera toutes les caractéristiques du modèle Pro. Les précédentes informations provenant de la chaîne d’approvisionnement évoquaient des dalles OLED moins sophistiquées que celles de la gamme supérieure, avec un taux de rafraîchissement qui pourrait rester limité à 60 Hz.
Apple chercherait ainsi à améliorer sensiblement la qualité d’affichage sans effacer les différences entre ses tablettes.
Un iPad Pro mieux refroidi, et un modèle classique qui se fait attendre
Le futur iPad Pro devrait lui aussi profiter d’une mise à jour au premier semestre 2027. Mark Gurman évoque des performances accrues, ainsi que la possible arrivée d’un système de refroidissement par chambre à vapeur.
Déjà utilisé dans les iPhone Pro, ce dispositif permet de mieux répartir la chaleur produite par les composants. Son intérêt serait particulièrement important sur l’iPad Pro, dont le châssis extrêmement fin complique l’évacuation thermique lors des tâches exigeantes.
Les jeux vidéo, le montage ou certains traitements d’intelligence artificielle pourraient ainsi maintenir de meilleures performances sur la durée. Il s’agit toutefois d'une piste de développement déjà évoquée par Bloomberg, et non d'une caractéristique confirmée par Apple.
L'autre information concerne l'iPad d’entrée de gamme, dont le renouvellement se fait attendre. Initialement évoqué pour 2026, son lancement serait désormais envisagé au cours du premier semestre 2027.
Cette tablette devrait surtout bénéficier d'une modernisation de ses composants. De précédentes informations découvertes dans le code d’Apple évoquaient notamment une puce A19, 8 Go de mémoire vive et de nouvelles puces de connectivité. Une évolution qui pourrait notamment lui permettre d’accéder aux fonctions d'Apple Intelligence.
Apple n’a évidemment confirmé aucun de ces projets, ni communiqué de calendrier officiel. Mais après avoir profondément modernisé l'iPad mini, le constructeur pourrait consacrer les prochains mois à remettre le reste de sa gamme au goût du jour, avec des changements plus importants sur les modèles Air et Pro quitte à délaisser un peu son modèle historique.

articles.title: Clinics On Cloud raises $12.5M to expand microclinic network
articles.text:
Clinics On Cloud raises $12.5M to expand microclinic network
The Pune-based firm will use the funding to strengthen its artificial intelligence capabilities, expand research and development, and grow its connected microclinic network.
Healthtech company Clinics On Cloud has raised $12.5 million in Series A funding from Dubai-based Model42, a health and wellness growth platform powered by Enlightened Minds Investments.
The Pune-based firm said it will use the funding to strengthen its artificial intelligence capabilities, expand research and development, and grow its connected microclinic network. It also plans partnerships with healthcare providers and technology companies to integrate new screening tools and AI applications.
The United Arab Emirates will be its global hub, with planned expansion into Africa, the United States and Southeast Asia.
Founded in 2018, Clinics On Cloud builds technology-enabled healthcare access points. Its Health ATMs are compact screening stations combining connected medical devices, health checks and digital reports, alongside AI-assisted insights and telemedicine. Its portfolio also includes Health Lounges, Box Clinics and Mobile Medical Units for hospitals, workplaces, housing communities and underserved areas.
Founder and chief executive officer Abhay Agarwal said the company had spent eight years guided by the belief that “quality healthcare should never depend on someone’s PIN code”. The investment, he said, would help take that vision overseas, with the opportunity lying in “making these innovations accessible to people, wherever they are”.
Clinics On Cloud claims more than 3,500 deployments, over 12 million health screenings and operations in eight countries. Its systems have been used in government health centres, hospitals, corporate sites, rural communities and Indian defence establishments, including the Army, Navy and Border Security Force.
The funding comes amid a more selective investment climate. Venture Intelligence data showed Indian health-tech startup funding fell to $447 million in 2025 from $707 million in 2024.
However, capital continues to flow into specialised models. In October, preventive-health startup Cent raised $15 million in a Series A led by Blume Ventures and South Park Commons. In July, radiology AI company CARPL.ai secured $10 million in a round led by the International Finance Corporation.
Meanwhile, public digital infrastructure is also expanding. By May 2026, the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission had crossed 90 crore digital health accounts and 100 crore linked health records. Initiatives announced in June, including digital clinic-management tools and common data standards, aim to make health information easier to exchange.

articles.title: Du porno en pleine rue : une cyberattaque a fait dérailler les panneaux publicitaires dans plusieurs pays
articles.text:
Ces pirates ont sans doute trouvé la pire chose à afficher sur des écrans publicitaires dans les rues : de la pornographie. C’est ce que le groupe Leakers$, ou LeakerGov, a réussi à faire un peu partout dans le monde il y a quelques jours. Des incidents loin d’être inconnus : par le passé, on a vu d’autres opérations de piratage de panneaux publicitaires pour diffuser des images pornographiques.
Égypte, Malaisie, Brésil… des panneaux publicitaires touchés partout dans le monde
Plusieurs pays semblent avoir été touchés par ce piratage : l’Égypte, la Malaisie, le Brésil, etc. Le groupe pirate affirme même avoir eu accès à des systèmes en Irak et en Chine, sans que cela n’ait été confirmé par les autorités. L’épisode le plus marquant s’est néanmoins produit à Giza en Égypte, sur un grand panneau donnant sur l’axe du 26 juillet. Il s’agit d’une voie très fréquentée reliant Le Caire à ses banlieues ouest. Certains automobilistes se sont même arrêtés pour filmer ces panneaux. Dessus, on voyait des contenus sexuellement explicites, avec un texte juste en dessous : « Leaked by: Ch, 19ylegal never and nivex », accompagné d’un pseudonyme Telegram, @LeakersGov.
Le même jour, plusieurs écrans LED publics de Kluang, dans l’État malaisien de Johor, ont affiché des contenus obscènes du même genre. Le conseil municipal a d’ailleurs. Même chose au Brésil, un panneau publicitaire installé le long d’une avenue de Campo Maior, dans le Piauí, a aussi diffusé des images pornographiques. L’entreprise Ferreira & Ferreira Publicidade e Comunicação a indiqué avoir immédiatement coupé l’équipement, déposé plainte et présenté ses excuses, comme l’a rapporté The Star.
Un seul système visé, qui fait fonctionner tous ces panneaux ? C’est la principale hypothèse
Trois pays, trois entreprises différentes, mais des panneaux piratés au même moment. Aucune confirmation à l’heure actuelle, mais tout laisse à penser que les pirates de Leakers$ ont réussi à pirater un même système, utilisé par toutes ces entreprises à travers le monde. Ce serait alors le même cas que les réfrigérateurs de supermarchés piratés en France le mois dernier ; un système commun utilisé par plusieurs sociétés.
Et selon les explications du groupe de pirates sur Telegram reprises par The Cairo Report, ces derniers ont découvert des milliers de systèmes exposés grâce à un scan automatisé durant deux heures. Leakers$ a précisé que « l’opération n’était pas aussi complexe que beaucoup pourraient l’imaginer » et que « les entreprises factures des millions pour construire des infrastructures dans plusieurs pays, mais laissent les écrans LED et les réseaux publicitaires connectés à Internet sans même une protection de base ».
Enfin, sur sa chaîne Telegram, le groupe a expliqué que « l’Égypte reste sous dictature » et a critiqué le gouvernement en place pour sa répression envers la population et le niveau de vie des Égyptiens. Leakers$ dit ne pas demander de rançons ni même de dons, ajoutant avoir commis ce délit pour prouver que « n’importe qui peut prendre le contrôle d’écrans dans tout le pays en temps réel ».

articles.title: Una nueva oeada de ciberataques hace que las neveras suban hasta 50 grados. Está pasando en Bélgica y Suecia
articles.text:
Tener los dispositivos conectados permite su gestión centralizada y a distancia. Esto supone una enorme ventaja para las empresas con miles de estos dispositivos desperdigados, por eso las grandes cadenas de supermercados centralizan controles como el de la refrigeración de sus productos. El problema llega cuando el acceso al sistema no está suficientemente bien protegido: un ciberataque arruinó toneladas de productos en Francia.
Calor en las neveras del norte. Tras el grave problema que se desencadenó en Francia, donde los supermercados se vieron perjudicados, Suecia y Bélgica están viviendo un episodio similar: los frigoríficos de algunas grandes cadenas de alimentación vieron elevada su temperatura hasta llegar a límites de 50 ºC.
El incidente comenzó a afectar el pasado domingo por la noche en las tiendas de los países mencionados. La mecánica ha sido similar a la de Francia: repentinamente, los frigoríficos variaron su temperatura de frío sin que los operarios alterasen dicha temperatura. Aunque en un principio se hablaba de un fallo informático, actualmente son varios los medios que lo denominan ciberataque.
Dispositivos expuestos. Si en Francia se descubrió que el acceso a determinadas neveras Danfoss utilizaban "admin" como usuario de administración y el día como código de contraseña para acceder al sistema, aún no se sabe cuál ha sido el vector de intrusión en este nuevo ataque. Todo apunta a equipos antiguos, desactualizados, con acceso innecesario a Internet y protegidos por contraseñas no demasiado seguras.
Algunos de los supermercados afectados son Delhaize, Carrefour, Spar, Ica o Coop. Según las primeras averiguaciones, los atacantes activaron remotamente los evaporadores en modo descongelación (defrost), lo que hizo subir la temperatura de la cámara hasta poner en riesgo el producto refrigerado. Aún no se conoce el número total de tiendas afectadas ni hay una estimación de las pérdidas.
Desconectar, la primera defensa. Delhaize ha optado por lo más rápido: cortar el cable de acceso a Internet. Esto es lo fácil, lo difícil es solucionar el problema de fondo: según el CEO de Sabcobel, una instaladora que gestiona cientos de estos equipos en Bélgica, con una actualización de software no es suficiente.
Muchos frigoríficos necesitan modificaciones físicas, algo que no es precisamente rentable. Con Francia, Bélgica y Suecia en la lista de ciberataques en apenas tres semanas, cuesta pensar que las de hoy vayan a ser las últimas neveras hackeadas.

articles.title: 👨🏿🚀TechCabal Daily – AGOA, going, gone - TechCabal
articles.text:
Good morning. ☀️
Let’s dive in.
Read smart insights about Francophone Africa’s tech ecosystem—weekly.
Economy
South Africa and Rwanda lose access to AGOA
South Africa spent months fighting to keep its preferential access to the US market. It has now lost that fight.
What happened? The United States will remove South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) from January 1, 2027. Jamieson Greer, the US Trade Representative, said President Donald Trump found that both countries were engaging in practices inconsistent with the programme’s eligibility rules, including barriers affecting American trade and investment.
Explain like I’m new here: AGOA gives eligible African countries duty-free access to the US for thousands of products. However, it is not a permanent free-trade agreement. Countries are reviewed every year against requirements covering market access, rule of law, corruption, human rights, and other areas.
In September, the US Congress extended AGOA until the end of 2028, but countries still have to qualify for its benefits. The US is now removing South Africa and Rwanda from that list. The US said the removal of South Africa and Rwanda from the AGOA programme would take effect on January 1, 2027.
However, both countries can still export goods to the US. The difference is that those goods will no longer get AGOA’s duty-free treatment and may now face normal US import tariffs.
Why it matters: South Africa has much more at stake. It was Africa’s largest non-oil user of AGOA and exported $1.6 billion worth of goods through the programme in 2025, according to the US Congress. Passenger vehicles and parts alone accounted for 64% of its AGOA-eligible exports in 2024.
Yet, this is not a complete trade wipeout. AGOA-covered goods accounted for about 10% of South Africa’s exports to the US in 2025; so the pain is concentrated in businesses that built their American sales around those preferences.
Rwanda’s exposure is much smaller. The US imported only $43.3 million in goods from Rwanda in 2025, and America had already suspended its AGOA apparel benefits in 2018 after a dispute over restrictions on imported second-hand clothing.
Between the lines: The bigger lesson is about certainty. AGOA has been extended for another two years for African countries, but access is still decided country by country, every year. Exporters can have a trade programme on the books and still lose the tariff advantage they built their business around.

Funding
BII puts $3 billion behind Africa’s hardest markets
Some African countries struggle to attract investment not because they lack businesses or infrastructure projects worth funding, but because the risks are too high for many global investors. British International Investment (BII), the UK government-owned development finance institution, wants to go where certain types of capital will not.
What happened? BII plans to invest about £2.25 billion ($3 billion) in some of Africa’s riskiest markets over the next five years, Bloomberg reported. The commitment is roughly a quarter of the £9 billion ($10.07 billion) BII expects to deploy and mobilise across Africa under its 2026–31 strategy.
The money will target frontier economies where private investment is scarce, while BII works with local banks, pension funds and other investors to deepen local financial markets.
Explain like I’m new here: BII is not an aid agency handing out grants. It invests in companies, banks, infrastructure, and funds, and expects returns. But as a development investor, it can take longer-term risks that commercial investors may avoid.
Think countries such as Sierra Leone, Liberia, Ethiopia, and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where businesses may have customers and growth opportunities but still struggle to raise money because investors worry about currency depreciation, political instability, weak capital markets, or difficulty getting their money out later.
In 2025, BII committed £729 million ($815.7 million) to poorer and more challenging markets. Its new strategy requires 25% of new core investments to go to the world’s least-developed countries.
Between the lines: Africa does not only need more foreign capital. It needs investors willing to take the first risk.
If BII backs a bank, power project, or local VC fund, and it performs well, the bigger win is proving to pension funds, insurers, and asset managers that the market can deliver investable returns. BII can then bring those investors into later deals instead of funding everything itself.
Streaming
Netflix to continue spending $60 million annually on South African titles, despite global cuts
At MIP Africa, a film and television industry market held in Cape Town from October 28 to 30, Kaye Ann Williams, Netflix’s director of scripted content for sub-Saharan Africa, reassured producers that the company was not pulling back from South Africa or the rest of the continent. She noted that Netflix was actually ramping up its investment.
Explain like I’m new here: Williams is taking over from Ben Amadasun, Netflix’s Africa content boss, who was retrenched in October alongside roughly 1,000 employees globally, about 6% of the company’s workforce. Netflix has not publicly given a specific reason for Amadasun’s departure.
However, when the person overseeing a region disappears in a global restructuring, producers are bound to wonder what happens to the projects and relationships built under them.
Why this matters: South Africa accounts for 71% of Netflix’s content production and licencing investment in Sub-Saharan Africa. Williams said the company now commissions around 15 to 20 local shows and films annually, up from eight to 12. Its decade-long presence has also supported more than 8,000 jobs through partnerships with over 30 local production companies.
Economy
Kenya wants global giants to show how much tax they pay by November 17
The Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) has given large multinational groups until November 17 to notify them that they fall under the country’s new minimum top-up tax regulations. The rules cover groups with consolidated annual revenues of at least €750 million ($839.2 million) in at least two of the previous four years.
If their effective tax rate on profits earned in Kenya falls below 15%, they may owe additional tax to make up the difference. Potentially affected groups include Google, Microsoft, Coca-Cola, Nestlé, Unilever, DHL, and TotalEnergies, provided they meet the eligibility requirements.
Explain like I’m new here: This is Kenya’s version of the global tax reform under the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s (OECD) international tax framework.
The idea is to stop large multinational companies from moving profits between countries to take advantage of very low tax rates. Under the agreement, qualifying groups should face an effective corporate tax rate of at least 15% in each country where they operate.
If they pay less, a top-up tax can make up the difference. Kenya introduced its minimum top-up tax through the 2024 tax amendments in September, starting the 60-day notification countdown.
Why this matters: Kenya needs the money. The country is looking to strengthen government revenue without relying so heavily on borrowing. Collecting more tax from profitable multinationals gives the government another way to strengthen its revenue base and reduce borrowing pressure.
November 17 is the deadline to notify KRA. The notification must identify the Kenyan entity, its multinational group, the group’s ultimate parent company, its financial year, and other group members operating in Kenya. Separate deadlines apply to filing returns and paying any top-up tax owed.

articles.title: Disney+ : les abonnés Premium retrouvent 4K et HDR, mais uniquement sur certains appareils
articles.text:
Disney+ : 4K et HDR reviennent partiellement avec le codec VP9
Nouvel épisode dans la saga Disney+ autour des technologies 4K et HDR. Ces dernières sont de retours pour les abonnés au forfait Premium, mais seuls les utilisateurs disposant de certains équipements pourront à nouveau en profiter.
Depuis février 2026, à cause de déboires judiciaires liés à des brevets autour du codec HEVC, la présence des technologies vidéo 4K et HDR fait des apparitions et des disparitions au fil des mois sur Disney+ dans plusieurs pays européens, dont la France. En attendant le fin mot de l'histoire, la plateforme tente de contourner ce problème afin de reproposer ces éléments à ses membres Premium, qui s'aquittent de l'offre la plus onéreuse depuis des mois pour (presque) rien. Pour cela, Disney+ s'appuie sur un codec différent, à savoir le VP9.
Cependant, le retour à la normale est encore loin.
4K et HDR10 reviennent sur Disney+, mais pas pour tous
Grâce au codec VP9, libre d'utilisation, depuis août dernier c'est la 4K qui est revenue sur Disney+. Cependant ce codec ne gère pas la plage dynamique étendue, interdisant donc le support du HDR. Depuis quelques jours, le support du codec VP9‑2 est cependant de la partie, permettant désormais le retour du HDR10.
Seulement voilà, non seulement la 3D et le Dolby Vision sont toujours aux abonnés absents, mais surtout les codecs VP9 ne sont pas aussi supportés que le codec HEVC. Seuls les abonnés Disney+ Premium disposant d'un téléviseur récent Android TV/Google TV (chez Google, Philips, Sony, TCL...), d'une TV LG (webOS) ou Hisense (Vidaa), ou encore d'un appareil Amazon Fire TV, peuvent profiter de ces technologies avec le support des codecs VP9 et VP9-2.
Pour les appareils plus anciens ou trop récents (exit ceux fonctionnant sous Titan OS et TiVo OS par exemple), les consoles de jeux, les boitiers multimédia Apple TV 4K et Nvidia Shield, ou encore de multiples téléviseurs Samsung (Tizen) et Panasonic (hors Google TV), c'est raté.
Un avenir toujours incertain
Si des mises à jour pourront étoffer la liste des appareils compatibles VP9 à l'avenir, pour le moment cela fait tout de même beaucoup de personnes laissées sur le bas côté. De plus, dans son litige juridique avec Disney+ la société InterDigital a décidé d'étendre ses poursuites au codec VP9, ce qui pourrait obliger Disney à retirer à nouveau 4K et HDR de sa plateforme.
Les tentatives de Disney+ de limiter la casse risquent de ne pas plaire aux abonnés, ou encore à l'association pour les consommateurs Que Choisir, qui mettait en demeure la plateforme en septembre dernier. En attendant un vrai geste commercial ou une baisse de l'abonnement, il est possible de tenter de demander un dédommagement au service client, tandis qu'un désabonnement ou un retour au moins temporaire au forfait Standard restent des possibilités.

articles.title: Marvell to acquire optical component maker Lumentum in massive $115B deal - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Marvell to acquire optical component maker Lumentum in massive $115B deal
Marvell Technology Inc. today announced plans to acquire Lumentum Holdings Inc. for $115 billion, in one of the largest deals in tech history.
Lumentum investors are set to receive 4.5 Marvell shares for every unit of stock they own. That translates to about $1,132 per share, which is 23.9% higher than the company’s last unaffected stock price.
Investors, however, weren’t so sanguine about the deal. Marvell’s shares fell almost 13%, while Lumentum’s fell almost 19%. Chalk it up, again, to recent investor worry that the promised growth from artificial intelligence infrastructure may not last forever.
Marvell provides networking equipment for data centers and telecommunications infrastructure. Many of its products use fiber-optic cables to transmit data. Lumentum, in turn, makes components for fiber-optic network devices such as those offered by Marvell. The acquisition will give the latter company more control over its supply chain, which could enable it to more closely align upstream components’ design with its requirements.
Optical networks use laser emitters to generate the light which they transmit data. Lumentum sells a line of lasers based on indium phosphide, a semiconducting material that generates light more efficiently than silicon. The product family includes modular and continuous wave devices. Modulated lasers are used to physically connect servers to the host data center’s optical network, while continuous wave lasers power longer-range network links.
Lumentum also makes single-mode optical amplifiers. Such devices strengthen the laser signals that travel through long-haul carrier networks to reduce data transmission errors.
Last year, the company debuted a laser optimized for co-packaged optics, or CPO, chips. Such chips enable servers to connect to the host data center’s network without expensive modules called transceivers that are usually needed for the task. CPO technology has emerged as an important focus of Marvell’s growth strategy. Its chip design business can help customers integrate CPO modules into their custom artificial intelligence accelerators.
Lumentum doesn’t focus solely on the laser component market. It uses a material called indium gallium arsenide to make analog photodetectors, which customers can use to monitor their optical networks for errors. The company also sells optical circuit switches. Such devices use tiny mirrors to coordinate the flow of traffic, which removes the need to turn data into electrical signals and thereby saves power.
Notably, Lumentum will also give Marvell a presence in the industrial equipment market. The former company makes high-power lasers for cutting and welding machines. It’s unclear what will happen to that part of Lumentum’s product portfolio following the deal. After a large acquisition, companies sometimes spin off newly absorbed business units that don’t align with their core focus.
“By bringing together two leaders with highly complementary technologies, exceptional talent and specialized manufacturing capabilities, we intend to help shape the next era of AI connectivity and create exceptional stockholder value,” said Marvell Chief Executive Officer Matt Murphy.
The chipmaker expects to close the acquisition in the first half of 2028. The combined company will be led by Murphy, while Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston will join the board along with two of the optical component supplier’s directors.
Marvell expects the deal to become accretive to its adjusted earnings per share within a year of closing. In the longer term, the company hopes to achieve annual run-rate cost savings of more than $1 billion and accelerate revenue growth. Marvell estimates that Lumentum will expand its total addressable market to $550 billion.

articles.title: Intel "Wildcat Lake" Powers Zotac's New Fanless ZBOX Mini PCs
articles.text:
Monday, November 2nd 2026
Intel "Wildcat Lake" Powers Zotac's New Fanless ZBOX Mini PCs
Zotac has updated its webstore with the listing of three new ZBOX mini PCs based on Intel's "Wildcat Lake" platform. According to FanlessTech, who first spotted these mini PCs, this marks one of the first instances of passively-cooled mini PCs using Intel "Wildcat Lake" SoCs. There are three models in total: the CI431 nano, CI451 nano, and CI471 nano. They all share a passively cooled chassis measuring 204 × 129 × 68 mm, with a volume of 1.79 liters. The entry-level CI431 nano features a Core 3 304 processor with 1 P-Core and 4 low-power E-Cores, totaling five cores and five threads, and boost speeds reaching 4.3 GHz. The CI451 nano is equipped with a Core 5 320, while the CI471 nano has a Core 7 350. Both of these models feature 2 P-Cores and 4 low-power E-Cores, providing six cores and six threads, with maximum clock speeds of 4.6 GHz and 4.8 GHz, respectively.
Intel specifies 6 MB of Smart Cache, 15 W base power, and 35 W maximum turbo power for all three processors, which are manufactured using its 18A process. The graphics capabilities differ between models: the Core 3 has one Xe-core running at up to 2.3 GHz, while the Core 5 and Core 7 have two Xe-cores running at up to 2.5 GHz and 2.6 GHz, respectively. Their integrated NPUs deliver up to 15, 16, and 17 TOPS, respectively. Each system supports up to 64 GB of DDR5-6400 memory through one SO-DIMM slot, along with an M.2 2280 PCIe 4.0 x4 SSD.While tiny, these systems offer solid I/O selection. Options include two Thunderbolt 4 ports, two USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A ports, three USB 2.0 ports, 2.5 GbE, Wi-Fi 7, and Bluetooth 5.4. HDMI 2.0b, DisplayPort 2.0, and Thunderbolt display outputs support up to three 4K displays at 60 Hz. A VESA mounting kit and an external 65 W power adapter are included with each barebone system, while memory and storage are sold separately. Pricing and availability are not specified on Zotac's product pages.

articles.title: Ocho grupos de hackers de Corea del Norte usan IA para atacar más rápido, según Microsoft
articles.text:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence, el equipo de la empresa que sigue a grupos de hackers, informó el 29 de octubre que ocho grupos vinculados a Corea del Norte usan inteligencia artificial en sus operaciones. Los emplean para investigar víctimas, crear mensajes falsos y programar herramientas de ataque. Según el informe, publicado el 29 de octubre en la web de la empresa, el uso en el conjunto de esos grupos es “alto”.
Microsoft los clasificó en cuatro etapas. Tres grupos, Jade Sleet, Coral Sleet y Jasper Sleet, tienen la IA integrada en todo su trabajo. Otros cuatro, Diamond Sleet, Onyx Sleet, Pearl Sleet y Sapphire Sleet, están en fase de aceleración. Emerald Sleet la usa de forma más limitada. Ninguno figura en la etapa inicial o experimental.
La empresa precisó que las operaciones siguen dirigidas por personas y que no son autónomas. También sostuvo que la IA sirve a los objetivos de siempre: obtener dinero para el régimen, reunir información estratégica y, en algunos casos, causar daño. Entre los blancos habituales están las empresas de criptomonedas y finanzas.
Cómo operaron los grupos de IA
Entre el 8 y el 12 de junio, Jade Sleet se hizo pasar por reclutador de una supuesta empresa de inteligencia sobre blockchain (la tecnología que registra las transacciones con criptomonedas). Contactó a personas de ciberseguridad, IA y reclutamiento. En ese lapso repitió la maniobra con otras dos empresas falsas, con infraestructura parecida. Microsoft atribuyó esa velocidad al uso de IA generativa.
Onyx Sleet creó más de 100 archivos PDF con señuelos entre agosto y septiembre, dirigidos a usuarios surcoreanos. Los metadatos mostraron que generaba decenas de archivos en pocos minutos, algo que Microsoft atribuyó, con alta probabilidad, a una plataforma de IA. Esa producción en serie complica la detección, según el informe.
Coral Sleet, desde abril, usa un método para infectar repositorios privados de código en GitHub. Microsoft estimó que la capacidad se desarrolló con una herramienta de programación con IA. Sapphire Sleet probablemente también la usó en el ataque de agosto a desarrolladores del lenguaje Rust. Además, Onyx Sleet y Pearl Sleet emplean ARTEX, un programa de código abierto de pruebas de intrusión con IA.
Un precedente con 12 millones de dólares en billeteras
En abril, la firma de seguridad Expel describió a HexagonalRodent, un grupo que atribuyó a Corea del Norte. Según Expel, sus programas maliciosos obtuvieron datos de 26.584 billeteras de criptomonedas en 2.726 equipos de desarrolladores. Esas billeteras sumaban hasta USD 12 millones entre el 1 de enero y el 31 de marzo de 2026.
Expel no pudo confirmar si todo ese dinero fue retirado, porque algunas billeteras podían estar protegidas con llaves físicas. El grupo ofrecía empleos falsos a programadores y les enviaba una prueba técnica infectada. Según Expel, usó ChatGPT y Cursor, una herramienta de programación con IA, y dejó expuestos los textos que escribió para generar su código.
Marcus Hutchins, el investigador de Expel que firmó el informe, explicó a Wired que Corea del Norte envía a muchos trabajadores de informática al exterior, pero pocos tienen alta capacidad técnica. Según él, la IA permite a los menos hábiles dirigir campañas que dan resultado.
USD 2.000 millones robados en 2025
La firma de análisis de blockchain TRM Labs calculó en mayo que el 76% de las criptomonedas robadas en 2026 hasta ese momento estaba en manos de Corea del Norte, según Dark Reading. Ari Redbord, jefe de políticas de TRM, dijo que la IA elimina límites como el idioma y el tiempo para armar personajes creíbles. Informó además de un aumento del 500% en estafas asistidas por IA en un año.
Según Chainalysis, citada por The Block, los hackers norcoreanos robaron USD 2.020 millones en criptomonedas en 2025, incluidos USD 1.500 millones del ataque a la plataforma Bybit. Esa cifra corresponde al año anterior y no incluye los robos de 2026.
En agosto, la firma surcoreana Genians informó, según Reuters, que el grupo Kimsuky instaló programas de IA que funcionan en sus propios equipos, sin enviar datos a servicios externos. Genians dijo que el hallazgo indica que el grupo pasa de generar mensajes de engaño a preparar herramientas de ataque con IA.
El informe de Microsoft incluye recomendaciones de protección y detecciones para sus productos de seguridad, y concluye que los ataques con IA siguen apoyándose en ingeniería social, es decir, en engañar a personas con perfiles y ofertas falsas.

articles.title: Trajectory raises $45M to make AI model training accessible to nontechnical experts | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Whether developed by OpenAI or Anthropic or built on open source alternatives, current AI models share a critical limitation: They don’t learn from their mistakes without further training.
Businesses adapting these models for specialized fields, such as law and finance, typically get around this by fine-tuning general models. However, that often requires hiring internal research teams or relying on expensive consultants, commonly known as forward-deployed engineers (FDEs).
Trajectory, a startup founded about a year ago by three Stanford classmates with experience at Google DeepMind and Apple, wants to automate that process, allowing AI models to learn from feedback and continuously improve at specialized tasks.
The 18-person company just announced that it raised $45 million in a Series A round at a $300 million valuation, led by Sequoia, with participation from Nvidia, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Bain Capital Ventures.
Trajectory co-founder Ronak Malde compared foundational models to a very smart PhD student who’s always starting a new job. “But what the economy values is someone who worked on the job for 30 years,” he told TechCrunch.
The startup aims to solve this problem through an approach known as continual learning. Businesses using Trajectory can start with an open source AI model and connect the platform to their applications, allowing it to collect feedback on how the model performs. Trajectory then uses that information to retrain the model, helping it improve at specialized tasks over time.
With Trajectory, lawyers, doctors, and other specialists can improve the models near automatically themselves, Malde said. That capability could make deploying specialized AI faster and cheaper.
Companies like Harvey and Rogo are already using Trajectory’s platform to post-train open source models, helping them perform more like experienced lawyers or financial analysts by learning from previous tasks, such as reviewing a particular type of legal contract or valuing a company using a specific methodology. Trajectory’s other customers include Decagon, Mercor, and Nvidia. The startup is now making its post-training platform publicly available.
The people using Trajectory decide “what good looks like for their organization and can turn that into improvements for their model,” Malde said.
Trajectory’s approach to continual learning shares some similarities with recursive self-improvement (RSI), the idea that AI systems can improve their own capabilities. But co-founder Michael Elabd argues that keeping humans involved in the training process makes Trajectory’s approach safer, since autonomous self-improvement could lead to unintended or even dangerous outcomes.
Trajectory isn’t the only startup trying to automate post-training. Other companies going after this market include Thinking Machines Lab, founded by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati and the company behind the fine-tuning platform Tinker, Applied Compute, which was valued at $3.25 billion last month, and Prime Intellect, a platform that helps companies build and train their own AI agents.
Malde believes the startup’s biggest advantage is its team. He was among the handful of researchers Google DeepMind acqui-hired from Windsurf. Elabd also worked at DeepMind, while Trajectory’s third co-founder, Arjun Karanam, previously worked on generative foundation models at Apple. The startup has also recruited researchers and product designers from OpenAI, Stripe, and Netflix.
Why does design matter so much to a company focused on AI training? Karanam says the startup has developed an interface that makes post-training more accessible to its nontechnical customers.

articles.title: You can now use the AI-powered ‘Ask this book’ feature on the latest Kindles — but Amazon’s being weirdly quiet about its rollout
articles.text:
Amazon’s ‘Ask this book’ feature is finally rolling out to Kindles — but certain models and regions may be excluded
Get AI-powered insights and plot refreshers
- Amazon's 'Ask this book' feature is now rolling out to Kindles
- It's part of software version 5.20.2
- So far, users have only reported this landing on 2026 models, and it might currently be US-exclusive
Amazon launched ‘Ask this book’ almost a year ago now, with this AI-powered tool allowing you to ask questions about what you’re reading. However, it was initially only available for the iOS Kindle app, and only in the US.
Now, though, that availability is widening — at least a little. As spotted by some Reddit users and The eBook Reader, ‘Ask this book’ has started rolling out to certain Kindle models, including the Kindle Colorsoft 2026 and the Kindle Paperwhite 2026. It’s likely that the other 2026 Kindles will also receive this update, though that hasn’t been confirmed.
Indeed, Amazon itself has so far said very little about this rollout. The feature is part of software version 5.20.2, but this doesn’t yet have any release notes, or any confirmation beyond user reports of which models ‘Ask this book’ will actually work with.
Unclear availability
So, for now, there’s a question mark over whether the feature is coming to previous Kindle generations — I can say that my Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition 2024 does not yet have the update. But then it’s a UK model, and previously, the feature had only been available in the US — so it also remains to be seen whether other regions will get it.
For now, if you’re curious, you’ll seemingly have to wait and see whether your Kindle gets the update pushed to it — there is no way to force the update currently. The rollout might happen in stages, though, so even if you don’t have it yet, you may still get it. Just make sure Wi-Fi is on so your Kindle can update.
As for the ‘Ask this book’ feature itself, it’s potentially very useful, letting you, for example, ask about the plot or characters of a supported book and receive information based on where you’re up to in it — or for the whole book if you don’t mind spoilers.
As with most AI features, though, it’s also controversial, with Reddit comments about its original launch including “I hate it,” and “this feature is so invasive.” So it’s certainly not for everyone.

articles.title: iPhone Duo esgota na pré-venda e Apple não sabe quando situação vai melhorar
articles.text:
A Apple ainda não consegue prever quando terá unidades suficientes de seu primeiro iPhone dobrável, o iPhone Duo, para atender à procura pelo aparelho. O CEO da companhia, John Ternus, afirmou que a empresa trabalha para ampliar a oferta, mas não sabe quando a produção e a demanda estarão equilibradas.
Em entrevista à Reuters, Ternus disse que a fabricante está se esforçando para disponibilizar o dispositivo ao maior número possível de consumidores, mas que ainda não consegue estimar quando as restrições de fornecimento serão superadas.
O cenário ocorre pouco depois do lançamento do iPhone Duo, primeiro celular dobrável da Apple. Apresentado no mês passado por US$ 1.999 (no Brasil, os preços partem de R$ 21.999), o aparelho tem uma tela externa de 5,4 polegadas e painel interno de 7,6 polegadas.
Pré-venda esgotou rapidamente
A procura pelo iPhone Duo foi suficiente para esgotar rapidamente as unidades disponibilizadas na pré-venda. Algumas entregas já estão previstas apenas para 2027, enquanto a Apple também colocou uma quantidade limitada de aparelhos à venda em lojas físicas durante o lançamento.
A dificuldade para atender aos pedidos se soma a outros desafios enfrentados pela cadeia de suprimentos da empresa. A Apple vem lidando há meses com limitações de fornecimento e aumento nos custos de componentes.
Leia mais:
- IA faz preço de chips disparar e tira poder de barganha histórico da Apple
- iOS 27 permite verificar idade com selfie para acessar sites adultos
- Apple supera expectativas e registra melhor resultado financeiro da história
Memória mais cara pressiona a Apple
- Durante a teleconferência de resultados do quarto trimestre de 2026, realizada na segunda-feira (2), Ternus classificou como sem precedentes o cenário atual dos preços de memória;
- O executivo também afirmou que a companhia espera custos ainda maiores com esses componentes no trimestre encerrado em dezembro. Parte do impacto, porém, deve ser compensada pelos recentes reajustes de preços em produtos da empresa;
- As pressões já contribuíram para aumentos em diferentes dispositivos da linha Apple, incluindo os preços iniciais do iPhone 18 Pro e do iPhone 18 Pro Max;
- Apesar dos obstáculos, a companhia registrou receita recorde de US$ 57,58 bilhões (cerca de R$ 311 bilhões) com iPhones em seu quarto trimestre fiscal de 2026. O resultado foi alcançado mesmo sem o lançamento de um modelo convencional do iPhone 18 no período.
Apple comenta relatos de telas trincadas
Na mesma entrevista à Reuters, Ternus também abordou relatos de telas trincadas no iPhone Duo. Segundo o executivo, apenas uma parcela muito pequena dos aparelhos foi devolvida por causa desse problema, e a Apple está realizando a substituição das unidades afetadas.
A declaração ocorre em meio à atenção sobre a durabilidade do primeiro dobrável da empresa, que inaugura nova categoria de produtos na linha de smartphones da fabricante.
Por enquanto, a Apple não apresentou previsão para normalizar o fornecimento do iPhone Duo. A declaração de Ternus indica que os consumidores interessados no aparelho ainda podem enfrentar um período de espera prolongado.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Over 100 European Stores Hit as Supermarket Fridge Attacks Return
articles.text:
More than 100 stores in several European countries saw their fridges and freezers heat up overnight from Sunday to Monday, and several retailers have blamed a cyberattack. The incidents closely resemble the attacks that disrupted European supermarkets three weeks ago.
The affected businesses, ranging from major chains to small butcher shops, are in Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden. Some units were set as high as 50°C (122°F), and problems have also been reported in Finland, Italy and Portugal.
Nobody has taken responsibility for the attacks. Investigators have not established whether the two waves are connected.
The first wave hit France overnight from October 11 to 12. Around 700 supermarkets had their refrigeration units forced into defrost mode, including Intermarché, Carrefour, Coopérative U and Monoprix stores. Food was spoiled, and the attacks reportedly caused fires.
CERT-FR, the incident response team of France’s cybersecurity agency ANSSI, initially linked the compromises to Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC series controllers. A day later, it expanded its alert to cover Copeland and Dixell XWEB systems. Danfoss said most of the hacked units were legacy products it no longer updated.
Exposed Danfoss, Copeland controllers hijacked in new attacks
The technique appears to be the same. Stephan Moelans, CEO of Belgian refrigeration firm Sabcobel, told the Belga news agency that the attackers forced the units’ evaporators into defrost mode, as happened in France.
According to Moelans, a software update is not enough to fully resolve the weakness, and the affected equipment also needs to be physically modified.
Dutch broadcaster NOS reported that, as far as is known, the targeted devices were made by Danfoss and Copeland. An Estonian refrigeration supplier said the units attacked there were older Danfoss models.
Danfoss said that on October 13 it had told its customers to cut their systems’ internet connections and to reconnect only through a secure network. “Most stores took action at that time, but a small number did not,” a company spokesperson told NOS.
Security researcher Kevin Beaumont said people he spoke with had confirmed that every freezer hit on Monday had a management interface reachable from the internet. According to Beaumont, many of the devices are end-of-life and have no available patch.
Officials have not publicly explained how the attackers got in.
Deception security firm Lupovis told SecurityWeek that, between October 20 and 30, it saw suspicious activity aimed at its Danfoss AK-SM refrigeration controller sensors, including sensors in some of the affected regions. Most of the login attempts relied on factory-default credentials that Danfoss documents publicly, while others appeared to be trying to fingerprint specific Danfoss controller components.
“The activity peaked on 26 October, and importantly, we had not observed this behaviour on these sensors before 20 October. All authentication attempts were rejected by our sensors,” said Lupovis CEO Xavier Bellekens, adding that the timing is noteworthy.
Censys has found just over 1,000 Danfoss StoreView interfaces reachable online worldwide. “France continues to lead Danfoss StoreView exposures globally, followed by Belgium and the US,” the internet intelligence firm said.
The number of exposed StoreView instances in France has fallen sharply, from 1,825 before the October attacks to 220 at the time of Censys’ latest analysis.
By matching firmware build dates, Censys estimates that 41% of the French instances still online run a patched version. It counted 138 exposed instances in Belgium, 51 in the Netherlands and 50 in Sweden, of which 68%, 37% and 58%, respectively, appear to be patched.
Only a handful of exposed instances were seen in Luxembourg, Ireland and Estonia. Censys did not indicate whether any patched devices were among those compromised on Monday.
Belgium among hardest hit
Belgium appears to have taken the biggest hit. Delhaize said an IT incident disrupted refrigeration at several dozen of its stores, Carrefour counted 15 affected locations out of more than 700, and Colruyt said five franchised Spar shops were attacked.
An IKEA store in Mons was hit as well, and the Belgian federal prosecutor’s office has opened an investigation.
In Luxembourg, four Delhaize outlets were affected. In Ireland, SuperValu pulled chilled and frozen products from 13 stores where one specific refrigeration model was impacted.
Swedish grocer ICA confirmed that a limited number of its stores were impacted, while Coop reported problems at a handful of locations. An ICA store manager said they had to throw out significant amounts of food.
In the Netherlands, Danfoss said the systems of at least 17 businesses were hit, mainly butcher shops and small grocers.
Finnish retailer Kesko said a few of its smaller stores had temperature disruptions. In Italy, the operator of several Coop-branded supermarkets in Sicily alerted the national cybersecurity agency, and in Portugal, the Mosqueteiros group confirmed incidents at seven Intermarché stores.
EU agriculture commissioner Christophe Hansen called the attacks a deliberate bid to disrupt the food supply chain and erode consumer trust. “The repeated occurrence of these cyberattacks is deeply concerning,” he said.
Hansen said the bloc’s food security is not under threat for now, but he acknowledged the food that had to be thrown away and the harm to businesses.

articles.title: Mercado Bitcoin pode ter perdido R$ 217 milhões em ataque hacker • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Mercado Bitcoin pode ter perdido R$ 217 milhões em ataque hacker
Corretora brasileira afirma que clientes não tiveram prejuízos nem dados vazados. Depósitos e saques foram temporariamente suspensos.
Resumo
- Mercado Bitcoin identificou e conteve um incidente de segurança em um de seus sistemas.
- O incidente teria envolvido cerca de US$ 40 milhões, mas a empresa afirma que não houve prejuízos aos clientes nem vazamento de dados.
- A corretora está investigando o caso com a ajuda das autoridades e manterá atualizações regulares sobre o andamento da situação.
A Mercado Bitcoin, uma das maiores corretoras de ativos digitais do Brasil, informou nesta segunda-feira (02/11) que identificou e conteve um incidente de segurança em um de seus sistemas. Como medida preventiva, a empresa suspendeu temporariamente os serviços de depósito e saque.
O alerta sobre possíveis movimentações irregulares partiu da Hypernative, empresa especializada em segurança de blockchain. Segundo o monitoramento, cerca de US$ 40 milhões (aproximadamente R$ 217,7 milhões) teriam sido transferidos de carteiras ligadas à corretora.
Comunicado oficial: Identificamos e contivemos com rapidez um incidente de segurança em um de nossos sistemas nesta madrugada. Reforçamos que: • Não houve nenhum prejuízo aos clientes; • Não houve vazamento de dados. Como medida preventiva de proteção, depósitos e saques estão temporariamente suspensos. Nossas equipes estão mobilizadas investigando o caso, rastreando os ativos e coordenando as medidas junto às autoridades competentes. Manteremos atualizações regulares por aqui.
— Mercado Bitcoin (@MercadoBitcoin) November 2, 2026
A maior parte das transferências teria acontecido entre 3h19 e 3h53 de hoje, no horário de Brasília. Os ativos foram enviados para endereços recém-criados, associados pela empresa de segurança a um possível invasor.
Em comunicado, a Mercado Bitcoin afirmou que identificou e conteve o problema, sem prejuízos aos clientes ou vazamento de dados. A corretora, porém, não confirmou o valor estimado pela Hypernative, mas está investigando o caso junto às autoridades.
Binance sofreu roubo histórico há poucos dias
O incidente ocorre poucos dias após a Binance registrar o que foi apontado como o maior roubo de criptomoedas da história. Na sexta-feira (30/10), a principal corretora do mercado informou que uma invasão movimentou cerca de US$ 6,3 bilhões (R$ 33,9 bilhões) em ativos de carteiras de clientes.
A investigação inicial da Binance indica que os invasores podem ter acessado o notebook de um engenheiro de DevOps, profissional que atua na integração entre desenvolvimento e operações. A partir do computador, os hackers teriam conseguido entrar em serviços internos da corretora usando os privilégios de acesso do funcionário.
A Binance afirmou que vai cobrir integralmente os prejuízos causados pelo ataque. Na ocasião, a empresa também suspendeu depósitos e saques enquanto investigava o incidente e analisava seus sistemas. Os depósitos já foram retomados.

articles.title: Elon Musk mocks OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's claim that PCs having RAM is terrible — 'The people deserve to have their RAM too!'
articles.text:
Elon Musk mocks OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's claim that PCs having RAM is terrible — 'The people deserve to have their RAM too!'
Musk's memo called out Altman's claim that it's "quite terrible" for home computers to have RAM amid a global supply crunch.
SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has taken to X, the social network that he owns, to mock OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's stance that it's "quite terrible" for home computer users to have DRAM in their machines. Altman made the claim during an appearance on the YouTube channel Cheeky Pint, noting that it would be better for DRAM to be used in AI data centers instead. Mocking the point, Musk shared a meme on X that referenced a movie in which a German WWII officer appears to be hunting for people hiding sticks of DRAM.
Altman's stance has already drawn plenty of ire across the internet. "From a global allocation perspective, actually, it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used 5% of the time," Altman said during the YouTube interview. "You want maximum utilization in the cloud if you're trying to deal with this very supply-constrained environment. And somehow many people's intuition is the opposite of that."
OpenAI does, of course, offer some open-source models, but it makes its money from models hosted in data centers, which it can charge users to access at home. With that in mind, it's perhaps unsurprising that Altman would rather people not have home computers that are capable of running local models, negating the need for cloud-based alternatives. However, Altman's comments are ill-timed — computer enthusiasts and average users alike are facing increased prices across the board, whether buying DRAM kits themselves or computers as a whole. As chipmakers retool factories to produce components for AI data centers rather than the consumer market, prices have skyrocketed on everything from DRAM kits to the storage used in devices of all shapes and sizes.
Even Apple, a company previously thought immune to component price increases, hiked prices across its lineups earlier this year. Its recent iPhone launches saw a price increase across the board, too. Beyond Apple, Lenovo said in June that it didn't expect prices to return to pre-2026 levels anytime soon, if ever. Makers of DRAM, Samsung and SK hynix, have also warned that AI-driven memory shortages will last until 2027 and beyond.
As the perceived demand for more AI data centers shows little sign of slowing, the demand for the components that power them will similarly maintain levels that put all other technology at risk of price increases and limited availability.

articles.title: Synology NAS Devices Targeted in Ransomware Attacks Exploiting Patched DSM Flaw
articles.text:
Synology is urging customers to update the DiskStation Manager (DSM) software powering its Network Attached Storage (NAS) devices following ransomware attacks.
The Taiwanese vendor said it observed threat actors exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 to target devices running outdated versions of DSM.
"These attacks aim to encrypt data and extort ransom," it said in a statement released last week.
While Synology did not disclose the exact security flaw that's being exploited in these attacks, the company linked to a November 2024 security advisory that listed three vulnerabilities -
- CVE-2024-10441 (CVSS score: 9.8) - An improper encoding or escaping of output vulnerability in the system plugin daemon of DSM that could lead to remote code execution via unspecified vectors.
- CVE-2024-50629 (CVSS score: 5.3) - An improper encoding or escaping of output vulnerability in the webapi component of DSM that could allow remote attackers to read limited files via unspecified vectors.
- CVE-2024-10445 (CVSS score: 4.3) - An improper certificate validation vulnerability in the update functionality in DSM that could allow remote attackers to write limited files via unspecified vectors.
The issues were addressed in the following versions -
- DSM 7.2.2 - Upgrade to 7.2.2-72806-1 or above
- DSM 7.2.1 - Upgrade to 7.2.1-69057-6 or above
- DSM 7.2 - Upgrade to 7.2-64570-4 or above
- DSM 7.1 - Upgrade to 7.1.1-42962-7 or above
- DSM 6.2 - Upgrade to 6.2.4-25556-8 or above
The development comes amid reports from customers that their Synology devices have been hit by C3RB3R ransomware, which has been observed locking users' files with a ".L0CK3D" extension.
This is not the first time NAS devices have been the target of ransomware attacks. In 2019, NAS devices manufactured by Taiwan-based QNAP Systems were compromised by QNAPCrypt (aka eCh0raix) ransomware.
Then, in August 2021, Synology warned of brute-force attacks driven by a malware family called StealthWorker that led to ransomware infections.
"These attacks leverage a number of already infected devices to try and guess common administrative credentials, and if successful, will access the system to install its malicious payload, which may include ransomware," it said at the time. "Devices infected may carry out additional attacks on other Linux-based devices, including Synology NAS."
That same month, Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 also disclosed details of an eCh0raix variant targeting NAS devices from both QNAP and Synology by leveraging vulnerabilities like CVE-2021-28799 or brute-force their way in by making use of commonly used administrative credentials.
"Synology strongly urges all users running vulnerable versions to update DSM immediately to protect their systems," the company said. "Synology also recommends enabling automatic updates to keep DSM up to date at all times."

articles.title: Apple's inventory surges 154% as memory chip costs climb | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Apple’s stockpiling of inventory, particularly computer memory, continued in its fiscal fourth quarter, according to earnings reported Monday. The company reported that its inventory increased significantly in the quarter, growing from $11.09 billion in Q3 to $14.54 billion in Q4, a jump of 31.1%. Year-over-year, inventory grew 154.3% from $5.72 billion in the fourth quarter of 2025.
Apple’s forecast of a 45% to 46% gross margin in the December quarter was largely attributed to the impact of higher memory costs. The company reported a gross margin of 47.9% for the September quarter.
“What we’re seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented,” said Apple CEO John Ternus, speaking to analysts on the call. “As we said earlier in the September quarter, we did see higher memory costs as compared to the June quarter, which were partly offset by the benefit of carrying inventory and lower costs on certain non-memory components.”
He said that the company expected “even higher memory costs” in the December quarter, which would be partially offset by price increases implemented earlier this year on some devices, including Mac and iPad at the end of June and iPhones in September.
Ternus also said that beyond December, Apple expects memory costs “continuing to increase.”
“As we said before, we do believe we’ll see a decreasing benefit from the carry-in inventory on memory over time,” he noted, adding that the company was increasing its purchases of this key component. “As we work to improve supply, our manufacturing purchase obligations have increased by 33 billion dollars from June to the September quarter, which you’ll see in our annual filing when it comes out tomorrow.”
Apple also brought COO Sabih Khan, who oversees the company’s supply chain and manufacturing, onto the call to address questions about memory. He reiterated the increased purchase obligations but did not rule out future price increases on Apple devices.
The company also blamed supply constraints for weak iPad sales in the quarter. The iPad was one of the only product segments that didn’t grow, even as iPhone and Mac sales beat estimates. iPad revenue was $6.2 billion, below analysts’ expectations of $6.7 billion. The figure was also down 10% from the prior year.

articles.title: Hacker drehen die Kühlung ab: Nach Frankreich trifft es jetzt auch Supermärkte in Belgien und Schweden
articles.text:
Hacker drehen die Kühlung ab: Nach Frankreich trifft es jetzt auch Supermärkte in Belgien und Schweden
Erneut haben Cyberkriminelle Kühlanlagen in europäischen Supermärkten angegriffen. Die Angreifer sorgten in Belgien und Schweden dafür, dass Kühlschränke und Tiefkühltruhen wärmer wurden, wie die Nachrichtenagenturen Belga und TT berichteten.
In Belgien sind demnach unter anderem Supermärkte von Delhaize, Carrefour und Spar betroffen. Belga berichtet unter Berufung auf den Kühltechnik-Dienstleister Sabcobel von bislang rund zwanzig betroffenen Anlagen.
Damit ist das Ausmaß in Belgien nach bisherigem Stand deutlich geringer als bei einem ähnlichen Angriff in Frankreich Mitte vergangenen Monats. Dort waren etwa 150 Geschäfte betroffen.
Nach Angaben von Sabcobel wurden die Anlagen aus der Ferne in den Abtaumodus versetzt. „Wir haben heute Nacht ab 1 Uhr damit begonnen, Techniker zu mobilisieren, um die Situation unter Kontrolle zu bringen“, sagte Sabcobel-Vorstandschef Stephan Moelans der Nachrichtenagentur Belga.
Schweden ebenfalls betroffen
Auch in Schweden meldeten Supermärkte einen plötzlichen Temperaturanstieg in den Kühlanlagen. „Uns ist bekannt, dass eine begrenzte Anzahl von Filialen in der Nacht von einem Vorfall betroffen war, der die Kühl- und Gefriersysteme der Geschäfte beeinträchtigt hat“, sagte der Pressechef der Supermarkt-Gruppe ICA der schwedischen Nachrichtenagentur TT. Um wie viele Geschäfte es sich handelt, wollte er nicht sagen.
Der Supermarkt ICA Kvantum in dem Ort Sjöbo schrieb auf Facebook, die Temperatur in den Kühl- und Gefrierschränken sei auf bis zu 50 Grad gestiegen, die Probleme seien einem Hackerangriff geschuldet. Die ICA-Gruppe bestätigte das aber nicht. Auch sechs Supermärkte der Kette Coop meldeten Probleme mit den Kühlsystemen.

articles.title: iPhone Duo pliant : quand sera-t-il de nouveau en stock ? — Frandroid
articles.text:
Si vous attendez encore la livraison de votre iPhone Duo commandé le jour de sa sortie, sachez qu’Apple est aussi frustré que vous par ces longs délais de livraison. Lors de la présentation de ses résultats trimestriels, le PDG de la firme a expliqué que des problèmes logistiques limitaient toujours les quantités de pliables disponibles à l’achat.
Dans une interview accordée à Reuters, John Ternus a expliqué que les stocks de téléphones pliables « étaient soumis à des restrictions » et qu’il était pour l’instant « impossible de prédire quand l’offre et la demande seront en équilibre ».
Apple tente de cadrer le débat
Si le nouveau patron d’Apple estime que « la montée en régime » se passe bien, les mêmes éléments de langage ont tout de même été répétés par Sabhi Kahn, directrice des opérations d’Apple, aux actionnaires de la firme. Le but est clair, cadrer les débats autour de l’iPhone Duo autour de la demande supposément « inattendue » du produit plutôt qu’autour des difficultés d’approvisionnement d’Apple.
Sabhi Kahn a tout de même reconnu que le rythme de production de la plupart des appareils Apple était ralenti par la difficulté à se procurer des processeurs dotés de « composants suffisamment avancés ». De son côté, le PDG d’Apple a réaffirmé que le coût de la mémoire continuait à augmenter de manière « inédite », même si des économies ailleurs avaient permis à la firme d’équilibrer à peu près les choses.
Sans doute que la récente polémique autour de la casse des écrans d’iPhone Duo n’a rien dû arranger, puisque Apple s’est engagé à remplacer le « petit nombre » d’appareils touchés. Pourtant, il se pourrait justement que ce soit la tentative d’Apple d’augmenter la cadence de production qui soit responsable de ses défauts de contrôle qualité.
Des résultats toujours satisfaisants
Pour le moment, les premiers créneaux de livraison pour toute nouvelle commande d’iPhone Duo se situent toujours autour de janvier 2027. Sans doute que les délais ne vont pas se contracter tout de suite. Au moins, le prix du mobile n’a pas (encore ?) augmenté.
    Pour aller plus loin
iPhone Duo : on a mesuré ses performances, sa puce A20 Pro déjoue-t-elle le piège des smartphones pliants ?
            
Malgré ces complications logistiques, la firme affiche tout de même des résultats trimestriels toujours plus élevés avec 57 milliards de chiffre d’affaires sur la vente d’iPhone. Et ce, malgré l’absence d’un modèle d’iPhone 18 « standard » attendu pour le début d’année prochaine.
