articles.title: Il avait demandé à Claude si son texte trahissait l’IA : le numéro deux de Dartmouth démissionne
articles.text:
À Dartmouth, berceau de l'IA, Santiago Schnell a démissionné après une enquête sur ses publications. Les conclusions reposent notamment sur ses échanges avec Claude, sans recours à un détecteur de textes générés par IA.
Le 9 août dernier, Santiago Schnell signait dans le Washington Post une tribune consacrée à la triche à l’intelligence artificielle dans les universités. Le 28 octobre, Dartmouth annonçait son départ, après un examen de ses propres pratiques d’écriture. Il en était le provost, numéro deux de l’établissement chargé des affaires académiques.
Une tribune sur la triche, puis les soupçons
Le paradoxe mérite une précision : Schnell ne demandait pas de bannir l’IA, mais de préserver la capacité des étudiants à exercer leur jugement. Le 26 août, une analyse de Semafor rapportait pourtant que Pangram classait sa tribune comme « 100 % IA ». Schnell contestait cette qualification, tout en reconnaissant avoir utilisé ChatGPT pour affiner certains arguments et vérifier la grammaire. Or, les conditions du Washington Post interdisaient de soumettre un contenu créé ou modifié avec l’IA.
Le journal étudiant The Dartmouth a ensuite poursuivi les vérifications. Neuf textes publiés par Schnell en 2026 obtenaient un score médian de 96 % de contenu classé comme écrit par IA. Le journal avait même testé l’e-mail dans lequel il expliquait ses pratiques : Pangram l’avait, lui aussi, classé comme « 100 % IA ». Interrogé à nouveau, Schnell avait précisé avoir rédigé un brouillon, puis repris plusieurs suggestions d’un outil d’IA pour améliorer la langue et la clarté.
Ces scores restent les classifications d’un logiciel, pas une mesure directe du travail de l’auteur. Schnell invoquait notamment les biais des détecteurs envers les personnes dont l’anglais n’est pas la langue maternelle, comme lui.
Le 25 septembre, il présentait ses excuses dans The Dartmouth, reconnaissant qu’il aurait dû déclarer systématiquement ses usages dans ses écrits publics. La présidente de Dartmouth annonçait le même jour un examen mené par un comité piloté par des enseignants. Début octobre, une pétition réclamant son départ avait recueilli plus de 220 signatures parmi les membres de la communauté universitaire.
Ce que révèlent les échanges avec Claude
Le comité a choisi de travailler sans Pangram ni aucun autre détecteur. Son rapport s’appuie notamment sur des correspondances et les historiques du compte Claude professionnel de Schnell.
Pour un article publié dans ChemSystemsChem, ces échanges montrent qu’il avait utilisé Claude pour réviser substantiellement son manuscrit, corriger du code et générer des figures. Ces usages devaient être déclarés à la revue. Ils ne l’avaient pas été lors de la soumission ni de la publication.
Un autre échange est particulièrement révélateur. Schnell avait chargé dans Claude un manuscrit encore à paraître et demandé : « Ce texte comporte-t-il beaucoup de signes d’écriture par IA ? » Il avait ensuite soumis une version intégrant le type de modifications suggérées. Lorsque l’éditeur l’avait interrogé, il avait décrit une aide éditoriale et expliqué ne pas avoir compris qu’elle devait être déclarée. Pour le comité, cette présentation minimisait ses usages réels, tels qu’ils apparaissaient dans les historiques.
Voilà ce qu’un score de détection ne permet pas de reconstituer : les demandes adressées au modèle, les réponses obtenues et leur articulation avec les explications données aux éditeurs.
L’examen reste toutefois limité. Schnell avait publié au moins 30 textes depuis son arrivée en juillet 2025 ; le comité n’en a étudié qu’une poignée. Il n’a pas pu conclure à une violation des règles pour l’un des articles cosignés. Le dossier n’établit donc pas que tous ses écrits auraient été intégralement générés par IA.
Les enquêteurs ont également jugé sa coopération insuffisante : il avait remis son ordinateur professionnel, mais pas les historiques de ses comptes personnels demandés. Ils estiment que les manquements constatés pouvaient constituer des violations des règles de Dartmouth, notamment de son code de conduite. Leur examen ne relevait cependant pas d’une procédure disciplinaire et ils ne recommandaient pas de sanction. La présidente, Sian Leah Beilock, présente le départ comme une décision de Schnell.
L’affaire prend une résonance particulière dans cet établissement. C’est sur ce même campus qu’en 1956 s’est tenu l’atelier considéré comme l’acte de naissance de l’intelligence artificielle comme discipline scientifique. Soixante-dix ans plus tard, Dartmouth annonçait la démission de son responsable académique à la veille d’une conférence anniversaire. Elle s’ouvrait le 29 octobre autour d’une question : ce qui doit rester humain.
- Excellente compréhension des consignes complexes
- Très bon niveau en rédaction
- Analyse de longs documents efficace

articles.title: Le singles Day 2026 a de l'avance : les offres du Black Friday chinois sont déjà là
articles.text:
Le Singles Day, ou « Double 11 », porte de moins en moins bien son nom. Historiquement associé au 11 novembre, le « Black Friday chinois » s’étale cette année du 1er au 18 novembre sur AliExpress. Les promotions sont donc déjà accessibles, près de quatre semaines avant le Black Friday du vendredi 27 novembre.
À l’origine, le 11 novembre célèbre les célibataires en Chine. Alibaba, maison mère d’AliExpress, en a fait un événement commercial en 2009 sur sa plateforme Taobao Mall (devenue Tmall), avec seulement 27 marchands la première année. C’est devenu depuis l’un des plus gros événements d’achat en ligne au monde. Pour les acheteurs français, c’est aussi l’occasion de trouver des smartphones, des tablettes ou des accessoires à prix réduit sur AliExpress. On a fait le tri à votre place dans le grand catalogue.
Les meilleures promotions du Singles Day à ne pas rater
Tineco Floor ONE S6 Stretch Lite
Le Tineco Floor ONE S6 Stretch Lite est un aspirateur laveur sans fil qui aspire et nettoie les sols en un seul passage. Son prix passe à 147,06 € au lieu de 171,06 € avec le code promo 11FR24. Il peut s’incliner à 180° pour se glisser sous les meubles et les canapés, tout en conservant une aspiration efficace. Son capteur intelligent iLoop adapte automatiquement le nettoyage au niveau de saleté détecté.
Avec jusqu’à 40 minutes d’autonomie, deux réservoirs séparés pour l’eau propre et l’eau sale et une fonction d’autonettoyage automatique, il permet de nettoyer facilement toute la maison.
Console portable AYN Thor
L’AYN Thor est une console portable Android qui reprend le concept à clapet de la Nintendo DS, mais avec une fiche technique nettement plus ambitieuse. Son prix passe à 349,86 € au lieu de 409,86 € pour le Single Day, avec le code 11FR60. Elle embarque deux écrans AMOLED tactiles : une dalle principale de 6 pouces en Full HD à 120 Hz et un écran secondaire de 3,92 pouces à 60 Hz. La console embarque un Snapdragon 8 Gen 2.
L’AYN Thor est particulièrement intéressante pour les amateurs de rétrogaming et d’émulation. Elle peut également diffuser son image sur un téléviseur ou un moniteur externe.
Nothing Phone ( 3a ) Pro
Le Nothing Phone (3a) Pro est proposé pour les Single Days au prix de 255,09 € au lieu de 295,09 €, avec le code 11FR40. Le smartphone se distingue par son design transparent et son interface lumineuse Glyph, mais aussi par ses capacités photo. Il embarque trois capteurs arrière, dont un téléobjectif périscopique de 50 mégapixels avec zoom optique 3x. Son écran AMOLED de 6,77 pouces à 120 Hz, son processeur Snapdragon 7s Gen 3 et ses 12 Go de RAM lui assurent également une belle polyvalence au quotidien.
Avec sa batterie de 5 000 mAh et sa recharge rapide de 50 W, il constitue un smartphone équilibré, aussi à l’aise pour le multimédia que pour la photographie.
Nintendo Switch OLED
La Nintendo Switch OLED reste une excellente console pour profiter du catalogue de la première Switch, et cette offre AliExpress la rend particulièrement intéressante, à 229,96 € au lieu de 269,96 €, avec le code 11FR40. Son écran OLED de 7 pouces constitue son principal atout : les couleurs sont éclatantes, les contrastes profonds et les noirs parfaitement maîtrisés. Elle dispose également de 64 Go de stockage.
Une console hybride qui conserve tout son intérêt pour jouer à Mario, Zelda ou Pokémon aussi bien dans son canapé que dans les transports, et qui peut être un en excellent premier modèle pour un enfant qui souhaite disposer d’un catalogue de jeu complet sans vouloir les dernières nouveautés.
Honor Watch 6
La HONOR Watch 6 est une montre connectée qui mise sur un design élégant, un écran particulièrement lumineux et une autonomie généreuse, et passe au prix de 82,68 € au lieu de 95,68 €, avec le code 11FR13. Elle embarque une dalle AMOLED de 1,46 pouce affichant une définition de 464 × 464 pixels, avec une luminosité maximale de 3 000 nits pour rester lisible même en plein soleil.
Elle propose également plus de 120 modes sportifs, dont des profils dédiés au football et au badminton, ainsi qu’un suivi de la fréquence cardiaque, du sommeil, du stress et de l’oxygénation sanguine. Son GPS double fréquence permet aussi d’enregistrer ses déplacements sans avoir systématiquement besoin de son smartphone, ainsi qu’une autonomie de 17 jours en utilisation classique.
Xiaomi Poco X8 Pro Max
Le Poco X8 Pro Max 5G de Xiaomi a tout d’un smartphone haut de gamme, avec une fiche technique qui mise autant sur la puissance que sur l’autonomie. Son prix passe à 339,64 € au lieu de 399,64 €, avec le code promo 11FR60. Son processeur MediaTek Dimensity 9500s gravé en 3 nm lui permet de faire tourner les applications exigeantes et les jeux mobiles dans d’excellentes conditions.
Il embarque également un grand écran AMOLED de 6,83 pouces, avec une définition 1,5K et un taux de rafraîchissement de 120 Hz, et un appareil photo principal de 50 mégapixels avec stabilisation optique. Mais son principal argument reste sa batterie de 8 500 mAh, compatible avec la charge rapide 100 W. De quoi envisager sereinement de longues journées d’utilisation.
Nintendo Switch 2 Pro
Pour les longues sessions sur Switch 2, la manette Pro reste le choix du confort. Avec ses poignées pleines et ses deux palettes arrière programmables, elle offre une prise en main bien plus naturelle que les Joy-Con. Elle a aussi une prise casque 3,5 mm, que les Joy-Con n’ont pas, et un bouton C pour lancer le GameChat sans fouiller dans les menus. Elle tombe à 53,96 € au lieu de 79,99 € sur AliExpress avec le code 11FR08, à entrer au paiement.
JOYOR Y8-S
Joyor ne bénéficie pas de la notoriété de Xiaomi ou de Segway, mais ce spécialiste de la trottinette électrique existe depuis 2014. Avec la Y8-S, la marque mise surtout sur une grosse batterie de 48 V et 26 Ah, associée à un moteur de 500 W. Elle annonce jusqu’à 100 km d’autonomie, un chiffre constructeur à relativiser selon votre poids, le relief et la vitesse. La Joyor Y8-S revient à 323,24 € sur AliExpress avec le code 11FR60 à saisir au panier.
Ses pneus de 10 pouces, ses suspensions et ses freins à disque avant et arrière complètent un équipement intéressant à ce tarif. La contrepartie, c’est son poids d’environ 25 kg : mieux vaut avoir un endroit accessible pour la ranger plutôt que plusieurs étages à monter chaque soir. Elle conviendra davantage aux trajets effectués entièrement en trottinette qu’aux déplacements combinant métro et escaliers.
Zendure 1600W
Vos panneaux solaires produisent surtout quand vous n’êtes pas là ? Le Zendure SolarFlow 1600 AC+ stocke ce surplus dans sa batterie de 1,92 kWh pour vous le restituer le soir, au lieu de le laisser filer sur le réseau. Il suffit de le brancher sur une prise, et il s’adapte à n’importe quelle installation existante. Il est disponible à 457,98 € sur AliExpress avec le code FRD1180, bien en dessous des 719 € affichés par Zendure.
La capacité peut grimper jusqu’à 11,52 kWh, mais en ajoutant des batteries vendues à part. La puissance de 1 600 W ne se débloque elle aussi qu’avec une extension : seule, la batterie restitue 800 W, ce qui suffit pour l’essentiel de la consommation de fond d’un logement.
Shokz OpenRun Pro 2
Les Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 sont des écouteurs à conduction osseuse conçus pour le sport : ils laissent les oreilles libres, ce qui permet d’entendre son environnement tout en écoutant de la musique ou un podcast.. Sur Aliexpress, ils sont disponibles à 77,56 € au lieu de 199,99 €, livraison gratuite en France incluse.
La réduction de 13 € est appliquée directement au moment du paiement sur Aliexpress. À ce prix, l’offre s’adresse en priorité aux coureurs et cyclistes qui ne veulent pas se couper du monde extérieur pendant l’effort.
Singles Day 2026 : tout ce qu’il faut savoir
Le Singles Day, surnommé « Black Friday chinois », tombe le mercredi 11 novembre 2026. Mais il est aussi précoce que son cousin américain : chez AliExpress, les promotions s’étendent du 1er au 18 novembre.
Quels sites participent au Singles Day ?
AliExpress reste le principal rendez-vous de cette opération. D’autres marques organisent leurs propres promotions, comme Lenovo, qui annonce une édition 2026 sur ses ordinateurs et accessoires. Les dates et les conditions varient selon les enseignes.
Les codes promo AliExpress du Singles Day 2026

Y a-t-il des frais de douane ?
Pour un produit déjà stocké et dédouané dans l’Union européenne, il n’y a en principe pas de frais d’importation à régler à la livraison. En revanche, les règles ont changé en 2026 pour les commandes expédiées directement depuis la Chine :

Ces montants peuvent être intégrés au prix payé à la commande. Vérifiez les conditions du vendeur pour savoir si les droits et taxes sont compris et si des frais restent à régler à la livraison.$
Les produits fonctionnent-ils en France ?
Les mentions Global, EU ou HK demandent de regarder la référence exacte du produit. Pour un smartphone, vérifiez notamment les réseaux mobiles compatibles et les langues disponibles. Regardez aussi le format de la prise, les accessoires fournis et les conditions de garantie.
Les offres retenues pour ce live concernent des produits utilisables en France. Lorsqu’une version importée nécessite une manipulation particulière ou présente une restriction, nous le précisons dans le bon plan.

articles.title: NTT DATA explores expansion in Mangaluru and Udupi, meets Priyank Kharge
articles.text:
NTT DATA explores expansion in Mangaluru and Udupi, meets Priyank Kharge
NTT DATA is exploring expansion in Mangaluru and Udupi, with IT Minister Priyank Kharge discussing opportunities in data centres, cloud services, digital infrastructure, biotechnology and startup collaboration.
Karnataka wants its next wave of technology investments to reach beyond Bengaluru, and global IT companies are being encouraged to look towards its coastal cities.
NTT DATA is exploring plans to expand its operations in Karnataka, with Mangaluru and Udupi emerging as potential areas of focus. The company shared its expansion plans during discussions with Karnataka IT, BT and Rural Development Minister Priyank Kharge on November 2, 2026.
The discussions covered new areas of collaboration, technology investments and opportunities to strengthen the company's presence in the state. NTT DATA, which recently acquired Karnataka-based Niveus Solutions and WinWire, cited the availability of skilled talent as a key advantage in expanding its operations, particularly along the coast.
Beyond Bengaluru takes centre stage
Priyank Kharge highlighted the state's Beyond Bengaluru programme, which aims to develop technology ecosystems across Karnataka by extending investments, infrastructure and employment opportunities to emerging technology clusters.
“Through our Beyond Bengaluru programme, we are building strong regional technology ecosystems by investing in skilling, infrastructure and progressive policies. Our focus is on taking investments and opportunities to where the talent is,” he said.
He added that the government wanted to work closely with industry to develop solutions that could accelerate growth across Karnataka's emerging technology hubs.
Data centres, cloud and digital infrastructure on the agenda
The meeting also explored opportunities under Karnataka's Sustainable Data Centre Policy and potential collaboration with NTT DATA across data centres, cloud services and digital infrastructure.
Moreover, Kharge outlined plans for a cable landing station in Mangaluru, which is expected to strengthen the state's digital infrastructure, and discussed how NTT DATA's expertise could support the project.
The minister also encouraged the company to explore opportunities beyond cloud services in sectors such as biotechnology, healthcare, life sciences and automotive manufacturing. These areas align with Karnataka's existing industrial and research ecosystem.
Startup collaboration and new technology opportunities
Startup incubation and innovation were also part of the discussions. Priyank Kharge also mentioned the recently launched Government First programme, which allows startups to pilot their solutions with public sector departments.
He invited NTT DATA to partner with the initiative and contribute to Karnataka's startup ecosystem.
The meeting was attended by senior government officials, including Dr N. Manjula, Secretary, Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T; Dr Avinash Menon Rajendran, IAS, Director, Department of Electronics, IT and BT and Managing Director of Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS); and Sanjeev Gupta, CEO of KDEM.
NTT DATA was represented by Charlie Li, President and Global Head of Cloud, AI and Security; Ayman Husain, Worldwide Managing Director and VP, Google Business Unit; and Shashir Shetty, Chief Growth Officer.
With Mangaluru and Udupi being discussed as potential expansion destinations, Karnataka is looking to extend its technology footprint beyond Bengaluru and bring more specialised technology investments to its coastal region.

articles.title: Chinese hackers use ARTEX AI in automated attacks against 200 orgs
articles.text:
Chinese hackers used ARTEX, an open-source, multi-agent AI penetration-testing framework, in attacks against more than 200 organizations across 14 countries.
The operation began on October 17 and targeted government ministries, telecommunications providers, and organizations in the pharmaceutical, semiconductor, defense, nuclear, and financial sectors.
The threat actor compromised at least nine organizations and carried out password spraying attacks and credential scanning activity against at least 12 other high-value targets.
According to researchers at CrowdStrike, the "campaign marks an escalation in China-nexus use of AI agents, from single intrusions to multiple simultaneous engagements directed by a human operator."
Confirmed victims include telecommunications providers in the United States and Belgium, government organizations in Greece, the Middle East, and Latin America, and pharmaceutical firms in the U.S.
The researchers track the threat actor as Vapor Panda and say that in the attack against the Greek government entity, the AI agents forged an administrator token and read mailboxes by leveraging authentication keys from a 2022 mail-server directory export.
ARTEX AI is a penetration testing suite developed by Chinese developers and initially released as an open-source project. However, its creators later made it proprietary after it was used in real-world attacks, including a campaign against South Korean financial institutions.
In its most recent cyberespionage operation, Vapor Panda also used DeepSeek and a second, unidentified commercial language model to coordinate planning and worker agents across multiple intrusions simultaneously.
CrowdStrike says the attackers issued instructions in Chinese and intervened at critical points where decisions needed to be made.
The AI agents performed reconnaissance, exploited vulnerabilities, deployed web shells, obtained credentials, and pursued alternative attack paths when needed.
The operators explicitly instructed the agents to skip Windows machines protected by Falcon, CrowdStrike's solution for endpoint protection, and focused on unprotected hosts.
In one intrusion, the AI agents consumed more than 1.4 billion input tokens, the researchers believe.
CrowdStrike also found that the threat actor deployed BLOODALCHEMY, a backdoor active since 2023, against government entities in Latin America and the Middle East.
More ARTEX AI cases emerge
The Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure (DIVD) has shared more details about the cyberattack it suffered in September 2026, which it attributed to an AI agent.
According to its latest update, the tool used in the attack on its network was ARTEX AI, which acted autonomously.
DIVD explained in a post on LinkedIn that the attack went from initial access to root privileges in 12 minutes, chaining a Zammad zero-day with a second zero-day for local privilege escalation.
The agent performed numerous tasks simultaneously, including reading a compromised mailbox, scanning the internal network, extracting login tokens, and attempting password resets.
DIVD recorded over 450,000 requests and 2,500 scripts connected to the attack, describing the activity as “super loud and messy.”

articles.title: Juan Castro, electricista: “La IA hará que los electricistas y el sector oficio seamos los mejor pagados”
articles.text:
Para Juan Castro, la IA es una buena oportunidad. En el vídeo que publicó, señala que los oficios van a ser de los trabajos mejor pagados. Según cuenta, tiene más trabajo del que puede hacer y hay demanda de profesionales cualificados.
En la descripción de YouTube agrega otros aspectos. La IA puede ayudar a diagnosticar problemas y a realizar los cálculos de instalación. Además, pueden ahorrarse tiempo en presupuestos. Por eso propone unir lo propio con las herramientas de IA. De esta forma puede hacer más trabajos y mejorar lo que cobra.
“La IA no nos quita el trabajo”, escribe. En el vídeo menciona las oportunidades que ve en la IA para electricistas y fontaneros según el consejero delegado de NVIDIA, Jensen Huang. También anima a que se formen en oficios técnicos. Incluso dice que se puede llegar a ganar más de 2.000 euros (¿brutos? ¿netos?) después de unos meses de formación, sin concretar el periodo al que se refiere. Se puede solicitar información de formación.
Porque tiene algo de presencial. Lo explica en una entrevista del 10 de junio de 2026. “Si se va la luz en una vivienda, alguien tiene que ir físicamente”; aunque reconoce que la IA puede usarse en aspectos administrativos y de gestión, subraya que hay que aprender en obra y que además se debe seguir formando al cambiar las instalaciones.
También hay una conexión física con la IA en la demanda de estos profesionales. Google ha anunciado que va a apoyar un programa de formación para 100.000 trabajadores eléctricos y 30.000 nuevos aprendices en Estados Unidos. La empresa lo conecta con las necesidades de infraestructuras eléctricas de la IA (y de la industria avanzada y de la energía limpia). No es un programa de contratación, sino de formación.
Las ofertas de electricista en España
En el mercado español encontramos datos que muestran esta falta. En el análisis de InfoJobs de abril de 2026 (con datos de 2025) se muestran 8.179 vacantes de electricista. Con 31 candidatos por vacante (la media en la plataforma es de 56). En total, en el subsector de electricidad (hay más perfiles), se publicaron 29.847 vacantes.
Esto muestra que hay menos competencia que en la media de InfoJobs. No están diciendo que sigan estando vacantes, ni tampoco podemos saber cuál será el salario de quien empieza. Yaiza Canosa también hablaba de las oportunidades de los fontaneros frente a las de los desarrolladores.
Castro habla de una formación corta, pero hay que ver qué certifica. En el Reglamento electrotécnico para baja tensión (instrucción ITC-BT-03) se indica que para desarrollar la actividad es necesario estar en una empresa instaladora habilitada. Además, hay que demostrar alguna de las siguientes vías de cualificación: titulaciones con competencias adecuadas; experiencia profesional reconocida; certificación por una entidad acreditada… La duración de un curso no garantiza esto.
Ahorrar tiempo no garantiza un sueldo mayor
También hay que diferenciar entre cambio de tareas y eliminación de puesto. Por ejemplo, en el índice de exposición de 2025 de la Organización Internacional del Trabajo (OIT) y NASK se estima que uno de cada cuatro trabajadores del mundo tiene una ocupación expuesta (en mayor o menor medida) a la IA generativa. Todavía siguen siendo las ocupaciones administrativas las más expuestas. Los autores consideran que es más probable que haya un cambio de los empleos (no sustitución total), pues hay muchas tareas que necesitan humanos.
El hecho de ahorrar tiempo y cómo afecta al sueldo es algo que todavía no está resuelto en la previsión de Castro. En una revisión de la evidencia de la OIT (publicada el 1 de junio de 2026) se encontró que había ganancias de productividad asimétricas. Los ahorros de tiempo que declaraban los trabajadores todavía no se han visto en mayores ingresos medidos. No es un estudio específico de electricistas; por ello no puede asumirse que automáticamente podrá aumentar el número de encargos (con ayuda de IA) y pasar a ser uno de los mejores pagados. Hay que demostrarlo.

articles.title: iPhone Air 2 : face aux critiques, Apple préparerait ces 3 changements
articles.text:
Après le lancement de l’iPhone 18 Pro et de l’iPhone Duo, les projecteurs se tournent vers les futurs smartphones de la marque, dont l’iPhone Air 2. Selon des informations partagées par le leaker Digital Chat Station, le smartphone ultra-fin d’Apple pourrait corriger les principaux défauts de la première génération.
Plus de puissance et plus de finesse
L’iPhone Air 2 intégrerait une puce Apple A20 gravée en 2 nm, soit la même que celle inaugurée sur l’iPhone 18 Pro et l’iPhone Duo. Ce serait un bond en avant notable par rapport au processeur A19 Pro gravé en 3 nm du modèle précédent. On peut ainsi s’attendre à plus de puissance, mais aussi à une meilleure efficience énergétique.
Côté design, l’appareil continuerait sa cure de minceur en perdant quelques millimètres. Alors que la première génération affiche une épaisseur de 5,6 mm, l’iPhone Air 2 descendrait à 5,2 mm. D’autres changements internes sont attendus, comme l’arrivée de la puce sans fil N2 et du modem C2. Côté écran, on retrouverait une dalle OLED plate de 6,55 pouces avec un taux de rafraîchissement de 120 Hz.
Un second module caméra et une batterie plus grande
Le premier iPhone Air n’est pas donné et son unique module caméra de 48 mégapixels fait clairement partie des points faibles que nous avons soulevés dans notre test. Mais les dernières indiscrétions laissent entendre qu’Apple en est conscient et pourrait ainsi doter son iPhone Air 2 d’un second module de 48 mégapixels : un ultra-grand-angle, qui viendrait accompagner le grand-angle.
L’autonomie est également un défaut important du premier iPhone Air. Il faut dire qu’avec une batterie de 3 149 mAh, il ne fallait pas s’attendre à des miracles. Pour sa deuxième génération de téléphone ultra-fin, Apple pourrait intégrer une batterie autour des 3 500 mAh. Ajoutez à cela une puce A20 moins énergivore, et l’iPhone Air 2 devrait offrir une autonomie plus confortable que son aîné. L’une des grandes inconnues reste l’arrivée ou non d’un second haut-parleur. Le son mono du premier modèle faisait également partie des défauts remontés par les utilisateurs sur cette première génération.

articles.title: Obiex says Nigeria's stablecoin market needs bigger players
articles.text:
Obiex says Nigeria’s stablecoin market is far more efficient than it was in 2018 and 2019, when the gap between buying and selling a dollar of crypto in naira ran as wide as ₦20 to ₦30. Demand has scaled since, but the supply behind it is still spread across many small sellers.
That’s the current state of Nigeria’s stablecoin market, according to Temitayo Sadique, managing director of Obiex Business, the business arm of Nigerian crypto exchange Obiex.
“Because of the exceptional need for stablecoins from cross-border trade and remittances, and crypto exchanges cropping up every day, we’ve seen demand scale,” Sadique said at Moonshot by TechCabal. “But supply, on the other hand, has remained scattered.”
Sadique said $19 billion in stablecoins came into Nigeria in 2025. The country has taken about 60% of sub-Saharan Africa’s stablecoin inflows since 2019, according to a June report by the International Monetary Fund.
Scattered supply makes that volume expensive to move. A company filling a $1 million order might deal with 10 peer-to-peer (P2P) traders, Sadique said, each selling a slice at a slightly higher rate: ₦1,400 per dollar, then ₦1,402, then ₦1,403. By the end, its average price is worse than the first quote. As volumes grow, he argued, platforms that can fill large orders at one price will set the terms for everyone else.
Obiex has built its business on that bet. It began in 2016 as Paylot, a crypto payment gateway, before shifting to converting crypto into naira when it saw that was what users wanted. It has never raised venture funding.
Sadique said 105,000 merchants in Nigeria, Ghana and Cameroon now trade on Obiex, alongside more than 100 businesses, from exchanges and remittance companies to fintechs. By his count, $1 of every $10 in stablecoins that moved through Nigeria last year went through Obiex.
For Sadique, liquidity means delivering money on time. Promising someone $100 next week means little if the money isn’t there when the week comes, he said. “It’s kind of like a supply-chain question, where you’re answering: can I fulfil this obligation now, when the customer needs it?” Obiex’s answer includes credit that lets clients take liquidity today and settle tomorrow, and price locks while crypto deposits are still confirming.
For large trades, Obiex offers a quote system that fixes the rate on orders of $1 million to $10 million. “We don’t just give you an average price to execute your transaction; we give you a quote and lock in that price for you,” Sadique said.
Regulation is already pushing the market toward bigger players. Since January, Nigeria’s Securities and Exchange Commission has required crypto exchanges and custodians to hold ₦2 billion in minimum capital, up from ₦500 million, a bar many smaller platforms will struggle to clear.
In Sadique’s view, an efficient stablecoin market is one where a $1 million order clears at a single price, and that depends on who can supply liquidity when it is needed.

articles.title: Un fondo respaldado por OpenAI comprará ADT, la empresa de alarmas, por USD 15.300 millones
articles.text:
Thrive Holdings, un fondo de inversión respaldado por OpenAI, acordó comprar ADT, una de las mayores empresas de alarmas y cámaras de seguridad para hogares y pequeños negocios de Estados Unidos. El acuerdo, anunciado el 29 de octubre, valora a la compañía en USD 15.300 millones, incluida su deuda.
ADT recibirá USD 10 en efectivo por cada acción, lo que implica un valor de unos USD 7.600 millones para sus accionistas. Esa cifra supera en 45,6% el precio de cierre del 27 de octubre, de USD 6,87, y en 52,1% el promedio de los 30 días previos, según el comunicado de la empresa.
Cuando se cierre la operación, ADT dejará de cotizar en la bolsa de Nueva York y pasará a ser una empresa privada. El directorio aprobó el acuerdo por unanimidad. La compañía emplea a más de 12.000 personas, según su director ejecutivo, Jim DeVries.
El financiamiento viene de fondos administrados por filiales de Apollo Global Management, que fue dueña y vendió su participación restante hace cinco meses, según informó Axios. Es la segunda vez en una década que pasa a manos privadas, tras la compra de Apollo en 2016 y el regreso a la bolsa en 2018.
Un fondo que compra empresas tradicionales para aplicarles IA
Thrive Holdings nació el año pasado como un derivado de Thrive Capital, la firma de capital de riesgo de Josh Kushner, hermano de Jared Kushner, yerno del presidente Donald Trump, según recordó The Verge. Hoy controla más de 75 negocios de contabilidad, servicios informáticos y construcción, y la empresa de seguridad será la base de su área de seguridad del hogar.
OpenAI participa como socio e inversor del fondo, de acuerdo con TechCrunch. La empresa de ChatGPT aporta modelos de IA y también ingenieros que trabajan dentro de las compañías del grupo para rediseñar sus procesos.
Ni ADT ni Thrive Holdings dijeron qué productos nuevos con IA lanzarán. El socio de Thrive Holdings Kareem Zaki afirmó que el fondo aspira a que los equipos de ADT atiendan mejor a los clientes y entreguen más información útil a los profesionales que acuden a las emergencias.
La empresa vende sistemas de alarma, cámaras y dispositivos para el hogar conectado, y cobra suscripciones mensuales por el monitoreo. Sus técnicos también instalan dispositivos de Google Nest y de la nueva línea de hogar inteligente de Apple, alianzas que TechCrunch afirma que mantendrá.
Los datos de los clientes, el punto sensible
Un negocio de seguridad doméstica concentra información delicada: direcciones, horarios, imágenes de cámaras y contactos de emergencia. El comunicado de ambas empresas afirma que las políticas de datos y privacidad de ADT seguirán sin cambios y que no se compartirá información nueva sin permiso del cliente.
Anuj Mehndiratta, también socio de Thrive Holdings, dijo que el fondo está comprometido con los más altos estándares de privacidad y ciberseguridad. El comunicado no detalla cómo se aplicará esa promesa cuando los ingenieros de Thrive y de OpenAI empiecen a trabajar con los sistemas.
El acuerdo todavía no es definitivo. Necesita la aprobación de los accionistas de ADT y de las autoridades antimonopolio de Estados Unidos, y la empresa prevé cerrarlo en el primer trimestre de 2027. Hasta entonces, seguirá operando por su cuenta.
La compañía publicará sus resultados del tercer trimestre el 3 de noviembre antes de la apertura del mercado. La empresa dijo que, por el acuerdo, no responderá preguntas durante la conferencia con analistas posterior.

articles.title: Sam Altman, CEO de ChatGPT: "Es bastante terrible que la gente tenga memoria RAM en su PC utilizándose sólo el 5 % del tiempo"
articles.text:
John Collison es el cofundador de la plataforma Stripe y tiene un podcast llamado Cheeky Pint en el que altos mandos de empresas tecnológicas pasan a hablar de sus cosas. Un ejemplo reciente es el de Susan Li, CFO de Meta. Sam Altman, por su parte, no necesita presentación, y hace unos días pasó por el programa de Collison para hablar de varios temas. Entre ellos, uno que parece quitarle el sueño: que cada usuario pueda montar una IA local.
Apunta a un desperdicio de recursos, pero de fondo está el meme de "que me quedo sin comer".
En corto. En el podcast hablaron de varios temas, pero lo que no ha pasado desapercibido en las redes es el comentario del mandamás de OpenAI sobre la actualidad tecnológica en la que hay usuarios tomando modelos abiertos y ejecutándolos en su propio hardware sin depender de la nube de nadie más. Para Altman, la inferencia local es un terrible desperdicio de un recurso tan escaso como la memoria DRAM:
"La inferencia local es una terrible asignación de recursos escasos. Mucha gente quiere inferencia local y, de algún modo, asume que el problema está resuelto porque tenemos modelos de código abierto que podemos ejecutar en nuestros ordenadores y, así, no necesitar todas esas cosas que permiten los centros de datos.
Pero, desde una perspectiva de asignación global, en realidad es bastante terrible que todo el mundo tenga su propio ordenador con una DRAM que se utiliza apenas el 5% del tiempo cuando estamos en un momento en el que éste es un recurso tan limitado.
En ese entorno en el que ese suministro crítico es tan restringido, quieres la máxima concentración en la nube. Pero, de algún modo, la idea de la gente es la contraria."
Long story short: si tienes una IA local, estás desperdiciando recursos que podrían haber ido para alimentar un centro de datos, según Altman.
Lo de la DRAM. La cifra del 5% es de Altman y por eso estima que es un desperdicio que cada uno tenga algo así en su casa cuando, en un entorno con tan poca oferta, lo que se busca es la máxima utilización que sólo se consigue en un centro de datos. Claro, esa es su perspectiva, ya que en la otra cara de la moneda está esa gente que tiene su "propia IA" gracias a que los modelos abiertos ya resuelven el problema que quieren resolver y, además, buscan una mayor privacidad que la que se consigue usando ChatGPT.
Desde el punto de vista del CEO de OpenAI, esta afirmación tiene todo el sentido debido a que (y esto es algo que nos afecta a todos y, en especial, a los consumidores) en un entorno en el que Micron, Samsung o SK Hynix, que son los que controlan la producción de DRAM a nivel global no pueden aumentar esa producción al ritmo que los hiperescaladores necesitan, toda la capacidad mundial debería ir en estos momentos a los centros de datos, y no a los equipos caseros.
Nadie lo habría adivinado hace cinco años cuando los precios estaban por los suelos, pero la DRAM es un bien crítico y escaso en estos momentos, con precios que, según TrendForce, aumentaron entre un 90% y un 95% en el primer trimestre de 2026... y nada apunta a que vayan a caer a corto plazo. Más bien lo contrario.
Contexto. Y ese comentario llegó en un punto de la conversación en la que se trataba la escasez de cómputo. Altman sostiene que el mercado no está respondiendo como debería y que los grandes fabricantes de memoria están, pese a los tremendos beneficios que han conseguido estos últimos doce meses, manteniendo una inversión conservadora en relación con lo que la situación requiere.
Las tres grandes se han movido para habilitar nuevas plantas de producción, incluso limitando la producción de chips de consumo para que toda la maquinaria se ponga con la memoria HBM necesaria para los centros de datos, pero precisamente este es un segmento en el que no es fácil cambiar las cosas de la noche a la mañana y abrir nuevas plantas de memoria de alto rendimiento.
Que se lo digan a China, que lleva meses postulándose como una opción en el segmento de la DRAM, pero que de momento más que para HBM, están posicionados en el de la memoria de consumo debido a esas exigencias en los chips de vanguardia que comentaba hace un momento.
Solución. Aparte de que seas generoso y no compres componentes que podría usar OpenAI, Altman plantea como remedio que nuevos actores entren en la cadena de suministro.
Por ejemplo, OpenAI está desarrollando chips propios de la mano de Broadcom (Jalapeño) y, aunque seguirían necesitando DRAM, fabricar un chip a su medida permite optimizar todo mucho más. SpaceX está en las mismas, al igual que Amazon, Meta, Microsoft o una Google que tiene algo más de experiencia con sus TPU.
Nicho. Pese a todo, OpenAI lanzó en agosto de 2025 gpt-oss, sus primeros pesos abiertos desde GPT-2 pensados para poder ejecutarse en local y el propio Altman dijo en enero de ese año que OpenAI había estado equivocado respecto al código abierto. Claro, a comienzos de 2025 no estaba la crisis actual de la DRAM,.
Al final, mi duda aquí es si tan grande considera Altman que es el segmento de usuarios que usan una IA local y si tanto daño realmente hacen a la cadena de suministro cuando estamos viendo que la gente no paga por la IA porque lo que se ofrece "gratuitamente" ya cumple las necesidades que se puedan tener.
Quien tenga una máquina capaz de correr un modelo local sabe perfectamente por qué lo hace y puede ser por unas necesidades específicas, por poder usarlo sin conexión o, simplemente, porque no se fía de la seguridad de una empresa como OpenAI.

articles.title: Apple is warning iPhone users in 110 countries about mercenary spyware
articles.text:
What we know so far: Apple has issued high-priority threat notifications to iPhone users in 110 countries, warning them that they may have been targeted by sophisticated mercenary spyware. The company did not disclose details about the threat itself or the individuals suspected of being behind the attacks. However, it recommended several steps users can take to help protect their data and devices.
The spyware attacks were first reported on October 30 by cybersecurity researcher Costin Raiu, who noted that they were unrelated to the previous round of incidents, for which Apple issued alerts in August. According to Raiu, iPhone users in 99 countries, including several prominent journalists and documentary filmmakers, are among those who received the notifications.
On October 31, Apple confirmed that it had sent high-confidence threat notifications to select users in 110 countries worldwide, warning them that they may have been targeted by mercenary spyware. The company did not confirm whether any devices or accounts had been compromised, nor did it publicly identify the threat actors, attack vector, or software vulnerability associated with the incident.
While Apple has remained tight-lipped about the details, it has confirmed that the attacks are not broad phishing scams affecting millions of people but highly targeted attempts to exfiltrate data from specific individuals. Apple did not identify the victims, but mercenary spyware is known to target journalists, activists, politicians, and diplomats.
Targeted attacks are designed to compromise devices without requiring victims to download a file or even click an external link. When successful, these attacks can give threat actors deep access to victims' devices, potentially allowing them to retrieve private information such as call logs, messages, contact lists, location data, and media files.
 – Costin Raiu (@craiu) October 30, 2026
According to Apple's threat notification guidance, zero-click exploits and other types of mercenary spyware attacks are expensive, often costing millions of dollars. The company notes that the high costs and technical complexity involved in carrying out these attacks mean that only extremely well-funded operations can deploy them effectively.
Apple also noted that the short lifespan of targeted mercenary spyware attacks makes them difficult to detect and prevent. The company says the only way to learn more about the threat actors' modus operandi is through internal threat intelligence. It added that it typically withholds technical details about its detection methods to prevent attackers from learning how to circumvent its detection and remediation measures.
Apple advises users who may be facing a targeted cyberattack to enable Lockdown Mode. The feature is designed to protect iPhone users against sophisticated cybersecurity threats by limiting access to features that attackers could exploit. It can be found under Settings > Privacy & Security on supported iPhones. Apple also recommends keeping devices up to date to ensure they receive the latest security patches.

articles.title: On theCUBE Pod: AI bubble lets out some air - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
On theCUBE Pod: Stock market gets the jitters and Anthropic files IPO
The hubbub at the New York Stock Exchange was audible on theCUBE Pod last Friday, with concerns rising over the artificial intelligence bubble.
Several tech companies, including Intel Corp., Alphabet Inc., Amazon.com Inc., CoreWeave Inc. and Fortinet Inc., saw their stock fall, suggesting that investors may have doubts about all that AI infrastructure spending. At the same time, Anthropic PBC filed for an initial public offering with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, which looks to be a grand debut for one of the biggest AI developers out there (despite the company still not turning a profit).
Also causing a stir is the announcement that NYSE parent company, Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), will partner with Trade[XYZ] to bring perpetual futures markets built on cryptocurrency trading platform, Hyperliquid, to the U.S., subject to regulatory approval.
“The whole idea of exchange is going to change,” said John Furrier (pictured, left), executive analyst at theCUBE Research. “It reminds me of cloud computing, how it re-leveled the data center. NYSE is the cathedral of capitalism. Nasdaq started as an over-the-counter bulletin board. Tech was early there and then only listed there. But now the game has changed. It’s very interesting to see how the competition between the NYSE and the Nasdaq is going to play out.”
On the latest episode of theCUBE Pod, Furrier and Dave Vellante (right), chief analyst at theCUBE Research, discussed what Anthropic’s IPO and Friday’s stock market jitters suggest about a potential AI bubble. They also explored Intel’s missteps and the opportunity for full-stack infrastructure companies.
AI bubble releases some air
Last week, Alphabet’s stock fell more than 12% after it reported slower growth in search revenue, presumably because chatbots are drawing people away from the browser. Amazon also had a disappointing Friday, with its stock falling 7% as the company continues to dump money into an AI infrastructure buildout.
Despite investors’ concerns, Vellante sees the AI bubble letting out a little air. He views this as a healthy sign for the AI market’s future.
“Think of the tulip bubbles in the 1600s,” Vellante said. “Think about the Japanese real estate bubble in the 1980s. And you think about the dot-com. That dot-com was actually different. Dot-com, they were all … overhyped. They drove massive valuations. But the dot-com actually played out. It actually exceeded expectations. And I think there’s some things that we can learn from there.”
Furrier sees evidence for a positive growth cycle, starting with cloud growth, which is needed to support the AI expansion. He also suggested that the infrastructure boom could coexist with the neocloud shakeout, as enterprise AI starts to create jobs rather than taking them away. Last week isn’t necessarily indicative of the AI bubble popping any time soon, he argues.
“Rationale is kicking in, common sense,” he said. “You’re starting to see the beginning of a transition. Wall Street is trying to figure it out. I think they don’t yet get it. But if you look at the language of the experts on the inside and how all the IPOs are being positioned, the value of these IPOs — they want durability. That transition from Silicon Valley tech ecosystem platforms is going to move into the markets. This is a platform game.”
Intel suffers setback
Intel stock saw the steepest drop last week, almost 30% after its Thursday earnings report. The company has leaned into CPUs over GPUs, which Vellante thinks is missing the mark; the real game is not CPUs versus GPUs, but rather AI platforms. Nonetheless, he and Furrier predict Intel will make up some ground.
“Lip-Bu Tan and Intel have an opportunity,” Furrier said. “You basically lost the hyperscaler market that they once had a foothold in. You still run x86 on some clusters. But they got to look at other footprints. I think he’ll turn it around. It’s a multiyear journey, as he says. But the fact of the matter is why I don’t think it’s a bubble, is companies like Alphabet dropping major, major action, $500 billion, in a day.”
Intel is just one component in a rapidly changing ecosystem. Although the AI boom draws comparisons to the bubbles of yore, theCUBE concluded that this is still a unique phenomenon the market has to grapple with, and one that will play out over decades.
“This is just a natural adoption phase,” Vellante said. “What’s different is a lot of things. Like you said, tech is suddenly deflationary. We’re trading CapEx for labor, and that hasn’t really kicked in yet. We’re seeing individual productivity gains but it hasn’t shown up at the firm level yet. These things just take time. And, of course, Wall Street’s like, show me the money.”

articles.title: A Meta quer entrar na sua casa, agora com um robô humanoide • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
A Meta quer entrar na sua casa, agora com um robô humanoide
Criado em parceria com a chinesa Fourier, robô humanoide da Meta teria 1,5 de altura e tela na cabeça que mostra expressões faciais.
Quando o assunto é robô humanoide, talvez você se lembre imediatamente da Boston Dynamics. Mas, surpreendentemente, a Meta também está trabalhando em um projeto do tipo: trata-se de um robô de codinome Max, aproximadamente 1,5 metro de altura e um visor na cabeça capaz de mostrar expressões faciais.
Pelo menos é o que conta o site The Information, citando fontes próximas à Meta familiarizadas com o projeto. As mesmas fontes dão conta de que a turma de Mark Zuckerberg não está sozinha nessa empreitada: o robô estaria sendo desenvolvido em parceria com a Fourier, uma startup chinesa especializada em robótica.
Se os burburinhos estiverem corretos, o robô já está em fase avançada de desenvolvimento. Funcionários da Meta teriam passado cerca de dois meses na China trabalhando junto com a Fourier no projeto e, após esse período, viram um robô de 1,5 m de altura, 48 quilos e mãos com cinco dedos cada ganhar forma.
O fato de o Max ter um visor na cabeça que o permite mostrar expressões faciais deixa claro que o robô está sendo desenvolvido para interagir com humanos. Nesse sentido, o robô poderá ser direcionado à execução de tarefas específicas do lar, de ambientes públicos ou de escritórios, presumivelmente.
Reforça a possibilidade de o robô ser projetado para o convívio com os humanos a capacidade de suas mãos de pegar pequenos objetos, a presença de cinco alto-falantes em seu corpo e o fato de o Max ser baseado no Jetson AGX Thor, plataforma da Nvidia projetada para viabilizar principalmente projetos de robôs humanoides.
Ainda de acordo com os burburinhos, o projeto avança em ritmo acelerado, tanto que um segundo protótipo do robô já está a caminho: o Max 2, como vem sendo chamado, terá a parte superior do seu corpo redesenhada, mãos aprimoradas e sensores que o permitem subir escadas.
Note, porém, que nenhuma imagem do Max foi divulgada até o momento (a foto abaixo, ilustrativa, mostra os robôs da Fourier).
Ninguém sabe ao certo. Procurada para comentar o assunto, a companhia disse apenas que o Max é um projeto interno, razão pela qual os seus objetivos com esse robô não estão claros.
No fim das contas, é possível que o Max sirva de ponto de partida para o desenvolvimento de tecnologias de robótica ou de outros robôs. Ao que tudo indica, a Meta quer entrar de vez no segmento de robôs humanoides. Não por acaso, a companhia adquiriu, em maio deste ano, a Assured Robot Intelligence (ARI), uma startup focada justamente nesse tipo de robótica, como lembra o Engadget.

articles.title: SpaceX loses bid to dismiss lawsuit over xAI data center pollution — facility allegedly emits over 5,000 tons of nitrogen oxides and 47 tons of cancer-causing formaldehyde annually
articles.text:
SpaceX loses bid to dismiss lawsuit over xAI data center pollution — facility allegedly emits over 5,000 tons of nitrogen oxides and 47 tons of cancer-causing formaldehyde annually
A federal judge rejects xAI’s mobile-turbine exemption argument, allowing the NAACP’s Clean Air Act lawsuit over Colossus 2 to proceed.
SpaceX has suffered a setback after losing in a lawsuit aimed at stopping the Clean Air Act requirements on the turbines powering xAI’s Colossus 2 data center in Southaven, Mississippi. According to a report by CNBC, a judge rejected the company’s motion to dismiss the case on Friday, October 30, allowing the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) to proceed, rejecting xAI’s argument that its turbines fall under the ‘mobile sources’ category that exempts it from air permitting requirements.
The case, brought in April 2026 by the NAACP and represented by the Southern Environmental Law Center (SELC) alongside Earthjustice, targets xAI’s operation of a gas-fired power plant to supply electricity to its facility in the Greater Memphis area. SpaceX owns and operates xAI, implicating Elon Musk's wider aerospace and technology company.
According to court documents, NACCP accuses xAI and its subsidiary, MZX Tech, of installing 27 gas turbines in Southaven last year without obtaining the required permits. The applicants also argued that the company’s equipment has been polluting the environment through nitrogen oxide emissions and fine particulate matter, which can contribute to breath-related hazards to residents. The SELC particularly says the plant could emit over 5,00 tons of nitrogen oxides, 400 tons of fine particulate matter, and 47 tons of formaldehyde — a cancer-causing chemical — annually.
The judge also rejected xAI’s attempted classification of the turbines as mobile equipment, holding that the company did not qualify for exemptions under applicable regulations and that the turbines were not exempt from Clean Air Act permitting requirements. Just two weeks earlier, SpaceX suffered another setback after the same court rejected a separate Department of Justice lawsuit that argued against the case proceeding.
“This decision is another important victory in our effort to hold xAI accountable. The courts have repeatedly rejected attempts by xAI and the DOJ to dismiss the NAACP’s Clean Air Act case, affirming our right to pursue justice for communities impacted by pollution. Our position has been clear: xAI cannot operate gas turbines without the required permits. Now that the motion to dismiss has been denied, we look forward to continuing to defend our position in court,” Abre’ Conner, NAACP Director of Environmental and Climate Justice, said. SpaceX is yet to comment on the ruling.
Colossus 2 installed 59 natural gas turbines in July, immediately sparking concerns from residents about emissions and the impact on nearby communities. The Memphis facility plans for about 860,000 Nvidia GB300 GPUs across four Colossus buildings —but it could be more — with Musk stating, “There will be a total of around 1.2M Blackwells at Colossus 2 by end of year”
In August, the company stated that it would remove its unpermitted turbine generators and replace them with a larger permitted power plant — but that could take at least a year. The latest setback adds to a string of lawsuits surrounding the gas-powered infrastructure used to power xAI’s data centers. In June, the DOJ had asked the court to dismiss the NACCP’s lawsuit, arguing that Colossus 2 supports crucial national security operations. That request was, however, rejected. More recently, SpaceX started manufacturing turbine blades in-house to fast-track generator production for its xAI data centers.

articles.title: Cybersecurity M&A Roundup: 37 Deals Announced in October 2026
articles.text:
SecurityWeek tracked 37 cybersecurity merger and acquisition (M&A) deals announced in October 2026.
For a look at last year’s activity, see SecurityWeek’s 2025 Cybersecurity M&A Report, which covers more than 420 deals.
Here are some of the most important cybersecurity M&A deals announced in October 2026:
Absolute Security acquires FirmGuard
Endpoint security and cyber resilience firm Absolute Security has acquired FirmGuard, the UEFI BIOS firmware security and management business of Phoenix Technologies. Absolute will integrate FirmGuard with its firmware-embedded Absolute Persistence technology, adding below-the-OS management, continuous firmware integrity monitoring and patching, and compliance enforcement.
Aikido Security acquires OutKept and Cyberly
Belgian application security unicorn Aikido Security has acquired OutKept and Cyberly and used the two startups to launch Noon, a workforce security business. OutKept is based in Belgium and provides phishing simulations and security awareness training. Poland’s Cyberly develops AI-powered attack simulations and tools for tracking employee AI usage. Both deals closed in September but weren’t made public until October.
Anthropic to acquire Opaque Systems
AI company Anthropic has agreed to acquire Opaque Systems, a confidential AI company that grew out of research at UC Berkeley. Anthropic has described the deal as licensing Opaque’s technology and hiring some of its engineers, reportedly including CEO Aaron Fulkerson and CTO Rishabh Poddar. Financial terms weren’t disclosed.
Canadian AI developer Cohere has signed a letter of intent to acquire AISLE, a startup whose autonomous AI systems find and help patch vulnerabilities in critical software. AISLE’s roughly 50 employees will join Cohere, which is setting up a cybersecurity unit called Cohere Cyber. AISLE CEO Ondřej Vlček, the former CEO of Avast, will become its senior vice president.
Hex-Rays, the Belgian company behind the IDA Pro reverse engineering tool, has agreed to acquire HexAI, an Israeli startup founded in 2025. HexAI’s AI agents analyze source code and binaries to uncover vulnerabilities, malware and backdoors. The deal is reportedly worth $30 million to $35 million. Hex-Rays plans to grow HexAI’s Israeli operations and build new AI-powered research tools.
Quantum computing company IonQ has agreed to acquire zero trust security firm Elisity in an all-stock deal worth up to $1.3 billion, including up to $150 million in performance-based earnouts. IonQ will combine its post-quantum cryptography and quantum key distribution technology with Elisity’s IdentityGraph platform, which enforces least-privilege access for users, devices, workloads and AI agents. The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026.
Thoma Bravo-owned Proofpoint has agreed to acquire data security company Varonis for roughly $6.3 billion in cash. Together, the companies want to offer a single platform for discovering and protecting sensitive data, controlling access to it, and preventing data loss as organizations adopt AI.

articles.title: Intel "Larrabee" GPU System Surfaces with Working Drivers
articles.text:
Monday, November 2nd 2026
Intel "Larrabee" GPU System Surfaces with Working Drivers
Recovered drivers have reportedly restored 3D acceleration to an Intel "Larrabee" prototype, offering the community a rare chance to test the company's abandoned graphics project. Reddit user "pkellythompson" discovered the hardware in equipment purchased at a storage auction, along with two USB drives containing Intel's development software. The Intel Visual Adrenaline system includes a DX58SO motherboard, a C0 stepping "Larrabee" sample, and a diagnostic board. Getting it running required using DVI instead of HDMI and adjusting the storage controller's BIOS settings, so Windows 7 could boot. The recovered archives, approximately 82 MB and 728 MB, include drivers, documentation, development utilities, and VBIOS instructions.
First publicly detailed in 2008, the "Larrabee" project aimed to challenge NVIDIA and AMD's dedicated graphics cards. Larrabee handled much of its graphics processing through software running on simple in-order x86 cores with wide vector units, assisted by dedicated texture hardware. Intel canceled its consumer graphics launch in December 2009 after development fell behind expectations, although the architecture later powered Xeon Phi accelerators. The restored prototype reportedly ran Crysis at 1280×720p with Medium settings and antialiasing disabled. Initial results exceeded 17 FPS, with another recovered driver boosting performance to around 36 FPS.The important aspect here is that the files have been preserved and uploaded to the Internet Archive. These recovered files provide a starting point for further experiments, but working Xeon Phi gaming support and predictions of higher performance still need to be demonstrated.
Source:
				Reddit			
	
	
	
		
	
		
18 Comments on Intel "Larrabee" GPU System Surfaces with Working Drivers
I always wondered if the Larrabee architecture would have been absurdly good (for its time of course) at one or two seriously niche uses.
This pretty much is a whole dev box including the software required to actually use it, and play games.
17FPS on crysis shows why it was abandoned to begin with.
Yes, Intel has had a lot of delays. But these things aren't easy to build from scratch.
We'll eventually see DirectX 12 and Vulkan working on Larrabee samples now that these tools are out there. There's a lot of promise in doing some very cool things with early Xeon Phi as well now. Lots to look forward to.
(did a quick search with AI to compare some data, but i can see now why it flopped, was abandoned and so on.)
Larrabee didn't necessarily fail, either. It became an entirely new product line for Intel that lasted a decade. It wasn't released as a GPU, but the majority of the design was successful in other roles that GPGPUs were good for.
Edit to mention that while everyone was tearing into these software packages the idea did come up that there is fundamentally nothing stopping the Larrabee driver from being recompiled to function on something like a modern x86-64 processor, with the example of running it on one of the extremely high core count EPYC processors. Some effort in rewriting the driver model would be required but not really as much as you'd think.
Phi, on the other hand, seems like the ideal use for that kind of architecture (although presumably, software had to be manually coded to take advantage?)
www.slashgear.com/1863701/intel-project-larrabee-gpu-why-development-discontinued-explained/
Granted, these show 1080p + 1440p results, but by my estimates, 36 FPS @ 720p would be more in line w/ something like a GTX 280 perf., no? Which was nVidia's top-of-the line card around the time the Larrabee project was originally supposed to go to market, no?From conversations w/ folks who were involved at the time, the first phase of the Larrabee project was indeed a total disaster (think not low FPS but rather SPF (seconds per frame) LOL!).
At some point, management decided to pull the plug on existing productization plans that were based on original targets to release a "graphics" product by a certain date (around summer 2009 IIRC?). But, they did keep a smaller team of hardcore developers internally to continue work on an internal alternative driver prototype which showed more promise than the bloated monster that had been developed during the first phase mentioned above.
I was told that by the end of what I would call that "second phase", the new prototype driver's performance was actually showing some competitiveness against the original targets (e.g. GTX 280??) and additional performance optimizations in software and improvements in hardware (Knights Corner + Knights Landing) were still being planned to continue on the perf. improvement trajectory.
From what I gathered, there were some nasty internal politics involved in the final decision to ultimately pull the plug entirely on the whole "graphics" thing (think internal competition where the "Xe Graphics" team felt threatened by the prospect of becoming obsolete would the Larrabee project succeed), this despite what was demonstrated at the end of the second phase as mentioned above.
My guess is the "36 FPS" we're seeing here would be the results of a driver stack built during the end of the "second phase" (circa summer/fall of 2010 IIRC).

articles.title: Anthropic verbietet Claude Nachbau von Games – doch die Regeln treffen auch legitime Projekte
articles.text:
Anthropic verbietet Claude Nachbau von Games – doch die Regeln treffen auch legitime Projekte
In der Spielebranche sorgen KI-generierte Kopien zunehmend für Unruhe. Dazu kommt, dass sich im Vorfeld von Veröffentlichungen geäußerte Ideen oder verbreitete Demos mit KI-Support zur Game-Entwicklung missbrauchen lassen – inklusive entsprechender Erpressungsversuche.
Nachbau existierender Games verboten
KI-Anbieter Anthropic will dem jetzt einen Riegel vorschieben. Im Systemprompt seiner Modelle Claude Code und Claude Opus 5.5 findet sich ein Passus, der den „Nachbau spezifischer existierender Games“ untersagt. Das soll auch dann gelten, wenn die Entwickler:innen für das Ergebnis einen anderen Namen wählen, wie Tom‘s Hardware berichtet.
Weiter erlaubt sein soll Anthropics KI-Modellen aber die Hilfe bei der Entwicklung von Games, wenn die Nutzer:innen dabei ihre eigenen Designs und Materialien verwenden. Das Unternehmen hat die Änderung bestätigt und dabei auf mögliche Verletzungen geistigen Eigentums verwiesen.
Schutz vor möglichen Urheberrechtsklagen
Diese, so Anthropic-Mitarbeiter Addy Osmani via X, verstießen gegen die Nutzungsrichtlinien. Zudem dürfte das Unternehmen damit versuchen, sich vor möglichen Verfahren wegen der Verletzung von Urheberrechten zu schützen.
Allerdings scheint es im Zuge der strengeren Regeln auch zu Problemen bei legitimen Entwicklungsprojekten zu kommen. So soll Claude auch eigentlich unbedenkliche Versuche, Games per Reverse-Engineering zu analysieren, blockieren. Im Visier scheint demnach unter anderem das vielgenutzte Tool Reverse Engineer Anything zu stehen.
Claude soll legitime Projekte torpedieren
Auf GitHub häufen sich laut Tom‘s Hardware Meldungen von Nutzer:innen, dass die Anthropic-KI die Zusammenarbeit auch bei der Nachbildung von Spielmechaniken oder beim Patchen von Game-Code verweigert. Die Weigerung trifft laut Berichten auf Reddit und anderen Plattformen auch andere Entwickler:innen aus anderen Bereichen, die etwa einen Windows-Crash analysieren oder Junkware von einem Smart-TV entfernen wollten.
Inwiefern es sich bei allen Beschwerden um legitime Anliegen handelt, ist derweil nicht zu belegen. In einigen Fällen sollen aber bekannte und glaubwürdige Entwickler:innen Protest eingelegt haben.
Regeln zu streng? Anthropic will nachjustieren
Hat Anthropic also die Zügel zu eng angezogen? Der KI-Anbieter hat angekündigt, entsprechend nachjustieren zu wollen, um „ein Gleichgewicht“ zu finden. „Falls Claude in der Zwischenzeit etwas ablehnt, das dir gehört, dann schick es mir“, schrieb Osmani via X.

articles.title: WhatsApp ganha função que transforma números, endereços e datas em atalhos
articles.text:
O WhatsApp está liberando recurso que promete facilitar tarefas comuns do dia a dia. A novidade identifica automaticamente números de telefone, datas, horários, endereços e e-mails compartilhados em conversas e oferece atalhos para interagir com essas informações sem precisar sair do aplicativo.
Chamado de message text actions (ações de texto em mensagens), o recurso está em distribuição gradual para usuários de celulares Android e iPhone. A novidade foi identificada pelo site especializado WABetaInfo em versões recentes do aplicativo.
Como funcionam as ações de texto do WhatsApp?
Quando o aplicativo reconhece uma informação compatível, ele exibe um sublinhado pontilhado abaixo do trecho. Ao tocar no texto destacado, o usuário abre um menu com opções relacionadas ao conteúdo identificado.
O recurso funciona tanto em mensagens recebidas quanto nas enviadas. O menu também mostra o trecho reconhecido, permitindo conferir se o WhatsApp identificou corretamente a informação. Caso não queira utilizar nenhuma das sugestões, basta ignorar o destaque e continuar a conversa normalmente.
As opções variam de acordo com o tipo de conteúdo:
- Números de telefone: permitem copiar o número, adicioná-lo à lista de contatos ou fazer uma ligação pela operadora. No caso de números comerciais, também pode aparecer a opção de consultar informações da empresa;
- Datas e horários: oferecem a possibilidade de copiar os dados, adicioná-los à agenda do aparelho ou criar um evento diretamente no WhatsApp;
- Endereços: podem ser copiados ou abertos em um aplicativo de mapas;
- E-mails: permitem copiar o endereço ou abrir o aplicativo de correio eletrônico para iniciar uma mensagem.
Algumas dessas opções já existiam em versões anteriores do WhatsApp. A mudança está em reuni-las em um menu contextual, facilitando o acesso às ações disponíveis.
Leia mais:
- Quer ver mensagens apagadas no WhatsApp? Descubra o truque simples disponível em celulares Android
- WhatsApp: pais e responsáveis ganham recursos para ajustar como adolescentes usam o app
- WhatsApp libera entrada em chamadas de vídeo sem criar conta
Recurso não compromete a criptografia das conversas
Outro detalhe destacado pelo WABetaInfo diz respeito à privacidade. Segundo o site, o reconhecimento dos textos acontece diretamente no dispositivo, por meio de expressões regulares — padrões usados para identificar formatos específicos de informação.
Nesse processo, o conteúdo das mensagens e as sugestões de ações não são enviados aos servidores do WhatsApp. O site afirma que, por isso, a novidade não interfere na criptografia de ponta a ponta das conversas.
O aplicativo também permite avaliar as sugestões. Depois de selecionar uma ação, o usuário pode indicar se ela foi útil ou não. Caso a identificação esteja incorreta ou a opção seja desnecessária, é possível fornecer esse feedback. De acordo com o WABetaInfo, essa avaliação envia apenas um sinal à plataforma, sem compartilhar o conteúdo da mensagem.
Quando o recurso chega a todos?
As ações de texto estão sendo liberadas gradualmente para alguns usuários das versões mais recentes do WhatsApp para Android e iOS. Isso significa que nem todos encontrarão os sublinhados pontilhados imediatamente, mesmo que tenham atualizado o aplicativo.
O WABetaInfo informa que a distribuição deve alcançar mais contas nas próximas semanas. Até o momento, porém, o WhatsApp não anunciou uma data para disponibilizar a novidade a todos os usuários.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: The Philips Hue app now lets AI build smart light automations for you, but early adopters are running into errors and unhelpful limitations
articles.text:
Philips Hue just launched its ambitious Custom AI Behaviors, but early teething troubles show the smart assistant might not be quite ready for prime time
You can now create new Hue behaviors using natural language — if you have the Hue Bridge Pro and a bit of patience
- Custom AI behaviors have arrived in the Philips Hue app
- At the moment you can't edit what the AI creates
- AI features require the Hue Bridge Pro
When we spoke to Hue founder and head of technology George Yianni in September, he told us about some exciting new features coming to the Hue ecosystem including Custom AI Behaviors. And now they've arrived in the Hue app, provided that you have the Hue Bridge Pro.
Yianni told us that AI would be "a bit of a game changer" for the platform, and said of the custom behaviors that "natural language is a fantastic way to just describe arbitrarily how you would like your home to behave, and then we can use AI to translate that into a special programming language we’ve developed that runs the automation in the Bridge."
According to Yianni, "I now can finally have my home behave exactly the way I wanted to. I think that's a really big deal." But unfortunately according to HueBlog, the behaviors aren't quite behaving the way we'd like them to.
How to use Philips Hue Custom AI Behaviors
The idea behind Custom AI Behaviors is simple: tell the AI what you want and the AI will craft the appropriate behavior for you and add it to the app. For example, you could tell the AI that you want specific lights to go on at sunset, and to use different color themes each time.
That's what Hueblog tried, and the AI understood the mission. But unfortunately it didn't quite get it right: instead of turning on only the specified lights, the behavior turned all the lights on. When Hueblog tried to get the AI to fix the issue "it gave up and simply displayed the error message."
It looks like the goal — use AI to make things simple — is perhaps too simple, because as Hueblog put it "you’re entirely limited by the AI’s logic and reasoning. If it doesn’t cooperate, you’re out of luck." Unlike, say, Apple's Shortcuts on macOS and iOS, there's no way to tweak the shortcuts the AI has created if they're not quite doing what you want.
This feels like a typical version 1.0 issue, where a feature is rolled out first and then updated based on user feedback. That means the no-tweaking issue is likely to be short-lived: in my experience Hue's pretty good at updating its app to deliver new features.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
While the new AI features — the new Custom AI Behaviors and the previously launched SpatialAware scene optimization — are reserved for the Hue Bridge Pro, the app also provides updates for all Hue users including easier Screen Sync setup and improved scene recommendations. As ever the Hue app is available for both iOS and Android.
Follow TechRadar on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our expert news, reviews, and opinion in your feeds.
Contributor
Writer, broadcaster, musician and kitchen gadget obsessive Carrie Marshall has been writing about tech since 1998, contributing sage advice and odd opinions to all kinds of magazines and websites as well as writing more than twenty books. Her latest, a love letter to music titled Small Town Joy, is on sale now. She is the singer in spectacularly obscure Glaswegian rock band Unquiet Mind.
