articles.title: Anthropic warns that it's very close to RSI capability, aka self-building AI | TechCrunch
articles.text:
While much attention has focused on the updated financials Anthropic revealed in its revised S-1/A on Monday (revenue is soaring, but so are expenses), the AI lab dropped another little bombshell in the fine print.
The filing seems to warn that the company is on the cusp of creating a model capable of recursive self-improvement (RSI).
RSI is the point at which AI grows so good at training itself that it spawns a dramatic acceleration of AI capabilities. To the AI doomers, RSI represents the cataclysm from which there is no return, in which AI builds itself into something powerful enough that it slips beyond human control and may be indifferent to the damage it causes while achieving its goals.
To AI enthusiasts, RSI, or some version of AI reliably using itself to improve, represents the technology’s promise, where it becomes a tool of unimaginable productivity, scientific discovery, and more.
Anthropic seems to believe that RSI is both a promise and a peril. It says in the S-1 that it uses AI in its R&D, but it cautions: “Using AI to help build more capable AI could also pose a considerable safety risk, particularly if it sharply accelerates the pace of progress. This is one of the areas covered by our Responsible Scaling Policy, which sets out our plans to monitor and mitigate the risks as we approach what has been termed ‘recursive self-improvement.’”
When the term RSI became popular earlier this year, many believed it was a buzzword or, at best, a goal too hard to achieve, define, or prove.
But on Monday, Anthropic added new statements to its Risk Factors section, saying 1) it has already used AI to develop new models whose leaps in capability it didn’t recognize at the time, and 2) it may soon meet its own definition of RSI (bold emphasis ours, below):
In addition, our increasing use of AI systems to accelerate our own research and development may cause the capabilities of our models to advance more rapidly than our ability to develop, validate, and implement corresponding safety, alignment, and security measures. As a result, we have in the past not identified, and may in the future not identify, a significant acceleration in our rate of development until after it has occurred.
For example, our internal estimates and our expectations regarding future models, rather than our current models, indicate that we may imminently meet our Responsible Scaling Policy’s definition of “dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI.” We have not designated any of our current models as exceeding this threshold, and we continue to assess the underlying data.
However, Anthropic also said in the filing that none of its models have crossed this RSI threshold yet and that it is promising to keep humans in the R&D process for the foreseeable future. “We do not anticipate being able to safely use Claude to fully autonomously design and build successive generations of frontier models without meaningful human supervision or understanding, if and when that becomes technically possible. Accordingly, we are considering updates to our Responsible Scaling Policy to keep humans in control of frontier model development at Anthropic.”
Skeptics might point out that an S-1 functions as both disclosure and marketing, and that claims of being close to a model so powerful that it can build itself could fall into the latter category.
Nevertheless, there’s no question that Claude’s capabilities, especially in terms of coding, math, and cybersecurity, have grown leaps and bounds this year. If Anthropic thinks the possibility of RSI is close, maybe we should believe it and act — perhaps govern — accordingly.

articles.title: New Wave of Refrigeration Cyberattacks Hits Supermarkets Across Europe, Forcing Stores to Pull Food
articles.text:
Attackers remotely changed the settings on refrigeration controls at supermarkets in Belgium, Sweden, Estonia and other European countries overnight into Monday, November 2, warming fridges and freezers.
No chain reported more than several dozen affected stores, and some had to throw away chilled and frozen food or take it off the shelf. Danfoss, a Danish maker of refrigeration controls, said its products were involved, as they were three weeks earlier when attackers hit hundreds of French supermarkets.
No one had claimed the attacks by Monday night, and it was not known whether they were linked to the attack in France.
Refrigeration controls are computers that run a store's fridges and freezers. They can be connected to the internet, allowing refrigeration contractors to monitor them and fix faults remotely.
In Belgium, attackers switched cooling units into defrost mode, Stephan Moelans, chief executive of the refrigeration contractor Sabcobel, told Belgian media. Defrost mode is meant to clear ice, but in these attacks it made the units heat up instead of keeping food cold. Sabcobel manages refrigeration systems for the Delhaize supermarket chain.
In other cases, the temperature setting was raised. An ICA store in Sjöbo, in southern Sweden, said its fridges and freezers had been set to 50°C and that staff were throwing out the affected goods.
At a Selver supermarket in Estonia, a freezer was set to 50°C, said Jann Mutso, chief executive of the refrigeration supplier Kitman Coldtech. Its temperature rose by only about 2-3°C, and the problem was resolved within about 10 minutes, with no products damaged.
Danfoss's security advisories page listed no advisory about the attacks when The Hacker News checked on November 3. The most detailed steps for operators are still those in an October alert from CERT-FR, part of France's national cybersecurity agency.
Which Companies Say They Were Hit
Each company described the incident in its own words, and not all of them called it a cyberattack.
| Country | Company | Stores affected | What the company or its supplier said | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Belgium, Luxembourg | Delhaize | Several dozen, mostly in Belgium and a few in Luxembourg | An "IT incident" affected refrigeration. The range of fresh and frozen food was temporarily limited. | 
| Belgium | Carrefour | 15 of more than 700 | A cyberattack on its refrigeration, with very limited impact. | 
| Belgium | Intermarché | 10 to 15 | Problems with its fridges. | 
| Belgium | Spar, under Colruyt Group | 5, run by independent owners | Their fridge systems were attacked. | 
| Belgium | IKEA | 1, in Mons | A cyber incident hit the store's fridges and freezers. No other IKEA store in Belgium was affected. | 
| Sweden | ICA | A limited number. No count given | An incident affected refrigeration and freezer systems. ICA did not confirm a cyberattack. | 
| Sweden | Coop | 6 (to TT and AFP) or 7 (to Reuters and Bloomberg), of about 800 | A cyber incident in which someone tampered with its refrigeration without permission. | 
| Ireland | Musgrave, owner of SuperValu | 13 of 223 | A "cyber incident" limited to one refrigeration model. | 
| Estonia | Selver, through supplier Kitman Coldtech | 1 | An attack on an older Danfoss system. | 
| Netherlands | Businesses not named | At least 17 businesses, including butchers and small local shops | Attacked, according to Danfoss. | 
| Finland | Kesko | A few smaller stores | Unusual temperatures. The cause was under investigation. The stores' equipment is outside Kesko's central protections. | 
| Portugal | Intermarché, Mosqueteiros group | 7 | A cyberattack that appears to have targeted an outside company managing the refrigeration, according to AFP. | 
| Italy | Coop supermarkets run by Radenza Group | At least 4, in Sicily | An attack on its remote control system for frozen food sections, according to AFP. | 
At a De Laet & Van Haver butcher shop in Hove, south of Antwerp, the fridges were turned up as high as 18°C, owner Luc De Laet told Reuters. He estimated that about €15,000 worth of meat was ruined.
At the 13 SuperValu stores, Musgrave took chilled and frozen products off sale as a precaution. The company said on Monday afternoon that the incident had been resolved and restocking was under way.
What Companies Say About the Equipment and the Way In
Several of the systems that were hit were made by Danfoss. All of ICA's affected stores were connected to an outside refrigeration control system supplied by Danfoss, an ICA spokesperson told AFP. In Estonia, attackers reached the control computer of an older Danfoss system, Mutso said.
Danfoss is not named in every case. Musgrave's statement did not name the maker of the affected model.
An affected Belgian butcher told Dutch broadcaster NOS that equipment from a second maker, Copeland, was also attacked in Belgium. Copeland gave NOS no clear answer to questions about the attacks.
The Dutch systems that were hit were not on a secure network and still used default passwords, a Danfoss spokesperson told NOS. Most shops there had taken measures after the French attack, but a few had not, and those were the ones hit.
Danfoss also told Belgian broadcaster VTM that the weakness lies mainly in outdated software and that customers who had not updated were affected, Euronews reported.
Sabcobel knows of about 20 affected units among the hundreds it manages in Belgium. In the Belgian cases, attackers got into individual supermarkets' systems, not those of refrigeration contractors, Moelans told Belgian media. Sabcobel had advised stores to secure their internet connections, and many but not all had done so.
Mutso said old controllers that had not been updated were being targeted. Selver said the store that was hit was the last one it had not yet moved to a new system. ICA told NBC News that its own systems were not affected and that the affected stores used an outside supplier and were connected to a network outside ICA's central network.
Belgium's Centre for Cybersecurity told reporters on Monday that it had no further information. Sweden's National Cybersecurity Centre did not say in its notice how attackers got in.
What Operators Can Do
CERT-FR's alert covers Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC series controllers, as well as Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb. It says attack campaigns against these devices are probably still underway. When The Hacker News checked on November 3, the alert had last been updated on October 16.
For devices that have not been compromised, the steps are:
- Make sure the devices cannot be reached from the internet, including any device on a public IP address. Check your insurance contract before cutting the data feed to your refrigeration contractor.
- Check the whole configuration, especially the defrost schedules.
- Restore access only through a secure VPN or a protected network. In an emergency, you can filter the contractors' IP addresses at a firewall, but this should not be a lasting fix.
- Follow the maker's good practices, such as updating firmware. For Danfoss devices, set the security level to Strict and make sure default passwords have been changed.
For a device that has been compromised, two more steps follow: restart the Danfoss device or reset it to factory settings, then reconfigure it before putting it back into service.
End-of-life devices that no longer get security fixes are very likely to be compromised if they stay on the internet, CERT-FR warns. A factory reset alone leaves them open to attack again. In October, Danfoss said most of the units hit in France were older models it no longer updates, the AK-SM 800 and AK-SC 355.
Danfoss advised Dutch customers on October 13 to disconnect their systems from the internet and reconnect them only through a secure network. It had also been working with customers to put fixes in place.
Sweden's National Cybersecurity Center advised organizations to list which devices are connected to the internet, decide whether each one needs to be connected, and keep any that remain connected updated and protected with multiple layers of security.
Moelans said a software update alone is not enough, because the installations need physical changes that cost money. The simplest answer is a secure internet connection for managing the fridges, which most of Sabcobel's customers adopted after the French attack.
Who Is Behind It
Danfoss said the Dutch attacks were the same kind as the one in France, Sabcobel said the same method was used in Belgium, and Kitman said the method in Estonia was similar. A shared method does not show that the same people carried out both attacks.
Belgium's Centre for Cybersecurity said on Monday that it was not known who was behind the attacks and that "it may never be determined".
Belgium's federal prosecutor's office has opened a criminal investigation, it confirmed to VRT. Sweden's National Cybersecurity Centre said on Monday that it was following the incidents and sharing information with agencies in other Nordic and European countries.

articles.title: "At Home in Space" opens, caps Air and Space Museum renovation
articles.text:
A mock-up of an astronaut on a spacewalk welcomes visitors into "At Home in Space," the last of the space-themed galleries to open at the renovated National Air and Space Museum.
Credit:
Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
A mock-up of an astronaut on a spacewalk welcomes visitors into "At Home in Space," the last of the space-themed galleries to open at the renovated National Air and Space Museum.
Credit:
Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
After seven years of work and nearly $1 billion, the Smithsonian has completed the renovation of the National Air and Space Museum’s flagship building in Washington, DC.
On October 30, the museum debuted its last-to-open spaceflight exhibition, returning “home” with a gallery devoted to establishing a spacefaring civilization.
“Welcome to ‘At Home in Space’!” said curator Jennifer Levasseur, who guided us through a virtual tour of the gallery. “This is the story of long-duration spaceflight in the last few decades. We generally call it ‘reaching orbit.’”
“It’s the prep story, the space shuttle story. It’s what allows us to end up at a place where we have 25-plus years of long-duration spaceflight experience, the capacity for humans to be living in space on the International Space Station (ISS), and then it carries that story forward. So the middle of our story then becomes the ISS, and the end of the story are the next steps,” said Levasseur.
“At Home in Space” takes visitors on a 50-plus-year journey of learning how humans can live and work in space continuously and venture beyond Earth orbit.
Credit:
Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
“At Home in Space” takes visitors on a 50-plus-year journey of learning how humans can live and work in space continuously and venture beyond Earth orbit.
Credit:
Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
Entering “At Home”
Over the past several years, the National Air and Space Museum has introduced new galleries showcasing how US astronauts first entered space and landed on the Moon (“Destination Moon”); how robotic probes have explored every planet in our solar system (“Kenneth C. Griffin Exploring the Planets”); how technologies and infrastructure impact our daily lives (“RTX Living in the Space Age Hall”) and what approaches spaceflight will take in the years to come (“Futures in Space”).
“At Home in Space,” which follows the similarly themed “Moving Beyond Earth,” immerses guests in the equipment, spacecraft, and orbital platforms that have enabled humanity from simply visiting space to living there, setting up the near future for bases on the Moon and Mars.
“We have a great way to attract people into the gallery, which is this overhead mock-up of an astronaut on the end of the robotic arm, and then the backdrop to that is this photo mural—a full-size photo print—of the ISS,” said Levasseur. “Our astronaut up here is intended to be [an actual] person, but I’m not going to share who that is. They are wearing an Expedition 60 patch, so that’ll give you a little clue.”
Outer space outfits
Some of the gallery’s artifacts include a space shuttle main engine, Robonaut 1A (a prototype humanoid robot), and an extravehicular mobility unit (EMU) spacesuit.
“It’s pretty damn special,” said Levasseur of the EMU. “This, as far as I know, is the first and potentially only public display of a fully flown set of EMU equipment in the world. I know NASA has one in its EVA office, but it is not on public display.”
NASA astronaut Chris Williams and curator Jennifer Levasseur view the only fully flown extravehicular mobility unit spacesuit on public display in “At Home in Space.”
Credit:
NASA/Aubrey Gemignani
NASA astronaut Chris Williams and curator Jennifer Levasseur view the only fully flown extravehicular mobility unit spacesuit on public display in “At Home in Space.”
Credit:
NASA/Aubrey Gemignani
Unlike Apollo-era spacesuits sized to each astronaut, the EMU was designed to be reused, so its components can be swapped out to fit astronauts of different sizes. Introduced during the early years of the space shuttle program, the same EMU suits are still used on the International Space Station for US spacewalks.
The museum’s example is only missing a functioning portable life support system (PLSS), as all the backpacks are still needed for use. So the suit on display only has a PLSS shell for now, according to Levasseur.
The gallery also features Guy Bluford’s and Sally Ride’s in-flight suits, the “shirt-sleeve” outfits the first African American and first US woman wore on the space shuttle (on separate missions).
“Sally is notably missing her jacket, which was a late change to our plan. We were given a drawing of this, a 3D mockup of its display case, and our designers then put it in this way without the jacket on. And we thought, ‘Hey, that’s actually kind of a nice contrast. Let’s keep the jacket out,’” Levasseur told collectSPACE.
Flight clothes worn by the first African American astronaut, Guion “Guy” Bluford, and the first US woman, Sally Ride, on board the space shuttle, as on display in “At Home in Space.”
Credit:
Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
Flight clothes worn by the first African American astronaut, Guion “Guy” Bluford, and the first US woman, Sally Ride, on board the space shuttle, as on display in “At Home in Space.”
Credit:
Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
The gallery also includes recovered components from the Challenger and Columbia tragedies. It is only the second public display of fallen orbiter debris after a Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex exhibit that opened in Florida in 2015.
“We wanted to honor the individuals who were lost during the shuttle program,” said Levasseur. “So we have an elevon hinge from Challenger that washed up on the beach a few years ago and a little wiring panel fragment from inside the payload bay. And then from Columbia we thought it was appropriate to help tell that story with a piece of RCC [reinforced carbon-carbon]. This is a T-panel from the starboard wing. We also have a CD [compact disc] on a long-term loan from David Brown’s family.”
Inside ISS
Visitors can also walk through a full-size mock-up of the space station’s Destiny module, the US national laboratory on the station, and view its equipment on both sides, as well as above and below.
“Originally, the detailing on the floor was going to be a mosaic of real images, but we found that for accessibility reasons people might come in and see the cables and worry that they were real, creating a tripping hazard,” said Levasseur. “On the flip side, and I had to fight to get these, we had to have labels to indicate activity happens on the floor and happens on the overhead. People need to see this is a literally three-dimensional space.”
The module has interactive elements on one side and showcases some of the crew equipment-related artifacts, including coffee cups engineered for use in microgravity.
Visitors to “At Home in Space” at the National Air and Space Museum can walk through a full-scale mockup of the International Space Station’s US Destiny laboratory, the US National Laboratory, which includes interactive elements and artifact displays.
Credit:
Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
Visitors to “At Home in Space” at the National Air and Space Museum can walk through a full-scale mockup of the International Space Station’s US Destiny laboratory, the US National Laboratory, which includes interactive elements and artifact displays.
Credit:
Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
“This is probably the best section in my mind because it has fun stuff,” said Levasseur, pointing out the flown miniPCR biotech toolkit and MinION portable device used to sequence DNA in space for the first time.
“My absolute favorite thing to work on in this gallery answers the questions: What does space smell like, and what does the ISS smell like? We have little scent oils inside each of these that allow people to smell them,” she said.
Nearby, the first 3D printer used in space is also on display. In 2014, Made In Space (now part of Redwire) and NASA flew the printer, which produced hundreds of objects, from astronaut tools to space station repair parts.
Awaiting Artemis
The gallery concludes with a space reserved to exhibit the Artemis I capsule, the spacecraft that flew without astronauts to the Moon in 2022. A Lockheed Martin scale model of Orion holds the place until NASA delivers the real spacecraft to the Smithsonian, which is expected later this year.
“This is the piece of Wright Flyer fabric that went to the moon with Artemis II, so that’s on display here, too,” Levasseur said, concluding the tour.
“At Home in Space” displays a scale model of the Orion spacecraft as a placeholder for Artemis I that flew to the moon.
Credit:
Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
“At Home in Space” displays a scale model of the Orion spacecraft as a placeholder for Artemis I that flew to the moon.
Credit:
Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
The renovation of the National Air and Space Museum also included refacing the exterior cladding, replacing mechanical systems, and other improvements. The first half of the museum reopened in 2022 with eight new or reimagined galleries, the Northrop Grumman Planetarium, museum store, and the Mars Café. The second phase opened in 2025 with five new galleries, and five additional galleries opened July 1.
Following “At Home in Space,” “Modern Military Aviation” will open on November 11.
“We are thrilled to complete the most extensive project the museum has ever undergone,” Chris Browne, John and Adrienne Mars Director of the museum, said in a statement. “With the opening of these last two galleries, the public will once again be able to visit the entirety of the museum and learn from and engage with the nation’s world-class aerospace collection.”
Admission to all of the National Air and Space Museum galleries remains free, but timed-entry passes for the building are required to visit.
Robert Pearlman is a space historian, journalist and the founder and editor of collectSPACE, a daily news publication and online community focused on where space exploration intersects with pop culture. He is also a contributing writer for Space.com and co-author of "Space Stations: The Art, Science, and Reality of Working in Space” published by Smithsonian Books in 2018. He is on the leadership board for For All Moonkind and is a member of the American Astronautical Society's history committee.

articles.title: Andes Waits For Market Momentum For Cuzco CPU - EE Times
articles.text:
TAIPEI, Taiwan – Andes Technology has slowed development of its Cuzco high-end RISC-V CPU IP as it redirects engineering resources to a rapidly growing AI business, CTO Charlie Su told EE Times. Su insisted the project’s ambition remains, even if the technology emerges in a different form and on a different timeline than originally planned.
RISC-V IP vendor Andes had spun out Condor to develop Cuzco after identifying a future market need for a high-end data center CPU based on RISC-V, but pulled the technology back in-house earlier this year.
“The ecosystem needs to gradually go there before you have the hardware, otherwise you cannot catch the opportunity,” Su said. “We started, but as time went on, we found the AI part of our business continued to grow very strongly.”
Andes’s AI business currently accounts for half of its revenue, growing 30% last year and likely to grow 50% this year, Su said, which will require additional resources internally. Andes has a small deep learning accelerator (up to around 4 TOPS at 1 GHz) with its own compiler, but most of its revenue in AI comes from AI chip companies using Andes CPU cores for control, orchestration, and data movement (including Meta, d-Matrix, Fractile, and Axelera). Many of these licenses are for custom cores, and delivery schedules can be extremely demanding, Su said.
“We decided to consolidate and slow down [Cuzco], so we could put more resources on the immediate revenue generation part,” he said.
Once the need to reallocate resources emerged, Condor was an obvious target since Cuzco had not yet taken off commercially. The spinout received many inquiries after its launch at Hot Chips 2025, Su said, but these inquiries have been slow to convert to licenses.
“We could have put more effort into finishing Cuzco and maybe get one or two customers, but it’s not enough—we need to wait for bigger momentum,” he said. “So we decided to scale it back and move a little bit slower.”
Su also cited the rise of agentic AI in the early part of 2026 as a key driver for improving productivity and reducing headcount across the business this spring. Andes has its whole engineering team using AI agents to accelerate progress, with humans reviewing everything, Su said. Consolidating Condor was linked to this strategy.
Cuzco will still become a product, perhaps under another name, but the timeline has lengthened as Andes is working on it “slowly, while looking for signs we should speed up,” Su said. Winning in IP isn’t necessarily about getting to market first, he added; Andes’s embedded customers may use the same cores for 10 years or more, albeit on different process nodes.
“The core that brings us the most revenue today is one we designed more than 10 years ago,” Su said. “We want to do it right, make it reusable, instead of getting to market first.”
In the meantime, Andes’s experience with Cuzco can be leveraged within the company, while recent changes in Arm’s business model following its launch of high-end CPU silicon are positive for the IP giant’s competitors, including Andes, Su said.
“Arm changed its business model, and that has certainly affected customer trust, especially at the high end,” Su said. “[Embedded] customers also don’t know when it will hit their market.”
For now, high on Andes’s priority list is a main processor core for the storage market. The company already has 10 customers in production with smaller controller cores. It is also focusing on automotive and robotics.
“The bottom line is that the market Cuzco tried to address is still there and will continue, so that’s where we want to hit next in terms of our performance level,” Su said.

articles.title: Electra avait promis de ne pas toucher aux anciens forfaits de recharge : 6 mois plus tard, c'est raté
articles.text:
En matière de recharge rapide pour voitures électriques, la réputation se construit lentement sur la fiabilité des bornes et le maillage du réseau, mais elle peut se fissurer beaucoup plus vite pour des histoires d’argent. Jusqu’ici, la jeune pousse française Electra jouissait d’un bon capital sympathie auprès des électromobilistes : stations bien entretenues, communication soignée et offres attractives.
Pourtant, une vague de courriels envoyés en ce début de mois de novembre 2026 à ses abonnés de la première heure risque de gripper la machine. Lors du lancement de sa tarification dynamique et de ses formules « Smart » au printemps dernier, l’opérateur s’était pourtant voulu rassurant : les deux générations d’abonnements devaient cohabiter, permettant aux anciens clients de conserver leurs conditions avantageuses. Six mois plus tard, la promesse n’est déjà plus qu’un lointain souvenir.
L’ancien abonnement « Boost » est poussé vers la sortie par Electra
Dans les faits, Electra applique une double peine, selon le mode de facturation de ses abonnés Electra+ Boost (la formule historique à 9,99 €/mois qui garantissait un tarif fixe de 0,29 €/kWh) :
- Pour les abonnés mensuels : le forfait reste actif, mais le tarif au kilowattheure prend un coup de chaud. Dès le 2 décembre 2026, le prix passe de 0,29 € à 0,34 €/kWh sur les stations françaises (+17 %). Le mail annonce également l’arrivée de frais d’occupation dynamiques indexés sur le pourcentage de batterie restant (SoC), et les réductions accordées chez les opérateurs partenaires deviendront elles aussi variables.
- Pour les abonnés annuels : par message, Electra informe tout simplement ses clients que leur formule « ne sera pas renouvelée une fois arrivée à son terme », le forfait étant voué à disparaître.
Dans les deux cas, le message d’Electra se conclut par la même invitation appuyée : migrer vers la nouvelle offre Electra+ Smart, facturée 4,99 € par mois pour obtenir une remise de 0,20 €/kWh sur le prix affiché dans l’application.
Pourquoi le forfait Smart ne console pas tout le monde
Sur le papier, basculer vers un abonnement moins cher (4,99 € au lieu de 9,99 €) avec une réduction de 20 centimes par kWh semble attractif. Dans la réalité du quotidien, le calcul est loin d’être aussi avantageux.
L’ancien forfait Boost offrait une vraie sérénité : un prix bloqué à 0,29 €/kWh, 24 h/24, sur autoroute et en dehors, sans avoir à consulter sa montre. Or, la formule Smart applique sa remise de 0,20 € sur un tarif dynamique qui fluctue selon les tensions du réseau électrique.
Si ce système permet de recharger à prix cassé en heures très creuses (la nuit ou en milieu d’après-midi, parfois sous les 0,20 €/kWh), il devient pénalisant pour tous ceux et celles qui se branchent aux heures de pointe (grosso modo : le matin, entre 8h et 10h, ou en fin de journée, entre 17h et 20h). Sur ces créneaux où le tarif de base frôle ou dépasse les 0,55 €/kWh, la facture finale après réduction grimpe vite à 0,35 € voire 0,39 €/kWh ou davantage.
Pour les gros rouleurs ou les conducteurs sans borne à domicile qui dépendent du réseau public sur leurs trajets pendulaires, la disparition du tarif fixe s’apparente à une hausse déguisée.
Electra n’est plus forcément la meilleure offre du marché
Ce coup de canif dans le contrat de confiance arrive à un moment où le paysage de la recharge ultra-rapide n’a plus rien à voir avec celui d’il y a deux ans. Le réseau s’est densifié et la concurrence est devenue impitoyable. Les opérateurs de recharge ont donc tous dégainé des abonnements ou des offres de fidélisation (cashback, remises…) pour attirer les automobilistes sur leurs bornes.
Sur les groupes de discussion et forums d’utilisateurs, la grogne monte déjà. Face à cette incitation forcée à passer au tarif dynamique, nombre d’abonnés historiques regardent ailleurs :
- Atlante, qui multiplie les déploiements dans les zones périurbaines et les centres commerciaux avec des abonnements particulièrement agressifs au kilowattheure et un cashback souvent intéressant.
- Izivia Fast, qui séduit de plus en plus avec des grilles tarifaires lisibles et des tarifs préférentiels bien placés.
- Les supermarchés entrent aussi dans la compétition pour attirer les clients avec des tarifs plus attractifs (mais plus souvent sur la recharge lente).
L’automobiliste qui a besoin du réseau public est avant tout pragmatique : si l’avantage tarifaire disparaît et que les conditions d’utilisation se complexifient, la fidélité à une marque s’évapore en un clic.
En complexifiant son offre et en rognant les avantages de ses clients les plus fidèles, Electra prend le risque de les envoyer tester les bornes d’en face. Et sur ce marché, ceux qui partent reviennent rarement. Electra a certainement de bonnes raisons de justifier cette décision, mais la transparence des débuts s’effrite un peu.

articles.title: Une tablette à offrir pour Noël ? La Xiaomi Pad 7 256 Go tombe à 202,35€ pour le Black Friday AliExpress
articles.text:
À un peu plus de sept semaines de Noël, le Single Day d’AliExpress, lancé le 1er novembre, ajoute aux prix affichés des codes réservés aux lecteurs de Clubic. La Xiaomi Pad 7 en 8 Go + 256 Go y passe à 202,35 € avec le code CLU40, sous les 228,28 € relayés début octobre, pour une tablette dont l’écran reste le premier argument face à son successeur.
Présentée au MWC en mars 2025, la Xiaomi Pad 7 associe un écran LCD de 11,2 pouces en 3,2K à 144 Hz, une puce Snapdragon 7+ Gen 3 et une batterie de 8 850 mAh. Xiaomi l’avait lancée à 481 € dans cette version 8 Go + 256 Go.
Pendant le 11.11, AliExpress l’affiche à 242,35 €, et le code CLU40 retire 40 € dès 229 € d’achat pour la ramener à 202,35 €. Elle est vendue par la boutique MixTech Europe Store et expédiée depuis la France. L’offre vise d’abord ceux qui cherchent une grande tablette familiale pour lire et regarder, sans dépasser 210 €.
La Xiaomi Pad 7 en 8 Go + 256 Go est à 202,35 € sur AliExpress avec le code CLU40, au lieu des 242,35 € affichés pendant le Single Day.
Pourquoi choisir la Xiaomi Pad 7 ?
- Un écran pensé pour lire : La dalle de 11,2 pouces au format 3:2 affiche 3 200 × 2 136 pixels, plus proche d’une page que du 16:9 d’un téléviseur. Notebookcheck y a mesuré environ 850 cd/m², et le 144 Hz fluidifie le défilement.
- Une batterie qui tient les longues journées : Les 8 850 mAh ont dépassé 18 heures en navigation Wi-Fi dans les mesures de Notebookcheck. La charge à 45 W récupère 54 % en 30 minutes selon Computerwoche, mais le chargeur n’est pas fourni.
- Un vrai écran de salon : Quatre haut-parleurs compatibles Dolby Atmos accompagnent la définition 3,2K, dans un châssis de 6,2 mm d’épaisseur pour environ 500 g.
Du canapé au bureau, une tablette à partager à la maison
Sa place naturelle est le salon : une série sans casque grâce aux quatre haut-parleurs, une BD ou un magazine numérique qui remplit mieux l’écran au format 3:2. Le Snapdragon 7+ Gen 3 se situe au niveau d’un smartphone milieu de gamme, ce qui suffit à la navigation, à la vidéo et aux jeux courants. Lancée sous Android 15 avec la surcouche HyperOS 2, elle embarque des outils d’IA pour écrire ou retoucher des photos. En option, le stylet Focus Pen à 99,90 € et deux claviers la transforment en carnet de notes ou en outil de bureautique légère.
Elle conviendra à une famille qui veut une tablette commune, à un étudiant qui annote ses cours ou à un grand lecteur de PDF. Elle reste en revanche liée au Wi-Fi, faute de version 4G ou 5G, ce qui limite son intérêt loin d’une box sans partage de connexion. Les joueurs exigeants devront baisser les réglages sur les titres les plus lourds, et l’absence de lecteur d’empreintes, de prise jack et de port microSD se fera sentir chez certains. Le LCD, enfin, n’offre pas les noirs profonds d’un écran OLED.
Pad 7 ou Pad 8 : ce que valent 160 € d’écart
Dans notre comparatif des meilleures tablettes, c’est son successeur, le Xiaomi Pad 8, qui décroche le titre de meilleur rapport qualité/prix, avec une note de 7/10 et un prix indicatif d’environ 365 €. Il passe à une puce Snapdragon 8s Gen 4, plus haut de gamme, avec un écran LCD 144 Hz de 11 pouces. À 202,35 €, la Pad 7 coûte donc plus de 160 € de moins pour une expérience d’écran comparable. L’écart se justifie surtout pour ceux qui veulent davantage de puissance en jeu.
✅ Les points forts
- Écran 3,2K au format 3:2, jusqu’à 144 Hz
- Plus de 18 heures en navigation Wi-Fi selon Notebookcheck
- Quatre haut-parleurs compatibles Dolby Atmos
- 202,35 € avec CLU40, sous nos précédents relais
- Expédiée depuis la France
❌ Les limites
- Écran LCD, sans les noirs profonds de l’OLED
- Aucune version 4G ou 5G, ni lecteur d’empreintes
- Pas de prise jack ni de port microSD
- Chargeur non fourni dans la boîte
Le code CLU40 s’applique dès 229 € de panier : la tablette seule suffit, et revient à 202,35 € chez AliExpress avec une expédition depuis la France.
À 202,35 €, la Xiaomi Pad 7 en 256 Go coûte moins de la moitié de ses 481 € de lancement, et 25,93 € de moins qu’à notre relais du début d’octobre. Elle n’est plus la dernière génération, mais son écran 3,2K lumineux et son endurance restent ses meilleurs arguments. Pour équiper un salon ou glisser une tablette sous le sapin, c’est le prix le plus bas que nous ayons relayé pour cette version.
Prévoyez un chargeur USB-C si vous n’en avez pas, et le Focus Pen si la prise de notes compte. Ceux qui veulent jouer aux titres les plus lourds, ou rester connectés hors Wi-Fi, regarderont vers des modèles plus haut de gamme ou dotés d’une version cellulaire. Pour lire, regarder et partager à la maison, la Pad 7 coche l’essentiel à ce tarif.

articles.title: 3I/Atlas: Hinweise auf den Entstehungsort des interstellaren Kometen gefunden
articles.text:
3I/Atlas: Forscher finden Hinweise auf den Entstehungsort des interstellaren Kometen
Die Methan-Signatur von 3I/Atlas ist ungewöhnlich reich an schwerem Wasserstoff, was darauf hindeutet, dass die gefrorenen Bestandteile des Kometen in einer extrem kalten Umgebung um einen anderen Stern, oder in der Wolke, die diesem Stern vorausgegangen war, entstanden sind. Zu dieser Erkenntnis kam ein Forscher:innen-Team rund um Nathan Roth von der American University (USA).
James-Webb-Weltraumteleskop ist der Schlüssel zu den Ergebnissen
Mithilfe des James-Webb-Weltraumteleskops und der Unterstützung des Goddard Space Flight Centers der Nasa konnten sie das Verhältnis von schwerem zu gewöhnlichem Wasserstoff in 3I/Atlas bestimmen. Es ist etwa 13-mal so hoch wie bei dem Kometen 67P/Tschurjumow-Gerassimenko, der wahrscheinlich aus unserem Sonnensystem stammt. Ihre in der Fachzeitschrift Nature Astronomy veröffentlichten Ergebnisse bieten Wissenschaftler:innen eine seltene Gelegenheit, die frühe Chemie eines anderen Planetensystems zu untersuchen.
Schwerer Wasserstoff, auch Deuterium genannt, besitzt ein zusätzliches Neutron im Atomkern. Er kann in einem Methanmolekül den Platz eines gewöhnlichen Wasserstoffatoms einnehmen. Dieser Austausch verändert die Infrarot-Signatur des Moleküls, was es Astronom:innen ermöglicht, zwischen den beiden Varianten zu unterscheiden.
Beeindruckender Methan-Wert gemessen
Das James-Webb-Teleskop beobachtete 3I/Atlas am 22. und 23. Dezember 2025, als sich der Komet etwa 2,4-mal so weit von der Sonne entfernt befand wie die Erde. Das Teleskop untersuchte dabei das Infrarotlicht aus der Koma – jener Gaswolke, die den eisigen Kern des Kometen umgibt. Entdeckt wurde dabei ein Deuterium-Wasserstoff-Verhältnis (D/H-Verhältnis) von etwa 3,2 Prozent im Methan.
„Dieses D/H-Verhältnis übertrifft jeden anderen Wert, der jemals für Methan im Sonnensystem gemessen wurde“, schreiben die Autor:innen der Studie. Der Vergleich mit dem Kometen 67P, einem Kometen der Jupiter-Familie, ist besonders aufschlussreich, da dies der einzige weitere Komet ist, in dem deuteriumhaltiges Methan nachgewiesen wurde.
Das sind die 18 besten Bilder aus dem Weltall:
Entstand 3I/Atlas in einer kalten Wolke oder rund um einen entstehenden Stern?
Das D/H-Verhältnis (Deuterium-Wasserstoff-Verhältnis) im Methan war etwa dreimal so hoch wie der Wert, der zuvor im Wasser von 3I/Atlas gemessen wurde. Die Forscher:innen vermuten, dass das Methan möglicherweise erst später entstanden ist: zu einem Zeitpunkt, an dem die chemische Umgebung bereits mehr Zeit hatte, den schweren Wasserstoff anzureichern.
Laut den Wissenschaftler:innen passen ihre Ergebnisse gut zu der Theorie, wonach 3I/Atlas in einer kalten Wolke oder in der Umgebung eines entstehenden Sterns entstanden sein könnte. Und in einer Region mit vergleichsweise wenigen Elementen, die schwerer als Helium sind, und einer hohen Intensität an kosmischer Strahlung. Diese hochenergetischen Teilchen tragen dazu bei, jene chemischen Reaktionen in Gang zu setzen, die zu einer Anreicherung von Deuterium in Molekülen führen. Dies liefert laut der Wissenschaftswebseite phys.org zwar eine plausible Entstehungsgeschichte für 3I/Atlas, lässt aber noch keinen eindeutigen Geburtsort bestimmen.

articles.title: Beyond funding: Why every startup founder needs an insurance plan
articles.text:
Beyond funding: Why every startup founder needs an insurance plan
From personal term insurance to keyman and employee cover, here's how insurance solutions can help entrepreneurs protect their families, businesses, and teams.
Most founders are equity-rich and cash-poor, with household finances quietly tied to the venture: personal guarantees on business loans, savings deployed into the company, a spouse’s income covering monthly basics. That structure makes personal term insurance more urgent for a founder than for a salaried peer, not less. If the founder dies, the family inherits illiquid equity and live liabilities at the same moment, and only a large, immediate payout resolves that.
The sizing rule also needs adjusting. The standard guidance of 10-15X annual income understates the need for entrepreneurs who deliberately pay themselves a modest salary. Anchor instead to household expenses, outstanding personal guarantees, and the real cost of the family’s next 15 years. Self-employed applicants should expect income documentation requests, ITRs, and bank statements rather than salary slips, and treat that as an administrative step rather than a reason to postpone.
What Does ABSLI Super Term Plan Offer a Founder?
The payout structure matters for founders carrying loan guarantees. A lump sum clears liabilities at once, while the monthly income option keeps a household running for a defined period, and ABSLI Super Term Plan allows the two to be combined, with between 10% and 90% of the sum assured taken as income and the balance as a lump sum.
What is keyman insurance and who needs it?
Ask your co-founder a direct question: if either of you died this quarter, does the company survive the next funding conversation? Investors ask themselves the same thing, which is why keyman insurance appears in diligence checklists and shareholder agreements.
ABSLI Keyman Insurance Policy is a life insurance policy purchased by an employer on the life of a key employee, based on the insurable interest an employer has in that person. The payout gives the business capital to stabilise, hire replacement leadership, and reassure the cap table at the moment confidence is scarcest.
For partnership firms, ABSLI Partnership Insurance Scheme addresses a related risk: on the death of an insured partner, the firm has liquidity available to purchase the deceased partner’s share, so working capital is not diverted and surviving partners are not required to bring in additional funds. Cover is assessed against the firm’s net worth, including each partner’s share of capital, share of profit and share in goodwill.
How does employer-employee cover work for a startup team?
This is the part that belongs in your next HR planning cycle. Under ABSLI Employer - Employee Insurance Scheme, the employer proposes and owns a policy on the life of an employee, and assigns it to the employee after a defined period. Assignment can be absolute, transferring ownership at issuance, or conditional, transferring ownership once terms set by the employer are met. Any company, proprietorship firm, LLP, trust, NGO or society with a genuine employer-employee relationship is eligible.
The return on that spend is talent economics. Startups ask employees to accept risk, and benefits that protect an employee’s family are how a company signals it takes that trade seriously. The structure also matures with the company: the arrangement that covers a handful of employees becomes the foundation of the full benefits programme a later-stage HR lead will build. All products other than child plans can be offered under the scheme, and all riders other than Waiver of Premium can be attached.
Which ABSLI solution fits which need?
What should a founder do first?
- Buy personal term cover now, sized to household expenses and outstanding personal guarantees rather than declared salary, while age and health are on your side.
- Add keyman cover once the company has revenue or a valuation worth protecting.
- Put employer-employee cover in place for the team as an early, deliberate retention investment.
- Review all three annually, because cover set at seed stage rarely matches the liabilities of a Series A company.
- Disclose health, income and business details fully at proposal stage, since complete disclosure is what ensures a smooth claim later.
Key Takeaways
- Founders need personal term cover first, sized to household expenses and personal guarantees rather than declared salary.
- ABSLI Super Term Plan offers three plan options, entry from 18 to 65 years and a minimum sum assured of Rs 25,00,000.
- ABSLI Keyman Insurance Policy allows a company to insure a key employee, with the company as the policy owner.
- ABSLI Partnership Insurance Scheme helps a firm fund the purchase of a deceased partner’s share.
- ABSLI Employer-Employee Insurance Scheme lets an employer insure employees as a welfare and retention measure.
- Premiums paid under Keyman and Employer-Employee arrangements may be claimed as a deduction under Section 37(1), subject to applicable tax laws.
- GST is not applicable on individual life insurance premiums.

articles.title: Fintech platform Sageworks taken offline after suspected cyberattack
articles.text:
Financial technology company Abrigo has restored its Sageworks risk management application, except for borrower-facing capabilities, following an outage triggered by "irregular activity" in its environment.
On October 30, the company began emergency maintenance and took the Sageworks application offline to investigate suspicious activity detected earlier that day, with the outage continuing through the weekend.
Abrigo provides cloud-based software and analytics solutions for community banks and credit unions across the United States. According to the company, it serves more than 2,400 entities.
Its Sageworks product is a software platform that helps lenders process loan applications, analyze borrowers’ finances, assess creditworthiness, and monitor loan portfolios.
Due to its nature, Sageworks handles sensitive information, including banking customer details.
"We identified irregular activity in our environment, and, out of abundance of caution, we disabled the Sageworks application at approximately 11:25 am ET," the company said on Friday.
In status updates over the weekend, Abrigo said its investigation was ongoing but did not disclose details about the nature of the incident.
The incident impacted the following services: Online Portal Now, Sageworks Analyst, and Sageworks API.
In its latest update today, the company said that most of the Sageworks functionality had been restored, with the exception of borrower-facing features.
BleepingComputer reached out to Abrigo for more details, but we have not received a response by publication time. Until the nature of the incident is disclosed, it is unclear if the outage was caused by a breach or a technical issue.
Earlier this year, someone allegedly part of the ShinyHunters extortion group claimed an attack on Abrigo, saying that they stole 1.7 million Salesforce records containing personally identifiable information and various internal corporate data.
The threat actor said at the time that they exfiltrated full names, email addresses, phone numbers, employee and account data.
Although a data breach has not been confirmed, some cybersecurity researchers advised banks and credit unions using Abrigo's solutions to rotate the API keys for the Sageworks platform.

articles.title: Un nuevo estudio rastrea la famosa ‘Noche estrellada’ de Van Gogh hasta un cielo nocturno real de 1889
articles.text:
El cielo de “La noche estrellada” parece responder a una noche concreta. Por ejemplo, el 22 de julio de 1889 en Saint-Rémy-de-Provence (sur de Francia). Un equipo surcoreano ha analizado el cielo que representa y lo ha comparado con el real de aquel verano. Se trata de la mejor opción que han encontrado. Es decir, que era el cielo que podía verse entonces, pero eso no implica que fuera el día en el que pintó el cuadro.
En el estudio publicado en Scientific Reports (22 de octubre de 2026) proponen una revisión de la cronología habitual. El primero de los autores es Elijah Jeong-hyun Kim; además de ser doctorando en la Universidad Kyung Hee, dirige una empresa dedicada a telescopios. ¿Cuánto de observación hay en este cielo?
Una de las claves es la luna. Los investigadores tienen en cuenta que en el cuadro aparece menguante. También que Venus ocupa una posición concreta y que las Híades (un grupo de estrellas de la constelación de Tauro) están juntas. Todo ello es consistente con amaneceres cercanos al 22 de julio. Además, han cruzado datos meteorológicos con las cartas de Van Gogh y proponen que el cielo se corresponde con un momento aproximadamente un mes después de lo habitualmente aceptado.
Elijah fue a Francia en dos ocasiones en 2019 (a mediados de junio y alrededor del 22 de julio) para ver en primera persona cómo era el cielo en esos momentos. “Los cielos nunca son iguales. Siempre hay algo diferente”, explica Kim. Dice que él cree que Van Gogh tuvo en cuenta estos cambios; de hecho, no es necesario que sea una sola noche, puede haber días cercanos.
Otra de las claves son las menciones que hace a las cigarras. Los autores relacionan estas menciones con el calor de julio. Su análisis de las cartas sitúa más adelante en ese mes el momento de una crisis que sufrió el artista. Estos son argumentos históricos (basados en una interpretación de los documentos y de las fechas) que se cruzan con la reconstrucción del cielo.
José Luis Aragón (Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México) es físico y ha estudiado el cuadro, pero no ha participado en esta investigación. “Aun así, vería la fecha de julio como una hipótesis intrigante más que como una respuesta definitiva”.
En la ficha del MoMA (donde se conserva el cuadro) sigue apareciendo junio de 1889. En el museo explican que se trata de un cuadro pintado durante el día (en varias sesiones) a partir de una visión nocturna. El pueblo que aparece en el fondo (bajo las colinas) es de otras vistas (no era visible desde su ventana).
El software para reconstruir el cielo de 1889
El software principal con el que han trabajado es TheSkyX 10.5.0. Han contrastado sus configuraciones con Stellarium 25.2.0. Las posiciones de los planetas y el Sol las han contrastado con las efemérides DE441 de la NASA. Los investigadores admiten que esto no permite saber cuándo comenzó a pintarse o si hubo algún retoque posterior.
Algunas de estas herramientas son accesibles a todo el mundo. Stellarium es un planetario (software) gratuito y de código abierto. Hay versiones para Windows, macOS y Linux. Permite mostrar cómo es el cielo en un momento dado e incluso es posible modificar la velocidad a la que pasa el tiempo (para simular el movimiento aparente de los astros).
También existe un sistema de la NASA (Horizons) que permite obtener tablas de posición para un observador en un lugar concreto. Incluyen datos de visibilidad, documentan la altura sobre el horizonte, salidas y puestas e incluso tienen marcadores de crepúsculo. De esta manera podemos analizar si es cierta una afirmación más específica que el parecido global de dos imágenes.
Este servicio está pensado también para el gran público (no solo para investigadores o planificadores de misiones). Una tabla de posiciones permite verificar esta posibilidad, aunque para la fecha de una pincelada hacen falta otros tipos de evidencias.
Por otro lado, también hay que considerar la visibilidad. En Genbeta ya hablamos del mapa de contaminación lumínica para saber dónde es posible ver bien el cielo. En una reconstrucción histórica hay que considerar por separado dónde está la estrella (calculado) y las condiciones de visibilidad.

articles.title: Hack de Binance : le FBI accuse la Corée du Nord du plus gros vol de l’histoire de la crypto
articles.text:
Ce samedi 31 octobre, deux jours après l’attaque éclair sur Binance, le FBI a officiellement attribué l’opération à la Corée du Nord. Dans un avis publié sur son site, l’agence fédérale américaine pointe du doigt TraderTraitor, une unité de pirates au service du gouvernement nord-coréen, et qui fait partie de l’organisation Lazarus.
« La République populaire démocratique de Corée (Corée du Nord) est responsable du vol de plus de 6 milliards de dollars d’actifs virtuels sur la plateforme d’échange de cryptomonnaies Binance, aux alentours du 29 octobre 2026 », écrit le FBI.
La plupart des experts de la crypto et de la blockchain abondent dans le même sens que le FBI. C’est donc loin d’être une surprise. Dès le lendemain du vol, la société d’analyse TRM Labs attribuait l’attaque à TraderTraitor « avec une confiance élevée ». Chainalysis, autre spécialiste de la blockchain, a d’ailleurs remarqué que les fonds volés à Binance se sont mélangés à ceux dérobés à Bitget le mois dernier. Or, la plateforme avait été victime des pirates de TraiterTraitor.
 The FBI is releasing information advising the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion USD in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, on or about October 29, 2026. The FBI refers to this specific North Korean malicious cyber activity as “TraderTraitor.”
The FBI, together with partners at the USSS and IRS-CI, has observed TraderTraitor actors converting stolen assets primarily into Ethereum (ETH). It is expected these assets will then be further laundered by converting them using DeFi and instant swap services as they prepare them for further laundering stages.
How You Can Help:
FBI, USSS, and IRS-CI are urging private sector entities including THORNode operators, RPC node operators, instant exchanges, DeFi services, blockchain analytics firms, and other virtual asset service providers to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder these stolen assets.
A list of addresses associated with this activity is available here: https://t.co/g0oIWx0WeD
— FBI Cyber Branch (@FBICyberBranch) October 31, 2026
Des centaines d’adresses pour brouiller les pistes
Le FBI a aussi publié la liste des adresses utilisées par les pirates pour déplacer les cryptomonnaies volées. Les enquêteurs ont débusqué plusieurs centaines d’adresses Ethereum, 19 adresses Bitcoin et une adresse sur la blockchain Solana. Le FBI demande aux géants de l’industrie crypto de bloquer toute transaction liée à ces adresses. Les plateformes d’échange, les services de finance décentralisée (DeFi), les sociétés d’analyse de la blockchain ou encore les opérateurs de THORChain, un service d’échange entre blockchains déjà utilisé par les pirates, sont encouragés à geler les fonds.
Tout le monde risque de ne pas coopérer. C’est le cas de THORChain. Après le hack de Bybit en 2025, les pirates nord-coréens y ont échangé plus d’un milliard de dollars d’ether contre du bitcoin. Les opérateurs ont envisagé de bloquer les transactions pour venir en aide aux autorités, mais un développeur du projet a démissionné en signe de protestation. Environ 2,8 milliards de dollars ont cependant déjà été gelés, selon les investigations menées par Chainalysis.
« C’est un braquage de banque, à la vitesse d’Internet. Mais nous pouvons aussi suivre ces fonds à la trace en temps réel pour construire des enquêtes. C’est le jeu du chat et de la souris », résume Ari Redbord, responsable des politiques publiques chez TRM Labs.
Il est particulièrement complexe de suivre les fonds dérobés à Binance. D’après Chainalysis, les pirates utilisent déjà des milliers d’adresses à travers de nombreux réseaux différents. Dans les semaines à venir, ils pourraient utiliser des dizaines de milliers d’adresses différentes pour brouiller les pistes.
Un gang au service du régime nord-coréen
TraderTraitor n’en est pas à son coup d’essai. Rattaché au collectif criminel Lazarus, le groupe avait déjà dérobé 1,5 milliard de dollars à la plateforme Bybit en février 2025 et 292 millions de dollars au protocole KelpDAO quelques mois plus tard. L’an dernier, les pirates nord-coréens ont volé 2,02 milliards de dollars à des plateformes crypto, estime Chainalysis. Comme l’explique le chercheur Ari Redbord de TRM Labs, les fonds volés permettent à la Corée du Nord de financer une partie de ses activités, dont « la prolifération des armes et d’autres activités déstabilisatrices
». On sait notamment que les cryptomonnaies servent à financer les missiles balistiques du régime.
Pour arriver à leurs fins, les pirates nord-coréens se font souvent passer pour des recruteurs, ou n’hésitent pas à se faire embaucher comme salariés dans les entreprises qu’ils ciblent. Une fois dans la place, ils n’ont même pas besoin de casser le chiffrement des portefeuilles crypto. Il suffit de manipuler un tiers et d’en compromettre l’ordinateur. Dans le cas de Binance, la cyberattaque aurait débuté par le piratage de l’ordinateur portable d’un ingénieur avec un logiciel malveillant.
« Le maillon faible d’une cyberattaque reste l’humain, et les attaquants le savent parfaitement », souligne Silviu Stahie, analyste chez Bitdefender.

articles.title: Google and Meta Open-source TorchTPU to Bring Native PyTorch Support to Google TPUs
articles.text:
TorchTPU is an open-source project developed by Google in collaboration with Meta that provides a native PyTorch backend for Google TPUs. It enables PyTorch workloads to execute on TPU hardware with minimal code modifications, supporting eager and compiled execution, distributed computing, and hardware-specific optimizations.
Google began enabling PyTorch workloads to run on TPUs in 2020 through PyTorch/XLA, which leveraged JAX, XLA, and lazy tensors. According to Google, this approach had significant shortcomings:
Crucially, PyTorch/XLA required intrusive source-code modifications to explicitly define compilable regions, suffered from severe compile-time latency, lacked support for PyTorch's native imperative (“eager”) execution mode, and lagged in supporting emerging distributed computing primitives within the PyTorch ecosystem.
TorchTPU takes a fundamentally different approach, making eager execution a top priority, and enabling existing PyTorch workloads to run out with minor code modifications.
Specifically, migrating from GPUs to TPUs involves replacing the cuda device with tpu and the nccl distributed backend with tpu_dist. Alternatively, developers can use the new torch.accelerator.current_accelerator API to identify the available accelerator, as shown in the following snippet.
import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
def main():
    device = torch.device("cuda") # -> device = torch.accelerator.current_accelerator
    dist.init_process_group(backend="nccl") # -> dist.init_process_group()
    rank = dist.get_rank()
    word_size = dist.get_world_size()
    ...
    model = model.to(device)
    ...
TorchTPU support three eager execution modes: strict, debug, and DeferAndFuse. The latter is a new hybrid eager/compiled execution mode that Google claims "can be 50% or more faster than Strict Eager while reducing peak HBM memory".
To test TorchTPU's ability to run existing PyTorch models with no modifications, Google built an integration pipeline to evaluate about 5,000 Hugging Face models across 500+ architectures in both eager and compiled modes on TPU hardware generations starting from v5e.
We use a robust testing methodology grounded in corpus stratification and balanced architectural selection. Our approach relies on a two-tiered selection process designed to balance real-world adoption with broad architectural diversity, avoiding redundant testing of minor variations while ensuring real production weights are thoroughly evaluated.
To validate TorchTPU's performance, Google ran a 30-billion parameter Muse Glimmer model implemented in standard PyTorch. On a single TPUv7 chip, inference throughput reached 25.7k token/s at 5120 sequence length and 22.4k token/s at 10,240 sequence length. For training, using four TPUv7 chips, throughput reached 5.6k token/s and 4.6k token/s at 5120 and 10,240 sequence length, respectively.
Google also conducted experiments using Qwen3 MoE 235B for training workloads, scaling from 1,024 to 8,192 TPUv7 chips. For inference, Google reported competitive performance-per-dollar for large-scale MoE workloads using vLLM.
Commenting on the announcement, Hacker News user tingkuanpei observed:
Very interesting work. Google should have done this a long time ago. PyTorch's ecosystem is just so rich.
Other users pointed out that beyond offering TPUs through GCP, Google sells them to "enterprise client for on premises deployments", which include Anthropic and in Meta following potentially in the future.
TorchTPU is still at an early stage and therefore in continuous evolution. The project's roadmap include work on dynamic shapes, compilation performance, operator coverage, reinforcement learning, and quantization. For further details, make sure to read the original announcement, which provides a more comprehensive view of TorchTPU's architecture and scope.

articles.title: Votre écran d'accueil Android va changer : Google revoit les icônes de Messages, Téléphone et Contacts — Frandroid
articles.text:
Dans un court billet publié ce lundi 2 novembre sur son blog officiel, Google annonce de nouvelles icônes pour trois de ses applications de communication : Google Messages, Téléphone et Google Contacts. Les formes ne bougent pas : la bulle de Messages, le combiné de Téléphone et la silhouette de Contacts restent bleus sur un rond blanc. En fait, Google remplace surtout les aplats de bleu par un dégradé discret qui tire vers le violet, aux contours nets, et retouche un peu les courbes.
Si vous utilisez ces applications sur votre smartphone Android, votre écran d’accueil va donc changer légèrement dans les prochaines semaines.
Un dégradé hérité du « G » de Google
Google explique vouloir aligner ces icônes sur le reste de ses applications et sur son logo. Il faut dire que le « G » multicolore est passé au dégradé en mai 2025, avant que Google n’en fasse l’emblème de toute l’entreprise en septembre de la même année. Depuis, la marque redessine ses applications par vagues. Les icônes de Workspace y sont passées en mai, puis celles de plusieurs applications Pixel (Appareil photo, Horloge, Calculatrice, Météo…) en août, avec le lancement des Pixel 11.
    Pour aller plus loin
Google change ses icônes, et ce n’est clairement pas un hasard
            
Google précise aussi que le fonctionnement des trois applications ne change pas d’un iota. Les nouveautés de Messages passent par d’autres mises à jour, comme la nouvelle interface pensée pour une utilisation à une main, déployée depuis août.
Les nouvelles icônes arrivent par le Google Play Store, sans aucune manipulation de votre part. Celle de Messages est déjà visible dans la dernière bêta de l’application, et les versions web de Messages et de Contacts devraient suivre.

articles.title: Éclairage LED et fonction hiver : ce ventilateur de plafond Cecotec passe à 57,99 €
articles.text:
Le ventilateur de plafond Cecotec EnergySilence Aero 5600 Classic Iron&Black est à 57,99 € (-34 %)
Amazon propose le Cecotec Aero 5600 Classic Iron&Black à 57,99 €, soit 34 % sous l’ancien prix affiché. Il associe ventilation réversible et éclairage LED.
L’économie atteint 29,66 € par rapport à l’ancien prix de 87,65 €. Amazon indique également un plus bas sur 30 jours de 89,90 €, soit une baisse d’environ 35 %. Le produit est vendu et expédié par Amazon. Attention au délai : la livraison gratuite affichée est prévue le 26 décembre, avec une option accélérée au 5 novembre selon les conditions proposées.
Trois pales de 132 cm et six vitesses
Ce ventilateur de plafond utilise un moteur à courant continu de 40 W. Ses trois pales couvrent un diamètre de 132 cm, avec six vitesses pour ajuster le brassage de l’air. Son installation nécessite donc de prévoir suffisamment d’espace autour des pales.
La télécommande fournie permet de régler le fonctionnement à distance. Une minuterie propose un arrêt automatique après 1, 2, 4 ou 8 heures, tandis que l’éclairage LED intégré remplit aussi le rôle de plafonnier.
Une rotation réversible pour l’été et l’hiver
Le mode hiver inverse le sens de rotation pour favoriser la circulation de l’air chaud accumulé au plafond. Il complète ainsi le chauffage sans produire lui-même de chaleur, ni garantir une économie chiffrée.
La fiche Amazon affiche une moyenne de 4,2/5 sur 84 évaluations, réparties entre plusieurs finitions. Cette appréciation globale ne permet toutefois pas de préjuger du niveau sonore à chaque vitesse.

articles.title: Stablecoins in Africa are held back by spending
articles.text:
Stablecoins already move money in and out of Africa faster and more cheaply than banks. What keeps them from the mainstream is that people still can’t spend them easily, and regulators still can’t see where they go.
That was the view from “The Adoption Gap”, a panel at Moonshot by TechCabal on Thursday, October 29. Shalom Osiadi, founder and CEO of Esca Finance, a foreign exchange company serving businesses in emerging markets, and Demilade Olugbenga, B2B business development manager at Breet, a Nigerian crypto payments platform, discussed with moderator Nnanna Ijezie why adoption still lags.
“Some people use stablecoins, but they’re not able to spend them in the applications they use daily,” Olugbenga said. “Say I’m a freelancer and someone wants to pay me in stablecoins. If I look around and there’s no stablecoin option, I will tell whoever is paying me, ‘Sorry, I can’t accept this now.’”
Sub-Saharan Africa received more than $205 billion in on-chain crypto value between July 2024 and June 2025, with Nigeria taking in $92.1 billion, according to Chainalysis. Stablecoins made up about 43% of the region’s crypto volume over that period.
Olugbenga said sending anything from $5 to $500,000 on Breet costs 10 cents, while a bank transfer can take days and eat up to 8% of the amount. Banks charge that much, Osiadi said, because African currencies can move before a transfer lands, so they build wide margins into their exchange rates.
Central banks need to know where money comes from, where it goes and how it is used, Osiadi said, and privately issued stablecoins give them no such view. Nigeria has tried two routes. The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) launched the eNaira, Africa’s first central bank digital currency, in October 2021, but in 2023 the International Monetary Fund found that 98.5% of eNaira wallets went unused in any given week.
cNGN, a naira-pegged stablecoin issued by private company WrappedCBDC, went live in February 2025 under the Securities and Exchange Commission’s (SEC) regulatory incubation programme. Osiadi said the CBN should either issue a stablecoin or partner with issuers such as cNGN.
Most of Osiadi’s business customers, he said, do not care what moves their money. Esca, which says it processes between $75 million and $120 million a month for clients including NALA and MoneyGram, routes payments through stablecoins its corporate clients rarely see. “Truth be told, what we’re starting to learn now is nobody really cares,” he said. “They just care about value: how value arrives and how value is created for their business.”
Breet’s next step is making stablecoins spendable where people already pay. If TechCabal wanted Moonshot attendees to pay in stablecoins, Olugbenga said, Breet would take the payment, convert it and settle TechCabal in dollars or naira. “I can sit here and tell you with confidence that stablecoins are solving major business problems that currently exist,” she said.
Both panellists expect adoption to grow as more banks enter the market. “This thing isn’t going anywhere,” Osiadi said, urging regulators to work with operators. The SEC has proposed rules that would require foreign-pegged stablecoins to win its approval before they can be listed or held on regulated Nigerian platforms. However, once those rules land, they will shape the next phase of adoption as much as anything product builders do.

articles.title: Burgos ante la paradoja ferroviaria española: Renfe es un servicio público pero rechaza poner más trenes por su baja rentabilidad
articles.text:
"El tren a Extremadura... que lo lleve Renfe". Las palabras son de Óscar Puente, ministro de Transportes, y tienen más de dos años. Con ellas se quejaba del complicado juego de equilibrios que tiene que hacer la compañía entre sus obligaciones de servicio público y sus obligaciones... comerciales.
Una frase que resume a la perfección lo que se vive en Burgos.
¿Qué ha pasado? Que Renfe no pondrá más frecuencias de AVE para su conexión con Madrid. Así se lo ha hecho saber, según Álvaro Gutiérrez, presidente de la Asociación de Usuarios de AVE de Burgos, en palabras recogidas por Cope. Esta asociación reclama más conexiones rápidas con la capital pero, de momento, parecen que no llegarán.
Según las informaciones recogidas por el medio, Renfe no pondrá más trenes de este tipo porque "no son rentables", algo que la asociación pone en duda asegurando que este verano había días que era complicado comprar un billete porque la oferta estaba casi cubierta en su totalidad.
En Xataka nos hemos puesto en contacto con la compañía pero nos han indicado que no hacen valoraciones sobre este tema.
¿Qué piden? En estos momentos, cada día se puede viajar entre Burgos y Madrid hasta en nueve frecuencias pero sólo en dos de ellas se puede realizar en trayecto en menos de 100 minutos. Sólo los AVE de las 6:40 y de las 17:21 se mueven en estos tiempos de viaje. La mayoría de frecuencias se acercan a las dos horas y en algunos casos hay trenes Intercity que se van por encima de las cuatro horas.
Lo que piden desde Burgos es que se incluya una nueva frecuencia de alta velocidad incluso más madrugadora que la ya existente. La actual llega a la estación de Chamartín a las 8:13. Una opción anterior aumenta las posibilidades de quienes prefieren vivir en Burgos y trabajar en Madrid o llegar a una cita a primera hora de la mañana.
Y es que, hasta hace unos meses, este tren estaba acompañado de un Intercity que salía a las 8:06 pero se ha retrasado temporalmente a las 8:50, desplazando gran parte de los trabajadores y estudiantes que utilizaban esta opción a la franja horaria anterior.
Un corredor con mucho trajín. El corredor Atlántico se ha convertido en uno de los espacios ferroviarios más concurridos en los últimos años desde que la alta velocidad se asentara y, sobre todo, desde que llegara a Galicia. Tanto han subido los desplazamientos que incluso las aerolíneas han retrocedido en favor del tren.
Eso ha llevado a que más y más gente se haya planteado Valladolid como una ciudad para vivir mientras se trabaja en Madrid. El combo del aumento de precios en la ciudad, la compatibilidad con el teletrabajo y el tren de alta velocidad está convirtiendo a la ciudad en una opción más que atractiva para un mayor número de trabajadores.
Burgos quiere ser otra alternativa castellanoleonesa. "Es un poco contradictorio que se esté diciendo a los ciudadanos que tenemos que utilizar menos el vehículo y más el transporte público, y resulta que luego tenemos menos opciones de coger el transporte público que, por ejemplo, otras ciudades", aseguraba Álvaro Gutiérrez a Cope como representante de esta asociación de viajeros.
Ya hemos visto esto. El tren de alta velocidad en el eje atlántico ha sido tan exitoso que Renfe no deja de enfrentarse a demandas de quienes piden más trenes. En Sanabria (Zamora) han peleado por aumentar el número de trenes que paran en su estación. Y es que el verano pasado veían pasar por sus instalaciones 22 trenes pero sólo ocho de ellos hacían parada. A su vez, desde Galicia presionaban para que estos trenes no se detuvieran y el trayecto se redujera en 15 minutos.
El problema era el mismo que se plantea en Burgos. Los vecinos de Zamora aseguraban que el tren pasaba demasiado tarde por la estación y reclamaban una frecuencia más madrugadora. Si la reclamación era la misma, también los objetivos: poder llegar antes a los trabajos, las aulas y las citas médicas en Valladolid o Madrid.
Pero, ¿no es público? Renfe tiene que lidiar con su obligación de prestar servicios como operador público y seguir ofreciendo trenes para mantener sus cuentas como empresa privada saneadas. Con esto último no tienen que lidiar en Ouigo o en Iryo, quienes pueden seleccionar mejor en dónde quieren competir y con cuántos trenes, como se quejaba Puente en 2024.
Esto tiene implicaciones directas sobre dónde y cómo se ofrecen los trenes. Y es que para que Renfe actúe como operador público (como se espera con un Avant madrugador si a la compañía no le salen las cuentas) tiene que ser el Estado el que defina este servicio como tal. Dicho servicio formaría parte de un contrato con la Administración General del Estado, tal y como puedes encontrar en este enlace.
Si las comunidades autónomas, pese a sus reclamaciones, creen que el Estado no ofrece el servicio público que debería utilizando los trenes de Renfe, son las comunidades autónomas las que pueden subvencionar esos trenes.
Y un problema. Señalan en Diario de Burgos que la línea de alta velocidad que llega hasta la ciudad tiene un problema. Herida por la crisis del 2008, la línea de alta velocidad que debía favorecer las conexiones con la capital llegó herida porque el ramal de Venta de Baños es de vía única por lo que se produce un embudo en la cantidad de tráfico que puede soportar. Y no sólo eso, si un tren sufre retrasos tiene su consecuencia en todos los trenes posteriores.
La gran esperanza es que una vez el AVE Madrid-País Vasco llegue, parte de este embudo se desatasque. Según este medio, las previsiones del Ministerio de Transportes es que el tráfico de pasajeros se multiplique por 10 ya que se contará con mayor número de frecuencias y horarios más atractivos.

articles.title: Intel's long-lost Larrabee GPU turns up in storage unit with working drivers, and yes, it can run Crysis
articles.text:
TL;DR: Larrabee prototypes have surfaced before, but almost always as barebones hardware with no drivers to make them work properly. This find includes Intel's own software stack, now preserved on the Internet Archive. For the first time, owners of surviving cards can test what Intel's ill-fated GPU could actually do.
A Reddit user bought the contents of a storage unit at auction and ended up with what looked like an old Intel desktop. Inside was a development machine labeled "Intel Visual Adrenaline," containing an Intel DX58SO motherboard, a working Larrabee prototype and a separate diagnostic card. Larrabee was the x86-based graphics processor Intel hoped would take on Nvidia and ATI before the project collapsed.
When Intel shelved the GPU in late 2009, it said Larrabee would instead be used as a software development platform for high performance computing. This system appears to be that kind of hardware.
Also see: The Last Time Intel Tried to Make a Graphics Card
According to the user, getting it to boot took some work. The card produced no image over HDMI and only worked over DVI. The GPU itself is a C0-stepping engineering sample, reportedly one of the later Larrabee revisions. The real find was two USB drives stored with the system that included graphics drivers and documentation. The owner has since backed them up and published them on the Internet Archive.
But can it run Crysis?
With the drivers installed, Windows 7 recognized the card and DirectX applications ran with hardware acceleration. Then came the obvious test. Running Crysis at 1280×720, medium settings and no anti-aliasing, the card managed just over 17 FPS. A different driver build from the same archives roughly doubled that to around 36 FPS.
Even taken at face value, 36 FPS would have been unimpressive by 2008-2009 standards. Popular GPUs of the era, like the GeForce 8800 GT and Radeon HD 3870 used to do better even at higher resolutions.
The difference in performance between two driver sets is the telling result. Larrabee strung together many simplified x86 cores derived from the Pentium MMX. It lacked fixed-function hardware for rasterization, interpolation and pixel blending, relying instead on raw throughput and promised "game-specific" drivers to make up the difference.
On a GPU that was mostly software, driver maturity was everything. These builds show how much of that software was still unfinished when Intel walked away.
But Larrabee's architecture didn't just disappear. It resurfaced in 2012 as the Xeon Phi coprocessor for supercomputers. When Intel rehired Larrabee architect Tom Forsyth in 2018, he described the project as a "pretty huge success," arguing it was never primarily a graphics card.
Intel wouldn't make another serious run at discrete gaming GPUs until Arc, more than a decade later. Arc launched with drivers that needed a lot of work, which made this history look familiar.
Among the enthusiast crowd, this kind of surviving hardware commands real money. A working Larrabee card without drivers sold for €4,650 on eBay in 2022. Now a complete development system with Intel's own software is freely available. Other owners can finally run their cards, and maybe we'll get to see more benchmarks from the GPU Intel never shipped.

articles.title: Nova TV QNED Mini LED 55" da LG despenca 38% no mês da Black Friday • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Nova TV QNED Mini LED 55″ da LG despenca 38% no mês da Black Friday
LG QNED70 de 55" tem painel 4K com tecnologia avançada de cores e IA que recomenda conteúdos; smart TV da LG sai 38% mais em conta no Pix em oferta da Amazon
A QNED70 Mini LED de 55″ está saindo por apenas R$ 2.478 no Pix na Amazon. A smart TV 4K da LG, que conta com tecnologias avançadas para reproduzir cores mais realistas, recebe desconto de 38% no Black November sobre o preço original de R$ 3.999.
Lançada em 2026, a nova QNED70 conta com um painel 4K QNED de 55″ com tecnologia Mini LED, que oferece maior controle de iluminação e evita “vazamentos” de luz, como os efeitos de backlight bleeding. Ela também resiste mais ao burn-in do que modelos OLED, e oferece qualidade similar com cores realistas, preto profundo e brilho forte.
Seu chip AI α7 4K Gen9 e o sistema operacional webOS 26 contam com recursos de IA, como upscaling e ajustes de imagem com base nas preferências do usuário. Os chatbots Microsoft Copilot e Google Gemini recomendam conteúdos e auxiliam na resolução de problemas.
O controle remoto possui função de mouse e controla um cursor na tela, permitindo navegar por menus de maneira simples. Assim, a experiência de uso durante o consumo de filmes, séries e esportes se torna mais prática.
O webOS 26 suporta várias plataformas de streaming, como Netflix, Globoplay, Apple TV, Disney+ e HBO Max, e jogos na nuvem via Xbox Game Pass e Nvidia GeForce Now, com suporte a controles Bluetooth de latência ultrabaixa (ULL). No entanto, a taxa de 60 Hz é menos que o ideal para o público gamer.
A smart TV LG QNED70 de 55″ (apenas R$ 2.478 no Pix) suporta redes Wi-Fi 5 e Bluetooth 5.3 e possui três portas HDMI, uma Ethernet e uma USB-A, mas a porta S/PDIF legada foi removida.
