articles.title: Stablecoins will not become mainstream by one company
articles.text:
Stablecoins are moving beyond crypto trading to become part of how African businesses move money across borders, panellists said at Moonshot by TechCabal in Lagos.
The session, “The New Payment Backbone”, brought together Mercy Emmanuel, stablecoin and blockchain vertical lead at Flutterwave; Tayo Oviosu, group CEO of Paga; and Ife Johnson, co-founder and CEO of Juicyway. Vivian Mbene, chief operating officer of Breet, moderated.
The case for stablecoins starts with speed. A payment from Lagos to Nairobi has often travelled through correspondent banks in New York or London, taking days to clear and stopping for weekends and bank holidays. Stablecoins, digital tokens pegged to currencies such as the US dollar, skip those stops.
“Stablecoins essentially collapse this journey, as a high-speed train would,” Emmanuel said. “Settlement happens in seconds; it happens in minutes.”
Oviosu said customers care about the result. They want payments that are fast, cheap and arrive when promised, and most will never know a stablecoin was involved. Building stablecoins into everyday payment systems, he said, makes cross-border transfers simpler without asking users to learn anything new.
He also said the industry will have to build it together. “No one company is going to solve it on their own,” he said. “There are going to be multiple companies that have specific solutions that will target different audiences.”
Regulators have shifted too, Oviosu said. “Three, four years ago, who could have said CBN will support stablecoins, and NCC welcomes the idea?” Johnson said companies need to keep building trust with regulators as the market grows.
Shared infrastructure was the panel’s common thread. Stablecoins can make cross-border payments faster and cheaper, but only if payment companies, banks and regulators connect their systems. For millions of African businesses that pay suppliers abroad, that would mean settlement in minutes in place of days.

articles.title: José Navarro, fontanero autónomo: "Si a mí me ofrecieran hoy un trabajo asalariado y me pagaran 4.000 euros al mes, no aceptaría"
articles.text:
Al valorar un cambio de trabajo, el sueldo suele ser una de las primeras cosas que miramos. También miramos el horario, aunque no siempre es fácil saber hasta qué punto nos permitirá organizar el día a nuestra manera. Para José Navarro, esa libertad acabó pesando mucho en la decisión de volver al oficio que había aprendido con su padre.
Este fontanero de Bétera (Valencia) lo cuenta en una entrevista en Sector Oficios: "Si a mí me ofrecieran hoy un trabajo asalariado y me pagaran 4.000 euros al mes, no me iría". Y aclara: "No quiere decir que yo gane más". Prefiere poder organizar su tiempo, incluso si para tomarse un viernes libre tiene que trabajar hasta las nueve de la noche el día anterior.
El fontanero conocía las ventajas de una nómina y un coche de empresa, con el combustible pagado. Había pasado 14 años en una empresa de vehículos, primero aparcando coches y después vendiéndolos. Entre comisiones e incentivos llegó a cobrar 4.300 euros en su mejor mes, aunque la media rondaba los 2.000. De la presión comercial recuerda: "Todos los meses con el objetivo y siempre más y más y más y nunca tienen bastante".
Con la pandemia empezaron los cambios en la empresa y dejó de estar a gusto con las tareas que le asignaban. Fue despedido, en una salida que él también había propiciado, y aprovechó el paro para sacarse el certificado profesional y recuperar conocimientos teóricos. Volvió a trabajar con su padre y, cuando este se jubiló, se puso por su cuenta. Contaba con la cartera de clientes familiar, una ayuda que reconoce al hablar de sus comienzos.
Ya había probado a regresar a la fontanería mucho antes de convertirse en vendedor. En aquella ocasión pidió una excedencia, atraído por la promesa de ganar 2.000 euros al mes trabajando para una aseguradora. Llevaba años sin ejercer y las averías le desbordaron. Aguantó tres semanas y recuerda que llegaba a casa llorando de ansiedad.
"Ser autónomo no es fácil, pero a mí me encanta", asegura. Le cuesta decir que no cuando se le acumulan los encargos: "Yo no puedo estar en dos sitios a la vez". Procura dar fechas que pueda cumplir y tampoco acepta trabajar para clientes que le exigen rebajar el presupuesto.
Con los cobros también es claro: "No acepto pagos ni a 30 ni a 60, ni mucho menos ni a 90". Tampoco trabaja para administraciones de fincas. Y aunque tenga obras grandes, sigue atendiendo pequeñas reparaciones de particulares. Cambiar una cisterna y cobrar 40, 50 o 100 euros al terminar también le viene bien para llevar el negocio.

articles.title: Des hackers ont fait sonner une alerte à la bombe nucléaire sur des milliers de téléphones, en Ukraine puis en Russie
articles.text:
Alerte nucléaire : des hackers piratent les applis d’urgence, des milliers de téléphones sonnent en Ukraine, puis en Russie
Dimanche soir, des téléphones ukrainiens ont affiché une menace radiologique sur Kyiv, avec un message en russe qui se moquait de la panique. Quelques heures plus tard, Moscou reconnaissait le piratage de sa propre application d'urgence, qui annonçait des ogives nucléaires sur tout le pays. Deux nuits de fausses sirènes numériques, aucun auteur identifié.
Tard dans la soirée du dimanche 1er novembre, Air Alert, l'application officielle d'alerte aérienne ukrainienne, a diffusé de fausses alertes radiologiques, chimiques et de combats de rue à Kyiv. L'outil n'a rien d'anecdotique : selon son éditeur Ajax Systems, il compte 6,7 millions d'utilisateurs actifs. Quelques heures plus tard, le ministère russe des Situations d'urgence constatait à son tour le piratage de sa propre application.
Air Alert : une alerte nucléaire rédigée en russe
Parmi les notifications, un message en russe a surgi, relevé par le média indépendant Meduza. Il brandissait l'Oreshnik, un missile hypersonique russe déjà tiré sur Dnipro en 2024, puis sur la région de Lviv en janvier 2026.
	
Salut ! Il y aura une alerte nucléaire sur toute l’Ukraine tout de suite ! Ne vous inquiétez pas, l’Oreshnik [NDLR : missile balistique russe hypersonique de portée intermédiaire, capable d’emporter une charge nucléaire] arrive !
L'application a ensuite signalé une "interférence non autorisée" de personnes extérieures et coupé ses notifications. Le ministère ukrainien de la Transformation numérique a précisé que les sirènes et les autres canaux d'alerte fonctionnaient toujours.
Sur la carte publique des alertes, Kyiv et Zaporijjia arboraient encore à 23 h 10 des symboles de danger radiologique et chimique, sous un bandeau avertissant que ces informations ne correspondaient pas à la réalité.
La capitale disposait d'un filet de sécurité : sa propre application d'alerte, distincte d'Air Alert, a continué de fonctionner normalement, selon les autorités de Kyiv.
	
L'application d'alerte aérienne semble avoir subi une influence ennemie. Il n'y a aucune menace radiologique !
Le Centre ukrainien de communications stratégiques SPRAVDI désigne les Russes comme responsables, sans avancer de preuve à ce stade.
Unfortunately, Russians have hacked the "Air Alert" app.
This is evidenced by the appearance of several unusual alerts. Additionally, there is a message in Russian about "Oreshnik."
If you see strange messages in the app, disregard. pic.twitter.com/fU7KHmKxs1
— SPRAVDI — Stratcom Centre (@StratcomCentre) November 1, 2026
Côté russe, des ogives nucléaires sur toutes les régions
Tôt lundi 2 novembre, le ministère russe des Situations d'urgence a dénoncé une "attaque massive" contre son application. Ses abonnés ont reçu des notifications affirmant que des ogives nucléaires venaient d'être lancées vers toutes les régions du pays. Le ministère a reconnu que les pirates avaient réussi à diffuser de fausses informations, tout en assurant que le système public d'alerte restait intact.
NEW: The Russian Ministry of Emergency Situations says its mobile app was hacked.
The hackers sent a fake alert, warning of a nuclear strike. pic.twitter.com/tQ77L2INfx
— BNO News Live (@BNODesk) November 2, 2026
Aucune revendication n'a été publiée et, selon l'agence Reuters, rien ne permet encore de relier les deux attaques. Reste un constat glaçant : en une seule nuit, deux pays en guerre ont vu l'outil censé protéger leur population se retourner contre elle.

articles.title: Java News Roundup: TornadoVM 8.0, JNoSQL, Endive, JReleaser, JBang, LangChain4j, Quarkus Almanac
articles.text:
This week's Java roundup for October 26th, 2026, features news highlighting: the GA release of TornadoVM 8.0; point releases of JNoSQL, Endive, JBang, JReleaser and LangChain4j; a maintenance release of JobRunr; beta releases of Hibernate ORM and Hibernate Reactive; and introducing the Quarkus Almanac.
JDK 28
Build 22 of the JDK 28 early-access builds was made available this past week featuring updates from Build 21 that include fixes for various issues. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
For JDK 28, developers are encouraged to report bugs via the Java Bug Database.
TornadoVM
The release of TornadoVM 8.0.0 delivers their new pure-Java compiler, known as the TornadoVM Compiler (TC), that compiles Java kernels to CUDA C++, OpenCL C or Metal Shading Language. This replaces the Graal Compiler and Java-Level JVM Compiler Interface (JVMCI) that have been integral to TornadoVM for the past ten years. Developers won’t need to change their code with TC. Classes such as TaskGraph, TornadoExecutionPlan and KernelContext, and annotations such as @Parallel and @Reduce will work with TC.
TornadoVM now takes advantage of GraalVM Native Image and JEP 516, Ahead-of-Time Object Caching with Any GC, under the auspices of Project Leyden for improved startup time. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Eclipse JNoSQL
The release of Eclipse JNoSQL 1.2.0, a compatible implementation of the Jakarta NoSQL and Jakarta Data specifications, ships with notable changes such as: a new VectorTemplate interface to support vector databases; integrations of the Milvus, Qdrant, and Weaviate vector databases for vector search; and new fluent temporal query operations for working with time-series data. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Endive
The release of Endive 1.2.0 provides bug fixes, dependency upgrades and new features such as: support for SIMD instructions, by default, in the interpreter on JDK 11+ without the need to add or configure; improvements to Redline, their experimental, ahead-of-time (AOT) compiler, for more GC-friendly native memory; and continuous improvement on the Endive Component Model, an implementation of the WebAssembly Component Model Design and Specification, to support the Endive runtime. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
JBang
The release of JBang 0.143.0 delivers bug fixes, documentation improvements and two new features: replace use of SDKMan with mise-en-place as the former does not support WindowsOS; and a new unified syntax to execute a specific version of an alias. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
JReleaser
The release of JReleaser 1.27.0 ships with bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: the ability for the support for the JReleaser Tool Provider to be invoked and/or loaded using Java Modules; improved generation of the changelog when GitHub issues are linked inside commit messages; and the removal of XPath to parse POM files as there were issues when packaging JReleaser as a native image. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
LangChain4j
The formal release (along with the thirty-third beta release) of LangChain4j 1.23.0 provides bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: a new OllamaDecisionModel class to support decision models running in Ollama; and a new ConfidenceCascadePlanner class as a confidence cascade decision model-based agentic pattern. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Hibernate
The fourth beta release of Hibernate ORM 8.0.0 delivers bug fixes and notable changes such as: the ability to directly declare the @Filter and @SQLRestriction annotations on associations with the Jakarta Persistence @ManyToOne and @OneToOne annotations that include associations mapped using join tables; and a new @GeneratorOptimizer annotation that selects a "standard optimizer for sequence or table identifier generation directly on an identifier field or getter."
The first and third beta releases of Hibernate Reactive 5.1.0 and 5.0.0, respectively, ship with bug fixes and notable changes such as: a new platform Bill of Materials that manages the versions of Hibernate Reactive, Hibernate ORM and Vert.x SQL clients; and a version check during bootstrap to ensure that Hibernate ORM and Vert.x SQL clients on the classpath aren’t older than the minimum versions it supports. Both of these versions are compatible with Hibernate ORM 8.0.0.Beta4.
JobRunr
The release of JobRunr 9.0.3 provides bug fixes, documentation improvements and dependency upgrades and one new feature that updates the JobHandler class that improves the log messaging from the JobZooKeeper class. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Gradle
The first release candidate of Gradle 9.9.0 delivers notable changes such as: the ability for Kotlin DSL scripts to be incrementally compiled using the Kotlin Build Tools API for improved build performance; new test filters that may be applied to JUnit Platform tests that are not declared as methods; and improvements to the Problems API that provides a predefined hierarchy of problem groups from the Problems interface. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Quarkus Almanac
The Quarkus team has introduced the Quarkus Almanac, a utility for developers to compare changes between two releases. These changes include configuration properties, managed dependencies, extensions, and the API of the classes in the Quarkus jars. Developers can go as far back as November 2018 when Quarkus 0.0.1 was released.

articles.title: Tener tu propia IA en casa se está volviendo un lujo. Y a OpenAI no le viene nada mal
articles.text:
Llevo bastante tiempo detrás de una tarjeta gráfica potente no solo para subir de calidad mis juegos en el PC, también para tener un banco de pruebas para IA local. Y es imposible. Se me antojó una RTX 5090, después fui rebajando expectativas hasta conformarme con modelos mucho más antiguos (tengo un PC con una "modesta" RTX 4060). Pero nada, no tengo presupuesto para conseguir un equipo decente. Todo por la crisis de componentes provocada por la propia IA.
Los números. Que el hardware haya subido es algo que todos los que observamos el mercado de PC ya sabemos. Y se le pueden poner números a esa subida: la RTX 5090, concretamente, ha doblado su precio. En términos generales, las tarjetas gráficas han subido más de un 30 % estos últimos tres meses (datos de Price Squirrel, vía Reddit).
Lo curioso no es solo que se hayan encarecido las gráficas más actuales y potentes, es que hasta la segunda mano ha subido para las generaciones anteriores. Conseguir una RTX 3090 a buen precio es misión imposible, por ejemplo: basta una búsqueda por sitios como Wallapop para descubrir que están por encima de los mil euros (que se paguen es otra historia). Pagar más de mil euros por modelos de seis años, sin saber qué uso han tenido, me parece una locura.
Las tarjetas gráficas son la nueva fiebre del oro. Si renovar solo está al alcance de quienes tienen una cuenta bancaria a prueba de caprichos, el que ya posee una tarjeta tiene un tesoro. Es casi literal, porque la reventa puede generarle un gran beneficio. Y acaba impactando sobre los jugadores, que ven imposible actualizar sus equipos por una especulación generada por el mercado de la IA.
Los centros de datos no utilizan tarjetas gráficas de uso particular, pero sí que canibalizan el esfuerzo de la fabricación de componentes. A marcas como Samsung, SK Hynix o Micron les sale más rentable fabricar HBM para los aceleradores de IA que GDDR para tarjetas gráficas. Esta decisión logra que toda la tecnología se encarezca, especialmente las tarjetas gráficas.
De rebote, beneficio para quienes provocan la crisis. Los componentes también les salen más caros a los centros de datos, pero estos tienen una ventaja: las compras en alto volumen y a futuro. Con esto logran rebajar parte del incremento en los costes. Además, la idea es que recuperen esta inversión con beneficios, al menos en teoría. La práctica no lo deja tan claro.
Las tarjetas gráficas no solo permiten jugar a una calidad superior, también ejecutar modelos de IA locales para así esquivar la nube. No en todos los modelos funciona igual de bien la ejecución, las RTX de Nvidia son especialmente buenas en eso (benditos CUDA). Y, debido al incremento en sus precios, quienes buscamos una tarjeta para modelos locales terminamos dándolo por imposible. A empresas como OpenAI, xAI y Anthropic les viene perfecto. Como tokens llovidos del cielo.
Sam Altman no quiere IA local. Lo dejó bien claro la semana pasada: "La inferencia local es una terrible asignación de recursos escasos". Los grandes magnates de la IA quieren que usemos sus herramientas, no las que nos ofrecen modelos open source que funcionan en los equipos locales. Su miedo a que seamos autosuficientes es lógico: gran parte del uso que le damos a ChatGPT o Claude podríamos cubrirlo perfectamente con una buena tarjeta y modelos como GLM, DeepSeek o Qwen. Por eso a Sam no le gusta.
Que el hardware esté imposible les viene perfecto. Dudo mucho que pueda cubrirse todo el espectro de uso con modelos locales. Aun así, tener esa opción añade mayor libertad a los usuarios, justo lo contrario de lo que buscan las grandes empresas, aquellas que han invertido paladas de dinero en entrenar a sus LLM. El retorno de la inversión debería quedar a la altura. A diferencia de DeepSeek o Z.ai, que publican sus modelos en abierto y también cobran por usarlos en su nube, OpenAI o Anthropic solo dan acceso a través de sus servidores.
Las mismas empresas que han hecho subir de precio las tarjetas gráficas están de enhorabuena por la enorme barrera de entrada que plantean ahora esas tarjetas. No es algo buscado, pero así se aseguran de que los usuarios no puedan ejecutar modelos locales con suficiente capacidad y necesiten contratar ChatGPT, Claude y compañía. Es una relación causa/efecto inesperada que solo viene bien a una parte. Como suele ocurrir, los usuarios somos los más perjudicados.

articles.title: MazeBolt launches native RADAR deployment for Akamai DDoS protection customers - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
MazeBolt launches native RADAR deployment for Akamai DDoS protection customers
Distributed denial-of-service testing company MazeBolt Technologies Ltd. today launched a native deployment of its RADAR validation platform for customers of Akamai Technologies Inc.
Enterprises using Akamai’s DDoS protection can have continuous testing running within hours without taking services offline. The release targets the configuration gaps that open up as a company adds services, application programming interfaces and regions behind its DDoS protection.
Akamai setups are rarely tested independently against each of those changes, according to MazeBolt, and a gap can stay hidden until an attack reaches a login page or a payment flow. Founder and Chief Executive Matthew Andriani said testing “even a few times a year cannot keep pace” now that artificial intelligence projects keep adding new services and APIs.
Akamai’s own State of the Internet report, published in March, found that Layer 7 DDoS attacks rose 104% over two years, and the company blamed part of that growth on attack tools that use AI to make web applications and APIs easier to hit.
RADAR fires simulated attacks at Akamai-protected services from inside the customer’s own environment. The attack library covers known vectors as well as the AI-orchestrated and AI-generated attacks MazeBolt added with its VectorAI module in June. When RADAR first tests a production environment, about 37% of attack vectors get past the protection already in place, based on MazeBolt’s data from initial deployments.
Each run ends in a report with remediation guidance written for the specific protection vendor, and RADAR repeats the test once a fix is in place. “Deployed protection is not proven protection,” said Eyal Rahimi, vice president of engineering at MazeBolt. Customers also need to be able to prove which gaps they have closed, Rahimi said.
Most financial institutions test far less often. In a MazeBolt survey of 300 of their security leaders last year, 86% said they test their DDoS defenses once a year or less. Akamai reported in May that the median duration of Layers 3 and 4 DDoS attacks on the sector has risen 738% since 2024.
John Grady, chief analyst at Omdia, said misconfigurations and out-of-date rules remain the source of many security incidents. “DDoS is no different,” Grady said. “It is a critical area where security teams must ensure protection is current, because successful attacks impact availability and directly affect the bottom line.”
Native Layer 7 support for Akamai environments is available today to all RADAR customers. Cloudflare Inc., F5 Inc. and Radware Ltd. are among the other mitigation vendors whose products RADAR already tests across scrubbing centers, on-premises equipment and cloud services.

Começou a Black November, o mês oficial da Black Friday. O Magazine Luiza já está com cupons de até R$ 300 para você economizar na compra de celulares, smartwatches, tablets, TVs e outras categorias Confira abaixo quais os cupons disponíveis e como aproveitá-los.
Copie o código do cupom na tabela acima, clique no link do Magalu e busque o produto que você deseja comprar; é possível que o cupom apareça na própria pagina do produto. Caso o cupom não seja aplicado, confira se você o digitou corretamente. articles.title: Revolve Data Breach Impacts at Least 200,000 People
articles.text:
Online fashion retailer Revolve is notifying at least 200,000 individuals that their personal and payment card information was stolen in a data breach.
The incident occurred on September 11 and involved unauthorized access to certain systems, including the company’s online shopping platform.
Immediately after learning of the cyberattack, Revolve initiated incident response and contained and remediated the unauthorized activity.
The company’s investigation into the incident determined that the hackers may have accessed and exfiltrated the names, addresses, payment card numbers, and payment card expiration dates of customers who saved the data to their accounts on the company’s e-commerce platform.
“This incident has not resulted in operational disruption or interrupted service to any customers, and as of the date of this report, the company does not believe this incident will have a material impact on its business,” Revolve said in a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission.
The fashion retailer said it has notified law enforcement and retained a cybersecurity company to help with the remediation efforts.
Last week, the company started notifying the potentially affected individuals of the data breach. Based on notices filed with the Attorney General’s offices in Iowa, Massachusetts, South Carolina, Texas, and Vermont, Revolve sent notification letters to at least 197,072 people.
The company is not providing the affected individuals with free identity theft or credit monitoring services, but reminds them to review their account statements and remain vigilant for incidents of fraud or identity theft.
Revolve has not shared the number of impacted individuals or details on who hacked it and how. SecurityWeek has emailed the company for additional information on the data breach and will update this article if it responds.
*Updated the number of affected people to add 17,813 South Carolina residents.

articles.title: Nintendo tried to kill Switch emulation, but the PC is running Switch 2 games now
articles.text:
Mamma Mia, What-a-Mess: Nintendo tried to obliterate the Switch emulation scene by going against a popular open-source project in 2024. A couple of years later, the offspring of that project is capable of running commercial games released for the brand-new Switch 2 console. Nintendo's lawyers are likely going to get rough, but the Japanese company has only itself to blame for this mess.
A year after Nintendo released its popular Switch 2 console, resourceful developers have already started to bring the brand-new gaming experience to PC through AI-assisted emulation. The Eden-NX2 emulator can already run popular, Switch-exclusive games such as Mario Kart World and Donkey Kong Bananza, though there is still a lot of work to do before compatibility and performance can improve.
Either way, the emulation scene is now racking up an impressive list of never-before-seen milestones on both old and new gaming machines. Developer "Takoroka" stated that Eden-NX2 is a fork of the Eden emulator with experimental Switch 2 support. The emulator was released a few days ago, and Nintendo enthusiasts are providing plenty of video evidence that Switch 2 emulation on PC has officially become a thing.
How did developers turn a brand-new console into a virtual gaming experience in such a short timeframe? In this particular case, AI-assisted coding is just part of the equation. Nintendo mostly kept the same base hardware architecture and operating system as the original Switch, making code hackers' lives much easier.
 – Centro LEAKS (@CentroLeaks) October 30, 2026
According to people working on the Switch 2, updating existing Switch emulators to support the latest console is just a matter of adding a few new Arm64 CPU instructions to the program's dynamic recompiler. Existing rendering engines based on the Vulkan API are mostly compatible with the Switch 2 graphics architecture, and the same goes for audio rendering.
The Switch has never been a particularly powerful machine, and existing emulators can now run a lot of commercial games with excellent performance – even on older PC systems. When it comes to the Switch 2, the experimental Eden-NX2 build still requires a fairly powerful CPU and GPU combo to render compatible games in a somewhat playable state.
Eden is a capable Switch emulator that came out of the Yuzu disaster. Nintendo tried to eradicate Switch emulation by threatening the Yuzu team through its well-funded legal team, but open-source projects stay dead only if their code is unmaintainable spaghetti or no one is interested in them anymore. Eden, Suyu, Ryubing, and other active forks of the original programs are progressing fast, despite Nintendo's readiness to unleash the lawyers when it comes to protecting its gaming IPs.
As the Eden-NX2 case clearly shows, the Switch 2 might just be the same. Despite being in the early stages of its commercial lifespan, the new hybrid console has already been jailbroken. Modding, reverse engineering, game dumping, and emulation can only improve at this point.

articles.title: Binance: Coreia do Norte rebate EUA após FBI atribuir roubo ao país
articles.text:
A Coreia do Norte classificou como “retórica absurda” as acusações dos Estados Unidos de que o país estaria por trás de um ataque hacker que desviou mais de US$ 6 bilhões (cerca de R$ 32,5 bilhões) em criptomoedas da Binance, a maior plataforma de negociação de ativos digitais do mundo.
A declaração foi divulgada nesta terça-feira (3) pela agência estatal KCNA e atribuída a Kim Yo Jong, irmã influente do líder norte-coreano Kim Jong Un. Ela afirmou que a acusação demonstra a postura hostil de Washington em relação a Pyongyang.
Segundo Kim, o FBI tenta retratar a Coreia do Norte como um “Estado criminoso cibernético”, alegando ter obtido informações de que um grupo hacker apoiado pelo país participou do ataque. A dirigente chamou a declaração estadunidense de provocação política e disse que os Estados Unidos tentam atribuir ao governo norte-coreano crimes cibernéticos cometidos em diferentes partes do mundo.
Leia mais:
- Ataque hacker na Binance mostra ‘transformação’ nas ameaças digitais
- Binance garante segurança de brasileiros após ataque de R$ 33 bi
- Binance retoma saques após roubo de R$ 33,8 bilhões em criptomoedas
- Clientes da Binance sacam bilhões em criptomoedas após ataque hacker
FBI atribui ataque a grupo hacker ligado à Coreia do Norte
No fim de semana, o FBI afirmou que a Coreia do Norte foi responsável pelo roubo de mais de US$ 6 bilhões (cerca de R$ 32,5 bilhões) em ativos virtuais da Binance. O ataque pode representar o maior roubo financeiro já registrado envolvendo criptomoedas.
De acordo com a agência estadunidense, integrantes de uma unidade estatal norte-coreana conhecida como TraderTraitor participaram da invasão. Autoridades também observaram que os responsáveis estavam convertendo os ativos roubados em Ethereum, criptomoeda que poderia ser usada em etapas posteriores para lavar o dinheiro.
A Binance informou que cobriu a maior parte dos ativos desviados utilizando recursos próprios da empresa.
Pyongyang ameaça reconsiderar questões com os EUA
- Além de negar as acusações, Kim Yo Jong afirmou que a Coreia do Norte poderá “reconsiderar” questões não especificadas diante do que chamou de atitude hostil dos Estados Unidos;
- A declaração ocorre enquanto Pyongyang permanece em silêncio sobre as iniciativas do presidente estadunidense, Donald Trump, para retomar a diplomacia por meio de encontros de cúpula;
- Kim não detalhou quais medidas poderiam ser reconsideradas. Segundo a Reuters, especialistas avaliam que o governo norte-coreano pode estar analisando suas opções diante das propostas de Washington;
- A Coreia do Norte nega envolvimento em roubos de criptomoedas e outros crimes cibernéticos. Especialistas em segurança digital, por outro lado, afirmam que hackers ligados ao país estão entre os grupos mais ativos nesse tipo de operação e que os recursos obtidos ilegalmente ajudam a financiar programas de armamentos;
- O país também é acusado de direcionar recursos provenientes de atividades ilícitas para seus programas de mísseis balísticos e armas nucleares.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Web host Squarespace lays off 19% of its employees | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Squarespace, the web company that helps customers build and host their own websites, is laying off about one-fifth of its workforce, in a move that will affect hundreds of jobs.
Jeff Seedman, a public relations specialist representing Squarespace, confirmed the layoffs to TechCrunch. The Verge initially reported the layoffs.
“Squarespace is restructuring its organization and reducing its global workforce by approximately 19%, representing around 300 employees,” said Seedman. “The changes are intended to simplify how we operate, sharpen our priorities and enable the company to move faster as we position Squarespace for its next phase of growth.”
Website building has changed immensely over the last few years as a result of the generative AI boom. “Vibe-coding” website builders, which only require simple prompts from users to spin up functional front-end designs, have largely upended the industry, making it possible for users to create sites with significantly less effort.
These kinds of sites have become an increasingly central part of the website-building business. Last year, web host rival Wix bought Base44 for $80 million. Similar offerings, like Lovable, have generated significant investor interest; Lovable raised a $400 million Series C round in August that valued the company at $13.3 billion. Google also recently launched Stitch, a feature that allows users to swiftly generate user-interface designs.
Squarespace has also begun a big push into AI. In 2024, the company launched an AI tool called Blueprint. The company also recently announced Forma, an upcoming AI native platform, whose waitlist users can join.
Squarespace was founded in 2004 and went public in 2021 at a $10 billion valuation. However, the company struggled in the ensuing years to generate enthusiastic public market interest. Squarespace ultimately decided to go private again by way of a $7 billion private equity deal in 2024.
An earlier version of this report incorrectly stated that Squarespace had not yet launched AI tools; the story has been updated.

articles.title: Sony's final 4K Blu-ray player listed as out of stock in Japan, firm may be preparing to abandon standalone players — retailers reportedly told not to expect new stock of its remaining model
articles.text:
Sony's final 4K Blu-ray player listed as out of stock in Japan, firm may be preparing to abandon standalone players — retailers reportedly told not to expect new stock of its remaining model
Sony's Japanese 4K Blu-ray lineup is disappearing, raising questions about the future of standalone disc players
Sony may be preparing to abandon the standalone 4K Blu-ray players, and the signs are becoming harder to ignore. According to a report by Forbes, its last remaining model in Japan, the UBP-X700K, was marked as unavailable on October 22, with local retailers reportedly told not to expect another shipment— a development that has raised questions about the future of Sony’s dedicated followers. Sony's U.S. website has also listed the player as ‘out of stock’.
So, is Sony really done making 4K Blu-ray players? That isn't clear. The company is yet to announce a worldwide withdrawal, and its responses to questions about the reports leave that possibility open. When asked by Forbes whether Sony is leaving the market, its UK operation replied: “This information has not been publicly announced by Sony. We are aware of the recent media reports, but prefer to refrain from commenting on speculation.”
There is an important difference between what is happening in Japan and what buyers can still find elsewhere. The UBP-X700K remains listed on Sony’s U.S. website, with Best Buy offering it for $329.99 at press time, which means Sony 4K buyers haven’t missed their chance yet. However, Amazon is no longer selling the player directly as a new product. Finding one could be harder if the company decides not to restock.
This is not the first time Sony has stepped away from physical media. In January 2025, the company stopped producing blank recordable Blu-ray discs, later announcing in February that it would also end its production in Japan. In July 2026, Sony announced it would stop producing physical PlayStation game discs from 2028— although it remains unclear if the next PlayStation console will have a disc drive. Notably, the PS5 Pro launched without a built-in disc drive, but customers who want to play physical games can purchase the optional drive separately.
However, if Sony ultimately leaves the market, buyers will still have alternatives. Panasonic remains the biggest name in dedicated 4K Blu-ray players, although its products are not that cheap. Currently, the Panasonic UB154 lists on Amazon for $289.99, while the UB820 goes for $649.99, a steep climb from its original $499 launch price. The higher-end UN9000 is retailing at $1,299.99 on Walmart. Buyers could also consider gaming consoles such as a disc-equipped PS5, which is listed at $649.99, or the Xbox Series X, priced at $799.99. Both can play 4K Blu-ray movies, but neither supports Dolby Vision when playing discs.
Sony’s move, if true, would add it to a growing list of manufacturers that have dropped the Blu-ray hardware. In 2018, Oppo stopped producing players while Samsung ended plans for new U.S. Blu-ray players a year later. Other companies include LG, which dropped the business in 2024, with French company Reavon halting production in 2025.
But it's important to note that 4K Blu-ray demand has not collapsed in the same way as the wider physical disc market. Figures laid out by the Digital Entertainment Group show that overall U.S. disc sales declined by roughly 9% in 2025. Spending on 4K discs, however, climbed by 12% over the same period, before climbing another 18% in the second quarter of 2026. That said, for existing Sony owners, there is no reason to panic just yet. A player that works today will continue playing the discs already in a collector’s library — and there is no evidence that Sony plans to push an update that would stop existing players from reading movies.

articles.title: Board Partners Reportedly Still Await NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 24 GB GPU Kits
articles.text:
Monday, November 2nd 2026
Board Partners Reportedly Still Await NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 24 GB GPU Kits
NVIDIA's board partners reportedly still lack the supply of GeForce RTX 5080 24 GB design kits, making a nearby launch seemingly impossible. According to BenchLife, design kits have not yet been provided to NVIDIA's add-in card partners. These design kits typically include a GPU die and memory modules shipped directly from NVIDIA. NVIDIA negotiates GDDR7 module pricing and supply while also receiving GPU die shipments from TSMC. The company then packages these together and sends them to board partners for assembly on their custom PCBs and designs. Since this process takes time to validate and test new designs, board partners might be unable to meet the previously assumed launch in January.
Earlier rumors suggested that NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 5080 24 GB might arrive sooner than expected, with a post from Board Channels' ChannelGate account claiming NVIDIA is speeding up the launch, with availability now expected around January 2027. Apparently, NVIDIA has already cleared out its RTX 5080 16 GB GPU inventory, and the remaining stock should last around two months. However, since board partners aren't receiving those GPU kits yet, this timing might be impossible to meet, and the window would be around Q1 2027, but not in January.Reportedly, in earlier days, it was possible to launch a new GPU in six weeks once design information was shared with board partners. However, AI demand has pushed these dates back significantly, as everyone is fighting for component supply, and two months are now needed from getting the design information to launching the GPU. Currently, there are rumors that the CES 2027 show might be the release date for this GPU, with availability scheduled for a few weeks after that launch.

articles.title: Openreach: UK landline phones will be switched off in 100 days, so make sure your connections are ready
articles.text:
Openreach: UK landline phones will be switched off in 100 days, so make sure your connections are ready
Legacy PTSN infrastructure is being switched off in January 2027
- Openreach warns landline phones will stop working on January 31, 2027
- Legacy PTSN system is going digital, so users should switch now
- Openreach remind businesses and consumers alike to check their connections
Openreach has issued a reminder warning that the UK's legacy landline phone network will be switched off in less than 100 days.
BT's infrastructure arm, responsible for deploying, maintaining and upgrading most of the country's networks, has reminded users the copper-based Public Switched Telephone Network (PTSN) network will be retired on January 31, 2027.
There will be no extension to this cut-off, meaning users, both business and consumer alike, will need to ensure their systems are ready for the change.
Time to switch
The news of the "big switch off", as Openreach's advice hub calls it, should not be a surprise, as plans were first announced to shut down the PSTN and ISDN networks by the end of 2025 back in 2017 - with the deadline later extended to 2027.
It notes that the aging landline network is harder to maintain and more vulnerable to faults, whilst also being unable to keep up with the demands posed by modern usage.
Openreach says it has already supported the migration of around 15 million lines off the old copper-based network, and although most of our homes and offices will have already switched to digital-based Internet Protocol (IP) fiber networks, there are a wide range of systems which still rely on PSTN connectivity.
Among the items needing upgrading point-of-sale terminals in shops, fire and security alarms, and personal care alarms for elderly and vulnerable people.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“Businesses and organisations that delay action are making things harder for themselves, noted James Lilley, Director of All-IP at Openreach.
"The straightforward migrations have largely been completed. What's left are the complex connections that underpin critical operations, requiring careful planning, supplier coordination, and thorough testing. We are urging businesses to act now, audit their remaining analogue services, and work with their communications provider on a migration plan today.”
Openreach's website notes the move to digital phone lines will help provide users with a more reliable service, better-quality calls and smarter blocking of unwanted calls.
It tells users to not wait until the deadline, and to get in contact with your service provider as soon as possible to get the move going.
Anyone who has not switched by the January 2027 deadline may see limited service after that time, and may be moved to the Emergency Voice and Access Continuity (EVAc) service, a temporary emergency voice-only service which keeps basic voice calls working for a limited time.
An FAQ includes the question "I don't want broadband. Can I have a phone line only?" but includes only a wishy-washy response - "If you have a phone line but don’t have broadband, your service provider will help you find the most suitable digital option for your needs."

articles.title: Attackers Target Unpatched CryptoPayment Gateway Flaw That Can Expose Wallet Credentials
articles.text:
Threat actors are attempting to exploit an unpatched maximum-severity security vulnerability in the CryptoPayment Gateway WordPress plugin, according to findings from Defused Cyber.
The vulnerability in question is CVE-2026-81648, which carries a CVSS score of 10.0. Successful exploitation of the flaw could permit unauthenticated users to delete arbitrary files on the server and extract sensitive data, including stored wallet credentials.
"The CryptoPayment Gateway WordPress plugin from 1.2.1 to 1.2.2 does not apply an authorization check on one of its AJAX endpoints, allowing unauthenticated users to invoke administrative operations, including deleting arbitrary files on the server, overwriting the payment gateway configuration and recovering stored wallet credentials in cleartext," according to a description of the flaw on the NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD).
The vulnerability affects versions 1.2.1 through 1.2.2, which is the latest version. There are no known fixes for the flaw, according to WP Scan. As of August 28, 2026, the plugin has been closed on the WordPress Plugin Directory and is no longer available for download due to an unspecified "security issue."
Statistics show that the plugin has been collectively downloaded 1,845 times, including 20 downloads over the last seven days. It's unclear if it's actively installed on any WordPress sites.
"We are observing in-the-wild exploitation attempts against CVE-2026-81648, a critical (CVSS 10.0) flaw in the CryptoPayment Gateway for WordPress," Defused Cyber said in an X post. "The attacks we recorded came from infrastructure that markets themselves as 'Anonymous KYC-Free VPS Hosting.'"
In the absence of a fix, site owners are advised to remove the plugin, rotate wallet keys, and audit for any suspicious changes.

articles.title: Third person dies of bird flu since virus started jumping to livestock
articles.text:
A person in Washington state has died from bird flu after exposure at an infected dairy farm, state health officials reported Sunday. It marks the third human bird flu death in the US since a strain of highly pathogenic (H5) avian influenza (HPAI) made the unprecedented jump from wild, migratory birds to dairy cows, which was first reported in the US in March 2024.
The person who died was a Yakima County resident and was said to have had underlying health conditions, which could have made the person more vulnerable to the infection. On Friday, county officials reported that the person was severely ill and hospitalized. In the subsequent announcement of the person’s death, officials said they would not be releasing further information about the person, including their name, gender, or age, out of respect for the family’s privacy.
“Our hearts go out to the individual’s family and loved ones during this difficult time,” Dave Atteberry, health officer for the Yakima Health District, said in a statement. “Avian influenza can cause severe illness, particularly among people who have underlying health conditions. While this is a serious and heartbreaking outcome, the risk to the general public remains low.”
Continued threat
In all, three people have tested positive for bird flu in Washington since the virus was reported in dairy cattle in the state on October 8. All three have been in Yakima County. While announcing the death on Sunday, officials also reported the third case. That case, like the first case, was in a person who had exposure to an infected dairy herd in the county. Both people have reportedly not experienced severe illness nor been hospitalized.

articles.title: Apple is ‘not able to predict’ when it’ll have enough iPhone Duos to go around
articles.text:
Apple CEO John Ternus doesn’t have a timeline for when iPhone Duo supply constraints could lift. During an interview with Reuters, Ternus said the company is “working hard to get it to as many customers as quickly as possible, but at this point, we’re not able to predict when supply and demand will be in balance.”
Apple is ‘not able to predict’ when it’ll have enough iPhone Duos to go around
John Ternus says Apple is seeing ‘unprecedented’ memory pricing.
Apple launched its first foldable last month for $1,999, featuring a 5.4 outer display and 7.6-inch inner screen. Preorders for the iPhone Duo quickly sold out, with some shipments expected to arrive in 2027. Apple also made a limited number of iPhone Duo models available in-store at launch.
In his interview with Reuters, Ternus also addressed reports about cracked screens, saying “a very small percentage” of iPhone Duos were returned for this issue, and that Apple is replacing them.
The company has contended with supply chain constraints and rising memory costs for months now. This resulted in price increases across its product lineup, along with higher iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max starting prices. “What we’re seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented,” Ternus said during Apple’s Q4 2026 earnings call on Monday. Ternus added that the company expects to see “even higher memory costs” during Apple’s December quarter but notes that this is “partly offset” by recent price increases.
Even without a standard iPhone 18 model, Apple reported record-breaking iPhone revenue at $57.58 billion during its fourth quarter.

articles.title: Olvídate de usar Claude Code para clonar tus juegos favoritos: Anthropic cambia las reglas por la piratería
articles.text:
Si pensabas pedirle a Claude Code que te ayude a crear tu propio GTA 6 sin saber programar y sin gastar miles de millones de dólares, ve pensando en una idea mejor. Anthropic ha cambiado las reglas del funcionamiento de su plataforma de programación con IA para impedir la piratería.
A finales de la semana pasada, usuarios de Claude Code se toparon con que la inteligencia artificial había recibido un cambio clave. Una orden emitida desde los servidores de Anthropic determinó que la herramienta ya no puede clonar juegos ni realizar ciertas tareas de ingeniería inversa.
Desde la empresa confirmaron que la modificación buscaba desalentar las intervenciones sobre propiedades intelectuales alcanzadas por derechos de autor. "Añadimos dos frases al prompt de Claude Code en Opus 5.5 para disuadirlo de recrear el juego específico de otra persona, porque usar Claude para infringir propiedad intelectual va en contra de nuestra política de uso. Los juegos originales, los juegos de género y los juegos construidos a partir de tus propios diseños y activos están pensados para seguir funcionando", explicó Addy Osmani, empleado de Anthropic.
Según parece, el bloqueo a clonar juegos de propiedades intelectuales protegidas impacta sobre Opus 5.5 y no sobre versiones previas de la IA. Esto tal vez se deba a que los resultados con modelos anteriores no son tan convincentes como los de la opción más reciente y potente. Sea como sea, Claude Code ya no será la principal aliada de quienes intenten recrear títulos sin autorización.
Claude Code bloquea su uso para ingeniería inversa y clones de juegos
La decisión ya está causando polémica, como no podía ser de otra manera. Muchas de las respuestas al tuit de Osmani indican que los juegos a los que hacen referencia no pertenecen a Anthropic. Por ende, sostienen que están tomando atribuciones que no les corresponden. Los responsables de Claude Code refieren que la piratería es una violación de sus términos de servicio. Además, es lógico que quieran protegerse de cualquier represalia legal que puedan sufrir por parte de los estudios afectados.
El punto clave de esta historia es que el bloqueo de Claude Code no se limita a tratar de recrear juegos protegidos con derechos de autor. Usuarios de la plataforma de programación indican que las labores de ingeniería inversa ya no funcionan en Opus 5.5, incluso cuando intentan aplicarlas a código creados por ellos mismos.
Esto seguramente se deba al uso de Claude Code en proyectos para desarrollar alternativas a Photoshop y otras apps creativas sin tener que pagar suscripciones. Lo mismo, por la implementación de la IA en proyectos para decompilar juegos viejos y portearlos a plataformas para las que no se lanzaron originalmente.
Usuarios han logrado continuar con algunos de sus proyectos al bajar a Opus 4.8, aunque todavía no se sabe cuánto durará. Anthropic ha prometido revisar y actualizar el bloqueo para que sea balanceado y no afecte el uso genuino de Claude Code, aunque eso no ha impedido que el caudal de quejas sea cada vez mayor.

articles.title: 3D Integration Reduces Embodied-Emissions Impact Of GPU Scaling (imec, VUB)
articles.text:
Home
                        TECHNICAL PAPERS
		
								November 2nd, 2026 - 
								By: Technical Paper Link
								
							
Researchers at imec and Vrije Universiteit Brussels published “Embodied Emissions of 2.5D and 3D Scaling in Chipletized GPUs for Low-Carbon AI.”
Abstract
“GPU compute resources are scaling to support growing AI workloads, leading to further rises in the climate change impact of hyperscale data centers that rely on high-performance GPUs. To model how packaging decisions impact the carbon footprint we have estimated the embodied emissions (EE) of a chiplet-based GPU that has been scaled in 2.5D and 3D using the imec netzero modeling platform. We doubled the number of compute units and high bandwidth memory (HBM) capacity in the 2.5D and 3D scaled systems and found that 3D scaling results in an 89% increase in EE, as compared to an increase of 141% for 2.5D scaling, positioning 3D scaling as an attractive solution to limit the embodied emissions due to GPU scaling.”

articles.title: 10 SA founders selected for One Young World job creation programme - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Ten South African entrepreneurs have been selected for a new initiative run by global youth leadership organisation One Young World, which aims to support young founders in scaling their businesses.
With the Ichikowitz Family Foundation as its founding partner, the National Programme for Job-Generating Entrepreneurs supports founders aged 18-35 whose businesses show the potential to create meaningful employment. It is part of the legacy of the One Young World Summit, taking place in Cape Town from November 3-6.
The selected entrepreneurs come from sectors including technology, education, agriculture, transport, fashion and employment services. They include Christiaan van den Berg, co-founder of JOBJACK, a platform connecting unemployed South Africans with entry-level work. It has more than six million users and over 5,000 employer sites, and has placed more than 65,000 people into jobs.
Also selected are Ntwenhle Linda of rural poultry enterprises Qandalami and Bunye Qanda; Merishka Harilall of Alter Ego Promotions and Spenda Holdings; and Mandla Mazibuko of Jobox, which links young people with employers, educational institutions and funders.
The other six are:
- Akhil Boddu of Zaio Institute of Technology, which trains unemployed youth in software, data and AI.
- Bonolo Matjila of skincare brand Golden Hour.
- Huzaifa Khan of Resolute Education, which offers coding, robotics and future-skills education.
- Navhani Tshikosi of student logistics business HRA Transportation.
- Thapelo Nthite of Botlhale AI, which builds digital services in African languages.
- Thobey Cooper of Thobey Cooper and Fierce Creative Academy, which works in fashion and creative education.
The founders will attend the Cape Town summit, and then join One Young World’s network of more than 20,000 young leaders in over 190 countries and receive mentorship from established figures in South Africa’s startup ecosystem.
The programme ends with a Demo Day, provisionally planned for late May 2027, where participants will pitch to prospective investors and partners. The initiative does not provide direct funding, but instead focuses on networks, partnerships and market access.
“South Africa’s youth unemployment challenge demands more than preparing young people to find jobs. We must also support the entrepreneurs who have the vision and potential to create them,” said Kate Robertson, co-founder of One Young World.

articles.title: Google a caché une surprise pour le retour de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
articles.text:
L’arrivée du remake de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, le 5 novembre 2026 sur Nintendo Switch 2, est un événement. Et ça, Google l’a bien compris. L’entreprise est une habituée des easter eggs, ces petites surprises cachées qui apparaissent lorsque vous tapez certaines requêtes dans son moteur de recherche.
Pour le retour de cette aventure de Link, elle propose un voyage dans le temps. Direction 1998, l’année de sortie du jeu original sur Nintendo 64, mais aussi… celle de la création de Google.
Comment déclencher l’animation Zelda sur Google ?
Pour découvrir ce clin d’œil, tapez « Zelda » ou encore « The Legend of Zelda » dans le moteur de recherche. Une épée apparaît alors en bas à droite de la page, suspendue au-dessus d’un socle. Les habitués reconnaîtront l’Épee de légende, l’arme emblématique de Link.
Cliquez dessus : l’épée s’enfonce dans son socle, un cri de Link retentit et une animation envahit l’écran. Et lorsqu’elle se termine, la page a changé d’allure. Google retrouve son ancien logo et une interface beaucoup plus dépouillée, inspirée de son apparence de 1998.
Les résultats s’affichent dans une présentation rétro, loin des pages actuelles chargées d’images, de vidéos et d’encadrés. L’effet reste toutefois limité à cette page consacrée à Zelda : impossible de poursuivre toutes vos recherches dans ce décor.
Un clin d’œil aux voyages temporels de Link
Le choix de cette animation renvoie directement au jeu. Dans Ocarina of Time, Link explore Hyrule à deux époques, séparées de sept ans. La Master Sword lui permet de passer de l’une à l’autre : en la retirant de son socle au Temple du Temps, il se retrouve projeté dans le futur. En la replaçant, il revient dans le passé.
Google reprend donc ce geste pour faire remonter le temps à son moteur de recherche. Une manière d’accompagner le retour du jeu, près de 28 ans après sa sortie initiale. Sur Nintendo Switch 2, ce remake proposera notamment des graphismes entièrement revus et des commandes modernisées, à découvrir dès le 5 novembre. Pour les fans, une édition collector de la console aux couleurs de Zelda est déjà disponible.

articles.title: L'armée française vient de recevoir un Rafale pas comme les autres, qui va préparer le futur Rafale F5
articles.text:
La Direction générale de l'armement a livré à son centre DGA Essais en vol son premier Rafale avion banc d'essais. Désigné B374, ce laboratoire volant servira à tester les équipements et armements du futur Rafale F5.
Le ministère des Armées, par le biais de la Direction générale de l'armement (DGA), a annoncé ce lundi 2 novembre la livraison du premier Rafale avion banc d'essais (ABE) au centre DGA Essais en vol. Construit par Dassault Aviation et livré au standard F4.1, l'appareil sera progressivement transformé d'ici 2028 pour accueillir une instrumentation de vol complète. Il deviendra alors la plateforme d'essais des futurs équipements du Rafale F5, dont le radar de nouvelle génération RBE2 XG.
Ce Rafale n’ira pas en escadron, il va servir de laboratoire volant au futur Rafale F5
Un avion dit « banc d'essais », c'est en quelque sorte un laboratoire avec des ailes. Pour ce qui est du Rafale, l'appareil est modifié en profondeur pour embarquer des instruments de mesure et des enregistreurs qui collectent les données pendant le vol, un peu comme une boîte noire, mais en beaucoup plus bavard. Grâce à une liaison de données, ces informations parviennent aussi aux ingénieurs qui conduisent les essais depuis le sol. Qu'il s'agisse de la navigation, des systèmes d'attaque, des capteurs, des armements, des communications ou des logiciels de bord, chaque nouvelle technologie peut ainsi être éprouvée en vol, en conditions réelles.
Le B374 a aussi une particularité. C'est le tout dernier Rafale de sa fournée. L'État ne commande pas ses Rafale à l'unité, mais par lots successifs, par tranches. La quatrième tranche de production du Rafale, notifiée en 2021 aux quatre grands industriels du programme (Dassault Aviation pour l'avion, Thales pour l'électronique, Safran pour le moteur et MBDA pour les missiles), trouve avec lui son 73e et dernier exemplaire. Plutôt que de rejoindre un escadron, ce dernier-né file directement chez les experts de DGA Essais en vol, qui vont le remodeler en profondeur avec ceux de Dassault.
Le B374 est ainsi le premier Rafale banc d'essais affecté à DGA Essais en vol. Le centre travaille aujourd'hui avec le B348, que l'armée de l'Air et de l'Espace lui prête sur une longue durée, et que le nouveau venu remplacera à terme. Les essayeurs disposeront donc d'un appareil qui leur est affecté, et non plus simplement prêté.
Le Rafale F5, un chantier en trois temps jusqu'en 2028
Avant de se consacrer au Rafale F5, le B374 a du travail sur la version actuelle de l'avion. Il va d'abord recevoir une installation d'essais et de mesures (IEM), c'est-à-dire l'ensemble des instruments et enregistreurs qui transforment un Rafale en avion d'essais. Cette première installation sera réversible, on parle bien d'un équipement provisoire, que l'on peut retirer sans modifier durablement l'appareil. Ainsi équipé, il participera au développement du standard actuel du Rafale, le F4, en attendant sa grande transformation.
La vraie métamorphose interviendra à l'horizon du deuxième trimestre 2027. Dassault Aviation y intégrera les interfaces nécessaires pour que DGA Essais en vol puisse installer à bord une instrumentation complète et, cette fois, permanente. L'avion gagnera ainsi en capacités d'analyse pour les prochaines évolutions du standard F4, tout en préparant les essais du F5.
Après ce passage en atelier, le B374 retrouvera la flotte d'essais en 2028 avec un cerveau adapté à sa nouvelle vie. Son ordinateur de bord, l'Ensemble modulaire de traitement de l'information (EMTI), tournera alors avec une version logicielle spéciale, dite « orange », conçue uniquement pour les essais. C'est elle qui lui permettra d'accueillir les futurs capteurs du F5, à commencer par le radar RBE2 XG, encore en développement chez Thales, qui doit permettre au Rafale de repérer avions et cibles à grande distance. Une étape importante pour la DGA, qui renouvelle peu à peu sa flotte d'essais, à l'heure où se prépare l'avenir de l'aviation de combat française.

articles.title: From prompt engineers to tool builders: Intuit’s Vignesh Subrahmaniam on building AI that acts
articles.text:
Intuit
View Brand Publisher
From prompt engineers to tool builders: Intuit’s Vignesh Subrahmaniam on building AI that acts
At TechSparks 2026, Intuit’s Principal AI Scientist explained why reliable tools, high-quality data, and consent matter more than ever as AI moves from answering to acting
For the past few years, getting better results from AI meant learning to write better prompts. That is changing fast, as AI systems begin to reason, make decisions, and act across entire workflows on their own.
At TechSparks 2026, YourStory’s flagship event, Dr Vignesh Subrahmaniam, Principal AI Scientist at Intuit, spoke with Adith Charlie, Managing Editor of YourStory and The CapTable, in a fireside chat titled ‘Beyond the prompt: Building AI that thinks, acts, learns’. Drawing on Subrahmaniam's experience of turning AI research into scalable systems, the two explored what builders need to rethink as intelligence becomes increasingly agentic.
Teaching machines the game of business
The session opened with a question for Subrahmaniam about what a typical day looks like for him. He was also asked to simplify the concepts of fintech and AI for the audience. He responded with a chess analogy, posing a question: if an algorithm were never taught the rules of chess but was shown a million completed games and their winners, could it deduce both the rules and the strategies most likely to lead to victory? His team at Intuit applies a similar approach to supporting small businesses, as the company serves both consumers and accountants.
“How do we learn the game of business by looking at data, by looking at actual actions and outcomes that businesses are taking,” he said. The goal is to understand what helps a business win customers, grow quickly, and improve its cash flow.
From prompts to tools
The conversation then turned to the shift builders face, from years of learning to write smarter prompts to designing agents that are handed a goal and decide the steps themselves.
Subrahmaniam placed prompt engineering in the long history of programming languages, from binary and assembly to Fortran, C, and Python. Large language models let anyone program using plain English. However, this method has limits. Researchers quickly understood that intelligence should not only be in the model.
The model becomes an orchestrator, breaking a complex task into a series of actions and tool calls. The real intelligence moves into the tools it calls. Those tools must be built differently too, “not so that a human being can use them, or a software developer can use them, or anybody can use them, but in a way that an LLM orchestrator can really use them”.
That means high-fidelity tools with highly deterministic output. For builders, the craft shifts from clever wording to dependable components that a model can call on again and again without surprises.
The next frontier is beyond text
On where new data will come from, Subrahmaniam was candid that learning from text is now largely a solved problem. The harder challenge is learning from multimodal sources and real-world actions. He pointed to how a small child learns mostly from what she sees, hears and observes, not from reading, and argued that bringing such real-world signals into AI systems is what will help models go beyond generating text to suggesting actions. That, he said, is the next frontier.
Data quality still decides everything
Looking ahead at the challenges for a regulated industry, he took the audience back 18 years, to one of the first machine learning labs in Bangalore, where he worked on logistic regressions and multi-layer perceptrons. The biggest problem then was not the algorithm. “Actually, it was data quality,” he recalled.
That has not changed. Whether a team trains a simple regression or fine-tunes a transformer, “garbage in, garbage out” still applies. Enterprises that can collect, collate, and store data at the highest quality, he said, will have the edge.
Consent and privacy from the floor
In the short audience Q&A, an attendee asked how restrictions on where financial data can be stored affect Intuit’s work. Subrahmaniam called consent the heart of any learning system and cited the Framingham study, where residents of a Massachusetts town allowed doctors to follow their health over time, which shaped modern understanding of cardiovascular disease.
Companies, he added, must also explain the benefits of data use to the wider community.
What builders can take away
As the conversation drew to a close, one thread ran through every answer: as AI moves from responding to acting, the foundations matter more than the interface.
Prompts will remain a starting point, but the real work now lies in building dependable tools that agents can call on, feeding systems high-quality data, and earning the consent that lets them learn from it.
For builders looking beyond the prompt, that is where the next wave of AI will be won.

articles.title: BTCPay Server warns of hot wallet crypto thefts on outdated instances
articles.text:
The maintainer of BTCPay Server, an open-source cryptocurrency payment processor, has urged users to install the latest version as hackers have been draining “hot wallets” on instances running older versions.
Operators were initially advised to shut down their servers pending a full investigation into the unauthorized Bitcoin and Litecoin payments.
The BTCPay Server project provides businesses with a self-hosted payment processing solution that allows them to accept Bitcoin and other digital assets directly into their own wallets, eliminating payment intermediaries or paying platform processing fees.
It handles checkout invoices and payment verification, including payments over the Lightning Network.
Early Monday, the maintainer said it had “identified an attack vector targeting instances running version 2.4.1 (July 23, 2026) or earlier” and strongly urged users to update to version 2.4.7.
BTCPay founder Nicolas Dorier said the attacks did not target public servers. The investigation focused on determining how the threat actor was able to log in as an administrator to instances running versions older than 2.4.2.
On October 29, the company disclosed a critical vulnerability discovered via Anthropic’s Frontier OSS scanner, which prompted the release of version 2.4.7 as an emergency security update.
However, Dorier said that there were clues that the attacker used vulnerabilities in BTCPay Server versions earlier than 2.4.2, released on August 7, which the project later confirmed.
“Our incident response investigation identified an attack vector targeting instances running versions 2.4.1 (Jul 23, 2026) or older,” BTCPay Server says.
“We have no credible reports of hot wallet drains for users running the latest 2.4.7 release. We again urge everyone to keep their BTCPay Server updated.”
The BTCPay project began receiving reports of theft yesterday evening (UTC) and responded by asking VPS hosting providers to take affected server instances offline as a precaution to protect customers.
In a security alert today, the project maintainer said that it is currently responding to affected users and continues to receive incident reports. Users who lost funds as a result of the recent attacks are asked to send details to security@btcpayserver.org, and to report the losses to local authorities.
Impacted users should update to version 2.4.7 through Server Settings → Maintenance → Update.
For Docker installations, administrators can update BTCPay Server by logging in over SSH, running sudo su -, changing to the deployment directory with cd btcpayserver-docker, and executing ./btcpay-update.sh.
If running 2.4.1 or older, it is recommended to take the instance offline as soon as possible.
Update [10:23 EST]: Article update with information from the security incident report BTCPay Server published earlier today.

articles.title: La Palma se ha despertado sin luz en toda la isla: un apagón total ha dejado a oscuras 50.500 suministros en plena tormenta
articles.text:
La Palma se ha quedado sin electricidad en toda la isla, según ha publicado El País, a las 06:42 de este lunes. El apagón ha afectado a unos 50.500 suministros. Pasadas las 11:00, casi el 80% había recuperado la luz.
Qué ha ocurrido. A las 04:10 ha caído la línea Guinchos-Valle, la única de transporte de la isla. Dos horas y media después se ha desconectado la central térmica de Los Guinchos y el sistema se ha ido a cero.
Todo ha ocurrido en plena tormenta eléctrica, aunque el origen del fallo todavía no ha sido confirmado.
Entre líneas. Cada empresa ha señalado a la otra:
- Red Eléctrica ha apuntado a la desconexión de la central, la cual explota Endesa.
- Endesa ha recordado que la línea de Red Eléctrica seguía caída y complicaba reponerla.
En junio de 2025, otro cero energético dejó la isla a oscuras durante casi tres horas, con un cruce de acusaciones y culpas muy parecido. Endesa defendió entonces que el sistema debe resistir fallos simples e incluso dobles. Este lunes ha acabado a cero, aunque falta saber si ambos fallos están conectados o no.
El contraste. La Gomera estaba en la misma situación hasta este verano, cuando empezó a funcionar el cable de 66 kV que la une con Tenerife, con unos 36 kilómetros bajo el mar. La Palma sigue sin nada parecido. Cuando se va la luz, los técnicos tienen que arrancar los grupos de Los Guinchos e ir acoplándolos de uno en uno.
Y ahora qué. Primero hay que averiguar por qué ha saltado Los Guinchos y si tendría que haber seguido en marcha sin la línea. Si tenía que aguantar, las miradas se dirigirán hacia Endesa. Si no, la pregunta pasa a ser por qué toda una isla con casi 90.000 habitantes sigue colgando de una sola línea.

Lagos’s National Theatre, now the Wole Soyinka Centre for Arts & Culture, a brutalist landmark whose shape mimics a general’s cap, from October 27-29, played host to a different kind of uniform.
The attendees at Moonshot by TechCabal were not, on the whole, wearing the hoodies, fleece vests, T-shirts, and jeans combinations that Silicon Valley has exported to the world. Most people were dressed to be seen.
There was a richness to the dressing that felt entirely at home in a West African fashion capital. Boldly patterned shirts, flowing matching sets and colourful fabrics brought texture and brightness to the various rooms and exhibition halls.
The appeal lay in the freedom with which guests put it all together. West African fashion influences sat comfortably alongside contemporary tailoring, sculptural dresses and easy separates. Styles could be practical, exuberant and polished within the same outfit.

articles.title: « Si je suis viré demain » : un responsable Xbox vend la mèche sur l'IA
articles.text:
Le 19 octobre, Brandon Stirrup, responsable de la stratégie chez Xbox, un intitulé sans dimension technique, a lâché sur X que son employeur utilise l’IA « comme toutes les entreprises en 2026 ». Le compte a été désactivé le jour même (mes ses posts restent accessibles par d’autres moyens). Près de deux semaines plus tard, ni Microsoft ni sa division jeu vidéo n’ont réagi.
Trois heures de week-end et un aveu
La veille, ce cadre sans bagage de développeur racontait avoir fabriqué en deux jours, dont trois heures de travail effectif, un petit jeu de football « mauvais mais améliorable ». Il décrivait ses idées en langage courant, l’IA écrivait le code : une méthode que le milieu surnomme le « vibe coding ». Et d’asséner que les studios rétifs à l’outil n’ont, selon lui, plus rien à faire dans le métier.
Aux critiques qui pleuvaient, l’intéressé s’est dit « content de prendre le coup si des centaines de personnes chez Xbox peuvent arrêter de faire semblant ». Et de conclure, dans une formule disparue depuis avec le reste du fil : « si je suis viré demain, ce sera parce que je vous ai dit la vérité que personne ne veut que vous sachiez ». L’homme assurait aussi « aimer Xbox et Microsoft » et avoir « passé plus de dix ans à le prouver ». Sa page LinkedIn le donne toujours en poste. Depuis, l’entreprise n’a ni démenti ses propos, ni confirmé la moindre sanction, ni commenté la disparition du fil.
Huit mois après la promesse anti-bouillie
Le 20 février, Asha Sharma, nommée à la tête de Microsoft Gaming en remplacement de Phil Spencer, promettait aux équipes de ne pas inonder Xbox de « bouillie d’IA sans âme ». La promesse répondait à un an de grogne, entre le modèle génératif Muse accueilli froidement par les joueurs et des studios essorés par les plans sociaux. Son prédécesseur écartait avant son départ toute directive imposée d’en haut et cantonnait l’IA à des usages discrets, la modération en tête. Le 13 octobre, cinq jours avant le fil de Brandon Stirrup, Microsoft officialisait pourtant Xbox Labs, une cellule d’expérimentation autour de l’IA confiée au directeur technique Scott Van Vliet.
L’enquête annuelle de la Game Developers Conference, publiée fin janvier auprès de 2 300 professionnels, compte 36 % d’utilisateurs d’IA générative, dont 30 % au sein de leur studio. 52 % des répondants jugent la technologie néfaste pour le secteur, contre 30 % un an plus tôt et 18 % en 2024, quand 7 % seulement y voient un effet positif. Un pointage de mars fait même retomber l’usage déclaré à 29 %. Epic Games, de son côté, a sommé ses équipes de se réoutiller pour une « accélération maximale par l’IA », jusqu’au lanceur maison, en partie « vibe codé » lui aussi. Le secteur s’équipe et se crispe dans le même mouvement.

articles.title: La Guardia Civil compra por 2,5 millones un sistema para acceder de forma remota a móviles Android y iPhone
articles.text:
La Guardia Civil ha adquirido un sistema capaz de registrar a distancia dispositivos móviles (Android e iPhone) y acceder a su contenido y comunicaciones. En el anuncio de formalización de este contrato se habla de la capacidad de alojar software en los dispositivos y permitir el “acceso transparente” a sus contenidos y comunicaciones. No se detallan los métodos de instalación ni las restricciones.
Una adjudicación de marzo. El contrato se adjudicó el día 26 de marzo a la empresa Fortier Europe, S.L.U. (Boadilla del Monte, Madrid). El importe de la oferta elegida fue de 2.066.115,70 euros sin IVA (con el 21 % ascendería a unos 2,5 millones). Aunque se ha publicado en octubre (el anuncio), no quiere decir que haya sido adjudicado en ese mes.
Solo se presentó una oferta. Se utilizó un procedimiento negociado sin publicidad. Se justifica porque el fabricante ha otorgado derechos exclusivos de suministro y distribución. En el anuncio se indica quién es el proveedor (no se menciona el fabricante) y no se concreta qué versión de Android e iOS soporta. Tampoco se especifica que se pueda instalar siempre de forma remota (sin acceso físico).
Esta empresa ya había trabajado anteriormente con la Guardia Civil. El día 20 de abril de 2020 se le adjudicó el mantenimiento de la plataforma EGOBOX (por valor de 99.130 euros).
Qué límites legales tiene el registro remoto
En la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal se establece que para poder examinar de forma remota el contenido de un dispositivo sin que el titular o usuario tenga constancia de ello es necesario contar con una autorización judicial.
Los delitos que pueden ser objeto de este tipo de registros son los siguientes:
- Delitos cometidos en el seno de organizaciones criminales.
- Delitos de terrorismo.
- Delitos contra menores o personas con capacidad modificada judicialmente.
- Delitos contra la Constitución.
- Delitos de traición.
- Delitos relacionados con la defensa nacional.
- Delitos cometidos con tecnologías informáticas o de comunicación.
En dicha resolución es necesario concretar qué dispositivos se van a registrar (qué tipo de dispositivos), cuál es el alcance del acceso (a qué se va a poder acceder), qué software se utilizará y qué agentes están autorizados. Además, hay que incluir las garantías de integridad de los datos.
El plazo máximo es de un mes (se puede prorrogar por periodos iguales hasta tres meses). En caso de que los investigadores piensen que los datos están en otro sistema, deberán informar al juez para que pueda autorizar la ampliación del registro.
Tampoco se puede identificar como Pegasus. Nosotros ya hicimos un seguimiento del caso Pegasus. Aunque comparten compatibilidad con Android e iOS, esto no quiere decir que sea el mismo producto.
Qué protecciones tienen el iPhone y Android
Los usuarios que puedan verse atacados de forma dirigida cuentan con una protección en el iPhone de Apple: el modo de aislamiento. Este modo (opcional) ofrece ciertas protecciones adicionales que hacen que el spyware tenga menos oportunidades de ataque. Entre otras cosas, inhabilita la mayoría de los tipos de adjuntos en la aplicación de Mensajes. También desactiva ciertas tecnologías web. Esto puede provocar que algunas páginas funcionen peor o que pierdan ciertas funcionalidades. Las llamadas telefónicas o los mensajes de texto sin formatear sí que siguen siendo posibles.
Para activarlo, hay que ir a Ajustes. En el apartado de Privacidad y seguridad encontraremos un apartado de Modo de aislamiento. Seguimos los pasos y reiniciamos el teléfono. Se trata de un modo pensado para los pocos usuarios que pueden verse atacados de forma especialmente sofisticada. No podemos asegurar que este sistema en concreto (que no se ha publicado cómo funciona) vaya a ser bloqueado por esta protección de Apple.
Por otro lado, Google también ha lanzado en Android 16 un modo avanzado de protección del dispositivo. Este modo agrupa varias medidas de seguridad (contra aplicaciones maliciosas y ataques dirigidos). No se pueden inhabilitar individualmente mientras este modo está activo. Para activarlo, según la actual ayuda de Android, hay que ir a Ajustes > Seguridad y privacidad. En el apartado de Otros ajustes buscamos Protección Avanzada. Una vez allí, activamos la opción de Protección del dispositivo (podría ser necesario reiniciar).
