articles.title: Digital billboards across the globe hacked to show porn, attackers say "anyone with two brain cells" could do it
articles.text:
Facepalm: Not for the first time, digital billboards have been hacked to play pornography. On this occasion, however, the incident took place on a global scale as the explicit footage appeared on public signage in multiple countries. A group claiming responsibility says the hack was so easy that "anyone with two brain cells" could have done it.
The most visible hack took place on a digital billboard stretching across one of Egypt's biggest highways: the 26th of July Axis in Giza. Drivers stopped their cars to film as the screen broadcast the adults-only material, which was overlaid with the text "Leaked by: Ch, 19ylegal never and nivex" and the Telegram handle @LeakersGov.
According to CNN, Egypt's Interior Ministry blamed a cyberattack on the website of an unnamed international company contracted by the billboard's operator. It said the breach caused footage to appear in several countries simultaneously, and that legal proceedings had begun.
 – ILTV Israel News (@ILTVNews) November 1, 2026
The Egyptian operator, Al Arabia United, said it shut down the affected screen after detecting unauthorized access and was working with authorities to investigate.
The highly conservative country has tried to block pornographic websites in the past, but online access remains popular – Pornhub Insights showed that Egypt was one of the top 20 countries visiting pornography websites in 2025.
Malaysia's Kluang Municipal Council also confirmed that several public LED screens had been compromised. The council switched off its screens and said it was working with its vendor to investigate and improve security.
Gizmodo also reports a confirmed incident in Brazil, while there are also claims involving Iraq and China.
As for how the screens were hijacked, the group calling itself Leakers$ said it exploited a flaw in software used to send content to LED displays. Its members claimed an automated scan uncovered thousands of exposed systems in around two hours. The systems were allegedly accessible via web pages and interfaces that lacked basic security protections. The group claimed its aim was to expose poor security, rather than collect a ransom.
"It was a genuine vulnerability in the software responsible for transmitting content to LED displays," a Leakers$ member told The Cairo Report. "After exploiting it, we gained access to display systems in several countries, not just Egypt, but also Malaysia, Brazil, China, and others."
Anyone experiencing a sense of déjà vu might remember a 2019 incident in Auburn Hills, Michigan. A billboard beside the I-75 and M-59 interchange played pornography for around 20 minutes before being shut down. Police were looking for two suspects believed to have broken into the control shed beneath the sign. No accidents were reported in the Michigan incident, but police warned that the footage was a major distraction for drivers, obviously.
There was also an Asics store in New Zealand whose outdoor screens showed porn for nine hours, as well as similar previous hacks in Australia, Indonesia, and Iraq.

articles.title: Télécommande et minuterie : ce radiateur à bain d’huile de 2 500 W passe à 151,99 €
articles.text:
Le radiateur à bain d’huile Aigostar Oil Monster de 2 500 W est à 151,99 € (-24 %)
Sur Amazon, l’Aigostar Oil Monster est à 151,99 €, soit 24 % sous l’ancien prix affiché. Ce radiateur de 2 500 W dispose d’une télécommande et d’une minuterie.
L’offre représente 48 € d’économie par rapport aux 199,99 € indiqués comme ancien prix. Face au plus bas des 30 derniers jours, de 159,99 €, la baisse est de 8 €, soit 5 %. L’appareil est vendu et expédié par AIGOTECH sur la marketplace Amazon.
Trois puissances et un thermostat réglable
Ce radiateur à bain d’huile comporte 13 éléments et propose trois niveaux de puissance : 1 000, 1 500 et 2 500 W. Son thermostat se règle de 5 à 35 °C pour adapter la température souhaitée à la pièce.
Le mode Eco ajuste le fonctionnement selon la température ambiante. Il ne garantit toutefois pas une économie chiffrée : la consommation dépend notamment de la consigne, de l’isolation et de la durée d’utilisation.
Des réglages à distance et des roulettes
L’écran LED affiche les réglages, accessibles également depuis la télécommande fournie. Une minuterie jusqu’à 24 heures permet de programmer le fonctionnement. La poignée et les roulettes facilitent les déplacements entre deux pièces.
L’appareil dispose de protections contre la surchauffe et le basculement, ainsi que d’un verrouillage des commandes. La fiche Amazon affiche une moyenne de 4,4/5 sur plus de 2 100 évaluations, un indicateur globalement favorable qui ne remplace pas un test de chauffe.

articles.title: Uber Builds MCP Gateway to Govern Access to 800+ Servers and 5,000+ AI Agent Tools
articles.text:
Uber has built an MCP Gateway to standardize how AI agents discover and invoke internal services, addressing fragmented integrations, duplicated infrastructure, and inconsistent security practices as agent adoption expands across the company. The platform supports more than 800 MCP servers and 5,000 tools, providing a common layer for discovery, protocol translation, authorization, and execution.
Uber engineers describe this approach as a microservice architecture that exposes existing APIs as MCP tools without requiring changes to the underlying services. The architecture separates the MCP Registry, which acts as the control plane, from the Proxy Gateway, which handles runtime execution. The registry maintains tool definitions, schemas, ownership, and enablement settings, while the proxy translates MCP requests into HTTP, gRPC, or TChannel calls and converts responses back into MCP-compatible results.
Uber MCP Gateway with APIs as tools (Source: Uber Blog Post)
The architecture has drawn comparisons with established API gateway patterns. Ajay Sharma, Principal Software Engineer at Microsoft CoreAI, wrote in a LinkedIn post,
Azure API Gateways has been doing this for a while now. It's a recipe for order to the chaos that LLMs come with.
Kelly Goetsch, President at Pipe17, similarly observed in a LinkedIn post that
Uber's new MCP gateway looks identical to gateways we've built over the decades for APIs and later GraphQL.
Tamir Dresher highlighted in a LinkedIn post the continuing relevance of established distributed systems concerns, including security, discovery, observability, and governance.
Uber’s AutoCrawler automates tool discovery using Cadence. It scans internal interface definition language (IDL) registries and extracts API definitions from Protocol Buffers and Thrift schemas. It then generates MCP-compatible schemas and uses a large language model to produce tool descriptions. Newly discovered tools remain disabled until their owning teams review and explicitly enable them. Configuration changes propagate to the data plane without requiring service restarts or redeployments.
Auto Crawler Flow (Source: Uber Blog Post)
The gateway enforces authorization at both server and tool levels through Uber’s internal access control system. It also supports redaction of personally identifiable information (PII) and other sensitive data in tool responses. For third-party integrations, including Jira and Google, a separate service exchanges internal user tokens for the corresponding third-party authentication tokens.
As the tool catalog grows, loading definitions for thousands of tools into an agent’s context becomes inefficient. Uber developed Omni MCP to support incremental discovery, allowing agents to search for servers, discover relevant tools, retrieve individual schemas, and invoke selected tools as needed. Response Projection lets agents request specific response fields instead of receiving complete payloads. Uber’s aifx command-line interface also enables coding agents to discover and invoke tools, writing results to files for selective inspection.

articles.title: Getting the most out of your collaboration strategy
articles.text:
Getting the most out of your collaboration strategy
Implementing AI to enhance communications infrastructure
Collaboration platforms have become central to working life, with Microsoft Teams alone serving more than 320 million monthly active users worldwide. Everywhere you look, they are now part of workplace culture and have been a driving force for change in the use of voice services.
Part of their ongoing appeal is that they are extremely simple to deploy and their familiarity flattens the learning curve for many users almost entirely. For IT teams, one of the key benefits is that they sit within an established supplier environment and, as a result, can help make procurement more straightforward.
Head of Product, Applications Group at Vonage.
Sounds great, but communication infrastructure must also be able to adapt over time - for example, when a business expands or changes how it serves customers. Depending on the platform, any functional limitations may only become clear when a business needs to connect communications with other systems or adapt services for new teams and locations.
The point is that inflexibility can create complications that significantly increase the initial cost of a collaboration solution; something that businesses can easily overlook.
The hidden cost of inflexibility
But what do we mean by complications? Well, any given collaboration platform may work perfectly well for everyday internal calling, yet they all have the potential to become restrictive when communications need to support more specialized processes.
To break this down, everyday internal calls have relatively simple requirements because employees already know who to contact and how to reach them. However, in use cases such as customer-facing communications, employees may require calls to be directed based on factors such as location or the nature of the inquiry.
They may also need access to relevant customer information while the conversation is taking place, whether it is held in a CRM platform or another business application, including a bespoke system where technology integration is more challenging.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
This is where the level and quality of the integration becomes extremely important, as any limitations may force employees to switch between applications or search manually for information that should be readily available.
Get this wrong, and users may require a customer to repeat information, which can extend the interaction and cause frustration. Some businesses may also need more detailed insight into call activity when they are trying to identify problems or improve customer service. For many, this is a central objective when building these systems and processes.
Adding workarounds, such as asking staff to look up customer records manually or using a separate connector to pass data between systems, is one option. However, these can make it harder for IT teams to manage the service consistently as requirements change.
Why AI changes the equation (again)
The issues are becoming even more consequential as businesses look to use AI to handle a greater share of customer communications, because these systems need access to the right information to respond usefully.
For an assistant to deal with an inquiry properly, it needs to draw on the same customer information that a human employee would use. But when an inquiry cannot be resolved automatically, the conversation needs to reach the appropriate person without losing its context.
This is where any disconnect between the communications environment and core business systems can really limit what an AI assistant can do well. AI that cannot access the right information can create an additional layer of friction for customers and employees.
Ideally, these compromises should be avoided entirely. A business should be able to retain the collaboration tools employees already know while adding communication and integration capabilities where needed.
In fact, seamless connectivity and interaction between the user, the AI tools being used, and the relevant customer and operational data should be a core objective rather than a nice-to-have. This means that the technology should be able to accommodate changing requirements without creating a dependence on manual workarounds, so organizations have full control over the pace at which they adopt new technologies and processes.
Businesses planning to expand their use of AI, which is likely to include a great many of them, should consider whether their current communications infrastructure can support those connections. Granted, it is usually possible to retrofit systems to bridge functionality and service gaps, but if the objective is to use AI effectively across a growing number of customer interactions, flexibility needs to be built into the foundation from the outset.

articles.title: Exclusive: Guardz brings Palo Alto Networks browser protection to MSPs serving small businesses - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Exclusive: Guardz brings Palo Alto Networks browser protection to MSPs serving small businesses
Cybersecurity startup Guardz Cyber Ltd. today added browser protection from Palo Alto Networks Inc.’s Prisma Browser for Business to its security platform for managed service providers that protect small businesses.
The integration is aimed at phishing attacks that slip between separate security tools. A typical one starts with an email that lures an employee to a counterfeit login page, and the credentials typed there can put connected accounts at risk. “For most small businesses, the browser is now the office,” said Shivam Srivastava, vice president of product at Palo Alto Networks.
Prisma Browser for Business can block the page when the link is clicked. Guardz then matches that browser event to the original email, related Microsoft 365 activity and endpoint telemetry for the same user identity. From there, the provider and Guardz’s 24/7 managed detection and response team can work the whole chain as a single incident.
The browser-side detection comes from Palo Alto Networks. Inline machine-learning models screen pages for phishing, and Advanced URL Filtering helps block malicious sites, including fake sign-in pages and attacks built to steal live session tokens. The company’s WildFire service analyzes suspect files. Uploads and downloads are scanned as they pass through the browser, which also picks out risky extensions.
Guardz Co-founder and Chief Executive Dor Eisner called the browser “the primary gateway to the modern workspace.” Traditional security tools work in silos that leave gaps in visibility and response, he said, and the agents running on Guardz’s platform are meant to let providers investigate threats autonomously anywhere in that workspace.
Setup falls to Guardz, which handles provisioning and default configuration. Kevin Kehoe of early-access provider Datawise Networks Inc. said the rollout through his firm’s remote monitoring and management software was “super smooth.” Within minutes, he said, the browser extension was “on every Chrome and Edge profile.”
For generative artificial intelligence services used in the browser, Guardz’s AI Usage and Control features let technicians set a separate policy for each client. Those policies can restrict copying, pasting and file transfers by website or by category. Guardz has also introduced a report that gives providers a per-client view of AI tool usage.
Palo Alto Networks moved into enterprise browsers with its 2023 acquisition of Israeli startup Talon Cyber Security Ltd. Prisma Browser for Business, its version for small businesses, went on sale in the U.S. in March.
Guardz is a venture capital-backed startup that has raised $84 million, including a $56 million Series B round led by ClearSky in June 2025.

articles.title: Hackers sabotam freezers de supermercados na Europa • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Hackers sabotam freezers de supermercados na Europa
Ataques atingiram sistemas de refrigeração na Bélgica, Estônia, Luxemburgo e Suécia. Temperaturas foram alteradas remotamente para 50° C.
Supermercados de diferentes países europeus foram atingidos por um ataque cibernético nesta segunda-feira (02/11). Geladeiras e freezers conectados à internet começaram a superaquecer na Bélgica, em Luxemburgo, na Suécia e na Estônia. Em alguns casos, a temperatura foi alterada remotamente para 50° C, o que levou à perda dos alimentos.
De acordo com a agência Reuters, várias lojas espalhadas pelos países tiveram os mesmos problemas nos equipamentos. O Centro Nacional de Cibersegurança da Suécia investiga os casos. Segundo o diretor John Billow, há um número considerável de dispositivos de tecnologia operacional expostos no país, o que reforça a necessidade de atualizações e correções de segurança.
O gerente de um dos supermercados afetados em Estocolmo afirmou que os alimentos “estão destruídos”. O ataque teria acontecido por volta das 22h de ontem (01/11), mas só foi percebido hoje.
Há cerca de um mês, outros ataques aconteceram contra redes de supermercados na França. Na ocasião, hackers assumiram o controle de unidades de refrigeração e elevaram as temperaturas também até 50° C, provocando incêndios e perdas de alimentos. As autoridades não identificaram os responsáveis.
Os incidentes lembram outro caso registrado em setembro, na Coreia do Sul: consumidores relataram problemas em geladeiras inteligentes da linha Bespoke AI 4-Door, da Samsung. Uma atualização de software distribuída por engano fez alguns aparelhos pararem de refrigerar, causando a perda dos alimentos armazenados.
A Samsung interrompeu a distribuição do pacote e substituiu as placas-mãe dos equipamentos afetados. A empresa pediu desculpas pelo transtorno e orientou os proprietários dos aparelhos afetados a agendar uma visita técnica, onde os técnicos poderiam substituir a placa-mãe dos equipamentos.
Diferentemente dos ataques registrados na Europa, porém, esse incidente não envolveu invasores: a falha ocorreu durante o processo de atualização do software.

articles.title: Googling "Zelda" today offers a glimpse of how search worked in 1998
articles.text:
The year was 1998. Britney Spears topped the charts, Bill Clinton was impeached, and a couple of little websites called Google and Ars Technica came online. It was also the year Nintendo released The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo 64. Google, which has come to dominate the Internet (Ars is still working on that), is celebrating the imminent release of the Ocarina of Time remaster by temporarily transporting us back to that storied year with a search Easter egg.
To access the Google time machine, you just have to search for either “Zelda” or “Ocarina of Time.” Google will load the standard 2026 results page, but you’ll see an animated Master Sword in the lower right corner. It appears on both mobile and desktop—just click the sword and enjoy the show.
After a little time-skipping animation and a Link shout (you know the one), you’ll swear it’s 1998 again. The search page is transformed into a simple list of blue links with retro Google branding. This is particularly apt given the time-shifting mechanics in Ocarina of Time.
Classic Google used to provide a list of 10 links on each page, but there are only seven included in the Easter egg. This is a curated list of links rather than a real search. You get the official Nintendo Zelda page, Zelda on Wikipedia, Zelda games on Amazon, and a couple more.

articles.title: Google Introduces $250,000 Root-in-Cloud Bug Bounty Reward
articles.text:
Google has expanded its Cloud Vulnerability Reward Program (VRP) with a new $250,000 top-tier reward for security weaknesses that could lead to full administrative control.
The premier payout is “specifically designed to recognize high-impact architectural research” and will be handed out to researchers who can demonstrate gaining ‘roles/owner’ privileges or complete IAM control over arbitrary Google Cloud organizations or projects.
According to the internet giant, to qualify for the reward, the exploit path should not depend on pre-existing access to a project, previously compromised credentials, or user interaction/social engineering.
Reports that demonstrate remote code execution (RCE) in Borg (Google’s underlying production infrastructure) or root-in-production will also be evaluated for the new $250,000 root-in-cloud reward.
“Because code execution in Borg has the potential to impact service availability or cross-tenant data, researchers must halt all probing immediately upon achieving any execution in Borg. Escalation, extracting production credentials, and lateral movement are not allowed and will result in researcher disqualification,” Google Cloud CISO Chris Betz said.
The company has added the root-in-cloud validation criteria to its Cloud VRP page, explaining that it will award the bug bounty if its analysis of the initial entry point, execution context, and attack surface demonstrates that full arbitrary tenant or project takeover is possible.
“Identifying tenant-isolation bypasses and complex cross-service logic flaws requires human creativity, intuition, and rigorous systems analysis combined with the power of agentic systems,” Betz noted.
According to Michael Cote, Google Cloud’s vulnerability reward program lead, first-time researchers who combine their own intuition with agentic tools are finding more interesting bugs, on average, than novices did two years ago.
He also pointed out that finding bugs eligible for the new root-in-cloud tier requires deep architectural intuition and AI.
“High incentives require clear, safe rules of engagement. We never want researchers testing exploits against real customer projects. Instead, we created a deterministic proof-of-root mechanism using a designated service account. Researchers can cryptographically prove unauthorized access against that identity,” Cote said.

articles.title: El HomeView es solo el principio: filtrados los planes de Apple para una versión Ultra con brazo robótico
articles.text:
De la mano del HomeView, Apple recientemente ha dado el salto a una nueva de dispositivos para el hogar conectado. Pero este es solo el primer paso para ganarse un lugar en el segmento de las pantallas inteligentes. La compañía tiene planes todavía más ambiciosos de la mano de un HomeView Ultra, según un nuevo reporte de The Information.
El citado medio indica que el presunto HomeView Ultra llegará en algún momento de 2027 y expandirá el catálogo de Apple en el segmento de la robótica aplicada al hogar. En tal sentido, la publicación ratifica algunos datos que ya había filtrado Mark Gurman antes de que los de Cupertino introdujeran el HomeView.
Puntualmente, se menciona que el HomeView Ultra estaría equipado con una pantalla más grande, de 9 pulgadas, y que esta se acoplará a un brazo robótico que podrá girar 360° sobre su base. El diseño del soporte, que también funge de altavoz, sería muy parecido al de HomeView original. Por su parte, la extensión motorizada para sostener y mover el panel la haría parecerse al iMac G4 o a la lámpara de Pixar.
Apple pretende que el HomeView Ultra pueda realizar una cantidad de tareas de forma automatizada, como encender las luces cuando una persona ingresa a la sala. Asimismo, podría sacar provecho de la IA para tomar medidas proactivas; por ejemplo, para pedirle a un gato que se baje de la mesa.
La compañía también lo dotaría de un sistema inteligente para que el brazo robótico evite golpear otros objetos dentro de su trayectoria, y más. Aunque es posible que su función más notoria sea el seguimiento de personas dentro de la habitación, pues se encargaría de ajustar la ubicación de la pantalla para que el usuario tenga siempre la mejor vista posible.
Apple lanzaría el HomeView Ultra con brazo robótico en 2027
Según The Information, Apple comenzó a desarrollar este dispositivo en 2019. Aunque revela que las pretensiones originales de la compañía eran mucho más austeras que las que se plantean ahora con el HomeView Ultra. La evolución de la IA aplicada a este tipo de dispositivos habría revitalizado el proyecto en los últimos años.
El reporte incluso menciona que el hardware del HomeView Ultra estaría terminado desde hace un par de años, pero que su lanzamiento se vio afectado por discrepancias dentro de Apple por su software. Al parecer, los ingenieros y ejecutivos de la firma no se habrían puesto de acuerdo respecto de qué funciones incorporar en la primera generación y cuáles en modelos subsiguientes.
Si bien la idea de Apple sería lanzar el presunto HomeView Ultra en algún momento de 2027, no se descarta que pueda postergarse hasta 2028. En cuanto al precio, el modelo con brazo robótico sería considerablemente más caro que el HomeView actual. De acuerdo con la información publicada, su PVP podría rondar o superar los 1.000 dólares. Sin dudas, un salto drástico desde los 299 dólares de la versión que se anunció semanas atrás.

articles.title: Military explores commercial 5G networks for enemy drone defense — AI agents developed the system recently used in battlefield trials in Latvia
articles.text:
Military explores commercial 5G networks for enemy drone defense — AI agents developed the system recently used in battlefield trials in Latvia
AT&T and Ericsson demoed a similar system in Texas last week.
The military is looking at leveraging commercial 5G communications to enhance battlefield sensing. We have two examples of the reuse of existing communications infrastructure for drone detection. In Latvia, NATO recently tested an AI-agent-assisted counter-drone engagement system that made use of existing 5G masts. Meanwhile, in the U.S., AT&T and Ericsson demoed “drone detection using advanced network sensing over a 5G network” near a large sporting venue.
Drones and drone-defense capabilities are clearly vital in current armed conflicts and are beginning to be taken very seriously worldwide. We’ve seen rapid developments in this theater, particularly in Russia, Ukraine, and also in the Middle East this year. If the military could leverage the extensive cellular networks across most nations for drone sensing, it sounds like a clear win. However, we’d worry about 5G masts becoming an even more attractive target.
In Latvia, NATO ran a Digital Backbone Experimentation exercise, known as DiBaX 2026. Between October 19 and 30, the organization investigated whether 5G towers could passively detect and track flying objects, specifically drones. If the trials were successful, it could mean existing large-scale telecommunications networks would gain another purpose – enhancing national security. Moreover, it would help NATO gain resilience to disruption, thanks to multiple networks, satellites, etc.
The NATO-tested solution is said to have been designed by AI agents. “We have connected systems that were never designed to communicate with each other, using artificial intelligence to overcome interoperability barriers,” said Admiral Pierre Vandier, NATO’s Supreme Allied Commander Transformation. “It’s the first time that we have, for example, a Maven system that is speaking to a national system, and that has been fixed in hours with Agentic AI.”
Three methods of utilizing commercial 5G were tested in the Baltic country, which conducted the exercises alongside the United States, Canada, Germany, Finland, Lithuania, and other allies. Some tests admittedly failed, but when things don’t work as expected, you can learn some important lessons.
In the U.S., AT&T and Ericsson demonstrated drone detection over 5G outside of AT&T Stadium, in Arlington, Texas. Apparently, this is an early taster of 6G technology, which officially includes both comms and sensing. According to the official PR, this system was capable of detecting and locating multiple drones, then tracking their movement. The drones flew at altitudes between 300 and 400 feet within the coverage area.
It seems like the sporting venue was chosen for the demo, as such places can be targeted by terrorists and the like. A potential advantage of this sensing tech is that it can “support new levels of low altitude threat detection and tracking around major venues, public spaces and other complex environments.”
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
With the above two experiments delivering promising results, 5G (and 6G) drone sensing networks piggybacking on commercial masts looks like something that will be genuinely useful for defense, with little extra investment required.
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Mark Tyson is a news editor at Tom's Hardware. He enjoys covering the full breadth of PC tech; from business and semiconductor design to products approaching the edge of reason.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Critical CVEs, Linux DDoS Botnet, Device-Code Phishing, Android Spyware and More
articles.text:
Some attacks this week didn't need much of a trick. A fake support call, a trusted extension, a shared link, or a device with no password. Small things that people barely think about. Yet each was enough to cause serious trouble.
Then there were the bigger messes. Billions stolen, hidden networks of hacked devices, poisoned software, and attackers finding new ways to turn normal tools against their users. Even the places meant to keep money and systems safe ended up with problems of their own. The strange part is how often the damage started somewhere nobody was looking.
And that's before getting to the long list of fresh bugs, shady services, and scams making the rounds. Quite a bit to sort through. Here's what made the list.
⚡ Threat of the Week
N. Korea Sets New Record with Binance $6.43B Crypto Theft — The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has officially attributed the theft of more than $6 billion in virtual assets from Binance to a North Korean hacking group called TraderTraitor. The haul eclipses the $1.46 billion plundered from Bybit in February 2025, making it the largest cryptocurrency theft in history. The funds were stolen across 11 blockchains, 82% of which were on Ethereum and Bitcoin. Of the $6.43 billion stolen by TraderTraitor, $2.85 billion of the assets have been frozen on-chain by Tether, Circle, Ripple, Arbitrum, and Optimism.
Mythos: Map Attack Paths to Collapse Lateral Breach Routes
Access the Gartner® CTEM report to see how the Mythos platform continuously maps cross-domain attack paths and isolates key choke points to break active lateral movement to critical assets.
Get the full report ➝
🔔 Top News
- Volt Typhoon Uses Covert Silent Train Network in 0-Day Attacks — Chinese state-sponsored hacking group Volt Typhoon has been using a framework that relies on rotating chains of connected devices compromised on demand, including to facilitate zero-day attacks targeting high-value systems. It's codenamed Silent Train because the threat actor uses it against select targets, cleans it up after each operation to minimize detection and attribution, and refreshes it continuously. Silent Train is a relay infrastructure formed of compromised devices to hide the origin of its attacks. The findings highlight evidence of efforts to pre-position access within what it described as "strategic communications, critical infrastructure and other ecosystems that become essential during geopolitical tensions or crises." Silent Train is built around "rapidly rotating chains of compromised SOHO, IoT and enterprise devices." The nature of these victims "indicates deliberate efforts to maintain access to critical ecosystems that support defense, logistics, communications, military and civilian operations, especially during heightened tensions or crises in the Indo-Pacific region."
- Polymarket Briefly Suspended Trading After Third-Party Hack — Prediction market platform Polymarket temporarily suspended trading after hackers compromised DebugBear, a third-party service, to distribute cryptocurrency-draining JavaScript that siphoned approximately $2.7 million in assets from 33 deposit wallets in under an hour. "Our DNS server records were compromised through our domain registrar. We are currently unable to receive emails sent to our domain," DebugBear said in an update shared on October 31, 2026. "Based on our initial investigation this attack targeted the website of a specific customer. We have not seen any indication of a compromise of our internal systems, though we will continue to investigate this." In June, Polymarket disclosed another third-party compromise that injected a malicious script into its frontend, leading to reported losses of around $3 million.
- Shared ChatGPT Links Lead to Code Execution — Researchers from Parameter Labs disclosed a now-patched flaw in ChatGPT that turned an ordinary share link into an attacker-controlled JavaScript running inside the signed-in session of whoever opened it. "An attacker could create a malicious conversation, publish it using ChatGPT's normal sharing feature, and send the link to another user," Parameter Labs said. "When the victim opened the share, the payload executed as chatgpt.com with access to the victim's authenticated web session." Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to enumerate the victim's conversation list, retrieve content from a private conversation, and send data from that conversation to an external server.
- Official Claude Code Extension on Cursor Marketplace with SSH Backdoor — Two versions of the Claude Code extension distributed through Cursor Marketplace were tampered with to install a persistent SSH backdoor on affected systems. Cursor said the incident impacted up to 5,000 users. In response to the incident, Cursor said it rotated its keys, rebuilt the marketplace, and worked with the cloud provider to take the server offline so that the reverse shell is no longer functional. It also stressed that no other extensions were maliciously modified as part of the attack. However, several questions surrounding the supply chain attack remain unanswered, including how the threat actor managed to publish a malicious extension under Anthropic's name on Cursor's marketplace and what level of access they were able to obtain.
- FBI Seizes bulletproof hosting provider Virtualine — The U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) announced the seizure of a domain associated with a bulletproof hosting provider (BPH) named Virtualine. The DoJ said the service was being used to commit and facilitate prolific criminal activity, including "the advertisement of sexually explicit images of minors, the intentional disclosure of nonconsensual intimate visual depictions of adults and minors, and international money laundering designed to conceal and promote criminal conduct. However, the long-term impact of such crackdowns has been questioned. According to Intel 471, disruptions have driven customers to newer services operated by former resellers, fragmenting the market rather than eliminating demand. The disclosure comes as the Australian Signals Directorate said it gained backend access to Amadey's operations and severed its access to 180,000 computers across the globe.
- Keystone to Destroy 18,835 Hardware Wallets — Keystone confirmed a security incident involving its official website where an attacker exploited a vulnerability in a third-party data monitoring tool to escalate privileges and obtain some customer information and a key used to verify the authenticity of our devices. This included 25,964 records containing names, contact details, shipping addresses, and order information, along with 12,873 checkout records containing names, contact details, and shipping information submitted by users. Besides stopping the use of the old key, Keystone plans to destroy 18,835 devices in existing inventory that contain the old key. "Shipping of all unshipped orders from our official website has been suspended," it said. "Sales will switch to a preorder model until production of devices using the new key is complete, after which shipping will resume." In a related development, another hardware cryptocurrency wallet maker Trezor said it received credible reports about a suspected hardware crypto-theft implant in a Trezor Safe 5 sold by its reseller CryptoBilis in Southeast Asia. "If you bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis from March 2026 onwards and are using it to store funds, please move your funds to a newly created wallet with a new seed as soon as possible," it said.
- uCreator Android Spyware Can Clone WeChat Accounts — A commercial Android spyware offering called uCreator is designed to target ordinary users of mobile wallets and messaging applications across China and Southeast Asia, including GCash (Philippines), WeChat, WeCom, QQ, Telegram, WhatsApp, LINE, Zalo, KakaoTalk, Viber, and MoMo. It can also be used to clone WeChat accounts. Victims install repackaged copies of legitimate applications disturbed through sideloading or social engineering flows. The attack leverages a variation of on-device virtualization techniques observed in malware like GodFather to conduct fraud. "GodFather spins the banking app up inside a virtual container and drops a fake overlay on top to phish credentials: the victim is really typing into the attacker's screen," security researcher Ovi Liber said. "uCreator shares the substrate but it draws no overlay. This is a case really of overlay-the-app versus instrument-the-app, with the second being quieter and also not being confined to a login screen. As an operator, it scales to any app the vendor writes a module for."
- Gheist Turns GitHub Actions into a Secret Extraction Service — An automated campaign dubbed Gheist has been observed planting a secret-dumping workflow named "sync-check" in every repository that stolen GitHub tokens can reach. "The workflow seeks to print the repository's secrets into its own workflow log," Wiz said. "Then, the tool downloads the log through the GitHub API and deletes the run seconds later." The Google-owned cloud security company said it recovered more than 13,500 planted branches from more than 850 compromised accounts. The campaign was first detected in mid-September 2026.
️🔥 Trending CVEs
Bugs drop weekly, and the gap between a patch and an exploit is shrinking fast. These are the heavy hitters for the week: high-severity, widely used, or already being poked at in the wild.
Check the list, patch what you have, and hit the ones marked urgent first — CVE-2026-115889, CVE-2026-115893 (Wasmtime), CVE-2026-90975 (Fireblocks mpc-lib), CVE-2026-91141 (COVESA vsomeip), CVE-2026-88781, CVE-2026-75775, CVE-2026-75779, CVE-2026-93489, CVE-2026-17518, CVE-2026-75753, CVE-2026-102438, CVE-2026-14911, CVE-2026-16528, CVE-2026-19386, CVE-2026-19396, CVE-2026-93495, CVE-2026-14157, CVE-2026-13313 (ASUS), CVE-2026-114573, CVE-2026-9082, CVE-2026-118539 (Drupal), CVE-2026-114595, CVE-2026-114596, CVE-2026-114597, CVE-2026-114598 (EPICS Base), CVE-2026-97631 (TianoCore EDK II), CVE-2026-115881, CVE-2026-115884 (GoAhead), CVE-2026-110720 (HashiCorp consul-k8s), CVE-2026-90885, CVE-2026-85250, CVE-2026-88901, CVE-2026-88900, CVE-2026-78165, CVE-2026-85251 (Apache Camel), CVE-2026-115547 (Okta), CVE-2026-114349, CVE-2026-111551 (Apache Kafka), CVE-2026-118306, CVE-2026-118331, CVE-2026-118348, CVE-2026-118344, CVE-2026-106378 (Google Chrome), from CVE-2026-117860 through CVE-2026-117954, from CVE-2026-118005 through CVE-2026-118017 (Mozilla Firefox), CVE-2026-98432 (Linux kernel), CVE-2026-18672, CVE-2026-19219 (Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX), TRA-2020-14 (Kodi), CVE-2026-107239, CVE-2026-107238, CVE-2023-22793 (Veeam), CVE-2026-103401, CVE-2026-103402, CVE-2026-103403, CVE-2026-103404, CVE-2026-103405, CVE-2026-103406, CVE-2026-103407, CVE-2026-103408, CVE-2026-103409 (Juniper Networks Session Smart Router), CVE-2026-111585 (TeamViewer), CAN-2026-2035970 (Intelbras IP cameras), CVE-2026-103594, CVE-2026-112709, CVE-2026-112710, CVE-2026-93857, CVE-2026-103593, CVE-2026-93865, CVE-2026-93866 (WatchGuard Fireware OS), CVE-2026-101296, CVE-2026-101356, CVE-2026-103119 (Apache Tomcat), CVE-2026-112816 (Canonical LXD), CVE-2026-93680, CVE-2026-110186 (Langflow OSS), and a preauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in TightVNC.
🎥 Cybersecurity Webinars
- Learn How to Turn Identity Context Into Faster, Smarter SOC Response → Your security tools can detect suspicious activity, but without identity context, critical threats may go unnoticed. As machine identities and AI agents expand the attack surface, SOC teams need deeper visibility to respond effectively. Join this expert-led webinar to discover how connecting identity intelligence with security operations can help uncover hidden risks, accelerate investigations, and contain threats faster.
- From Zero-Days to Exploits in Minutes: Are You Ready for AI Threats? → AI-powered cyberattacks are accelerating, shrinking the time security teams have to detect, investigate, and respond. Are your defenses ready to keep up? Join this expert-led webinar to discover how to strengthen AI threat readiness, improve attack-surface visibility, and build faster, more resilient security operations before attackers gain the upper hand.
📰 Around the Cyber World
- A massive search-hijacking campaign called Searchjacked involving 319 Chrome extensions with a combined 13.4 million reported installations hijacked users' searches through tracking servers, captured queries, and collected referral payments from Microsoft Bing and Yahoo. The findings from Socket expand on the April 2025 discovery of 57 Chrome extensions with six million users, adding 264 newly identified add-ons with another 8.7 million users. Although they are hosted on the Chrome Web Store, they are unlisted and don't appear in users' searches on the extension store. Instead, the extensions are promoted through sketchy advertisements shown as pop overs or pop unders on websites. Socket also discovered a cluster of malicious Firefox extensions that mimic Phantom, Jupiter, and Bitget wallets to steal recovery phrases and private keys. A third campaign, documented by Am I Being Pwned?, involves 60 Chrome extensions with 2.3 million installs across 4 publisher accounts. Called OffiDocs, the extensions masquerade as document programs and exfiltrate all URLs visited by users to be shared with business partners, and other third-parties, or redirect users to one of their pages on redcoolmedia.net or runapps.org
- Microsoft revealed details of two human-operated intrusions in which threat actors used Microsoft Teams messages and calls to impersonate IT or help desk personnel and socially engineer users into granting interactive remote access, primarily through Quick Assist. "Once connected, the threat actors staged portable Python, Bun, or Java runtimes, performed host and network discovery, and assessed Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) for certificate-based authentication paths," Microsoft said. "This intrusion pattern is high impact because a user-approved remote session can become certificate-backed access to privileged identities and domain infrastructure."
- Threat actors are increasingly turning to vulnerabilities as a means for breaking into corporate systems, as exfiltration and extortion-only attacks emerged as the fastest-growing category in the third quarter of 2026.
- Check Point detailed three anti-detect browsers, Kameleo, AdsPower, and MultiLogin, that could enable a single operator to silently manage thousands of isolated accounts across multiple platforms, and evade detection systems that look for scams and coordinated inauthentic behavior. "Threat actors abuse these platforms, taking over accounts and using them for financial fraud, phishing and malware distribution," Check Point said. "These accounts can also be used to coordinate influence operations, which becomes an even greater concern ahead of elections. These tools already use AI integration, from built-in automation templates to offering a dedicated MCP server that pipes LLM-generated content directly into pre-warmed account profiles at machine speed. Running a large-scale social media operation now requires only a credit card instead of a technical team."
- Russia and Ukraine both revealed their emergency alert systems were hit by cyber attacks. The attacks caused the two systems to send fake emergency alerts. Per BBC, Ukraine's air raid app sent false red-level air raid warnings nationwide. A few hours later, Russia said its alert app was also attacked, but said that it was only an "ancillary" service among sirens and other warnings. It’s not clear if the two incidents are connected.
- A sophisticated Android malware campaign has been targeting the Indian banking sector since July 2025 using seven distinct trojan families that facilitate banking fraud through coordinated phishing, credential theft, and unauthorized cryptojacking. It is orchestrated by a financially motivated threat cluster codenamed CyberDakait that's operating in India since January 2025. The malware families are GhostBat, cyb3rx, godz, d-passive, d-shine, tenxen, and appkjl. Distributed via coordinated smishing and vishing campaigns, they are designed to harvest sensitive information, including bank mobile application credentials, credit card details, outstanding balances, through sophisticated overlay attacks. "The main goal of the campaign is the distribution of Android malware to conduct cryptojacking and elaborate banking fraud," Group-IB said. "The malicious applications are commonly hosted on GitHub repositories to maintain legitimacy and evade security controls, where the initial APK functions as a dropper that downloads and executes the main payload alongside a cryptocurrency mining module, enabling the threat actors to generate revenue through both direct financial theft and unauthorized cryptocurrency mining on infected devices." A total of at least 17,960 compromised devices have been identified, and about 7.6 million SMS messages were intercepted from victim devices.
- A new phishing campaign has disguised credential theft as an invitation to a private AI event from Anthropic, and uses GoTo Webinar branding, a Zoom-style registration page, and convincing Google and Microsoft login pages to steal login credentials. "Risks to the organization from this campaign include threat actors compromising a sensitive account, accessing the account’s sensitive documents (e.g., proprietary marketing material), and using the compromised account as an initial vector to further infiltrate the organization," Cofense said.
- A new campaign is using judicial-themed phishing emails targeting Colombian organizations to deliver XWorm via a multi-stage chain. The initial payloads resemble legitimate Colombian administrative or judicial correspondence, according to Arctic Wolf.
- Multiple Russian-language traffer teams that have adapted affiliate-fraud models to capitalize on growing public interest in prediction markets such as PolyMarket and Kalshi. "The platforms offered by three such teams — AtlasCore, PolyFucked, and Magnetic Team — provide websites, administrative panels, cryptocurrency payment infrastructure, victim-management capabilities, technical support, and promotional guidance," Recorded Future said. "This model lowers barriers to entry for affiliates and enables campaigns to scale rapidly as new trends attract potential victims. The services combine convincing prediction-market interfaces with established fraud mechanisms designed to manipulate victims and prevent them from recovering deposited funds." Advertised compensation includes 70% to 80% of net profits for AtlasCore affiliates, a minimum 60% revenue share for PolyFucked affiliates, and a base 70% share of victim deposits for Magnetic Team affiliates.
- Nozomi Networks detailed a new Go-based malware for Linux called Kairos that turns a compromised machine into a node in the operator's DDoS botnet. "On command, the bot opens hundreds to thousands of TCP connections to a target chosen by the operator and keeps them open for the requested duration, sending a single near-empty keepalive byte every few seconds," Nozomi Networks said. "Initial access came through Telnet, using the default credentials (user root, empty password). The operator then staged the payload with a short shell sequence that downloaded it over HTTP from the same server the bot later calls home."
- A previously undocumented Microsoft device code phishing kit codenamed MadApe is using business-themed PDF lures, configurable redirects, and fake document-sharing pages to trick victims into completing Microsoft device code authentication. It was first observed by Group-IB on January 7, 2026.
- Threat actors behind Aur0ra ransomware, aka Gold Ogre, are extensively using AI to develop tools and to orchestrate and execute ransomware operations, Sophos said. The AI-assisted post-exploitation framework is developed with Cursor AI assistance. "The threat actors used Cursor to escalate from credential access to domain administrator in preparation for data collection and ransomware deployment," Sophos said. "AI guardrails were bypassed by framing the intrusions as authorized red team activity or 'diagnostics testing.' Intrusions were orchestrated by Cursor's Composer agentic coding model as well as AI models provided by Anthropic, xAI, and Moonshot." Although the threat actors initially used Anthropic almost exclusively, they have since introduced other models.
- Malicious model repositories on Hugging Face are being used to fuel a cryptomining and backdoor campaign. "The payloads were written for GPU hosts running self-hosted inference, especially Xinference and GPUStack, along with rented GPU machines, shared research notebooks, and CI jobs that pull small test models without anyone reading the code," Pluto Security said. Instead of using poisoned weights or pickle exploits, the campaign abuses a Hugging Face option, trust_remote_code, that lets a model ship its own Python code. When this option is set to true, that code is automatically executed on a victim's machine as soon as the model loads.
- Bitdefender and NETGEAR found that Smart TVs and connected plugs accounted for a large share of recorded security weaknesses. Televisions represented 22.7% of vulnerability observations, followed by smart plugs at 22.4%. "Before buying connected equipment, the support period deserves attention alongside the price and features," the 2026 IoT Security Landscape Report said. For equipment already in the home, knowing whether updates are still available is part of knowing whether it should stay connected.
- A tech-support scam is directing victims to install the commercially available remote access application UltraViewer. Infoblox, which broke down details of the campaign, said it found links to a long-running QuickBooks phishing campaign. "That campaign uses over 350 QuickBooks-lookalike domains and directs victims to call scammers who attempt to steal QuickBooks credentials," Infoblox said. The scam has been found directing users to trojanized UltraViewer and UltraMailer, installers that lead to the deployment of DarkKometa and njRAT, respectively.
- In an analysis of The Com ecosystem, Flare said the loose-knit collective comprises three distinct intrusion clusters, Scattered Spider, LAPSUS$, and ShinyHunters, while SP1D3R HUNTERS (aka Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters) represents an amalgamation of all three. Security researcher Jon DiMaggio warned against attributing any activity post-2022 to LAPSUS, which ceased operating years ago. "LAPSUS$ operated at full capacity for roughly nine months, from its December 2021 attack against Brazil’s Ministry of Health through its concentrated campaign in early 2022, before a series of arrests in mid-to-late 2022 ended it as an organized entity," DiMaggio said. "Scattered Spider and LAPSUS$ overlapped by a few months at the start and by at least one individual across their lifespans, and they still ran different playbooks against different targets toward different ends."
Conclusion
That's about it for this week. Some attacks were carefully planned. Others worked because someone clicked the wrong thing, trusted the wrong tool, or left something exposed. Different methods, same result. And with so many systems connected to other systems, even a small mistake can travel further than expected.
The bigger concern is how normal some of these attacks have become. Nothing particularly clever is needed when the easy routes still work. Keep an eye on what has access, check what needs fixing, and don't assume familiar means safe. See you next week.

articles.title: Apple reports record iPhone sales quarter even without base iPhone 18
articles.text:
Apple just had released its fourth-quarter earnings report, and it was a particularly big one.
Notably, the company reported US$57.58 billion (about C$80.5 billion) in iPhone revenue, a 17 per cent jump from the same time last year. For context, this was achieved with a smaller-than-usual phone lineup.
Traditionally, Apple has launched the standard and premium versions of its phones in the same September window, but for this year’s iPhone 18 family, it only debuted the 18 Pro and Pro Max, as well as its first-ever foldable, the Duo. The base iPhone 18 has yet to be released, with reports suggesting it will come in early 2027 alongside the lower-cost 18e and Air 2.
In other words, Apple still managed to have a record iPhone quarter on the back of its more expensive phones. It’s also important to stress that the Duo, which starts at a whopping $3,000 in Canada, isn’t included in this report since its pre-orders and launch took place in October.
Overall, Apple reported US$114.5 billion (about C$160 billion) in revenue, marking a 12 percent increase. The Mac and services businesses grew during Q4, the latter of which actually reaching an all-time high of US$31.57 billion (about C$44.1 billion), although iPad revenue declined 10 per cent year-over-year.
Looking ahead to the next quarter, Apple has the aforementioned Duo and a new touchscreen MacBook. It will also be John Ternus’ first full quarter as CEO, as he took over from Apple veteran Tim Cook on Sept. 1.
Source: Apple

articles.title: New York Times and other outlets sue web browser Brave over alleged content scraping | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The New York Times sued Brave, the 11-year-old, privacy-focused browser company, on Monday, alleging it scraped the outlet’s copyrighted content and unlawfully distributed it to customers the suit names as Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere.
Separately on Monday, the Daily News, the Chicago Tribune, and the Orlando Sentinel filed a similar lawsuit. Both were brought in federal court in Manhattan.
The New York Times, which has also sued OpenAI and Perplexity over similar claims, likens Brave to a “supplier, dealer, and distributor of stolen copyrighted content” for AI companies.
“In this way, Brave acts both like a burglar that misappropriates the content of publishers, and an AI ‘fence’ that sells stolen content to third parties,” the suit reads. It says Brave built an index of more than 30 billion web pages using an unidentified crawler, leaving publishers unable to block it.
The suit also targets a Brave browser feature that bypasses paywalls and the company’s practice of blocking publishers’ ads while selling its own.
Founded in 2015, Brave has raised roughly $250 million to date, according to private-market trackers. The Times seeks an injunction and damages.
Brave did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

articles.title: NASA procura ajuda para salvar o Hubble
articles.text:
A NASA abriu uma nova rodada de consultas ao setor privado para avaliar alternativas de manutenção do Telescópio Espacial Hubble. A iniciativa ocorre mais de dois anos depois de serem consideradas arriscadas as propostas comerciais analisadas pela agência anteriormente.
Publicada em 29 de outubro, a solicitação de informações (RFI, na sigla em inglês) convida empresas a apresentar tecnologias e serviços que poderiam ser utilizados em uma futura missão ao observatório. Os interessados têm até 30 de novembro para encaminhar suas propostas. A consulta não representa, necessariamente, a contratação de uma missão.
Mesmo após mais de 36 anos em operação, o Hubble continua produzindo resultados científicos importantes. A última missão tripulada de manutenção do telescópio ocorreu em 2009, com o uso do Ônibus Espacial.
Desde então, o telescópio apresentou problemas técnicos, incluindo falhas em seus giroscópios, componentes responsáveis por ajudar a controlar sua orientação. Ainda assim, a procura por observações supera em sete vezes o tempo disponível.
Outro desafio é a perda gradual de altitude do observatório. Atualmente, o Hubble está a aproximadamente 470 km da superfície terrestre, mas o atrito com as camadas superiores da atmosfera reduz sua altitude ao longo do tempo. Segundo as estimativas da NASA, existe 10% de probabilidade de reentrada atmosférica até setembro de 2032. Esse índice sobe para 50% até dezembro de 2033.
NASA considera três possibilidades para o Hubble
A nova consulta apresenta três alternativas que poderiam ser desenvolvidas com participação comercial. A primeira prevê o envio de uma espaçonave para elevar a órbita do telescópio de aproximadamente 470 para pelo menos 600 km, reduzindo os efeitos do arrasto atmosférico e prolongando seu funcionamento.
A segunda proposta combina o reajuste orbital com serviços de manutenção. O objetivo seria melhorar o desempenho do observatório e aumentar sua capacidade de continuar operando diante de problemas técnicos.
Já a terceira alternativa considera uma solução diferente: em vez de prolongar sua vida útil, uma espaçonave ajudaria a direcionar o Hubble para uma reentrada controlada na atmosfera terrestre.
Tentativas anteriores não avançaram
A NASA já havia demonstrado interesse em parcerias privadas para atender o telescópio. Em setembro de 2022, a agência firmou um acordo com a SpaceX para estudar a possibilidade de utilizar uma cápsula Crew Dragon em uma missão de manutenção. A iniciativa também envolveu Jared Isaacman, hoje administrador-chefe da agência, que na época participava do programa Polaris, voltado a voos espaciais tripulados privados.
Três meses depois, a NASA publicou outra solicitação de informações para receber propostas de diferentes empresas. Foram apresentadas oito respostas, incluindo uma da Astroscale, especializada em serviços de manutenção e remoção de satélites, em parceria com a desenvolvedora de veículos de transferência orbital Momentus.
Em junho de 2024, porém, a agência decidiu não avançar com nenhuma das propostas. Naquele período, um dos três giroscópios que ainda funcionavam no Hubble apresentou falhas, obrigando o observatório a operar com apenas um desses componentes. A mudança limitou algumas possibilidades de observação.
Na ocasião, Mark Clampin, então diretor da divisão de astrofísica da agência, afirmou que os riscos envolvidos poderiam provocar perda prematura de dados científicos e envolver dificuldades tecnológicas. Ele também esclareceu que o trabalho realizado com a SpaceX era um estudo de viabilidade, e não uma recomendação formal para executar a missão.
Nova avaliação considera custos e experiências recentes
Isaacman voltou a defender a possibilidade de uma missão recentemente. Em comunicado, afirmou que o estudo anterior com a SpaceX havia chegado a uma recomendação favorável à manutenção. A declaração, entretanto, contrasta com a avaliação apresentada por Clampin em 2024. O relatório final do estudo não foi divulgado integralmente, e uma apresentação obtida por meio de um pedido de acesso à informação estava quase toda censurada.
Em junho deste ano, Shawn Domagal-Goldman, atual diretor da divisão de astrofísica da NASA, também demonstrou abertura para reconsiderar uma missão robótica. Segundo ele, os custos dessas operações estão menores do que o previsto inicialmente, o que poderia ajudar a reduzir despesas operacionais estimadas em quase US$100 milhões por ano.
A decisão final depende agora das propostas que a indústria privada apresentar até o final do prazo – soluções que podem definir o futuro de um dos instrumentos mais importantes da história da astronomia.
Flávia Correia é jornalista do Olhar Digital, cobrindo Ciência e Espaço.

articles.title: Privatsphäre in Gefahr? Whatsapp erkennt jetzt Kalenderdaten und Telefonnummern
articles.text:
Whatsapp erkennt jetzt Kalenderdaten und Telefonnummern: Wie steht es um die Privatsphäre?
Whatsapp-Absprachen zu Terminen, etwa in Gruppenchats, dürften bei Milliarden App-Nutzer:innen keine Seltenheit sein. Und doch fehlte dem Messenger diesbezüglich lange ein wichtiges Feature. Das liefert Meta jetzt nach, wie WABetaInfo berichtet. Nach einem Update soll die App für iOS dazu in der Lage sein, Daten, wie Termine oder Telefonnummern selbstständig zu erkennen und passende Shortcuts anzubieten, um damit zu interagieren.
Shortcuts für Termine, Telefonnummern, Mail-Adressen, Daten
Hat Whatsapp entweder einen Termin, eine Telefonnummer, eine Mail-Adresse oder eine Adresse ausgemacht, soll die App die Daten mit einer gepunkteten Linie unterstreichen. Wer drauftippt, sieht je nach Art ein Menü mit mehreren Optionen. Immer dazu gehört eine Kopierfunktion, um die jeweiligen Daten in die Zwischenablage des Smartphones zu laden. Bei einer Wohnadresse bietet Whatsapp zudem an, die Kartenansicht zu öffnen, und bei einer Mail-Adresse die entsprechende Mail-App.
Mehr Möglichkeiten habt ihr bei Kalenderdaten: Ihr könnt sie wahlweise zu eurem Kalender hinzufügen oder direkt in der Messenger-App ein sogenanntes Whatsapp-Ereignis erstellen. Über die Funktion könnt ihr etwa alle in einer Gruppe zu einer Feier einladen. Telefonnummern könnt ihr wiederum zu euren Kontakten hinzufügen oder direkt anrufen. Sollte es sich dabei um die Service-Rufnummer eines Business-Accounts handeln, könnt ihr über einen Button auch Informationen dazu abrufen.
Was bedeutet das für die Privatsphäre?
Natürlich kann man sich jetzt fragen, wie es bei dem Feature um die Privatsphäre steht, wenn der Messenger selbstständig mehr oder weniger sensible Daten erkennt. Laut WABetaInfo gibt es allerdings keinen Grund zur Sorge. Die App würde die Daten direkt auf dem Gerät erkennen, muss dafür also keine Daten an Server senden. Demnach versuche Whatsapp, Muster zu identifizieren, die mit bekannten Formaten übereinstimmen. Einen Einfluss auf die Ende-zu-Ende-Verschlüsselung soll das Feature nicht haben.
Obwohl die Funktion nicht in einer Beta-, sondern in der regulären Version für iOS und Android ausgerollt werden soll, erhalten nicht alle Nutzer:innen sofort Zugriff darauf. Den Angaben zufolge will Meta das Feature über die kommenden Wochen für weitere Accounts freischalten.

articles.title: Apple set an iPhone sales record even without a new standard iPhone
articles.text:
Apple had a record-breaking quarter for iPhone sales — despite not releasing a standard model during its latest refresh. In its fourth-quarter earnings report released on Monday, Apple says it earned $57.58 billion in iPhone revenue, a 17 percent jump from the same time last year.
Apple set an iPhone sales record even without a new standard iPhone
iPhone revenue jumped 17 percent with Pro-only models during this year’s refresh.
The increase in revenue follows the launch of Apple’s iPhone 18 lineup in September, which included a pricier iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max model. The company raised prices across its older models at the same time. Apple also took the wraps off its first folding phone, the iPhone Duo, but its preorder sales aren’t included in this earnings report.
Like other device-makers, Apple has been dealing with supply chain constraints and rising memory costs, leading it to raise prices across its products. Meanwhile, Apple only had a “limited” number of iPhone Duos available in store at launch, with some estimated shipment dates extending into 2027. “We saw higher memory costs as compared to the June quarter, and that was partly offset by the benefit of carrying inventory and lower costs on non-memory components,” Apple CEO John Ternus said during an interview with CNBC.
Apple reported a 12 percent increase in revenue overall, ballooning to $114.5 billion. Its Mac business grew 24 percent to $10.79 billion, while Apple’s services division, which includes App Store commissions along with subscriptions to services like Apple TV and Apple Music, grew to $31.57 billion. iPad revenue declined 10 percent year over year, with $6.23 billion in sales.
Apple shook up other areas of its product lineup with some other major launches over the past several weeks. It made a big push into the smart home space with its first smart home display and a series of video doorbells, security cameras, and door locks, made in collaboration with LG and Schneider Electric. Last week, Apple also revealed a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen — a design choice that its executives famously resisted.

articles.title: ChatGPT copia a Claude con un cambio clave: su app de escritorio será mucho mejor
articles.text:
OpenAI ha comenzado a probar un cambio que simplificará y mejorará significativamente la app de escritorio de ChatGPT. Según reporta TechCrunch, la empresa va a fusionar las pestañas de Chat y Work, de un modo similar al que recientemente implementó Anthropic en Claude.
De esta manera, los dos apartados de ChatGPT quedarán integrados en un único espacio. Lo que sí permanecerá por separado será Codex, la herramienta de programación con inteligencia artificial. Por lo pronto, los de Sam Altman están probando este cambio en sus apps de escritorio con un número reducido de usuarios.
El objetivo de OpenAI es recibir comentarios del público sobre esta simplificación de la app de ChatGPT, antes de comenzar con un despliegue masivo que llegue a sus usuarios en todo el mundo. Todavía no se sabe cuándo puede llegar a suceder esto último, aunque si el feedback es positivo seguramente no hay que esperar demasiado.
Al unificar Chat y Work, los usuarios de ChatGPT ya no tendrán que elegir manualmente qué herramienta o apartado de la app desean utilizar. La IA será capaz de determinar qué funciones o utilidades necesita, dependiendo de la consulta o tarea que se le realice.
ChatGPT fusionará las pestañas de Chat y Work en sus apps de escritorio
Como indicamos al comienzo, Anthropic ya hizo algo similar a lo que planea implementar ChatGPT. En septiembre, Claude unificó su ventana de chat con Cowork. Esto permite realizar un sinfín de acciones desde una interfaz simplificada, incluyendo el acceso a los artefactos y a Claude Design, sin que el usuario tenga que adivinar desde qué apartado obtendrá los mejores resultados. Lo que sí se ha mantenido por separado es Claude Code.
Ahora bien, el cambio que va a implementar OpenAI en los clientes de escritorio de ChatGPT va a tener implicaciones más fuertes de las que crees. Y puede que esto no sea una buena noticia si tienes un consumo de tokens alto. Con la unificación de Chat y Work, los de Sam Altman indican que en adelante los tokens de ChatGPT y Codex será compartidos.
De modo que si dependes de Codex para labores de programación, si usas más tokens de lo habitual con la versión unificada de Chat/Work, es posible que tus límites de ChatGPT se consuman más rápido. OpenAI dice que la modificación no modificará la experiencia de la mayoría de los usuarios, aunque sí puede traer consecuencias para quienes hacen un uso más intensivo de la IA.
