articles.title: Gears of War: E-Day's half-billion-dollar budget was no rumor
articles.text:
The big picture: Most of the talk around BioWare's closure last month has focused on EA's new owners and the debt they loaded onto the publisher. But the studio's end may have just as much to do with how expensive big games have become. Xbox's latest Gears of War entry is a prime example, since it reportedly cost $500 million to make.
Bloomberg's Jason Schreier brought up the figure in a video explaining why EA chose to shut BioWare. Gears of War: E-Day cost Xbox $500 million, he said. "That is a real number, that is real," he added. In Schreier's view, that's simply what AAA games cost to make now, especially in North America.
About a week earlier, a source familiar with Xbox's business had already told Kotaku that E-Day cost over $500 million. That figure didn't even include marketing.
Windows Central's Jez Corden thinks the number actually covers everything The Coalition spent since its last game. After all, the studio also builds dev tools for Xbox and has chipped in on Forza and Fable. Even so, he believes most of that money did go into E-Day.
So much of that cost is The Coalition being on the hook for the Microsoft branch of Unreal and one of the flagship titles. I should know, I tried to get leadership to support a plan to have other studios adopt it and write off the support costs. Same problem with Turn10 and ForzaTech.
[image or embed]
– Derek Reese is making games (@derekree.se) 30 October 2026 at 21:04
Analytics firm Alinea estimated E-Day sold just 230,000 copies in its first week, despite a score of 87 on Metacritic. Sales did pick up after that. About three weeks after launch, a source told The Verge's Tom Warren that sales had passed 400,000 across Xbox and Steam.
Of course, neither count includes Game Pass, where Alinea estimates around 1.7 million people played the game instead. About 722,000 of them still paid $30 for early access. Those upgrades helped push E-Day's early revenue to roughly $37 million.
Even if Microsoft pocketed the full $70 from every copy, though, it would need to sell over 7 million just to cover development.
Budgets have grown far faster than sales, Schreier argued in the same video, so publishers are moving work outside North America and sticking to only their biggest franchises. At EA, that reportedly meant backing a new Star Wars Battlefront over Mass Effect.
Xbox, meanwhile, kept E-Day off PS5 and put it in Game Pass on day one. Kotaku figured that if a PS5 version sold as well as Gears of War: Reloaded, it would have added only about $33 million anyway, so subscriber numbers may end up mattering more to Xbox than copies sold.

articles.title: With Agentic Studio, LinearB provides the critical context needed to accelerate software delivery - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
With Agentic Studio, LinearB provides the critical context needed to accelerate software delivery
Application development intelligence startup LinearB Inc. said today it’s trying to ease the growing congestion in organization’s software delivery pipelines that has arisen with the widespread adoption of artificial intelligence coding tools.
It’s doing so with Agentic Studio, a new offering announced today that’s focused on providing more actionable context for human engineers and autonomous coding agents alike.
The startup says the emergence of generative AI coding tools such as Claude Code and Codex has led to new headaches for enterprise software development teams. Though writing software code now can be basically effortless, shipping that code into production is still as painful as it has always been, and now they have much more of it to ship.
In its recent Software Engineering Benchmarks report, the company analyzed more than 2.7 million pull requests across 250 organizations and found that those who rely on AI coding tools have almost doubled their merged code changes year-over-year. But the problem is that AI-assisted pull requests are nearly 2.6 times larger, and consequently they’re waiting more than five times longer to be reviewed.
That has led to significant backlogs. And it’s compounded by the fact that AI agent’s proposed code changes are merged just 79% of the time at “elite organizations,” compared with 92% for human-authored code.
LinearB says that human software engineers struggle to clear this backlog because the traditional dashboards they’re forced to work with only provide metrics, rather than the context needed to resolve those pull requests. With Agentic Studio, it’s trying to address this by normalizing the data and insights generated by Git repositories and project tracking tools into a unified context layer. It means that instead of muddling through various charts to try and understand why release velocity has stalled, software engineers can ask questions in plain language to understand the root cause and receive recommendations on how to speed things up.
Co-founder and Chief Executive Ori Keren said context has become the new king, not only for AI tools but also for humans. “We realized we hold a knowledge graph that nobody else has of everything that is happening across the software delivery lifecycle,” he said. “That’s exactly what agents and teams need to deliver high quality software faster, so we rebuilt LinearB around it.”
What’s different about Agentic Studio is that it’s designed to help autonomous coding agents just as much as human software engineers, Keren said. By integrating through protocols such as the Model Context Protocol, it feeds historical context such as rework rates, past production incidents and code ownership to AI agents, preventing them from making blind modifications to pull requests.
Early adopters have benefited from dramatically increased productivity with Agentic Studio. A case in point is the cryptocurrency exchange Kraken, which used LinearB’s MCP integration to pinpoint why its code reviews were lagging. It discovered that timezone misalignments were the main culprit rather than pull request sizes, and subsequently reorganized its workflows to cut its review times by more than half within just four months.
“For years, engineering leaders told us the same thing: metrics are useful, but they don’t tell you what to do,” said LinearB’s chief operating officer Dan Lines. “A dashboard says your cycle time is two days, but so what? Now [with Agentic Studio] a leader can ask what to improve in their engineering organization and get a clear answer. When that same context goes to coding agents, the platform is not just reporting, it’s acting.”
To help AI agents operationalize the context it provides, LinearB is developing a bunch of new agent skills. The first one, an “effort skill,” is available in early access now and analyzes the complexity of a pull request and its proposed code changes, its rework history and risk to calibrate dynamically how much computational effort a coding agent needs to expend as it works on it.
Simple, low-risk changes are done faster with minimal tokens. More sensitive, high-priority modifications will be implemented with deeper reasoning and more exhaustive testing to ensure nothing goes wrong.
LinearB said it’s planning to expand its agent skills library in the coming months with additional skills focused on automated code review, merge governance and token cost optimization.

articles.title: Malicious Claude Code Extension Served in Cursor Supply Chain Attack
articles.text:
Cursor users have been targeted with malicious versions of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension in a new supply chain attack.
The incident occurred on October 29 and involved versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 of the anthropic.claude-code extension, which were live in the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace for roughly 11 hours.
Aiming at both macOS and Windows users, the extension contained JavaScript code designed to run when modules were loaded to establish a reverse SSH tunnel.
Roughly 5,000 developer systems might have downloaded the malicious versions, security researcher Kevin Beaumont notes.
The modified extension versions were not developed by Anthropic, and neither was pushed to the Microsoft Visual Studio Marketplace, Open VSX, or the NPM registry.
“A malicious actor used access to Cursor’s marketplace to publish a tampered copy of the Claude Code extension, which we didn’t build or publish. The versions on our official channels are not affected, and this only impacts Cursor users,” Anthropic’s Felix Rieseberg said.
To avoid confusion, Anthropic updated its legitimate Claude Code extension directly to version 2.1.314.
Cursor removed the modified Claude Code extension from the store immediately after identifying it and suspended the marketplace to investigate the incident. Cursor found no other malicious extensions, rotated all keys, and rebuilt and reopened the marketplace.
Additionally, it worked with the cloud provider hosting the attacker’s server to take it offline.
“We have no evidence that other versions of the extension or the official distribution are affected,” Cursor said.
The modified extension versions contained a JavaScript function that was executed during module loading to collect host information, modify files, and run OS commands.
“The loader first collects host reconnaissance. It then attempts to install an SSH key, enable SSH, create a reverse tunnel, and configure persistence. A delayed callback subsequently attempts to send host details,” Microsoft notes.
The code was observed collecting information such as hostname, username, OS, system architecture, working directory, and global Git email, as well as deploying platform-specific scripts and startup configurations for persistence.
According to Cursor, because enabling the local SSH service requires admin rights and the extension does not have them on most macOS and Windows systems, the step failed, preventing the attackers from logging in through the tunnel.
Users should remove the malicious extension versions as soon as possible. Cursor has released a script to help users detect infections, along with indicators of compromise (IoCs) to identify potential compromises across environments.
“Isolate hosts showing evidence of payload execution or backdoor installation. Remove the unauthorized SSH key, persistence mechanisms, and running tunnel processes, and assess whether the host should be rebuilt. Uninstalling the extension may not be sufficient — the payload drops standalone persistence scripts that keep running,” Cursor notes.

articles.title: Is Mistral overlooking Europe? 10 homegrown startups that could join its connector ecosystem | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Of the 12 companies listed by French AI unicorn Mistral as available Connectors (ready-made integrations connecting AI to external applications), not one hails from Europe; raising questions about the continent’s competitiveness.
Despite what this may imply, there are plenty of European software platforms that could potentially become managed Connectors for Mistral – many of which have even seen significant backing over the past five years.
Mistral’s Connectors allow users to link its AI tools with external services such as Gmail, Slack, Notion, GitHub and Stripe. Once connected, users can ask the AI assistant to retrieve information, analyse records and, where authorised, perform actions across those services without navigating between different applications.
Drawing on EU-Startups’ coverage between November 2021 and November 2026, here are 10 European startups and scale-ups whose products could plausibly join Mistral’s managed connector ecosystem.
The European Connectors
Attio (United Kingdom): Founded in London in 2019 by Nicolas Sharp and Alexander Christie, Attio raised €44 million in August 2025. The startup develops an AI-native customer relationship management (CRM) platform that helps businesses organise customer information, manage sales pipelines and automate workflows.
Attio is particularly suited to the connector concept because its software acts as a central repository for customer relationships. Its developer platform already supports a REST API, webhooks and OAuth authentication. A potential Mistral connector could allow sales teams to retrieve customer records, identify outstanding opportunities or update pipeline information through natural-language instructions.
Cloudsmith (United Kingdom): Belfast-based Cloudsmith raised €61.5 million in April 2026 in a Series C round. Founded in 2016 by Alan Carson and Lee Skillen, Cloudsmith provides a platform for managing, distributing and securing software packages and repositories. Its product allows engineering teams to control the software components used across development environments and monitor software supply chains. Unlike companies whose primary offering is integration middleware, Cloudsmith operates a standalone developer platform with its own customer accounts, records and management workflows.
Its REST API could support a future Mistral connector, particularly within Vibe Code. Developers could potentially inspect repositories, retrieve package information or review software supply-chain policies through AI-assisted workflows.
Factorial (Spain): Founded in Barcelona in 2016 by Jordi Romero, Bernat Farrero and Pau Ramon, Factorial raised €129 million in June 2026 in a Series D round. The financing valued the business management platform at €2.1 billion. Initially focused on human resources, Factorial has expanded into areas including expense management, project management and training. Its platform helps companies manage employee information, leave requests, administrative tasks and internal processes.
Factorial also offers an API and OAuth-based integrations. A potential Mistral connector could enable authorised managers to retrieve employee records, check outstanding leave requests or review administrative workflows. Its broad range of business functions makes it a credible candidate for extending Mistral’s capabilities beyond communications and project management.
Mews (Netherlands): Amsterdam-based Mews raised €255 million in January 2026 in a Series D round. Founded in 2012 by Richard Valtr and Matthijs Welle, the company develops a hospitality operating system covering reservations, hotel operations, guest management and payments. Mews also offers an Open API ecosystem, including a Connector API that allows third-party software to access hotel operational data.
While this API is not itself a Mistral-managed connector, it provides a possible route for integration. Hotel operators could potentially ask Mistral to retrieve booking information, examine occupancy records or identify operational tasks requiring attention.
Pennylane (France): Paris-based Pennylane secured €75 million in April 2025. Founded in 2020, with Arthur Waller among its co-founders, the company combines accounting, invoicing, expense management and financial reporting in one platform. Members of its founding team previously worked on PriceMatch, which was acquired by Booking.com in 2015. Pennylane provides APIs for accessing financial information and supports OAuth for integration partners. This makes it a potentially useful connector destination for Mistral, particularly for small and medium-sized businesses.
With appropriate permissions, an assistant could retrieve outstanding invoices, inspect accounting records or prepare summaries of company expenditure. However, because the platform handles sensitive financial information, any managed integration would need appropriate authentication and access controls.
Perk (Spain): Founded in Barcelona in 2015 by Avi Meir, Javier Suarez and Ron Levin, Perk secured €191 million in January 2025 in a Series E round. Rebranded as Perk in 2025, the platform allows companies to organise employee travel, bookings, invoices and spending. Its developer tools include REST APIs, webhooks and access to travel and expense data.
A potential Mistral connector could allow employees to retrieve travel itineraries, review bookings or request expenditure information without opening the travel management platform.
Personio (Germany): Munich-based Personio raised €190 million in June 2022 in an extension of its Series E financing. Founded in 2015 by Hanno Renner, Roman Schumacher, Arseniy Vershinin and Jonas Rieke, the company develops an HR software platform for SMBs. Personio provides tools for employee administration, recruitment, attendance, absences and other people-related workflows. Its developer platform supports third-party integrations through APIs with configurable access to employee and organisational information.
A managed Mistral connector could potentially help HR teams retrieve authorised employee records, inspect absence information or review administrative processes. However, integration design would be particularly important given the sensitivity of HR data and the permissions required to access it.
Spott (Belgium): Leuven-based Spott raised €18.3 million in September 2026 in a Series A round. Founded in 2024 by Lander Degreve, Manu Vanderveeren and Samuel Smeys, the company develops recruitment software combining applicant tracking, CRM and AI-powered workflows. The platform helps agencies organise candidate records, manage vacancies and coordinate recruitment activities. Spott also advertises an open API for custom integrations, alongside its separate MCP offering.
A potential featured Mistral connector could enable recruiters to search candidate databases, review recruitment pipelines or retrieve vacancy information through natural language. Its focus on a specific professional workflow makes it a particularly interesting candidate alongside broader business applications.
Storyblok (Austria): Linz-based Storyblok raised €73.6 million in June 2024 in a Series C round. Founded in 2017 by Dominik Angerer and Alexander Feiglstorfer, who previously worked together at a digital agency, the company offers a headless content management system that allows businesses to create and manage content across websites and digital channels. Storyblok has documented APIs for retrieving, creating and updating content, including OAuth-based access to its Management API.
A managed Mistral connector could potentially allow marketing teams to locate published material, prepare website updates or manage content without manually navigating the platform. This would give Mistral a practical connection to the publishing and content-management workflows used by businesses.
Typeform (Spain): Barcelona-based Typeform secured €123 million in March 2022. Founded in 2013 by Robert Muñoz and David Okuniev, the company develops online forms, surveys and interactive experiences for collecting information. Typeform’s documented APIs and OAuth authentication provide a technical basis for third-party integrations.
If Mistral introduced a managed Typeform connector, users could ask their AI assistant to summarise survey results, identify recurring customer complaints or create forms directly from a conversation. This would give Mistral access to a type of structured feedback data not currently represented by its featured connectors.

articles.title: Most of our measures of a key cognitive process don't agree
articles.text:
It’s widely acknowledged that it’s nearly impossible to publish negative results in scientific journals. “We didn’t see anything” is a much harder sell than finding that a hypothesis is clearly right. Findings of no effect tend to either be shuffled off to low-profile journals or left behind as unpublished lab lore.
The high-profile journal Nature, however, made a notable exception this week, publishing a study that tells us that a bunch of methods we have been using to try to measure a key emotional ability don’t seem to be measuring the same thing. The results mean that we don’t have a good way to measure the impact of a concept that is the basis of a key method in therapy.
Inconsistencies
One of the most successful forms of therapy is cognitive behavioral therapy, or CBT. In part, CBT is based on getting people to step back and engage in “cognitive reappraisal.” This requires people to think over a situation that has caused a negative emotional response and find ways to reinterpret it so that it has less impact on them. The ability to engage in this process has been linked to emotional resilience.
Given its importance, a lot of studies have looked at what’s going on in the brain when people engage in cognitive reappraisal. There are also a number of questionnaires that are thought to measure a person’s capacity to engage in the process. So, a large international collaboration of researchers decided to look at these more carefully. “We focused on three widely used indices that are often assumed to reflect related facets of reappraisal capacity: trait questionnaires, task-based affective ratings following reappraisal, and amygdala down-regulation during reappraisal,” they wrote.

articles.title: Snap settles lawsuit accusing platform of fueling teen depression and eating disorders | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Snap has reached a settlement in a lawsuit brought by two teenagers who accused the company of designing its platform to be addictive and contributing to their depression, anxiety, and eating disorders, as first reported by Reuters. The plaintiffs had previously reached settlements with Meta, TikTok, and YouTube.
The trial was set to be Snap’s first in a broader wave of litigation over social media’s impact on young users. The company had already settled its other cases scheduled for trial. Snap CEO Evan Spiegel was expected to take the stand.
The plaintiffs said they started using YouTube as young as age 3 and other social media platforms at around age 9. They said they developed compulsive usage habits, which they attributed to features such as autoplay and infinite scrolling.
“The Parties are pleased to have been able to resolve this matter in an amicable manner,” a Snap spokesperson said in a statement to TechCrunch. “We’ve built safeguards, launched safety tutorials, and partnered with experts and because safety is never finished, we remain committed to continually strengthening the safety, privacy, and well-being of our community.”
Social media giants are facing thousands of lawsuits in federal and state courts over claims that they knowingly designed their platforms to hook young users and fuel a youth mental health crisis involving anxiety, depression, and suicide.

articles.title: Technology is reinventing fraud: Financial institutions must keep up
articles.text:
Technology is reinventing fraud: Financial institutions must keep up
How can banks fight the financial crime AI evolution?
In the UK, fraud losses reached £1.3billion, showcasing how fraud operates at a growing scale. One of the factors driving this growth is the increasing use of technologies, such as AI, which are becoming dangerous and effective weapons in the hands of a new generation of criminals
As they continue to evolve, criminal networks are becoming faster and more sophisticated in their operations, and financial institutions face the challenge of adapting to a new era of cybersecurity and fraud prevention powered by the same force threatening the system and customers’ trust.
Fraud and Identity SME at Feedzai.
AI is reinventing cybercrime
Fraudsters are already using advanced technologies including generative AI to industrialize social engineering. As the marginal cost of a sophisticated attack approaches zero, criminal networks are undergoing a measurable structural shift in how they operate. Skills that previously lived inside a small number of highly specialized criminal groups are now commoditized.
Generative AI and synthetic identity creation can now produce composite identities that pass Know Your Customer (KYC) checks, build believable credit histories and operate undetected for months before the fraud is executed. Deepfake-enabled authorization fraud produces voices and videos convincing enough to trick humans into authorizing transactions or transferring access credentials.
These examples all reveal a common pattern: they attack the trust layer, the moment where a system or a human decides something is legitimate. Even with incredibly sophisticated models, the tactics will target the system and subsequent operations. AI can now manufacture trust at a speed and quality that was simply not possible before.
Why traditional security is falling behind
Such technologies now have the upper-hand as they are largely defeating the customer, not the bank's systems. Fraudsters are using AI to manipulate people into authorizing transactions themselves with more convincing scam calls, more realistic impersonation, more personalized social engineering that erodes the skepticism that used to protect people. The fraud arrives at the bank's systems looking entirely legitimate, because in a technical sense it is.
That is where the battle is being fought today. As banks continue to invest in AI-driven detection and the customer manipulation route becomes harder to exploit at scale, the incentive to attack the banks' systems directly increases.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
We are in a transitional phase, where technology is helping fraudsters to defeat people, this could evolve toward AI directly probing and attacking the institutions themselves. The financial sector should be preparing for that second phase now.
Against an adversary that probes, adapts and iterates continuously, the current static nature of traditional security controls are not sufficient. In financial fraud and cybersecurity, AI-driven attacks are not just evading controls, they are mapping them. They behave almost as if they understand the shape of the detection system and are deliberately staying outside its boundaries.
A symbiotic relationship between workforce and technology
In banks and financial institutions, fraud prevention teams are increasingly struggling to keep up with the constant technological evolution of the threats, mostly because they have been trained to think in terms of incidents: if something happens, you detect it, you respond, you close the case.
The ones making the most progress are those treating detection as a research function rather than an operational one. They are looking at shifts in behaviors that might suggest something is being tested against us. This different analytical posture ultimately aids in prevention over detection.
The professionals who will matter most in five years are the ones who can reason about systems rather than just operate them. There is a need to move from expertise in specific tools to expertise in the underlying principles that make tools work. Principles, such as statistical reasoning, adversarial thinking, systems design, feedback loop analysis, compound over time and remain relevant regardless of what the technology stack looks like in years to come.
Not all organizations are equipped to operate this way, and while hiring to fill this gap might be the obvious solution, the reality is that, thanks to advancements and widespread adoption, today we have cutting-edge AI tools that can be easily integrated within existing infrastructure and operations.
The way forward is to invest in the work of external providers that make these tools accessible and easy to deploy, combining statistical analysis, reasoning and full explainability.
Deploying new technologies without fueling risks
You don’t need to be technically sophisticated to deploy a technically sophisticated attack, and this democratization of capability is what makes the next wave genuinely different. The questions practitioners are working through now are not whether new technologies work, but how to leverage the next generation of capabilities to stay ahead of increasingly automated attacks.
The most important principle is to treat your systems as attack surfaces from day one rather than as an afterthought once they are in production. Every model you deploy has assumptions baked into it, and adversarial actors will probe those assumptions systematically. If you have not done that probing yourself first, you are outsourcing your red team function to people with very different intentions.
To be effective, AI-driven defenses must work in milliseconds - fast enough to spot risk without disrupting the customer experience. Every transaction is assessed in real time, analyzing hundreds of signals and comparing them against historical patterns to identify any signs of anomalous activity.

articles.title: Apple supera expectativas e registra melhor resultado financeiro da história
articles.text:
A Apple registrou receita de US$ 114,5 bilhões (aproximadamente R$ 622,7 bilhões) no quarto trimestre fiscal de 2026, encerrado em 26 de setembro. O resultado representa crescimento de 12% em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado e estabelece novo recorde para o trimestre. O lucro líquido também avançou, chegando a US$ 30,7 bilhões (R$ 167 bilhões), alta de aproximadamente 12% na comparação anual.
Os resultados foram divulgados nesta segunda-feira (2) e superaram as expectativas de Wall Street. O desempenho foi impulsionado principalmente pelas vendas do iPhone 18 Pro, enquanto a divisão de serviços também alcançou sua maior receita histórica.
O lucro por ação diluída ficou em US$ 2,10 (aproximadamente R$ 11,42), avanço de 14% em relação ao quarto trimestre fiscal de 2025. A margem bruta foi de 47,9%, incluindo impacto positivo de aproximadamente um ponto percentual relacionado a reembolsos de tarifas.
Este foi o primeiro balanço trimestral apresentado sob a liderança de John Ternus, que assumiu o cargo de CEO em setembro, sucedendo Tim Cook.
iPhone e serviços impulsionam resultados da Apple
A divisão de smartphones foi o principal destaque do balanço. A receita com iPhones chegou a US$ 57,6 bilhões (aproximadamente R$ 313,2 bilhões), crescimento de 17% em relação ao mesmo trimestre de 2025.
O resultado superou a expectativa dos analistas, que projetavam aproximadamente US$ 56,5 bilhões (R$ 307,4 bilhões). A procura pelos modelos iPhone 18 Pro ajudou a impulsionar as vendas, mesmo com a nova estratégia da companhia de distribuir os lançamentos de aparelhos ao longo do ano.
A divisão de serviços também apresentou desempenho expressivo. A receita alcançou US$ 31,6 bilhões (R$ 171,7 bilhões), avanço de aproximadamente 10% na comparação anual e um novo recorde histórico. O segmento reúne atividades, como App Store, Apple Music, iCloud e outros serviços oferecidos pela companhia.
Já a divisão de computadores Mac faturou US$ 10,8 bilhões (R$ 58,7 bilhões), crescimento de aproximadamente 24% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior. O resultado também ficou acima das projeções do mercado.
Por outro lado, duas categorias apresentaram retração:
- iPad: receita de US$ 6,2 bilhões (R$ 33,9 bilhões), queda de aproximadamente 10%;
- Wearables, Casa e Acessórios: US$ 8,3 bilhões (R$ 45,1 bilhões), recuo de cerca de 8%.
Os resultados mostram que o crescimento da Apple continua concentrado principalmente no iPhone e nos serviços, embora os computadores também tenham apresentado expansão significativa.
Leia mais:
- MacBook Pro: Apple redefine rota e agora aposta em notebook com tela touch
- IA faz preço de chips disparar e tira poder de barganha histórico da Apple
- iOS 27 permite verificar idade com selfie para acessar sites adultos
Apple enfrenta aumento nos custos de componentes
Apesar dos resultados positivos, a companhia precisa lidar com o encarecimento de componentes utilizados na fabricação de seus dispositivos, especialmente chips de memória.
O aumento dos custos está relacionado à maior demanda por esses componentes, impulsionada também pela expansão da infraestrutura de inteligência artificial (IA).
Segundo John Ternus, os preços mais elevados de alguns produtos ajudaram a compensar parcialmente essa pressão sobre as margens. A Apple aumentou em US$ 100 os preços de determinados modelos da linha iPhone 17 e também reajustou alguns computadores MacBook.
A margem bruta de 47,9% ficou acima dos 47,5% projetados por analistas consultados pela LSEG.
Outro ponto destacado pelo CEO foi o desempenho da Siri reformulada com IA. Segundo Ternus, a assistente processa atualmente cerca de 2,5 bilhões de solicitações por dia.
Novo iPhone dobrável enfrenta limitações de estoque
A Apple também comentou o desempenho do iPhone Duo, primeiro smartphone dobrável da companhia, lançado em outubro. O aparelho esgotou rapidamente nas vendas on-line e provocou filas em lojas da empresa. Entretanto, a demanda continua acima da capacidade de fornecimento.
Em entrevista à Reuters, Ternus afirmou que uma parcela muito pequena das unidades foi devolvida por problemas relacionados às telas. A companhia está substituindo os aparelhos afetados. O executivo também reconheceu que ainda não existe uma previsão para equilibrar oferta e demanda.
Como o iPhone Duo chegou ao mercado em 23 de outubro, suas vendas não foram contabilizadas no balanço divulgado nesta segunda-feira. Os resultados do dispositivo deverão aparecer no próximo trimestre fiscal.
Apple encerra ano fiscal com receita de R$ 2,6 trilhões
O desempenho do quarto trimestre ajudou a companhia a fechar seu melhor exercício fiscal em receita.
No acumulado de 2026, a Apple registrou:
- Receita total: US$ 478,8 bilhões (aproximadamente R$ 2,6 trilhões), alta de 15%;
- Lucro líquido: US$ 132,2 bilhões (R$ 718,9 bilhões), crescimento de aproximadamente 18%;
- Lucro por ação diluída: US$ 8,98 (R$ 48,85), avanço de aproximadamente 20%.
A empresa também informou ter gerado US$ 28 bilhões (R$ 152,3 bilhões) em fluxo de caixa operacional durante o quarto trimestre. O mesmo montante foi devolvido aos acionistas por meio de dividendos e recompra de ações.
O conselho de administração ainda declarou dividendo de US$ 0,27 por ação (aproximadamente R$ 1,47), com pagamento previsto para 16 de novembro.
Apesar de superar as expectativas financeiras, as ações da Apple recuaram aproximadamente 1% nas negociações após o fechamento do mercado, em meio à volatilidade dos papéis.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Supermarket freezers across Europe struck in second crippling cyberattack
articles.text:
Supermarket freezers across Europe struck in second crippling cyberattack — hackers raise temperatures to 50 degrees Celsius in Belgium and Sweden, destroying food stocks
"We've been working all night and morning to disconnect the affected units from the network"
Update, Mon 2 Nov, 7 am ET: Reports are now emerging that supermarkets in Ireland, Estonia, and the Netherlands have also been affected by today's cyberattack. The rest of the story remains below as first published.
Just weeks after an 'unprecedented' cyberattack struck supermarket fridges in France, destroying foodstuffs, a similar hack has crippled supermarket chains in Belgium and Sweden, Bloomberg reports. Hackers targeted supermarkets owned by Dutch outfit Ahold Delhaize, as well as ICA and Coop locations in Sweden. As with the previous attack, hackers remotely raised temperatures in these online-controlled freezers to 50 degrees Celsius, rapidly defrosting their contents and likely destroying millions of dollars worth of items.
Belga News Agency reports that a cyberattack targeting refrigeration units at Belgian supermarkets started on Sunday night at around midnight. Sabcobel, a refrigeration fitter in the region, estimates that at least twenty units are affected across Belgium. The report says that affected supermarket chains include Delhaize, Carrefour, and Spar. As mentioned, and reflecting the previous attack, hackers remotely activated the freezer's built-in defrost mode, overriding the temperature and time spent defrosting, the exact same method as the France attack.
CEO Stephan Moelans said that while the company has been working "very hard" to protect its fridges against the vulnerability, physical modifications to its units are required. The company says switching units to a secure internet connection is the simplest solution in the meantime, a measure carried out by most of its customers in the wake of the France attack.
Elsewhere, supermarkets ICA and Coop are reporting similar disturbances in Sweden. Aftonbladet reports refrigerators and freezers have been struck "in several ICA and Coop stores." Pictures on the ground show staff throwing out shopping carts full of goods. "We are extremely sad and working hard to get everything back up and running," Ica Kvantum wrote on Facebook.
The attack, which is the second such instance in just a few short weeks, is a worrying reminder that many of society's most basic functions and infrastructure are heavily reliant on internet connectivity, making them vulnerable to cyberattacks. The increase in cyber intrusions into the physical world also seems to be commensurate with the proliferation of AI agents, which continues to heavily impact global cybersecurity. In October, a hacker suspected of using AI agents stole the data of 25,000 customers from banks in South Korea. Officials at the time commented that AI models mean actors can "hack with ease even without specialized skills."

articles.title: Ford pledges no driver data sales as GM settles data sale lawsuit
articles.text:
Ford is taking a dig at its longtime rival, General Motors (GM), following legal trouble over selling customers’ driving data.
The auto manufacturer announced a new initiative on Monday called the Ford Privacy Promise, essentially promising not to sell information about how you drive your vehicle to data brokers or insurance companies.
The announcement comes days after GM agreed to pay US$220 million (about C$307.7 million) to settle allegations brought by a coalition of 36 attorneys that say the auto manufacturer illegally sold its drivers’ personal information to third parties.
According to the Washington State Attorney General, the company sold its driving behaviour and location data to data brokers, which then sold the information to insurance companies. It is alleged that GM enrolled millions of drivers in its Smart Driver program between 2016 and 2024, which tracked drivers’ habits and was marketed as a tool to help them improve their driving safety—while also telling drivers their information would not be shared with insurers without their consent (yikes).
The New York Times noted in an investigation that the information sold included how often people drove, how often they braked or accelerated quickly, and whether they exceeded speed limits; in some cases, it was used to determine customers’ rates.
Of course, auto companies selling data gathered by vehicles is nothing new. A few years ago, Mozilla’s *Privacy Not Included buyer’s guide noted that 25 cars collected data about drivers, including race, facial expressions, weight, health information, and where people drive. The company even found that some cars collected data on sexual activity, and even immigration status. At the time, the two biggest offenders were Nissan and Tesla.
Now, although it was conveniently timed to align with its competitor’s suit, a Ford executive told Gizmodo that it isn’t directly linked, saying instead that Ford wants to build trust with customers.
The automaker also launched a new site that explains what data its vehicles actually collect, how it’s used, and how you can adjust your privacy settings. That has been available for a while, but Ford says it wants to make it easier for Ford owners to understand and use.
Source: Ford, Washington State Attorney General Via: Gizmodo

articles.title: Meta will end Quest 2 OS updates in 2027
articles.text:
Meta is planning to release the last OS update for its Quest 2 and Quest Pro VR headsets by March 2027, the company announced today. The last OS update for those devices is planned to be v213, and after that, Meta will continue to ship security patches and critical bug fixes through the end of 2027. Apps that support the Quest 2 or Quest Pro can also be submitted through December 2027, Meta says.
Meta will end Quest 2 OS updates in 2027
The Quest 2 and Pro were discontinued in 2024, and next year, Meta will stop releasing OS updates for the VR headsets.
Meta is calling the Quest 3 and 3S “now the baseline for Meta VR gamers.” The company is announcing this shift ahead of the planned release of its new VR Glasses, which are set to launch sometime in spring 2027.
“Quest 2 and Quest Pro laid the foundation for this platform, and millions of people still play on them,” Meta says. “Quest 3 and Quest 3S give your apps more performance headroom and mixed reality built in, and apps built for them carry forward to Meta VR Glasses, which run on the same OS and SDKs.”
Meta launched the Quest 2 in 2020 and the Quest Pro in 2022. It discontinued both products in 2024.

Te permite crear tu propia nube privada, sin depender de terceros, de manera local centralizando el almacenamiento y sin tener que pagar cuotas mensuales a otros proveedores como Google, Apple o Amazon.
Si estás buscando un NAS completo, potente, con un rendimiento muy bueno y con la mayor fiabilidad posible, entonces debes echar un vistazo a los dos nuevos lanzamientos de UGREEN.
UGREEN lo hace todo bien
Cuesta decir esto de un fabricante pero en el caso de UGREEN es cierto. Cables de carga, estaciones, PowerBanks y, en este caso, NAS. Basta con dejarse caer un poco por las opiniones de los clientes en ecommerce como Amazon para ser consciente que UGREEN ha dejado de ser una marca china más que prima el bajo precio por encima de la calidad, para convertirse en un fabricante que ha alcanzado un equilibrio perfecto entre altas prestaciones y precio ajustado.
UGREEN NASync DXP6800 Ultra
Aunque se trata del modelo “más básico” de los dos, el UGREEN NASync DXP6800 Ultra es una pasada. Atento a todo lo que lleva: un procesador Intel® Core™ 5 120U de 10 núcleos y 12 hilos, una configuración de 6 bahías con hasta 208TB de almacenamiento, dos puertos de red 10GbE de alta velocidad con un ancho de banda de hasta 20Gb/s y velocidades de descarga de hasta 2500 MB/s y 8 GB de memoria DDR5 a 4800 MHz, ampliable. Además es compatible con discos de otros fabricantes como Seagate o Western Digital, no sólo de UGREEN, para que lo personalices a tu gusto.
La gran ventaja de este equipo no es sólo la inmensa capacidad para almacenar datos e información que puede tener, es la simplicidad para gestionar archivos, usuarios y permisos desde un único lugar o la seguridad que existe en todo el proceso, por ejemplo si accedemos desde otro lugar.
UGREEN NASync DXP8800 Ultra
Este modelo presenta algunas diferencias con respecto al modelo anterior, la principal es que pasa de 6 bahías a 8, por lo cual el almacenamiento es significativamente mayor. Si en el 6600 Ultra es de más de 200 TB, en este caso supera los 270TB.
Otra diferencia es el procesador. En este modelo vemos un Procesador Intel® Core™ 7 150U de 10 núcleos y 12 hilos. En el resto de aspectos es idéntico al modelo anterior:dos puertos 10GbE de alta velocidad, 8 GB de memoria DDR5 a 4800 MHz ampliable y compatibilidad con otros fabricantes.
Además de las buenas prestaciones de los dos NAS, la otra gran noticia es el descuento de lanzamiento que UGREEN ha lanzado. Desde el 28 de octubre, usando el código HIPERTUX puedes descontar el 8% en el precio

articles.title: „Das Zeitfenster schließt sich bald": Bundesregierung schlägt im KI-Wettbewerb Alarm
articles.text:
„Das Zeitfenster schließt sich bald“: Bundesregierung schlägt im KI-Wettbewerb Alarm
Im weltweiten KI-Wettbewerb werden nach Erwartung der Bundesregierung die nächsten eineinhalb Jahre darüber entscheiden, ob Deutschland den Anschluss hält. Deutschland drohe „trotz einer starken Ausgangsposition insbesondere in der Forschung“ in eine Situation zu geraten, in der sich der Abstand zu den führenden KI-Standorten USA und China stetig vergrößere.
„Das Zeitfenster, um diesen Abstand zu verringern, schließt sich bald“, heißt es im Abschlussbericht der von der Regierung eingesetzten KI-Taskforce, der beim Digitalgipfel der Bundesregierung in Berlin vorgelegt werden soll. Die nächsten zwölf bis achtzehn Monate seien für die Weichenstellung daher entscheidend, heißt es weiter.
Politico berichtete zuerst darüber. Das Dokument liegt auch der Deutschen Presse-Agentur vor. Die Regierung macht darin zahlreiche Zielvorgaben, damit Deutschland vorn mitspielen kann. So sollen etwa bis 2030 mindestens 80 Prozent der Großunternehmen und 55 Prozent der kleineren und mittleren Unternehmen KI einsetzen, die Zahl der KI-Startups soll sich verdreifachen, der Anteil der Wirtschaftsleistung, der KI-basiert erwirtschaftet wird, soll mehr als 10 Prozent betragen, 90 Prozent der Bundesbehörden sollen bis dahin mindestens eine KI-Anwendung zur Bearbeitung von Kernaufgaben nutzen.
Gestärkt werden sollen den Plänen zufolge Alternativen zu großen KI‑Modellen. Dafür soll die Zusammenarbeit etwa mit Frankreich und Kanada ausgebaut werden.
Deutschland soll „KI-Nation“ werden
Die KI-Taskforce unter Leitung des Bundesdigitalministeriums war im Sommer vom Nationalen Sicherheitsrat der Bundesregierung eingesetzt worden. Ihr Papier gibt als Ziel aus, Deutschland bis 2030 zur „KI-Nation“ zu machen. Bereits im Koalitionsvertrag von Union und SPD war von Deutschland als „KI-Nation“ die Rede. Hierzulande sollten, wie es im Text weiter heißt, „Talent, Kapital, Forschung, Rechenkapazität und unternehmerische Initiative zusammenfinden, um Innovationen schnell, verantwortungsvoll und wirksam in Wachstum, Wohlstand, Sicherheit sowie gesellschaftlichen Fortschritt, Teilhabe und demokratische Resilienz zu überführen“.
Wer die technologischen Grundlagen, Talente, Infrastruktur und Anwendungen nicht rechtzeitig aufbaue, werde langfristig von den Entscheidungen anderer abhängig sein.

articles.title: Google Disrupts 1.3 Million-Device Android Botnet, Says TV Box Maker Sold Criminal Access
articles.text:
A botnet of more than 1.3 million Android devices, mostly TV set-top boxes, lost control of its servers in late October in a takedown led by Google.
Google says it is highly confident that device maker Videostrong intentionally put a backdoor in the boxes and sold access to criminals.
They used the boxes for ad fraud and to pass other people's internet traffic through owners' home connections. The backdoor is still on the boxes, and owners cannot remove it themselves.
Videostrong, based in Shenzhen, China, makes Android TV boxes and other devices under its own name and for other brands. The backdoor, called x.cpe, was built into many device models and brands over several years. Google does not believe a rogue insider or a mistake was to blame.
Google used legal action to take down the domains and servers that controlled the botnet. It also took down the control domains of more than a dozen malware families loaded through the backdoor. Japan's National Police Agency, Lumen, HUMAN Security, Plume, Synthient and TrendAI worked with Google on the operation.
Because the criminals behind that malware also spread it in other ways, Google expects the action to cut off their access to at least 10 million more infected devices. It warns that backdoor operators and the criminals who buy from them quickly switch to new tools when one part of their setup is disrupted.
Google has cut ties with Videostrong. It banned the company, and any future subsidiaries or affiliates, from building or selling certified Android devices and from supplying software to other certified device makers.
What the Backdoor Did
The x.cpe backdoor runs as a system app inside the firmware, with system-level access, according to Google's analysis. It reports to the botnet's command-and-control (C2) servers and waits for orders. To install software silently, it first turns off the app checks in Google Play Protect, Android's built-in security feature.
Through the backdoor, the botnet's operators could install apps without the owner knowing, run commands, capture the screen and map the network the box sits on.
Google says it saw Videostrong's operators use some of these powers. They took live screenshots, sent keystrokes, copied out account details, device information, app lists and system logs, and opened reverse shells, which give a remote command line into the box.
Most of the criminals' modules, the add-on programs loaded through the backdoor, turned the boxes into residential proxies or sold their spare bandwidth. A residential proxy service sells access to a home internet connection, so a customer's traffic appears to come from an ordinary household. Other modules faked views of online ads.
Most infected devices are Android TV set-top boxes, but the backdoor also turned up on telehealth devices, karaoke machines and digital signage.
TrendAI, Trend Micro's enterprise business unit, counted 1,472,554 infected devices across 206 models between June 3 and October 1, and says the real number is at least that high. Malaysia, Brazil, Iraq, Mexico and Taiwan had the most. The U.S., Germany, the U.K., Australia and Canada each had about 26,000 to 42,000.
What Owners Can Do
Synthient, which tracks proxy networks and botnets, has published a list of 182 device model names seen in the campaign. The list warns that a model name alone does not confirm that a box is infected.
Synthient's report focuses on MECOOL-branded boxes, which it links to Videostrong. It bought a MECOOL KM9PRO Max and found the backdoor preinstalled. Plume, which makes Wi-Fi software for internet providers, found more than a dozen different devices using the botnet's control server, most of them from MECOOL.
Because x.cpe is part of the firmware, removing it does not stick. It reinstalls itself when the box restarts. TrendAI says the backdoor runs as a system app signed with the maker's key, so cleanup needs "vendor action, platform protection or replacement of the device."
Plume recommends a full factory reset, because the modules may have installed more backdoors, but it does not say whether a reset removes x.cpe itself. Synthient goes further, telling consumers to throw the boxes away for good because they pose a high risk of malware.
For organizations, Synthient recommends these steps:
- Use its published indicators to find MECOOL or similar devices on the network.
- Disconnect and throw away any that turn up.
- Block the control domains and IP addresses its report lists.
- Keep other smart devices on separate network segments, away from sensitive systems.
TrendAI advises companies with remote staff to treat unmanaged consumer devices on home networks as part of their attack surface, and to keep corporate access behind managed devices.
How Videostrong Was Identified
In Google's account, x.cpe passes settings from the C2 server to other Videostrong apps, including its YokaTV Player streaming app. One of the GitHub accounts that hosted the botnet's packages is named yf-videostrong.
Synthient, which worked with Google, also concluded with high confidence that Videostrong runs the operation. It points to a document signed by Videostrong's research and development director in an open folder on one of the botnet's servers, and to a Videostrong web domain that shares an IP address with the operators' control panel.
Plume found that Videostrong supplies both the firmware for these devices and tools to manage them remotely.
A Gap in Google's Device Tests
Google requires device makers to go through a set of compatibility and security tests. It says Videostrong hid its code to bypass a gap in those tests and loaded the malicious code after a device's first boot.
Google has changed its review process and is improving its checks of the firmware on certified Android TV devices.
As of November 2, Videostrong's own website listed products it calls "Google Certified Android TV Box" and "Google Certified Android TV Stick."
Plume says the botnet included both Google-certified devices and devices running the Android Open Source Project (AOSP) version. Google's report does not say how many certified devices were affected.
When Google sued over the BadBox 2.0 botnet in July 2025, the more than 10 million devices involved were uncertified.

articles.title: Trois jours après la cyberattaque, Binance relance les retraits de cryptomonnaies
articles.text:
Ce dimanche 1ᵉʳ novembre 2026, Binance a commencé à rouvrir les retraits de cryptomonnaies. Trois jours plus tôt, la plus grande plateforme d’échange de cryptomonnaies au monde a été victime d’une intrusion d’envergure dans ses portefeuilles. En exploitant le PC compromis d’un ingénieur, des pirates ont siphonné les portefeuilles de l’exchange. Environ 6,3 milliards de dollars en cryptomonnaies ont disparu en une vingtaine de minutes. C’est le plus gros vol de l’histoire des cryptos.
À lire aussi : Le Bitcoin est dans le rouge – le hack de Binance plombe tout le marché crypto, 1,5 milliard de dollars envolés
Une réouverture progressive et prudente
La reprise des retraits se veut progressive. Dans un premier temps, Binance s’est concentré sur les retraits en bitcoin, en ether, en BNB, en Solana et en XRP. C’est le Bitcoin qui a ouvert le bal, suivi par les retraits d’ether, de BNB et des stablecoins USDT et USDC sur les réseaux Ethereum et BNB Smart Chain.
 Withdrawal Update
Withdrawals have now been restored for the following assets and networks:
– Ethereum Network: USDC, USDT, ETH
– BNB Smart Chain (BSC): USDC, USDT, BNB
We will continue to restore additional assets and networks in phases following the completion of our security checks. Further updates will be shared through official Binance channels.
— Binance (@binance) November 1, 2026
Comme l’explique Binance, chaque réseau n’est rouvert qu’à la suite d’une série de contrôles de sécurité. La plateforme s’est engagée à rouvrir les retraits pour les autres monnaies numériques « par étapes », sans calendrier précis. Binance donne la priorité aux cryptomonnaies les plus demandées par ses utilisateurs. Les dépôts, eux, n’ont jamais été interrompus.
Une vague de retraits
Sans surprise, de nombreux clients se sont empressés de retirer leurs fonds des comptes de Binance. Dimanche après-midi, Binance a traité 4,6 milliards de dollars de retraits, pour 1 milliard de dépôts, rapportent nos confrères de The Guardian. L’exchange a donc enregistré une sortie nette d’environ 3,6 milliards de dollars, soit un peu plus de 2% des 171 milliards de dollars d’actifs confiés à la plateforme.
Comme l’explique Ari Redbord, responsable des politiques publiques chez TRM Labs, à Reuters, il s’agit d’une « réaction de précaution plutôt que d’une véritable fuite des capitaux ». Binance indique d’ailleurs que « les volumes de retraits ont diminué et se stabilisent comme prévu ». Bref, les investisseurs ne fuient pas Binance, en dépit de la cyberattaque de la semaine dernière. La situation de Binance n’est pas comparable avec celle de FTX, qui a fermé ses portes en quelques jours en 2022 à la suite d’un exode massif d’utilisateurs, et de capitaux.
À lire aussi : 351 millions de dollars de cryptos dérobées – la plateforme Bitget a été piratée par des hackers nord-coréens
Binance absorbe les pertes
Avant de rouvrir les retraits, Binance devait d’abord combler le trou laissé par les pirates. La plateforme affirme avoir désormais reconstitué environ 95 % des actifs volés, notamment en piochant dans ses propres réserves et dans son fonds d’urgence SAFU. Pour éponger les pertes, Binance a injecté plus de 6,34 milliards de dollars, puisés dans son fonds d’urgence, dans des réserves d’assurance et dans sa trésorerie. Richard Teng, codirigeant de Binance, rappelle que « Binance absorbera l’impact financier des fonds volés, pas nos utilisateurs ».
 Today, we’re beginning the phased resumption of withdrawals, taking a careful approach to ensure services return safely and securely.
We’ve now replenished approximately 95% of the impacted assets, and our commitment remains clear: Binance will absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds, not our users.
Thank you for your patience, understanding, and continued trust. We know this hasn’t been easy, and we’re committed to seeing the recovery through.
— Richard Teng (@_RichardTeng) November 1, 2026
En parallèle, on apprend que le FBI a officiellement attribué l’attaque à TraderTraitor, un gang de pirates nord-coréens. Il s’agit du même groupe criminel à l’origine du piratage de Bybit en février 2025. Selon le FBI, les pirates ont converti l’essentiel du butin en Ether. Environ 3 milliards de dollars ont toutefois pu être bloqués avant qu’il ne soit trop tard. Le reste est en cours de blanchiment à travers les blockchains, sous la forme de milliers de transactions.

articles.title: Hackers disrupt refrigeration systems at European supermarkets
articles.text:
A cyberattack on refrigeration systems has disrupted stores run by multiple supermarket chains across several European countries after hackers remotely changed temperature settings on freezers and cooling systems.
In some cases, hackers shut down refrigerators or activated defrosting systems, causing temperatures to rise, resulting in significant product losses and forcing store managers to intervene early in the morning.
Refrigeration failures were identified at dozens of supermarkets, but it is unclear whether they were hit in a coordinated attack or targeted individually.
More than 115 stores in Belgium, the Netherlands, Sweden, Luxembourg, Ireland, and Estonia have been affected. Spokespersons for multiple chains confirmed the issues in statements for BleepingComputer.
Supermarket chains that acknowledged refrigeration issues include:
- ICA (Sweden) - At least 4 locations affected
- Coop (Sweden) - 7 locations confirmed affected
- Ahold Delhaize (Belgium and Luxembourg) - Around 40 locations affected
- Carrefour (Belgium) - 15 locations affected
- Spar Colruyt (Belgium) - 5 locations affected
- Intermarché (Belgium) - Around 15 locations affected
- SuperValu (Ireland) - 13 stores
- Selver (Estonia) - 1 store
In the Netherlands, at least 17 butcher shops and neighborhood stores have been affected.
Additional stores are dealing with the same problems in Belgium, including an Ikea superstore in Mons, grocery stores, and chocoloate shops.
Spokespersons for ICA, Ahold Delhaize, and Spar Colruyt told BleepingComputer that their companies are providing support to affected stores and working to resolve the situation.
“We can confirm that we have been informed of an incident overnight affecting a small number of ICA stores operating outside ICA’s central network,” stated ICA’s press officer.
“The incident impacted the stores’ refrigeration and freezer systems. ICA is currently supporting the affected stores in managing the situation.”
A representative of the Colruyt Group told BleepingComputer that "there is an impact on the refrigeration systems at around five Spar stores."
"These stores are operated by independent entrepreneurs who have their own refrigeration systems. We are currently doing everything we can to resolve the issue."
In a statement for BleepingComputer, Ahold Delhaize stated that refrigeration systems at several dozen stores have been impacted by an IT incident.
“We have identified an IT incident affecting the refrigeration systems in several dozen stores,” the company's communications department said, adding that the company "immediately took the necessary measures to keep our stores operational."
A spokesperson for Coop, one of the largest grocery store chains in Sweden, said that refrigeration units at a small number of stores were impacted, and in once case the system started to generate heat.
"We can confirm that a small number of stores were affected overnight into Monday - specifically 7 out of more than 800 stores," Coop told BleepingComputer.
"The situation is currently contained and under control. The issues have ranged from completely shut-down refrigerators and freezers to partially functioning units, and in one case, the system beginning to generate heat."
In Belgium, only Carrefour stores in two regions were affected, and all hypermarkets remained completely operational.
"The impact at Carrefour is very limited: currently 15 of our 700 stores are affected, both in Flanders and Wallonia," Carrefour stated.
"Not a single hypermarket is among them. All stores remain open because it only concerns a few refrigeration units, mainly freezers. Quick action was taken so that all stores can stay open."
An ICA store manager told TV4 that temperature settings had been changed overnight to +50°C (122°F) and could not be modified, forcing the store to discard frozen food.
According to RTL media publication, Ahold Delhaize warned managers by SMS around 4 a.m. about refrigeration issues, and some stores used refrigerated trucks to try to preserve stock.
The publication also identified Sabcobel as the vendor of refrigeration systems across several of the impacted locations.
According to Sabcobel's director, Stephan Moelans, the attacker leveraged the same vulnerability used in similar attacks last month in France.
Moelans said that technicians started disconnecting affected installations since 1a.m. and attributed the disruption to remotely activated defrost functions.
Although the company tried to protect customer's systems, a simple software update is not enough, as refrigerators also require physical modifications.
"The simplest solution is to manage the refrigerators via a secure internet connection. Most of our clients have adopted this solution since the attack in France," Moelans told RTL.
BleepingComputer has contacted Sabcobel to learn more about the incident and its level of involvement, but we are still waiting for a response.
Last month's refrigerator attacks in France impacted hundreds of stores using Danfoss AK-SM/AK-SC and Copeland/Dixell XWEB refrigeration controllers that were compromised by remote attackers who set them to defrost mode.

Nouveautés Canal+ : les films et séries à ne pas rater en novembre 2026
Quels sont les nouveaux films, séries et documentaires à rejoindre le catalogue de Canal+ en novembre 2026 ? Voici la liste des titres à ne pas manquer ce mois-ci en streaming.
Après Netflix, Disney+ et HBO Max, c'est au tour de Canal+ de dévoiler son programme à venir pour le mois de novembre 2026. Une livraison de nouveaux films, séries et documentaires particulièrement alléchante, et teintée d'un esprit "années 80".
Ce retour en arrière nostalgique est dûe notamment à l'arrivée du biopic blockbuster Michael au catalogue, mais aussi du film Juste une illusion de Toledano et Nakache. Les abonnés à la chaîne cryptée pourront aussi voir Marty Suprême et Super Mario Galaxy, ainsi que les séries Singapura et Yellowjackets. Bref, il y en a pour tout le monde.
Retrouvez ci-dessous la liste des nouveautés de Canal+ en novembre 2026, à la suite de notre suggestion film et série du mois sur le service de streaming.
La série du mois sur Canal+
Singapura
Justine débarque à Singapour, bien décidée à se réinventer et à offrir un nouveau départ à son couple. Elle découvre la petite communauté très policée des expatriés français et se laisse aussitôt fasciner par Élisa, un esprit libre, fantasque et tourmenté qui détonne dans ce cercle fermé. Lorsque celle-ci est assassinée, Justine se retrouve embarquée aux côtés de l’inspecteur Adam Wong dans une enquête où le vernis de l’expatriation se craquelle peu à peu.
La nouvelle création originale de Canal+ nous emporte dans l'univers des "expats" de la cité-état asiatique. Un monde à part, entre gratte-ciel et mangrove, propice à un thriller moite et suffoquant, où les crimes et les adultères vont de paire. Une série en mode "whodunit" certes un peu trop dans les rails du genre, mais avec un beau récit d'émancipation féminine et un casting solide, dont Naïlia Harzoune (66-5), Soji Arai (Tokyo Vice) et India Hair (Polar Park).
À partir du 2 novembre sur Canal+.

Le film du mois sur Canal+
Marty Suprême
Marty Mauser, un jeune homme à l’ambition démesurée, est prêt à tout pour réaliser son rêve et prouver au monde entier que rien ne lui est impossible.
Entre Uncut Gems, Attrape-moi si tu peux de Spielberg et After Hours de Martin Scorsese, Marty Suprême de Josh Safdie est le faux biopic d'un pongiste prêt à tout pour toucher le succès. Une fable capitaliste qui emporte pendant 2h30 dans des montagnes-russes fiévreuses et jubilatoires, où le spectateur se retrouve accroché à l'énergie désespérée d'un Timothée Chalamet au sommet de son art. articles.title: Educating an Architect: A Conversation with Luca Mezzalira
articles.text:
In this podcast, Michael Stiefel spoke to Luca Mezzalira about software architecture as a socio-technical discipline that balances technological design with an organization's social and managerial context. They explored how architectural choices must be adapted to a company's unique culture and team structure rather than relying blindly on universal best practices, noting that friction within a system serves as critical feedback regarding team and technical alignment. Since placing a dedicated architect on every team is unworkable, the discussion highlighted a shift toward an enablement mindset. Architects should be encouraged to act as coaches who empower developers to make decentralized decisions by establishing clear system guardrails and architectural fitness functions.
The best of architectural education comes from collaborative study and shared experiences rather than traditional lectures, allowing knowledge to organically evolve over time. As AI is increasingly used within systems, the architect must identify the areas of high volatility that require the careful supervision and guidance of experienced engineers, and the generic domains where delegation to AI agents can be more safely done.
Key Takeaways
- Software architecture is as much about the social and managerial context of the organization as the actual technological design of the system. Communication between the business and the engineering organization, as well as within the engineering groups is critical. The beliefs and knowledge of the technical teams, as well as the past history of the organization is important as well.
- Architectural choices, (e.g. choosing between microservices or monoliths, or team organization) must not be done by blindly applying universal best practices, but by adapting them to the organization’s culture and team structure. Friction within a system is a source of architectural feedback indicating a misalignment between the technical design, trade-offs, and team structures.
- The best architectural training comes from collaborative study among architects, using case studies and shared experience. Lectures and methods can give people a starting reference point, but that knowledge has to evolve over time.
- The architectural design must understand where there is a high volatility and experienced engineers are needed, and generic domains (e.g. standard payment integrations) that allow for greater delegation to probabilistic AI agents.
- Having dedicated architects on every team is unsustainable, architects should embrace an enablement and coaching mindset. Architects should focus on creating system guardrails, and architectural fitness functions to allow developers to make decentralized design decisions.
