articles.title: Hands on with the ASUS ROG XBOX Ally X20 - portable gaming paradise - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Tech Guide has gone hands-on with the ASUS ROG Xbox Ally X20 handheld gaming PC which is ideal for the gamer who wants to play the latest titles anywhere.
The 20th anniversary edition has a translucent design and gold accents to make it stand out from the regular model.
If a Windows gaming PC and an Xbox got together and had a child this would be the result.
A product that has the power of a PC and the gaming features of an Xbox – and with all the titles that go with it including the latest release of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 that we enjoyed playing on the move on the X20.
What grabs your attention from the get-go is the 7.4-inch OLED display, which has 1080p resolution and a 120 Hz refresh rate.
It’s also more glare-resistant than the previous model to ensure your gaming anywhere, even outside, is distraction-free.
On that stunning screen games they look great but are also quite responsive at the same time.
There’s a dedicated Xbox button on the top-left side of the device so you can hop straight into your games.
The ergonomically designed controllers feel comfortable in your hands and give you easy access to buttons above it, beside it and below it to make use of all the features and weapons at your disposal.
The joysticks are solid and responsive – regular gamers will be impressed by their precision.
Under the hood is the AMD AI Ryzen AZ extreme processor with 24GB high-speed LPDDR5x RAM and a 1TB SSD.
This is the same chipset as the previous model but still performed remarkably well even with the latest games like call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Star Wars Galactic Racer and Forza Horizon 6.
The 80Wh battery give you up to 3 hours of gameplay when you’re playing more intense and processor-sapping games.
If you want to settle for solitaire and the odd game of Sudoku, then you’ll get hours more out of it.
There’s also no charger in the box so if you are intending to buy one for the device, then look for a faster 35W charger to get you back up to full capacity even faster.
The only real downside of the ROG Xbox Ally X20 is the price, which is $2,499.
We understand there are a lot of pricing pressures with the memory and storage shortage affecting every tech manufacturer and ASUS is no different.
The Ally X20 was also available in a sold out bundle (priced at $4,499) that included the exclusive ROG XREAL R1 Edition 20 Gaming AR glasses, ROG XD Brand Kill Switch case and a ROG X Pelican Protector case.
The ROG XREAL R1 Edition 20 Gaming AR Glasses is even more immersive with the onboard OLED 240Hz display providing the equivalent of a 171-inch virtual screen at 4m.
The ROG XBOX Ally X20 handheld gaming PC is available now ahead via the ASUS Store and from JB Hi-Fi.

articles.title: Crypto’s next chapter: Regulatory sandboxes, AI co-pilots and the rise of derivatives
articles.text:
Crypto’s next chapter: Regulatory sandboxes, AI co-pilots and the rise of derivatives
At TechSparks 2026, Rajagopal Menon of WazirX, Satish Mishra of Pi42 and SharkExchange, and Sharat Chandra of EmpowerEdge Ventures discussed how regulation, risk management and AI are reshaping crypto investing in India
Crypto investing is evolving beyond its early hype cycles. Regulation, investor awareness, risk management and new technologies are changing how people trade digital assets, all while raising pertinent questions about what responsible participation should look like.
At TechSparks 2026, Rajagopal Menon, Vice President at WazirX; Satish Mishra, CTO of Pi42 and SharkExchange; and Sharat Chandra, Founder of EmpowerEdge Ventures, joined Swetha Kannan, Deputy Editor at YourStory, to discuss the changing crypto landscape, the need for regulatory clarity, and the growing role of AI in trading.
A new crypto landscape emerges
India’s crypto market has historically been a dynamic space, growing rapidly during the 2021-22 bull run, where Menon noted that WazirX’s spot markets processed close to $48 billion in transactions during that period. This was succeeded by the taxation measures introduced in the subsequent Budget that changed the market significantly.
According to Menon, the resulting environment of these changes has placed Indian exchanges at a disadvantage compared with foreign platforms. Domestic exchanges must deduct tax at source (TDS) and operate within the 30% tax framework, while foreign exchanges have not faced the same requirements, he argued. “I think a stable environment or a better environment would be that the same rules apply for everybody, so that Make in India is made for Indian exchanges,” he shared.
Menon also pointed to a shift in trading activity. As spot trading volumes declined, futures and derivatives began gaining traction. He expects this segment to see significant adoption in India.
Regulation that makes room for all players
Moving to the question of regulation, Chandra shared that exchanges had helped educate investors about different crypto assets and the importance of understanding risks, but that gaps in the regulatory framework remained. “I think once this space is regulated, that can lead to a lot of capital inflow to the country,” he said.
Chandra pointed out that while exchanges are required to follow KYC norms, there are still gaps when it comes to verifying identities as assets move on-chain. He suggested that regulatory sandboxes could help address some of these challenges. SEBI and IFSCA already have sandboxes to encourage innovation in the capital markets, but digital asset native fintech players have not yet been given the go-ahead to participate.
He also highlighted the potential of tokenisation, pointing to the tokenisation of corporate bonds as an example. For now, participation is limited to institutional players. Chandra suggested that opening up regulatory sandboxes to more web3 fintech companies could help them test new ideas, improve existing processes and play a bigger role in the tokenisation journey.
Crypto infrastructure: Built for endurance
Unlike traditional financial markets, crypto trades 24 hours a day, seven days a week. For tech teams, that means monitoring systems, managing risk and responding to incidents without the predictable downtime offered by market closing hours.
Mishra described how trading activity on crypto platforms can pick up during evenings and weekends, partly in response to movements in US markets. This places continuous demands on observability, alerts and leverage monitoring.
His experience building a spot trading exchange also showed how quickly demand for derivatives can outpace infrastructure development. At Pi42, the team took a different approach from the outset, building a platform specifically for derivatives rather than adapting a spot-trading system.
Production incidents, Mishra noted, had occurred over weekends when systems could not keep pace with demand. The experience underlined the need to build infrastructure around crypto’s round-the-clock operating model.
Beyond the hype: When risk management is embedded in processes
As more people enter the crypto market, investor education and effective compliance become increasingly important. Menon pointed to WazirX’s ‘Gangs of Cryptopur’ campaign, which aims to help investors understand what they’re trading. He also spoke about taking a disciplined approach to crypto, comparing the historical returns of different asset classes with Bitcoin. His advice was to think long term rather than treat crypto as a series of short-term bets.
For exchanges, making the process easier for users is just as important as maintaining compliance checks. Mishra explained that KYC can be frustrating when an application fails and users have to start all over again. Technology can make this simpler by letting users pick up where they left off and clearly explaining what needs to be corrected.
He added that genuine users are generally less likely to be bothered by compliance checks than those trying to get around them. The aim is to make the process smoother for users while retaining the checks needed to identify suspicious activity.
Putting AI to work in crypto: regulation, education, innovation
AI is also changing how traders research markets and assess potential trades. Menon said WazirX has introduced an AI-powered feature that scans more than 300 tokens to spot those showing bearish momentum. WazirX AI - India’s first AI-powered crypto agent is a conversational co-pilot that handles advanced, multi-step requests, including technical indicators such as the Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) and Relative Strength Index (RSI), and offers recommendations for users to consider. Traders must confirm their chosen strategy before the AI places an order with stop-loss and take-profit parameters.
Menon sees AI as a way to analyse large volumes of market data and spot patterns, but he also highlighted that AI should support decisions rather than make them for users.
Mishra also urged traders to backtest AI-generated strategies and monitor their performance before using them in live markets, saying “If you ask AI to give you a strategy and then run with it, make sure that you are also observing it so as soon as it goes wrong, you can unplug it.”
Chandra noted that regulatory implications will depend on how AI is used. Educational tools could be treated differently from systems that offer personalised investment advice, which could fall under investment-adviser regulations. He also stressed the need for AI systems to be trustworthy, explainable, auditable and fair.
What comes next for crypto?
As the crypto landscape changes with new regulations, AI disruptions and evolving investor expectations, Menon, Chandra and Mishra were asked what would represent the next phase of the sector.
For Menon, it was futures and derivatives. Mishra agreed, noting that derivatives have continued to grow and address specific needs within the crypto ecosystem.
Chandra pointed to another emerging possibility: compute futures, with developments such as the launch of compute futures by CME in the US indicating how new asset classes could emerge at the intersection of AI and digital assets.
As the market evolves, the discussion highlighted three interconnected priorities: clearer regulation, stronger infrastructure and more informed use of AI. The next phase of crypto investing in India will depend not just on new products and trading opportunities, but also on how effectively the ecosystem manages risk and builds trust.

articles.title: Microsoft fixes Smart App Control broken by October Windows update
articles.text:
Microsoft has resolved a known issue that prevented some users from activating the Smart App Control security feature after installing the October 2026 KB5127648 Windows 11 security update.
Smart App Control uses Microsoft's code integrity features and app intelligence services, and it works alongside SmartScreen and Microsoft Defender to block potentially harmful apps or binaries.
As the company explained when it acknowledged the issue last month, the Smart App Control option is grayed out and cannot be toggled on affected devices running Windows 11 24H2 and later.
"After installing this update, some devices might be unable to turn on Smart App Control in the Windows Security app if it has been turned off. On affected devices, the option to turn on Smart App Control might be grayed out," Microsoft said in the KB5127648 advisory. "Devices where Smart App Control is already turned on are not affected and remain protected."
On Wednesday, the company confirmed that the issue has been fixed for users who installed this month's KB5127936 preview update.
"This issue was resolved by Windows updates released October 28, 2026 [..] and later. We recommend you install the latest security update for your device as it contains important improvements and issue resolutions, including this one," it noted in a service alert sent to IT administrators.
Workaround available
Microsoft also shared a temporary fix for admins who don't want to deploy the preview update on enterprise-managed devices and want to wait for next month's Patch Tuesday cumulative updates.
This requires them to edit the registry on affected Windows 11 devices to restore the ability to turn on Smart App Control by going through the following steps:
- Open a Command Prompt window by typing cmd in the Search box.
- Select Run as Administrator.
- At the command prompt, enter the following commands and then restart the device: reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Policies\Microsoft\FeatureManagement\Overrides" /v 2883193997 /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Policies\Microsoft\FeatureManagement\Overrides" /v 2850574478 /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
They can also work around the issue by installing the Group Policies below, which turn on Smart App Control and enable logging for troubleshooting:
- Windows 11, versions 24H2, 25H2, and 26H2 - KB5074105 261015_19222 Feature Preview
- Windows 11, versions 24H2, 25H2, and 26H2 - KB5074105 261015_19221 Feature Preview
The Group Policy settings are under Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > {Group Policy name} > Windows 11, version 24H2, 25H2, and must be set to Enabled after installation. Admins must also restart affected devices to apply the Group Policy settings.
Last month's KB5127936 preview update also resolves Remote Desktop failures caused by recent Windows updates when the "Administrator protection" security feature is enabled and finally fixes Always On VPN issues triggered by the September 2026 cumulative updates.

articles.title: Hacienda confirma que los mayores de 65 años pueden donar su vivienda habitual a sus hijos sin pagar IRPF por la ganancia
articles.text:
Poner la casa a nombre de los hijos antes de fallecer es una alternativa que se plantean muchos padres, pero esa donación no pasa desapercibida y tiene consecuencias en la declaración de la renta de quien la hace. Y es que los mayores de 65 años cuentan con una exención en el IRPF que les evita tributar por la ganancia que obtienen al donar su vivienda habitual. Eso sí, no es una medida nueva y tiene requisitos concretos.
Lo que dice la ley. La exención está en el artículo 33.4.b de la Ley del IRPF, que deja fuera del impuesto la ganancia patrimonial que obtienen los mayores de 65 años al transmitir su vivienda habitual, y la Agencia Tributaria la incluye entre las rentas que no se declaran en su manual para mayores de 65. Pero en principio la donación sí genera una ganancia para quien entrega la casa, según explica la Dirección General de Tributos (DGT) en su consulta vinculante V2752-21. En esa respuesta, de noviembre de 2021, Tributos ya aplicaba la exención a un mayor de 65 años que quería donar su vivienda habitual a su hija.
El peso de la revalorización. La ventaja se nota sobre todo cuando la vivienda se compró hace décadas y desde entonces ha ganado mucho valor, porque la ganancia se calcula restando lo que costó al valor que se le asigna en la donación. Vamos, que cuanto más se haya revalorizado la casa, más dinero deja de integrar en su IRPF quien la dona.
Tiene que ser la vivienda habitual. El requisito clave es que el inmueble cuente como vivienda habitual a efectos fiscales. Según el mismo manual de la Agencia Tributaria, que remite al Reglamento del IRPF, eso exige haber residido en ella de forma continuada al menos tres años, salvo excepciones como un matrimonio o un traslado laboral, y que lo siga siendo al donarla o lo haya sido en algún momento de los dos años anteriores.
Y la DGT lo volvió a aplicar en la consulta V0217-26, fechada el 4 de febrero de 2026: un contribuyente mayor de 65 años que llevaba más de 14 años sin vivir en la que fue su casa, alquilada durante ese tiempo, no podía acogerse a la exención porque habían pasado más de dos años desde que dejó de ser su residencia habitual.
El hijo no se libra. Aunque el padre o la madre se ahorren el IRPF por la ganancia, el hijo o la hija que reciban la vivienda quedarán sujetos al Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones. Y no van a pagar lo mismo en todas partes, porque, si el hijo reside en España, la donación de un inmueble tributa con carácter general según la normativa de la comunidad autónoma donde está la vivienda, que es la que fija reducciones y bonificaciones, como detalla una contestación vinculante de la Comunidad de Madrid.
Así que la ventaja existe, y haciendo esta donación el donante puede salir ganando en su IRPF. Pero no es una operación sin impuestos, porque estos tendrán que pagarlos quienes reciben el inmueble.

articles.title: Digital Detox beim Abendessen: Sardinische Gaststätten verbannen Tablets und Smartphones vom Tisch
articles.text:
Digital Detox beim Abendessen: Sardinische Gaststätten verbannen Tablets und Smartphones vom Tisch
Alle beim Essen im Restaurant mit Handys am Tisch, die Kinder am Tablet mit irgendwelchen Videos oder Spielen beschäftigt? Auf Sardinien hat ein Pilotversuch begonnen, mit dem Familien am Esstisch wieder zum Reden gebracht werden sollen. An der zunächst auf einen Monat befristeten Aktion „A tavola senza schermi“ („Zu Tisch ohne Bildschirme“) nehmen seit diesem Sonntag auf der italienischen Mittelmeerinsel insgesamt 15 Gaststätten teil.
Dabei verpflichten sich die Gäste mit Betreten des Restaurants, alle Handys und Tablets entweder tief in den Taschen zu verstauen oder in einem Korb abzulegen. Als Ausgleich gibt es für Familien mit Kindern ein «Begegnungsset» mit Spielen und Buntstiften. Das Projekt wurde vom Gastgewerbeverband der Insel zusammen mit der dortigen Kinder- und Jugendbeauftragten Anna Cau entwickelt.
Teilnahme auf freiwilliger Basis
Ziel der Initiative ist es, Kinder und Jugendliche zumindest im Restaurant „vom Netz zu nehmen“, damit sie spielen, malen und reden, anstatt auf den Bildschirm zu starren. Die Teilnahme ist freiwillig. Ein striktes Handyverbot gibt es in den beteiligten Gaststätten nicht. Ausnahmen sind erlaubt, müssen aber abgesprochen werden. Falls es doch wichtige Telefonate gibt, sollen diese abseits vom Tisch und außer Hörweite geführt werden.
„Die digitale Welt muss gut geregelt werden“, sagte die Kinderbeauftragte Cau. „Minderjährige müssen vor dem Missbrauch elektronischer Geräte und vor ungeeigneten Inhalten geschützt werden. Eltern müssen sich der Risiken und Chancen technologischer Geräte bewusst sein.“ Der Vorsitzende des Gastgewerbeverbands, Emanuele Frongia, meint, dass ohne Handys auch Erwachsene wieder besser ins Gespräch kämen: „Ein Restaurant ist ein Ort, an dem man sich trifft, miteinander spricht und Zeit miteinander verbringt.“
An der Aktion nehmen Gaststätten aus größeren Städten wie der Inselhauptstadt Cagliari teil, aber auch aus kleineren Gemeinden. Sardinien wird auch viel von Touristen besucht.
Entschuldigung – aber IMHO heisst das adjektiv in deutscher Sprache korrekt: „sardisch“, nicht „sardinisch“

articles.title: Diagnose Distributed AI Workload Failures with NVIDIA Attribution | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
In distributed AI workloads, a single error can produce a cascade of symptoms. A GPU or fabric event may surface as NCCL errors on other ranks, scheduler state changes, and thousands of downstream messages. The reported exception shows where the workload stopped, not where the failure began.
In this post, you’ll learn how to run NVIDIA Attribution on sample workload evidence, inspect the diagnosis, and explore how attribution rules identify failure patterns.
NVIDIA Attribution correlates workload-scoped logs, metrics, telemetry, and scheduler state and returns a structured diagnosis: outcome, root cause, affected nodes, supporting symptoms, and evidence trail. Workload-centric means analyzing failures in the context of a workload rather than as isolated node events. Deterministic rules make the results reproducible and customizable, while structured output enables integration with existing health and recovery systems.
NVIDIA health and resilience software helps teams keep AI workloads running. NVIDIA Attribution explains why a workload failed and provides evidence to guide the next action. It complements readiness checks, continuous health monitoring, and the systems that repair infrastructure and restart workloads.
Used in production across NVIDIA AI infrastructure for years, NVIDIA Attribution analyzes millions of workloads each week across hundreds of thousands of GPUs. In one large RDMA-backed cluster, it correlated port errors, connection resets, and scheduler events to identify patterns around specific host and switch ports, helping teams target fabric repairs and congestion tuning.
It includes two deployable components: the NVIDIA Attribution Service and the NVIDIA Attribution Blueprint; both components utilize a core attribution engine. The Service makes attribution available through a RESTAPI; the Blueprint connects cluster schedulers and telemetry sources to the Service and writes the result.
Turn workload evidence into one diagnosis
NVIDIA Attribution Service analyzes one workload attempt at a time. The Blueprint gathers the workload context and evidence, the Service extracts and correlates events, and the Blueprint returns a structured result.
The path has four stages:
- Scope the workload. The Blueprint identifies the workload attempt from scheduler identifiers or from an explicit execution window and node allocation.
- Collect observations. Log and metric connectors produce workload-scoped Observation records from application logs, syslogs, GPU driver and Fabric Manager messages, scheduler history, node and network metrics.
- Extract and correlate events. The Service invokes the attribution engine to identify significant events such as GPU XIDs, NCCL failures, scheduler transitions, and metric conditions. Deterministic rules evaluate their timing and interaction, separate downstream symptoms from the event that caused the failure, and identify the root cause.
- Return a structured result. The Blueprint combines the verdict with the workload outcome (terminal_state), attributed domain (sub_domain), symptoms, affected nodes, and a record of collector coverage and errors.
From applogs to attribution
What follows is a worked example of extracting evidence, interpreting events, and preserving the symptoms that explain a distributed workload failure.
Consider a multi-rank training workload in which one GPU encounters a hard fault e.g: XID 149 and NCCL errors follow across other ranks. NVIDIA Attribution correlates events across nodes, identifies the XID as the root cause, retains the NCCL failures in the symptom chain, and names the responsible node. The workload is reported as a hardware failure rather than a set of independent communication errors.
A failed collective can leave error reports on several nodes. Those reports tell us where the workload noticed a problem. To explain the failure, NVIDIA Attribution combines them with evidence from other sources and evaluates the symptoms together.
In this synthetic workload, application logs contain three different NCCL errors. System logs on node-02 contain XID 149 with error words that decode to NVLink signal integrity issue. We will follow that evidence through the rules pipeline.
Interpreting logs with extraction
The Extraction phase is the first to run; it runs on the raw input logs and produces structured events to be processed by later stages.
Decode NVLink evidence during filtering
Filter rules read and write the event stream. The EARLY-stage HandleXidBurstEvents rule reads the XID burst evidence, decodes the error words, and emits an attribution event for signal integrity issue on node-02. The three NCCL events remain unchanged during this step.
Figure 2, above, The figure abbreviates the decoded symptom as XID-149.4 signal integrity issue. The filter also emits parser information for inspection.
Refine the symptoms into one attribution
The framework materializes events into per-node symptoms, runs per-node scrubbing, and aggregates the surviving symptoms into a job-wide set. In this example, all four candidates reach FINAL refinement.
Xid149AndNvlinkFiltering retains the signal integrity symptom and demotes the other node symptoms. Gb200PriorityRootCause reduces the active job-wide symptom set. Outcome mapping then produces the hardware-failure attribution.
The attribution surfaces node-02 and signal integrity issue. The NCCL reports remain useful evidence: demotion preserves their original sources as “interesting,” so they can still be inspected.
When multiple causes fit the evidence, sub_domain is ambiguous. Quality of attribution is dependent on the quality and completeness of the underlying telemetry. The diagnosis records that distinction, correctly reflecting uncertainty instead of converting incomplete evidence into a definitive diagnosis.
Service and Blueprint architecture
The attribution engine contains the rules engine and core attribution logic. The Attribution Service exposes that logic through an HTTP API, and the Blueprint handles cluster-specific integration. This separation lets teams apply the same attribution logic across clusters while adapting scheduler, telemetry, and output connectors to each environment.
Attribution Service: A self-hosted HTTP wrapper around the core attribution engine that receives normalized observations and returns one verdict for each workload.
Attribution Blueprint: A Python reference orchestrator that discovers workloads, resolves the ExecutionContext, runs collectors, calls the Service, enriches the verdict, writes the AttributionBlueprintResult, and supplies a read-only dashboard. This is intended to be a reference implementation for practitioners to customize the solution to their environment. 
The Blueprint ships with:
- Execution-context connectors for Slurm, Kueue, and static inputs
- Log and metric connectors for Loki, local files, Kubernetes pod logs, and PromQL metrics
- Output connectors for stdout and SQLite
Blueprints can run near each cluster’s data sources, with either a dedicated Attribution Service for each Blueprint or a shared Service for multiple Blueprints. There is flexibility on how you want to customize your deployment, e.g: one to one or one to many. Downstream systems consume terminal_state and sub_domain instead of parsing product-specific logs.
Extending Attribution to your infrastructure
Open sourcing NVIDIA Attribution enables infrastructure teams to encode a failure pattern once and apply it across workloads and clusters. Developers can add rules for new failure modes, implement connectors for their schedulers and telemetry backends, and route AttributionBlueprintResult records into incident, recovery, and fleet-management systems. Because extensions use the same ExecutionContext, Observation, and result contracts, new integrations feed the same diagnosis pipeline.
Walkthrough
The earlier example illustrates how a GPU fault can lead to NCCL errors across ranks. In this walkthrough, you’ll use NVIDIA Attribution to analyze NVLink error evidence from a recorded training workload. You’ll run the included sample, inspect the diagnosis and source evidence, and examine the rule that narrows the reported symptoms. You’ll then use the NVIDIA recovery guidance to identify the next action for the affected node.
The walkthrough uses two components:
- The Attribution Service runs the analysis rules.
- The Attribution Blueprint reads the workload context and logs, calls the Service, and stores the result for inspection in a local dashboard.
The sample evidence ships with the repository, so you can follow the analysis before connecting a live cluster.
Run the sample workflow
The NVIDIA Attribution quickstart builds the Attribution Service and dashboard in Docker, then uses the Blueprint to process sample workload evidence committed to the repository. You need Docker and the uv package manager.
Clone the repository and run the sample workflow:
git clone https://github.com/dsx-ai-factory/attribution.git nvidia-attribution
cd nvidia-attribution
docker build \
  -f blueprint/docker/Dockerfile \
  -t attribution-blueprint-web:quickstart \
  "$PWD"
mkdir -p .attribution-sample
docker run -d --rm \
  --name attribution-blueprint-web-local \
  -e ATTRIBUTION_DB=/data/attributions.db \
  -p "127.0.0.1:8000:8000" \
  -p "127.0.0.1:8080:8080" \
  -v "$PWD/.attribution-sample:/data" \
  attribution-blueprint-web:quickstart
uv run --project blueprint --frozen nvidia-attribution-blueprint \
  --configs blueprint/examples/static/configs \
  --connector attribution service_url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  --connector output db sqlite path .attribution-sample/attributions.db
Open http://127.0.0.1:8080 to inspect each workload’s diagnosis, affected nodes, supporting symptoms, and evidence trail.
The rules engine uses checked-in declarative and Python rules. This production rule recognizes an invalid Pyxis argument in an application log and includes a co-located test case:
[[extractor]]
name     = "SrunInvalidPyxisArgument"
match_re = "srun: error: Invalid --(?:no-)?container-\\S+ argument:"
emit     = { type = "bad_node", symptom = "srun: invalid pyxis argument" }
[[extractor.cases]]
expect  = "bad"
line    = "srun: error: Invalid --container-mounts argument: /nonexistent"
symptom = "srun: invalid pyxis argument"
At startup, the Service loads the bundled rule catalog and evaluates the inline cases. A rule change is committed and shipped with the Service; rules are not uploaded dynamically through the HTTP API. The repository’s rule-authoring guide explains how to select the appropriate rule form, register new symptoms, add tests, and verify the complete catalog.
Get started
Clone the NVIDIA Attribution repository and follow the quickstart to run the sample and inspect its diagnoses. To use Attribution with your own infrastructure, see the Blueprint configuration reference for scheduler and telemetry connectors, and learn how to add an extractor rule for new evidence patterns.
Acknowledgements
Aaron Blakeman, Ajay Hotchandani, Alex Shaposhnikov, Ashwin Poojary, Ben Gueret, Chunyang Sheng, Dorrin Poorkay, Gargi Prasad, Felix Abecassis, Grace Tan, Jason Sewall, Mayuri Gupta, Pasha Shamis, Pavan Kumar Gondhi, Piero Orderique, Rahul Kandu, Rakesh Konda and Sirshak Das contributed to NVIDIA Attribution and to this post.

articles.title: Marvell Proposes Acquiring Lumentum to Combine Optical Circuit Switching with AI Connectivity Silicon
articles.text:
Marvell Technology announced today that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction with an implied value of about $115 billion. The proposed deal aims to merge Marvell’s electrical interconnect and custom silicon portfolio with Lumentum’s high-performance lasers, optical circuit switching (OCS), and compound semiconductor manufacturing capabilities. For AI infrastructure designers facing the physical limits of copper, this combination could drive deeper co-design across the entire signal chain, from distributed data centers to connections within advanced semiconductor packages.
Bridging the Copper Wall with Integrated Optics
The primary driver for this acquisition is the industry transition from electrical to optical connectivity as AI clusters scale. At the Marvell Computex 2026 Keynote, CEO Matt Murphy described connectivity as the next major bottleneck in data center design, noting that compute performance gains are outpacing connectivity and networking gains. Marvell has positioned itself to address this by offering solutions across various distances, from long-haul coherent links to short-reach scale-up domains. However, the “copper wall,” or the maximum distance copper can viably support before signal integrity fails, is moving closer as lane speeds increase. A copper-to-optics transition is underway in the industry, albeit slower than many people thought it would be 10 years ago.
Marvell’s existing portfolio addresses parts of this challenge with products like the COLORZ 800 module, which we examined in Going 800Gbps at up to 1000km with the Marvell COLORZ 800. That module uses coherent detection and a local oscillator to maintain signal integrity over vast distances, packaging complex DSPs and photonics into a standard OSFP form factor. While effective for long-reach scale-across links, the move toward co-packaged optics (CPO) requires even tighter integration between the switch silicon and the optical engine.
The proposed combination pairs Marvell’s electrical and optical interconnect, CMOS/silicon photonics, switching/custom silicon design, and packaging expertise with Lumentum’s specialized compound semiconductor manufacturing, including indium phosphide (InP), plus high-speed and high-power lasers.
As we saw in our Marvell TX9190 CPO switch coverage from OCP 2025, near-package optical engines shorten the electrical path, with fiber runs and pluggable light sources replacing long PCB traces. We also saw some neat technology on our recent AWS Networking Lab tour.
By acquiring Lumentum, Marvell intends to control more of this supply chain internally and design solutions across a larger domain instead of having to go to different companies for different parts.
Beyond component integration, Lumentum brings optical circuit switching (OCS) to the combined portfolio. The Lumentum R300 OCS establishes direct optical paths between endpoints using micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) mirrors, eliminating intermediate packet processing and optical-electrical-optical (OEO) conversion along those switched paths. Lumentum says this results in dramatically lower latency, higher signal integrity, and significant reductions in network power for large GPU clusters.
Acquiring Lumentum and its technology will not come cheap, however. The $115 billion deal is being financed entirely with Marvell’s stock, significantly leveraging the value of the roughly $175 billion company in order to pay for the deal. In effect, this makes the deal closer to a merger than a buy-out. Following the settlement of the deal, Marvell shareholders will own 67% of the new company, while Lumentum shareholders will own the other 33%. Similarly, the deal will see three members of Lumentum’s board of directors join Marvell’s board, bringing it up to 10 members.
Final Words
This deal, expected to close in the first half of 2028, so some time away, coordinates Marvell electrical and optical interconnect plus silicon design with Lumentum lasers, optical manufacturing, and OCS. The companies intend closer co-design and optimized, pre-validated optical solutions, faster time to market, and high-volume production, but that close is a long way away. This is a huge deal when companies are seeing valuations soar due to AI demand.

articles.title: Juicyway recieves approval from Nigerian SEC for exchange
articles.text:
Juicyway, a cross-border payments company, is building a platform connecting African assets with global investors, its founder and chief executive, Ife Johnson, said, arguing that faster payments alone cannot solve the continent’s financing problem.
Speaking at Moonshot by TechCabal in Lagos, Johnson outlined plans for the ‘People’s Exchange’, which would use tokenisation, creating blockchain-based records of assets and securities, to help businesses raise money across markets. Johnson said Juicyway has received approval in principle from Nigeria’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to build the exchange.
“We’ve produced category winners without producing enough shared infrastructure for entire categories to grow,” he said. “Africa needs more shared infrastructure and fewer isolated winners.”
Juicyway deals with this every day. Software can send a payment instruction in seconds, but the money to complete that payment still has to be sitting in the right currency, in the right country.
“For roughly 95% of the transactions that we have to carry out, we have to perform settlements,” Johnson said. The exchange’s first focus would be financing that liquidity, he said, with later uses in mortgages, trade receivables, energy, commodities and stakes in private companies.
His argument is that the same shortage runs through the wider economy, as businesses hold receivables, projects need investment and households need long-term loans, but the capital to fund them is split across dozens of small markets.
Africa’s unmet demand for trade finance was between $74 billion and $92 billion in 2024, according to the African Development Bank’s 2025 trade finance report. African companies raised about $220 billion in equity on local stock markets between 2000 and 2024, just 1% of the equity raised worldwide, according to the OECD’s Africa Capital Markets Report 2025.
Johnson proposed tokenising investments to structure them, record who owns them and sell them across borders, with stablecoins moving and settling the money. “I don’t think Africa needs 29 exchanges,” he said. “I think it needs one market that connects them all.”
The aim is to let African businesses reach investors beyond their home markets. Making that work will take more than a shared technology platform: investors will need confidence in the underlying assets, in their ownership rights, and in how they get repaid or sell their stakes.
Johnson framed the exchange as a long-term project, citing his son. “I want his generation to inherit markets that finance the ambitions, rather than ambitions constrained by the absence of markets,” he said.

articles.title: Alguien ha conseguido lo que parecía imposible: un Redmi Note 12 ejecutando iOS. Con ayuda de Claude, claro
articles.text:
A lo largo de todos estos años hemos visto mil y un ejemplos de modders intentando ejecutar iOS en teléfonos Android y viceversa. Han sido proyectos que, en su mayoría, han acabado en balde, pero en un contexto en el que existe la IA generativa (y mucho tiempo libre), ahora una oleada de aficionados se han puesto manos a la obra con resultados bastante sorprendentes.
Las redes sociales se han llenado de vídeos en los que usuarios han conseguido ejecutar iOS en Android. Un clip de iOS 16 en un Redmi Note 12 es uno de los que más ha dado de qué hablar estos días. Te contamos cómo lo han hecho.
Hito técnico. iOS está diseñado para funcionar únicamente en hardware de Apple, como seguramente sabrás. Ha habido proyectos anteriores para hacer justo lo contrario: ejecutar Android en un iPhone. Entre ellos se encuentra iDroid, que lograba arrancar Android en los primeros iPhone en 2010, y posteriormente Project Sandcastle, que hizo lo mismo con Android 10 en iPhone utilizando el chip AIO de Apple. Hasta ahora nadie había logrado hacer lo opuesto hasta ahora.
Cómo funciona. El movimiento, apodado "Hackios" e inspirado en la escena Hackintosh (macOS en PCs que no son de Apple), se remonta a un proyecto de código abierto en GitHub llamado ios-sweet. Sustituye el núcleo de Linux que los teléfonos Android usan normalmente por XNU, el núcleo que Apple utiliza en sus propios dispositivos. Un núcleo es el centro de un sistema operativo, básicamente la capa que permite que el software se comunique con el chip, la memoria y el almacenamiento. Lo bueno es que Apple publica el código fuente de XNU de forma abierta, por eso han surgido tantos experimentos.
En concreto, ios-sweet proporciona a XNU un árbol de dispositivos copiado de un iPhone X. Un árbol de dispositivos es algo así como la descripción del hardware en el que se ejecuta. En este caso, al entregarle el árbol de dispositivos de un iPhone X, el núcleo cree que está arrancando en un iPhone. Después se cargan archivos sin modificar de iOS 16 procedentes de un iPhone X, ejecutándose sobre el chip del móvil Android.
Por qué el iPhone X. Según cuentan desde Android Authority, el desarrollador del proyecto lo eligió porque es el último iPhone sin autenticación de punteros (PAC), una característica de seguridad requerida a partir del iPhone X en adelante. Los chips Qualcomm como el del Redmi Note 10 Pro no admiten PAC, por lo que un software de iPhone más nuevo no arrancaría. Así que lo más probable es que este mismo enfoque no funcione en móviles más modernos.
Qué funciona y qué no. Aún no es un sistema operativo que convierta en “utilizable” un teléfono móvil porque todavía hay bastantes elementos que no funcionan. En el ejemplo del Redmi Note 10 Pro, llega a la pantalla de bloqueo, la pantalla de inicio, el Centro de Control y Ajustes, y la entrada táctil y los botones físicos responden. Pero no funciona el WiFi, ni el Bluetooth ni los datos móviles. Tampoco funciona el audio, ni las cámaras, ni los sensores biométricos. Además, algunas apps del sistema como Mensajes, Teléfono o Fotos solo muestran una pantalla en negro.
Tampoco hay controlador gráfico, así que el sistema dibuja la pantalla a unos 20-30 fotogramas por segundo. Según cuentan desde Decrypt, esto hace que el móvil tarde en arrancar a este sistema entre 4 y 5 minutos.
Teléfonos compatibles. Más allá del Redmi Note 10 Pro, existen versiones que se han adaptado para el Redmi Note 12 Pro y el LG V60, según cuentan desde Android Authority. Los desarrolladores también están trabajando en el OnePlus 7T, el Redmi 5 Plus y el Galaxy S23 Ultra, aunque el código de momento aún no es público. También ha habido intentos con un Google Pixel 6 (con un chip Tensor) y un Galaxy S7 (con el Exynos 8890), pero no ha habido suerte aún.
La buena noticia es que el desarrollador encargado de adaptar el hack al Redmi Note 12 afirma tener sonido, WiFi y fondo de pantalla funcionando, pero el sistema sigue siendo muy inestable al parecer. Desde Decrypt también mencionan a un grupo independiente, OOSexGang, que afirma ejecutar iOS 16.5 en un Poco X5 Pro, publicando el proyecto en Github.
La IA. La mayoría de estas adaptaciones que han salido se apoyan en contenido asistido por IA generativa, ya que en el archivo NOTES.md de los repositorios se incluyen instrucciones para agentes de IA como Claude Code, ChatGPT Codex o Gemini. El ritmo con el que los agentes pueden desplegar software es muchísimo más rápido, de ahí que últimamente estemos viendo proyectos a cada cual más loco. Incluso en videojuegos, donde a lo largo de estos últimos meses se han publicado centenares de decompilaciones de juegos ejecutándose en entornos y consolas muy distintas a su intención original.

articles.title: Ça : Bienvenue à Derry : HBO Max crée la surprise avec un épisode bonus disponible dès maintenant !
articles.text:
Bienvenue à Derry : HBO Max dévoile un épisode surprise sur les origines du clown tueur
Pour Halloween, HBO Max a offert un cadeau aux fans de la série Ça : Bienvenue à Derry.
Un épisode spécial de la série Ça : Bienvenue à Derry est apparu sur le service de streaming HBO Max le jour d'Halloween, pour le plus grand plaisir des fans. Intitulé "Ça : La Légende de Derry," il revient sur les origines de Ça dans la forêt de l'Ouest.
Derry bien avant Grippe-Sou
La série préquelle de Ça est arrivée sur HBO Max en 2025 pour raconter les événements étranges liés au clown Grippe-Sou qui se sont déroulés dans la ville de Derry dans les années 1960.
La voilà de retour cette année avec un épisode inédit de 30 minutes qui remonte encore plus dans le temps, quelques centaines d'années plus tôt, pour revenir sur la rencontre terrifiante entre trois jeunes natifs américains et un ancien esprit.
IT's a surprise Halloween treat.
Catch this never-before-seen special exploring the origins of IT in Derry. #AStoryOfDerry is streaming now on HBO Max. 🎈 pic.twitter.com/NH3NcMLt8n
— HBO Max (@hbomax) October 31, 2026
Récemment reconduite pour une saison 2, la série Ça : Bienvenue à Derry devrait revenir sur HBO Max d'ici à fin 2027 ou en 2028 selon le showrunner Brad Caleb Kane (Crystal Lake), qui a déclaré auprès de Deadline que la suite du show mettra en scène Grippe-Sou (Pennywise en VO) d'une façon encore jamais vue.
Cette saison 2 se déroulera durant la Grande Dépression, en 1935, et se penchera sur le massacre du Gang Bradley. Ce groupe de braqueurs de banque s'arrêtent à Derry pour acheter des munitions et se retrouvent alors confrontés à une horreur inimaginable.
1935. #ÇABienvenueADerry va revenir pour une saison 2 🎈 pic.twitter.com/3TcyyrDyMl
— HBO Max France (@HBOMaxFR) August 17, 2026
L'écriture de ces nouveaux épisodes est en cours, tout comme le casting de cette saison 2 qui arrivera donc prochainement sur HBO Max.

articles.title: Shopify Overexposed Scans GKE Ingresses and Cloud Run for Exposure
articles.text:
Shopify has introduced Overexposed. This internal scanner locates Kubernetes Ingresses on GKE and Cloud Run services. It checks for those that are accessible from the internet without authentication. After a first version based on repository config files produced false alarms and blind spots, the team rebuilt it on GCP Cloud Asset Inventory and an anonymous HTTP probe. In just a few weeks of tuning, this reduced inconclusive Ingress verdicts by around 80%.
The original scanner checked the infrastructure repository for Ingresses. It focused on public hostnames without authentication settings and then probed them. Shopify says this failed in three ways. Teams that configured proxy authentication annotations directly triggered false positives. Admission controllers that rewrite settings at admission time, but do not run in every cluster, meant a correct-looking config could have no effect. Ingresses created by other repositories or platform tooling were never seen. The authors summarize the lesson as: the repository shows intent; the cluster shows what is enforced.
The current version follows a schedule. It queries Cloud Asset Inventory. This inventory includes Ingresses accepted by GKE after admission, along with Cloud Run services and load balancers. A second search retrieves access policies without needing cluster credentials. The inventory also surfaced Cloud Run services in projects the first scanner had never covered.
Each candidate then receives a single anonymous request. The scanner sends HEAD first, falls back to GET, follows at most three redirects and checks each one. It also tests path variations such as /ADMIN, since path rules can be case-sensitive. Results map to six verdicts: exposed, expected, protected, not found, unreachable and inconclusive. "Expected" applies when an endpoint is open but matches a reviewed, in-code allowlist entry by exact host and path. Allowlisted endpoints are still probed on every run, and an entry that turns out to be protected or gone is flagged as stale.
Shopify stresses that status codes are context-dependent. A 404 behind an Ingress means the proxy answered and the path is missing. On Cloud Run, Google's front end can return a 404 before the application runs, so the scanner classifies it as inconclusive. A 403 is also not treated as proof of protection. For Cloud Run, the scanner distinguishes ingress settings from IAM: a service is public only if allUsers holds the invoker role or the invoker check is disabled. Services behind a load balancer use a URL map. This map decides which backend handles each path. It also shows where authentication, like Identity-Aware Proxy, is required.
In early runs, roughly three in four results were inconclusive in one July run. The team grouped results by reason, added verdicts where evidence supported them, and replayed rule changes against saved scan results before shipping. Uncertain evidence stays inconclusive rather than defaulting to protected. The scanner stores verdicts, reasons and team ownership, but not response bodies or credentials.
Because the scanner makes outbound requests to arbitrary hostnames, Shopify hardened it against SSRF. It validates every IP returned by DNS, rejects private and loopback addresses, connects directly to the checked IP to prevent DNS rebinding, and repeats checks on each redirect. The authors recommend also restricting the scanner's network egress, including cloud metadata endpoints.
The team built Overexposed with AI coding agents and AI code review. To catch tests that pass while checking the wrong thing, they apply mutation testing to security guards and keep one canary target per verdict.
Shopify’s experience illustrates a split that applies to exposure scanning in general. Rule-based checks, such as Trend Micro’s Cloud Run rule, look for allUsers bindings. This is affordable and easily integrable into CI. This tool report intent, not enforcement, so it miss resources created outside the repository and settings that an admission controller later rewrites.
Inventory-based approaches, such as Cartography and the Cloud Asset Inventory queries behind Shopify’s Overexposed, start from what the cloud actually runs, which closes those blind spots. Cartography still derives an exposed_internet flag from configuration, so it can’t confirm what an outsider sees. Overexposed adds an anonymous probe, an allowlist, and evidence-backed verdicts to the inventory. It sees uncertain evidence as inconclusive, not protected.
For teams creating something similar, use inventory as the main reference. Keep config analysis as an early signal in CI. Add a probe only if inventory can’t show whether access control works.

articles.title: Spotify plans to let users remix artists' songs using AI next year, but it'll cost up to $5 extra per month
articles.text:
A hot potato: Given the complaints about it being little more than slop – not to mention the legal troubles – you might think that music streaming services want to keep AI tracks to a minimum. Spotify, however, looks set to launch a previously announced paid service next year that lets subscribers remix songs using AI and upload them. Unsurprisingly, some artists aren't happy about this plan.
The Financial Times reports that Spotify aims to launch its AI-powered remixing service in the first quarter of 2027, meaning it could be unveiled around February's Grammy Awards.
The tool would cost an extra $4 to $5 per month on top of the standard subscription fee. It would allow users to create their own versions of songs on the platform. The FT gives the examples of transforming a folk song into a dance track or making one artist appear to cover another's music.
The remixes could then be uploaded to Spotify. Royalties from the fan-created tracks would flow back to artists, while the remixes would appear in playlists and plays would count towards the original songs in Spotify's charts.
Spotify is said to have already struck licensing deals with Universal Music Group, independent label group Merlin and French music company Believe for its AI remixing service. It is still negotiating with Sony Music and Warner Music.
Musicians who aren't happy about their work being remixed will be able to veto the use of their music, even if their record label has reached an agreement with Spotify.
The report adds that while some established older artists have been willing to go along with the plan, there are several unnamed major contemporary stars pushing back against the idea.
It seems Spotify isn't against AI music when it's being used on its own terms. In July, the company revealed it had removed 75 million AI-generated spam tracks in 2025, with a dedicated team tackling low-effort uploads, which it distinguishes from legitimate AI-assisted music.
Co-CEO Alex Norström defended the AI-remixing plans back in May, arguing that a licensed, controlled service was preferable to unauthorized AI music, while promising artist consent and compensation. But composer and artists' rights advocate Ed Newton-Rex warned that allowing fans to share their creations could flood Spotify with AI remixes, crowding out other songs and pressuring more musicians to participate.
There are also the problems of fraud and attribution. Deezer said last year that 70% of streams of AI-generated music were fraudulent. Sony, meanwhile, has reportedly developed technology to identify original music influencing AI tracks, potentially helping rights holders seek compensation when their work contributes to songs produced by generative systems.

articles.title: Enterprise AI strategy sees Cloudera bringing models to the data - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Enterprises bring AI to their data as privacy rules tighten and costs climb
Every enterprise AI strategy eventually comes down to the same question: Should proprietary data travel to the model, or should the model come to the data?
As privacy rules tighten and geopolitical risk rises, more organizations are choosing the second option. That is changing how data platform providers present themselves, and Cloudera Inc. has built its AI strategy around deployment flexibility. The company doesn’t ask customers to hand their data to an external AI service. Instead, it aims to run AI inside the environments where that data already lives, according to Wim Stoop (pictured), product director at Cloudera.
“Rather than saying, ‘Just give us all your data and we’ll in return provide you access to a model that’s then contextualized based on that data,’ we turn things around,” Stoop said. “We say, ‘We’ll bring AI to where the data is and where the data lives.'”
Stoop spoke with theCUBE’s Rebecca Knight and Paul Gillin at Cloudera EVOLVE26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how enterprises can bring AI to their data while maintaining control and managing costs. (* Disclosure below.)
Sovereignty moves to the center of enterprise AI strategy
Cloudera’s latest move in that direction is a partnership with Mistral AI SAS, which brings Mistral’s models into Cloudera’s data platform. For European customers in particular, the model maker’s local roots matter as much as its technology, Stoop noted.
“Certainly for us in Europe, having a French organization, a local company, that provides these models and provides the complete stack is very attractive for a lot of our customers,” Stoop said. “Mistral was a very easy choice for us to say, ‘Those are the ones that we’re going with.'”
AI is at the top of a maturity curve that starts with sovereign data, sovereign cloud and local operations, according to Stoop. Rules such as the European Union’s Digital Operational Resilience Act and the U.S. CLOUD Act are pushing organizations to prove they have control rather than simply claim it. But control alone won’t move AI out of the pilot phase. For many companies, the bigger obstacle in an enterprise AI strategy is the cost of running models at scale, because generating tokens takes a lot of hardware.
“If you use a public provider for that, the more you use your model, the more you get hit on cost,” Stoop said. “How do I get that high utilization of a good model inside my organization without being exposed to horrific costs? That, I think, is the biggest challenge that organizations are struggling with right now.”

articles.title: Chainalysis Discloses Data Breach Following AI-Driven Cyberattack
articles.text:
Blockchain analytics company Chainalysis has announced falling victim to an AI-driven cyberattack that resulted in a data breach.
“This month, Chainalysis detected an external actor using offensive agentic techniques to gain unauthorized access to Chainalysis systems and internal tools,” the company said.
The incident, it pointed out, is not related to the recent $6.36 billion Binance heist that was blamed on North Korean hackers.
According to Chainalysis, the attack did not result in the compromise of investigation content, transaction or query results, passwords in clear text, or other credentials and secrets.
“Some non-sensitive customer data, such as user IDs, full names, email addresses, and organization role labels for users provisioned on our platform were accessed, including such information relating to your organization and users,” Chainalysis said.
The company continues to investigate the full scope of the data breach and has not disclosed how many individuals were potentially affected.
“Our teams have been working around the clock to investigate unauthorized activity, patch vulnerabilities, and harden our systems,” it said.
Chainalysis noted that it has observed an industry-wide rise in AI-driven cyberattacks, as many other tech platforms have been hit in recent weeks.
The company has been working with external cybersecurity experts and LLMs to review its security posture and strengthen it against these evolving threats.
Because names and email addresses were compromised, it recommends that users watch for unexpected authentication prompts and password reset requests, and make sure they have MFA enabled.

articles.title: Swedish VC Creandum closes €668 million CVIII fund - its largest to date | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Stockholm-based venture capital firm Creandum has closed a €668 million ($750 million) fund, Creandum VIII, to back early-stage technology startups from pre-Seed to Series A.
The fund, its largest to date, will support approximately 30 investments over the next two years, with a particular interest in opportunities emerging from the rapid development of AI. It follows the firm’s €500 million Creandum VII fund, which closed in June 2024.
“We continue to focus on the early stage. 1 in 6 companies we’ve backed has become a $1B+ company. We have tripled our team in San Francisco in the past 12 months. We support founders globally from day 1,” said Peter Specht, Partner at Creandum, in a public statement.
Creandum VIII joins a series of European venture capital fundraising announcements in 2026.
London-based QuantumLight closed a €432 million second fund, Berlin-based Earlybird VC secured €360 million for Fund VIII, and Seedcamp raised €279 million across two investment vehicles.
In Sweden, Norrsken Evolve closed a €62 million pre-Seed fund, while Turbine Capital finalised a €54 million vehicle targeting Nordic DeepTech startups.
Across comparable announcements reported by EU-Startups this year, disclosed fund sizes total approximately €1.64 billion, rising to €2.31 billion when Creandum VIII is included.
EU-Startups previously covered Creandum’s €448 million sixth fund in 2022 and its role in leading AI software startup Lovable’s €14.3 million funding round in 2025.
“After almost a decade at Creandum, this is a proud and exciting moment. Grateful for the team and my partners, and just so excited about the incredible founders out there to back,” adds Peter.
Founded in 2003 by Staffan Helgesson, Creandum is a Swedish VC, with additional offices in London, Berlin and San Francisco. Before establishing Creandum, Helgesson founded Startupfactory, an investment firm focused on mobile internet businesses.
The new fund has secured commitments from approximately 30 institutional investors across Europe and the United States, including backing from university endowments, pension funds and charitable foundations.
The firm is known for its early investments in companies such as Spotify, Klarna, iZettle, Depop, Bolt and Trade Republic. More recently, its portfolio has expanded to include AI-powered software development startup Lovable, AI image-generation company Black Forest Labs, cloud infrastructure startup Modal and AI accounting platform Rillet.
Creandum VIII arrives at a time when AI is reshaping established technology markets and creating opportunities for new entrants. The firm believes that rapid changes in software development, enterprise technology and digital infrastructure are opening the door for startups to challenge existing products and business models.
In its announcement, Creandum reflected on previous periods of technological and economic uncertainty, including the aftermath of the dotcom crash, the 2008 financial crisis and the venture capital market correction of 2022.
“The pattern has repeated for over two decades: the biggest companies get founded when the ground is shifting. And the ground has never shifted like it is shifting today,” said the company.
Despite the growing importance of AI across its portfolio, Creandum intends to maintain its generalist investment strategy rather than limit the new fund to a particular technology or sector.
The fund also reflects Creandum’s expanding international ambitions. While the firm remains optimistic about Europe’s startup ecosystem, it is strengthening its presence in the United States to reach founders operating across different markets.
Having established a presence in San Francisco approximately a decade ago, Creandum has tripled the size of its West Coast team over the past two years. The expansion is intended to strengthen its investment activities and support European companies looking to enter the US market, alongside American startups seeking early-stage capital.
In its announcement, the Creandum team noted: “The best founders no longer belong to one geography, and neither do we.”
The firm also pointed to Europe’s universities, engineering talent and increasingly experienced founder community as reasons for its confidence in the region’s technology sector. It believes AI could enable European startups to compete more effectively with established global technology companies, particularly as access to advanced development tools becomes more widespread.
Internally, Creandum is adopting AI-based processes to improve how it identifies investment opportunities, evaluates companies and supports its portfolio. The firm describes these changes as part of a broader effort to adapt its investment operations to the technologies being developed by the startups it backs.

articles.title: Anthropic fatura R$ 91,8 bilhões em trimestre, mas prejuízo chega a R$ 124,2 bilhões
articles.text:
A Anthropic registrou receita de US$ 17 bilhões (aproximadamente R$ 91,8 bilhões) no terceiro trimestre de 2026, crescimento de 12 vezes em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado. Apesar da expansão acelerada, a desenvolvedora do Claude também contabilizou prejuízo líquido de US$ 23 bilhões (cerca de R$ 124,2 bilhões). Os números foram divulgados nesta segunda-feira (2), enquanto a companhia se prepara para possível abertura de capital ainda neste mês.
Os resultados representam atualização importante das informações financeiras apresentadas pela empresa em seu prospecto para uma oferta pública inicial de ações (IPO, na sigla em inglês). Até então, a maior parte dos dados disponíveis contemplava apenas os primeiros seis meses de 2026.
O desempenho do terceiro trimestre é especialmente relevante para investidores diante da velocidade de crescimento do mercado de inteligência artificial (IA). A avaliação de uma companhia desse setor depende não apenas da expansão da receita, mas também da capacidade de sustentar os investimentos necessários para desenvolver e operar seus modelos.
A possível abertura de capital da Anthropic poderia avaliar a empresa em até US$ 2 trilhões (aproximadamente R$ 10,8 trilhões). A oferta também poderia movimentar US$ 100 bilhões (cerca de R$ 540 bilhões), tornando-se uma das maiores operações desse tipo já realizadas.
Anthropic acumula prejuízo bilionário e compromete quase R$ 4,83 trilhões em infraestrutura
- Nos primeiros nove meses de 2026, a Anthropic acumulou receita de US$ 33 bilhões (aproximadamente R$ 178,2 bilhões) e prejuízo líquido de US$ 104 bilhões (cerca de R$ 561,6 bilhões);
- O resultado negativo, entretanto, foi influenciado principalmente por um lançamento contábil extraordinário de US$ 94 bilhões (R$ 507,6 bilhões), relacionado a notas conversíveis. Esse tipo de instrumento financeiro funciona como uma dívida que pode ser transformada em participação acionária posteriormente;
- Quando considerados indicadores que excluem determinados custos, o prejuízo operacional da empresa foi bem menor: quase US$ 1,3 bilhão (aproximadamente R$ 7 bilhões) no período;
- Outro número que chama atenção é o volume de compromissos financeiros assumidos pela companhia. Até o fim de setembro, a Anthropic havia contratado aproximadamente US$ 895 bilhões (R$ 4,83 trilhões) em obrigações relacionadas a data centers, chips e capacidade computacional;
- Desse total, quase US$ 70 bilhões (R$ 378 bilhões) vencem nos próximos 12 meses. Outros US$ 448 bilhões (R$ 2,42 trilhões) deverão ser pagos até o fim de 2030;
- A companhia informou ainda que possuía US$ 146,6 bilhões (aproximadamente R$ 791,6 bilhões) em dinheiro e investimentos de alta liquidez ao final do terceiro trimestre.
Crescimento da receita começa a desacelerar
Embora os números trimestrais tenham superado ligeiramente as projeções anteriormente apresentadas a investidores, o ritmo de expansão da Anthropic mostra sinais de desaceleração.
A receita cresceu 47% em relação ao segundo trimestre, resultado um pouco superior aos 45% que haviam sido antecipados em apresentação privada da empresa.
O avanço, entretanto, ficou distante dos 144% de crescimento registrados entre o primeiro e o segundo trimestre.
A desaceleração não significa necessariamente perda de força comercial, mas reforça as dúvidas sobre a capacidade da companhia de transformar sua expansão em resultados financeiros sustentáveis.
“Ela é eficiente, mas, à medida que constrói sua própria infraestrutura, o dinheiro vai começar a escorrer”, afirmou Brandon Ross, analista da LightShed Partners, ao comentar os investimentos da empresa ao The New York Times.
A preocupação não é exclusiva da Anthropic. Grandes empresas de tecnologia vêm ampliando seus gastos com infraestrutura de IA e recorrendo cada vez mais ao mercado de dívida para financiar projetos. Caso a demanda por IA fique abaixo das expectativas, esses compromissos podem aumentar a pressão sobre os resultados.
Leia mais:
- Com IPO, Anthropic terá de provar que consegue lucrar, dizem especialistas
- Por que a Anthropic alerta sobre riscos que ela mesma pode criar
- Gastos com IA acendem alerta financeiro para Meta e Anthropic
IPO também deverá incluir investidores individuais
A Anthropic confirmou que pretende reservar ações para investidores individuais em sua oferta pública, embora não tenha informado qual será a proporção destinada a esse grupo.
A decisão segue estratégia semelhante à adotada pela SpaceX em sua abertura de capital em junho, quando investidores de varejo representaram parcela significativa da operação.
Se concretizada, a oferta da Anthropic será a segunda grande abertura de capital do ano, depois da operação da empresa de Elon Musk. A OpenAI, responsável pelo ChatGPT, também trabalha com a possibilidade de uma oferta pública em 2027, com avaliação que poderia superar US$ 1 trilhão.
O movimento acontece em um momento de maior cautela dos mercados em relação aos investimentos bilionários em IA. Na semana passada, ações de empresas de tecnologia sofreram uma forte onda de vendas, em meio a questionamentos sobre a sustentabilidade dos gastos do setor.
Anthropic restringe uso do Claude Code para recriar videogames existentes
Em paralelo à preparação para sua abertura de capital, a Anthropic também reforçou as restrições de uso de suas ferramentas de IA. A empresa atualizou as instruções do Claude Code para impedir que a ferramenta seja utilizada na reprodução de videogames específicos já existentes.
A mudança foi identificada no prompt de sistema do Claude Code, na versão Opus 5.5. As novas orientações direcionam o modelo a desenvolver jogos originais, produções inspiradas em gêneros e projetos baseados em designs e recursos fornecidos pelos próprios usuários.
A restrição busca evitar que a IA seja utilizada para reproduzir diretamente jogos protegidos por propriedade intelectual, mesmo quando o usuário tenta apresentar a cópia como criação original.
Addy Osmani, representante da Anthropic, confirmou ao The Verge a atualização e explicou que a utilização do Claude para infringir direitos de propriedade intelectual contraria as políticas da empresa.
A companhia, entretanto, não pretende impedir a criação de jogos com IA. Projetos originais e desenvolvidos a partir de ideias e recursos próprios dos usuários continuam permitidos.
Segundo Osmani, a Anthropic pretende continuar ajustando as instruções para encontrar equilíbrio entre a proteção da propriedade intelectual e a liberdade de criação dos usuários.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Adivinha? Os preços do Raspberry Pi aumentaram de novo • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Adivinha? Os preços do Raspberry Pi aumentaram de novo
Modelos Raspberry Pi 5 e Compute Module 5 com 16 GB de RAM agora custam de US$ 40 a US$ 80 a mais.
O mês de novembro começou com uma péssima notícia para indivíduos ou organizações que planejam adquirir placas Raspberry Pi: as versões com 16 GB de RAM do Raspberry Pi 5 e do Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 acabaram de ficar mais caras, com reajustes de até US$ 80. Parece, mas essa não é uma notícia repetida.
Estamos falando do quinto reajuste de preços aplicado em produtos da linha Raspberry Pi desde dezembro de 2025. É verdade que os aumentos foram direcionados apenas a produtos específicos em cada rodada. Mesmo assim, esse movimento faz as placas perderem, cada vez mais, o apelo do custo-benefício.
A decisão mais recente fez o Raspberry Pi 5 de 16 GB passar de US$ 305 para US$ 385 (R$ 2.094 na conversão direta). Para você ter ideia do que isso significa, em 2025, o mesmo modelo era comercializado oficialmente por US$ 120. A placa teve aumento de preços em dezembro de 2025, em fevereiro e abril de 2026, e agora em novembro.
Já a variante de 16 GB do Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 teve um reajuste menor, mas ainda expressivo, de US$ 40. Note, porém, que os preços dessas placas variam de acordo com outras características escolhidas, como capacidade de armazenamento e presença ou não de conectividade Wi-Fi.
A essa altura, provavelmente você já sabe o motivo, mas não custa confirmar: a causa está no cenário de escassez de memória RAM. O CEO da Raspberry Pi comenta:
Infelizmente, a falta de fornecimento alternativo para DRAM de 16 GB, agravada pela escassez contínua de outros componentes, significa que agora precisamos fazer novos aumentos de preços em alguns de nossos produtos de maior densidade.

articles.title: In one of the largest deals in tech history, Marvell buys Lumentum for $115B | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Custom chip designer Marvell has signed a deal to acquire optical chip and networking equipment maker Lumentum in an all-stock deal with an enterprise value of $115 billion (including debt) and an equity value of about $80 billion. Marvell will provide 4.5 shares of its common stock for each share of Lumentum.
This makes the deal one of the biggest acquisitions in tech history. It compares to Microsoft buying Activision Blizzard for $68.7 billion in 2022 and Dell buying EMC for $67 billion in 2016.
Interestingly, the two companies have one major shareholder in common: Nvidia. In March, as part of a multi-year agreement to purchase Lumentum’s advanced laser components, the GPU giant invested $2 billion to support Lumentum’s R&D efforts and fab expansion. Later that same month, Marvell announced that Nvidia invested $2 billion in an effort to beef up Marvell’s optical networking and chips portfolio.
With Lumentum, Marvell says it will become a leader in AI connectivity, with products that range from chips to data centers. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of calendar year 2028, should both companies’ shareholders, and regulators, agree.

articles.title: Coming in 2027: Apple’s $1,000 home robot for FaceTime and switching on lights
articles.text:
Apple’s new CEO, John Ternus, is apparently pushing the tech company’s development of household robots—and the first to debut may be a home robot designed to autonomously roam around while supporting FaceTime calls and switching lights on whenever a person enters the room.
People who worked on Apple’s robotic projects told The Information that the AI-driven home robot, code-named J595, could be named HomeView Ultra in line with Apple’s new HomeView stationary smart display. The company is reportedly aiming to launch the robotic product with a possible price tag of $1,000 or more by 2027, although development delays may push that back to 2028.
The earliest prototypes of the home robot first came out in 2018 and received approval from former Apple CEO Tim Cook to continue the project. The Information describes Apple’s engineers as trying to give the robot more capabilities beyond being a “fancy way to make FaceTime calls” in order to justify a high price tag, even as the team has spent years refining the software and incorporating more AI technologies.
However, the robot’s few reported features seem underwhelming so far when compared with existing smart home devices and systems, or even a run-of-the-mill robot vacuum with a clearer use case for households. Is there a market for a smart home device costing more than $1,000 that moves around while hosting FaceTime calls, automatically handling room lights, and occasionally ordering the family cat to get off the dining table?

articles.title: Virgin Media O2 reportedly set to cut thousands of jobs in a bid to save costs
articles.text:
Virgin Media O2 reportedly set to cut thousands of jobs in a bid to save costs
VMO2 could lay off up to 25% of its workers, reports claim
- Virgin Media O2 currently employs around 16,000 workers
- However reports claim 25% could be set for redundancy
- Non-customer-facing roles will likely be heaviest hit
Sky News has reported that Virgin Media O2 (VMO2) plans to cut an unconfirmed number of jobs – understood to be in the thousands – amid ongoing cost reduction efforts and a bid to get a grip on company debt.
Though the number of workers said to be impacted is not yet known, the company currently employs around 16,000 workers, so 'thousands' would represent a significant chunk of its workforce.
VMO2 looks to be one of the latest companies in a long list to be flattening its hierarchy, with changes to management reportedly underway.
VMO2 job cuts look to be around the corner
Crucially, Sky News reports that non-customer-facing roles will likely be heaviest hit. The firm's customer services typically perform well, it seems, with Virgin Media reporting the fewest number of complaints compared with competitors (via Ofcom) on the broadband front. Though O2 sits somewhere toward the top on the mobile front, beating only Sky Mobile (which also uses the O2 network).
An unnamed insider believes as many as 4,000 jobs could be at risk, representing 25% of VMO2's entire workforce.
It's believed that the company could share precise numbers and details as part of its Q3 earning call on November 3. Overall company revenue dropped 7.9% last quarter.
But VMO2's biggest issue is likely debt. Last quarter, it reported a total net debt equivalent to 5.89x annualized adjusted EBITDA.

But VMO2 isn't the only telecoms giant adjusting its workforce in response to financial pressures – VodafoneThree also confirmed plans to cut 1,200 jobs in July 2026, though these were Europe-wide.
VMO2 declined to comment.
