articles.title: Su lavadora Samsung quedó abandonada y una IA encontró la forma de salvarla
articles.text:
Una de las cosas que más odiamos de vivir en esta era es que todos los productos tecnológicos tienen fecha de caducidad. Un ordenador, el móvil o cualquier otro dispositivo conectado dejará de recibir soporte en algún momento, lo que significa que ya no podrás instalar actualizaciones o usar ciertas funciones. La buena noticia es que la IA está acabando con la obsolescencia programada, como ocurrió con esta lavadora Samsung, que recuperó una de sus características clave.
Un usuario consiguió recuperar las funciones inteligentes de una lavadora con ayuda de Claude. En una publicación de Reddit, el propietario reveló que usó la IA de Anthropic para analizar el problema y encontrar una forma de devolver las capacidades conectadas que se perdieron cuando acabó el soporte oficial. La lavadora tenía más de 10 años de antigüedad y contaba con Wi-Fi, lo que le permitía sincronizarse con la app de Smart Things para controlarla por internet.
“Pagué una fortuna en aquel momento solo para conseguir todas esas nuevas funcionalidades”, dijo McArhony en Reddit. “Pantalla táctil, dosis automática (que sorprendentemente no es lo habitual), control inteligente por internet... era el Rolls Royce para los frikis de entonces”, añadió. Debido a que ya utilizaba otros productos de Samsung en el ecosistema, el usuario tomó la decisión de devolverle la vida a su lavadora usando la IA.
Tras dos horas de trabajo guiado por la IA, el propietario restauró las funciones de control inteligente y recuperó la comunicación entre la lavadora y la secadora. Claude consiguió reactivar todas las características y la lavadora funciona como nueva, con la gestión de programas, temperatura y velocidad de giro desde SmartThings.
La IA está ayudando a recuperar el control de dispositivos antiguos
El experimento de la lavadora de Samsung se suma a una oleada de proyectos en los que usuarios aprovechan a Claude y ChatGPT para modificar o restaurar dispositivos. Entre los más llamativos están aquellos que eliminan todo el bloatware, anuncios y el rastreo de los televisores. Tanto Samsung como LG han inyectado spyware en sus dispositivos y los usuarios están encontrando formas de revertirlo con ayuda de la IA.
Esto último ha generado controversia, ya que OpenAI y Anthropic están suspendiendo las cuentas de estos usuarios debido a una violación de sus términos de uso. Uno de los investigadores que vulneró Tizen en su televisor Samsung perdió acceso a su cuenta y todos sus créditos, ya que OpenAI dijo que incurrió en prácticas de abuso cibernético al analizar las vulnerabilidades y desarrollar exploits para sortear la seguridad de su Smart TV.
En el caso de la lavadora de Samsung, el autor publicó en GitHub una herramienta llamada smartthings-samsung-drc-washer, la cual permite integrar modelos antiguos en SmartThings mediante un controlador Edge. Entre las funciones disponibles se incluyen la visualización del estado de la lavadora, tiempo restante, inicio y pausa de ciclos, así como diferentes opciones de configuración. El objetivo del proyecto es mantener funcionando los modelos que Samsung dejó fuera de su ecosistema actual tras cumplir el tiempo de soporte.

articles.title: BMW is taking on Tesla’s FSD with urban driver assist starting in 2027
articles.text:
BMW says that it will expand its navigation-guided, partially automated driving capabilities into urban environments starting in 2027, launching first in Germany with other markets to follow.
BMW is taking on Tesla’s FSD with urban driver assist starting in 2027
BMW will bring navigation-guided city driving to select models via software updates in 2027, taking on Tesla’s FSD while facing growing scrutiny over Level 2 driver safety.
The new system can help steer, speed up, and slow down the vehicle on both highways and city streets using its built-in GPS navigation. While driving in town, it can assist with changing lanes, making turns, yielding to other cars, and driving through roundabouts. But as a Level 2 driver assist system, it still requires drivers to keep their eyes on the road and stay ready to take over at any moment. On the highway, BMW will allow drivers to remove their hands from the steering wheel — but on local roads, they’ll need to keep their hands on the wheel.
BMW is the latest automaker to commit to releasing a partially autonomous city driving feature to its customers, as the industry races to keep up with Tesla and its Full Self-Driving (FSD) system. BMW, in particular, recently introduced its next-generation Neue Klasse platform, which includes a driver assist system partly powered by Qualcomm’s technology. And with hands-free highway driving now widely available in many mass-market vehicles, the next frontier is a safe and capable city driving feature that rivals FSD.
BMW says its system works cooperatively with drivers rather than fighting their control, which means they can steer, brake, or speed up at any point to adjust their driving without shutting the system off. At the same time, the car shows what it sees and what the assistance system is doing right in your line of sight through the heads-up display and in a clear 3D map on the main dashboard screen.
The necessary cameras and sensors already come built into models like BMW’s 3 Series, 7 Series, X5, iX3, and iX4. BMW can activate the feature through an over-the-air software update. The system follows new European safety rules that let cars suggest and make automated driving moves on city streets for the first time. BMW says that outside experts have already road-tested the setup and confirmed it meets the technical standards, with final official government approval expected in early 2027.
With more cars equipped with partial automation hitting the road, safety researchers are growing increasingly worried about driver attention and the potential for these systems to cause crashes. There is compelling evidence that, regardless of the company, most driver-assist systems are less safe than normal human driving. Drivers tend to develop an overreliance on these systems to drive the car for them — even after a short period of use. And when it’s time to take back control of the vehicle, their reaction times are slower than what’s considered safe.
BMW is entering risky territory with the adoption of a Level 2 driving feature. Much like Tesla, the company is emphasizing that drivers remain responsible for the vehicle even while using the partially autonomous system in urban environments. Tesla does the same for its FSD feature, but some customers have successfully argued in court that the company bears some responsibility for crashes when they occur.

articles.title: Critical Langflow Flaws Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code on Servers
articles.text:
Two critical flaws in Langflow could let a remote attacker with no account bypass authentication or run arbitrary code, IBM said last week.
Langflow is an open-source tool for building AI agents and workflows, and its vulnerability reports go to IBM. Every release from 1.0.0 through 1.12.8 has the flaws, and the only fix is version 1.13.0.
Neither flaw is in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, as of the catalog's October 30 update. Six other Langflow flaws are listed there, most recently CVE-2026-9198, which was added in August.
The four Langflow flaws in IBM's bulletin, first published on October 28 and updated the next day, are:
| CVE | CVSS score (IBM) | Account needed | What IBM says it could allow | 
|---|---|---|---|
| CVE-2026-93680 | 9.8 (Critical) | No | Bypassing security restrictions, because of improper authentication | 
| CVE-2026-110186 | 9.8 (Critical) | No | Running arbitrary code, because of improper control of code generation | 
| CVE-2026-110193 | 8.8 (High) | Yes, a low-privileged account | Making the Agentic Assistant generate or submit component code that runs operating system commands on the server | 
| CVE-2026-110192 | 6.5 (Medium) | Yes | Getting sensitive information from insufficiently protected credentials | 
One of the flaws is "unauthenticated remote code execution exploitable through model context protocol tool enumeration," according to IBM. Through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), Langflow can offer its flows as tools to AI apps that support MCP.
A module in the public Metasploit Framework already cites CVE-2026-93680, the authentication bypass. It connects to a Langflow server's MCP endpoint without credentials, starts a session, and lists the tools the server offers. It does not run code or commands on the server.
Its author lists Langflow 1.5.0 through 1.11.4 as affected, a narrower range than IBM's.
When automatic login is enabled, Langflow logs users in as superusers without prompting them to sign in. The setting LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN is enabled by default in Langflow 1.12.8. Its code description warns that it "bypasses authentication and should only be used in development environments."
The module was tested on Langflow 1.8.4 with automatic login turned on. Another of the four flaws is "an incomplete remediation of an auto-login security control," according to IBM. The bulletin does not say whether servers with automatic login turned off are vulnerable.
Upgrading to 1.13.0
Langflow 1.13.0 came out on October 22. Version 1.12.8, released the same day, still has the flaws, and PyPI lists no later 1.12 release as of November 2. IBM offers no workaround for servers that cannot upgrade yet.
Langflow 1.13 turns automatic login off by default. To upgrade:
- Back up the database, the secret key and uploaded files.
- If the server uses automatic login, prepare the existing account for password sign-in, as Langflow's upgrade guidance describes.
- Upgrade the Python package with pip install --upgrade "langflow==1.13.0". For Docker, move to the langflowai/langflow:1.13.0 image and keep the deployment's persistent data.
- If you cannot sign in after upgrading, follow the recovery steps that the same guidance links to. Do not delete or reinstall Langflow to get access back, because Langflow's documentation warns this can permanently remove your flows.
On October 29, IBM also published CVE records for 29 other Langflow flaws and named versions 1.12.4 and 1.12.5 as their fixes. One of them, CVE-2026-104339, could also let an attacker with no account run arbitrary code, and IBM rates it 9.8. None of the 33 records, these four included, lists 1.13.0 as affected.

articles.title: Macronix Expands Flash Portfolio - EE Times
articles.text:
AI-driven high-bandwidth memory demand is reshaping memory markets, boosting mature flash products as Macronix expands its portfolio for AI workloads.
The artificial intelligence (AI) boom continues to rewrite the rules of the game in the memory industry. Over the past year, major memory makers such as Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron have continued shifting capacity and capital spending toward high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and advanced server memory, crowding out mature and specialty products. At the same time, the growing scale of AI models and inference workloads is expanding memory requirements beyond capacity and bandwidth to data tiering, movement and processing, further reshaping the architecture of the overall memory system.
Martin Lin, director of marketing at Macronix International, said in an interview with EE Times Taiwan that the changes brought by AI are not simply about increasing memory demand, but that “the entire memory architecture is changing.” From the growing use of NOR flash in AI servers and the search for more capacity- and cost-efficient memory tiers beyond HBM, to the growing importance of key value (KV) cache in inference performance, memory is gradually evolving from a conventional data-storage component into a core element affecting AI system performance, cost and architectural design.
Against what Macronix describes as the most significant structural transformation in the memory industry in decades, the company is expanding its NOR flash, NAND and eMMC portfolios toward higher densities, lower power consumption and greater reliability. Macronix has also raised its capital expenditure for 2026 to NT$37.8 billion to expand its 12-inch wafer capacity and meet the growing demand for 3D NOR, NAND, eMMC and other products.
MemFlation Driving Up Value of Specialty Flash
The latest changes in the memory market differ from previous recoveries driven primarily by inventory cycles. The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure is fueling demand for HBM and advanced memory, with capacity booked well into 2027. NAND is also being repriced as demand for AI data centers and enterprise solid-state drives (SSDs) increases.
At the same time, major memory makers continue to adjust their product mixes, squeezing mature-process capacity and reducing supply flexibility for products such as NOR flash, SLC NAND and eMMC.
The surge in AI and HBM demand has rapidly increased the value of the memory market. Market data indicates that the market surpassed $20 billion in 2025 and is expected to approach $70 billion in 2026. As mature-process capacity remains constrained, market growth is increasingly being driven by pricing rather than shipment volumes, creating what Macronix calls “memory inflation,” or “MemFlation.”
Prices for NOR flash, SLC NAND and eMMC are expected to rise further in the third and fourth quarters of 2026 before stabilizing at elevated levels. Even as new capacity comes online, equipment installation, process qualification and yield ramp-up can take two to three years, if not longer, making it difficult to close the supply gap in the short term. As AI demand continues to crowd out mature-process capacity, supply constraints and pricing pressures in the automotive market are expected to become more pronounced starting in 2027.
Against this backdrop, Macronix expects the market for NOR flash, SLC NAND and low-capacity eMMC (≤32GB) to expand significantly, reaching a combined value of around $24 billion in 2026. Growth is being driven by higher shipments, as well as price increases resulting from constrained supply. NOR flash is facing relatively moderate price increases, supported by previous capacity investments, while SLC NAND and eMMC are under greater supply pressure.
This shift in the supply structure is also directly reflected in demand for NOR flash in AI servers. These flash devices are primarily used for boot-up, firmware, system control and security functions. Lin noted that conventional servers typically required only about three to five flash devices, whereas AI servers use significantly more as the number of baseboard management controllers (BMCs), network switches and other control components increases. As a result, flash consumption per rack has risen rapidly.
“The previous-generation rack had around 600 to 800 devices. The latest generation now has more than 1,000,” Lin said.
Beyond HBM: New Memory Tiers Emerge
If the increased use of NOR flash in AI servers represents a change in memory demand in terms of “quantity,” the search for new memory tiers beyond HBM represents a deeper architectural shift.
AI training and inference rely heavily on HBM to provide the high bandwidth required by GPUs. But as models continue to grow, HBM capacity and cost are increasingly becoming limiting factors.
Lin said that “only HBM is fast enough” today, but increasing capacity and stacking more HBM layers also drive up costs, prompting the industry to seek memory tiers beyond HBM that can offer greater capacity and better cost efficiency.
High-bandwidth flash (HBF) has emerged as one such approach. Based on 3D NAND and combined with high-speed interfaces and high-density packaging, HBF seeks to strike a balance between bandwidth, capacity and cost, allowing data that does not need to remain in HBM to be moved to higher-capacity, relatively lower-cost NAND flash. The industry is also exploring AI server architectures incorporating SSDs with a high level of input/output per second (IOPS), with low-latency SLC NAND flash playing a key role in handling the large volumes of random data accesses required by GPUs and improving GPU utilization.
Such tiered architectures are particularly important for AI inference. Large language models (LLMs) and agentic AI workloads need to continuously retain conversation, task and historical information, causing KV cache to grow continuously. Citing continuous AI conversations as an example, Lin said that if memory capacity is insufficient, “you have to discard the earlier information.”
Future AI systems can therefore organize data into different tiers according to data age, access frequency and latency requirements. The most frequently accessed and latency-sensitive data can remain in HBM, while larger volumes of data that do not require consistently high-speed access can be moved to flash, SSDs and other tiers.
Macronix presented its dual-tier SSD architecture at the recent Future Memory and Storage conference (FMS 2026) in the United States as a solution for KV cache offloading, further exploring how different memory and storage tiers can be used to distribute AI workloads.
Data Movement Becomes New Bottleneck
As the computing capabilities of AI accelerators continue to increase rapidly, system bottlenecks are gradually shifting from compute speed to whether data can be delivered in time. “The GPU is already fast enough, but now, memory is actually too slow,” Lin said. Repeatedly moving data among the CPU, GPU, HBM, DRAM and storage devices not only consumes bandwidth but also adds latency and power consumption, meaning that simply increasing processor speed may not effectively improve overall system performance. 
To reduce the cost of data movement, the industry is revisiting memory-centric AI and processing-in-memory (PIM) architectures, which bring some computation closer to memory and, in some cases, allow memory to perform simple operations before outputting the results, reducing data transfers back and forth.
“Memory-centric AI” is not a new concept. In fact, Macronix Chairman and CEO Miin Wu proposed the concept as early as 2019. Today, as AI models, datasets and inference workloads continue to grow rapidly, the concept is once again drawing attention from both industry and academia.
Lin believes that the next stage of AI performance gains will depend not only on faster GPUs but also on more efficient memory architectures. The focus of AI system development will extend beyond compute speed to questions of where the data is, how it is moved and when it is processed, making memory an increasingly important element of AI system architecture.
Expanding the Flash Portfolio: Targeting Density, Low Power and High Reliability
This architectural shift is also reflected in Macronix’s product strategy. In addition to increasing supplies of high-density NOR flash to meet demand from AI servers, Macronix is expanding its NAND and eMMC portfolios and advancing 3D NAND technology to extend its product mix across a broad range of capacities and applications.
Macronix currently has 48- and 96-layer 3D NAND products in mass production and is continuing to develop higher-layer-count technologies. NOR flash is moving toward higher density, lower power consumption and greater reliability, with the process technology progressing from 55nm to 42nm and 3D NOR also under development. While its high-density NOR flash is already used in AI servers, Macronix is expanding into high-reliability applications across automotive, communications, medical and aerospace markets. To address power requirements in AI, industrial and embedded systems, low-voltage flash is progressing from 3V and 1.8V toward 1.2V.
Looking toward 2027, Lin expects tight memory supply and demand conditions to remain difficult to ease in the short term. Even as new capacity gradually comes online, additional time will be required for process qualification and yield improvement. For Macronix, balancing demand from AI servers, supply gaps in mature flash products, and next-generation technology development will be a key focus for the next stage.
As AI continues to reshape memory architectures and product requirements, Macronix will showcase its latest nonvolatile memory technologies and application solutions at electronica 2026, which will take place November 10–13 in Munich, Germany. The solutions will include applications in automotive electronics and edge AI. Macronix will exhibit at Hall C5, Stand 279.

articles.title: Pour jouer à GTA VI, la manette filaire Nacon Revolution X Pro Xbox/PC est à moins de 20 € pour le Black Friday — Frandroid
articles.text:
Nacon est une marque française (cocorico) spécialisée dans les accessoires gaming et la Revolution X Pro est un modèle plutôt orienté compétition, mais qui peut très bien s’utiliser pour une petite partie casual. C’est une manette qui offre un haut niveau de personnalisation et de modularité et ça se voit sur son prix de lancement à l’époque : 109,90 euros. Récemment, elle était plutôt vendue 59,99 euros mais là pour le Black Friday chez Fnac, elle est affichée à 19,99 euros, soit 81% de réduction par rapport à son prix de départ. Si vous jouez principalement sur PC ou sur Xbox, c’est un accessoire plutôt pratique.
Les atouts de la Nacon Revolution X Pro
- Son ergonomie repensée, plus large que la manette officielle
- Les joysticks vifs, précis et dotés d’une excellente résistance
- La présence de quatre boutons configurables à l’arrière pour les raccourcis
Lancée à 109,90 euros, la Nacon Revolution X Pro se monnaye plutôt autour de 59,99 euros ces derniers temps. Mais là, pour le Black Friday, vous avez une opportunité de la commander pour 19,99 euros sur Fnac.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant le Nacon Revolution X Pro Controller. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Le 19 novembre, Vice City vous attend. Et votre PS5 ? Avec Next Mobiles, pas besoin de payer 600 € d’un coup, louez-la sur la durée que vous souhaitez, dès 16,90 €/mois.
Il n’y a pas d’offres pour le moment, découvrez :
Un design ergonomique avec des joysticks précis
Sur le plan de la prise en main, la Revolution X Pro fait un choix audacieux en se révélant plus large que la manette officielle Xbox. Cette largeur supplémentaire permet d’excentrer les gâchettes et d’offrir une position plus naturelle et reposante pour les mains. Un bon point pour le confort, même si la qualité des matériaux trahit un peu les ambitions initiales du produit. Le revêtement global renvoie une sensation plastique assez basique, qui détonne par rapport au segment « Pro ». Malgré la possibilité d’ajouter des poids à l’intérieur des poignées, elle reste légère : 264 g sur la balance dans sa configuration la plus lourde, contre 290 g pour la manette Xbox standard.
Les joysticks sont un vrai atout pour cette manette : selon notre test, ils sont vifs, agiles et opposent ce qu’il faut de résistance pour conserver un maintien précis sans forcer. La croix directionnelle abandonne quant à elle le format en cuvette de celle de Microsoft pour revenir à une architecture classique pour un gain de précision appréciable, notamment pour les jeux de combat ou de plateforme. L’expérience se corse au niveau des gâchettes, qui manquent de résistance et qui rendant la jauge de pression difficile à évaluer. Et elles émettent un clic assez bruyant en bout de course.
Une personnalisation logicielle exemplaire
Les boutons d’action A/B/X/Y souffrent d’une course jugée un peu trop rapide, tandis que les boutons de tranches (LB/RB) sauvent la mise avec une activation réactive, couronnée par un clic très satisfaisant. Enfin, les quatre boutons supplémentaires situés à l’arrière sont utiles, bien que leur placement très sensible puisse occasionner quelques appuis accidentels lors des parties les plus tendues. Si le hardware montre quelques faiblesses, le logiciel Revolution-X est bien réussi. Il est simple, intuitif et complet, ce qui permet de la reconfigurer entièrement en quelques minutes.
Vous pouvez quasiment tout faire, comme ajuster la courbe de réponse des joysticks, modifier les zones mortes des gâchettes ou intervertir l’intégralité des boutons. Vous pouvez même enregistrer des profils distincts dans la mémoire de l’appareil selon le type de jeu. Même l’audio s’en sort bien puisqu’en branchant un casque filaire sur le port jack 3,5 mm, le logiciel débloquer un égaliseur, un réducteur de bruits parasites pour le microphone et surtout un traitement audio 3D. Un atout quand il s’agit de localiser des ennemis au son de leurs pas, comme dans Counter-Strike 2 par exemple.

articles.title: Acheter du matériel pour l’IA sur Amazon ? Il tente quatre commandes, son compte est banni
articles.text:
Des acheteurs de cartes graphiques et de machines dédiées à l’IA dénoncent des annulations en série sur le site marchand. L’un d’eux assure même avoir perdu son compte après une vérification alors que Tim Sweeney, le patron d’Epic Games, signale lui aussi des blocages.
Il attendait quatre ordinateurs NVIDIA, mais dit avoir reçu un avis de fermeture de son compte Amazon. L’utilisateur @nicksaraev explique sur X que ses commandes de DGX Spark, des machines destinées à faire tourner des modèles d’IA chez soi, ont toutes été annulées. Son récit relayé par Wccftech fait écho à celui de Tim Sweeney, le patron d’Epic Games, qui évoque ses propres déboires après avoir tenté d’acheter deux cartes graphiques sur Amazon.
Quatre commandes et une vérification qui finit mal
Le 1er novembre, @nicksaraev dit avoir passé quatre commandes distinctes de DGX Spark, toutes annulées par Amazon. Il assure n’avoir jamais rencontré ce problème auparavant et décrit des demandes de vérification aux explications particulièrement floues.
L’affaire aurait ensuite pris une autre tournure. Le client a partagé un e-mail dans lequel Amazon indique avoir examiné son dossier et décidé de bannir son compte. Le message ne précise pas ce qui lui est reproché. Pour l’acheteur, le problème dépasse donc désormais la livraison de ses machines puisqu’il doit aussi comprendre pourquoi le distributeur lui refuse l’accès à son compte.
Tim Sweeney signale des annulations jusque sur ses achats habituels
Le dirigeant d’Epic Games affirme que son compte est toujours ouvert, mais que ses deux cartes graphiques NVIDIA ne lui ont pas été livrées. Selon son témoignage, après cet achat, même ses commandes habituelles auraient été acceptées, puis annulées juste avant la livraison.
Ces blocages pourraient venir d’un dysfonctionnement ou d’un dispositif destiné à freiner les achats des scalpers, ces personnes peu scrupuleuses qui profitent de la rareté de certains produits pour les revendre plus cher, dans un marché déjà marqué par la hausse du prix de la RAM. Rien ne permet toutefois d’établir leur origine ni de savoir si les deux clients ont été confrontés au même problème.
Si une commande est annulée sans explication, mieux vaut demander au service client ce qui bloque avant de multiplier les tentatives. Pour s’équiper en grande quantité de matériel IA (cartes graphiques, ordis, mémoire vive, etc.), répartir ses achats entre plusieurs revendeurs permet aussi de limiter la dépendance à un seul fournisseur. Enfin, espacer ses achats peut aussi sembler être une bonne précaution, mais rien ne permet ici d’affirmer que cela évitera les annulations chez Amazon.
Source : Wccftech

articles.title: Over 1,000 GitLab servers vulnerable to ongoing RCE attacks
articles.text:
Over 1,000 Internet-exposed GitLab servers are still unpatched against a maximum-severity flaw actively exploited in remote code execution attacks.
Tracked as CVE-2026-97229, this vulnerability stems from an integer overflow weakness and was discovered in the CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler, which parses and evaluates regular expressions in pipeline configuration files.
"GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient regular expression validation," the company explained on October 12 when it released security patches to address the security issue in GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE) versions 19.4.2, 19.3.5, and 19.2.8.
"These versions contain important bug and security fixes, and we strongly recommend that all self-managed GitLab installations be upgraded to one of these versions immediately. GitLab.com is already running the patched version. GitLab Dedicated customers do not need to take action," it added.
On Friday, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) confirmed that attackers have begun exploiting the flaw in the wild and added CVE-2026-97229 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, ordering federal agencies to secure their servers by Sunday.
Although GitLab released patches three weeks ago, threat watchdog Shadowserver revealed over the weekend that it tracks more than 1,000 unpatched GitLab servers exposed to ongoing attacks.
CVE-2026-97229 is the latest in a series of GitLab security issues addressed since the start of the year. In January, GitLab fixed a high-severity flaw (CVE-2026-0723) that lets attackers bypass two-factor authentication, and in September, a maximum-severity vulnerability (CVE-2026-85706) in the repository commits API that can be exploited to steal credentials and other secrets.
CISA also flagged CVE-2026-85706 as actively abused in the wild after cybersecurity firm watchTowr reported that attackers had already begun scanning for vulnerable GitLab servers.
Last month, it addressed another maximum-severity Regular Expression Compiler bug (CVE-2026-110264) that lets threat actors run arbitrary code on targeted instances.
"We are currently tracking over 1000 GitLab instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-97229 (on @CISACyber KEV) and over 11300 instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-110264 (out of around 39K GitLab instances we see daily)," Shadowserver said on Sunday.
Since November 2021, CISA has added six GitLab flaws to its catalog of actively exploited vulnerabilities, one of which has also been used in ransomware attacks.
GitLab says its DevSecOps platform has over 70 million registered users and is used by more than 50% of Fortune 100 companies worldwide.

articles.title: Pablo, un español trabajando en Noruega: “El salario en la construcción es de 6.200 euros y trabajamos de 8 a 16”
articles.text:
Un albañil español que trabaja en Noruega desde hace siete años cuenta cómo es el mercado allí. Pablo González explica en sus vídeos de redes sociales qué sueldo se cobra en construcción en Noruega. Los más destacables son los de 6.200 euros/mes brutos.
El sueldo base es por hora. Según Pablo, los mínimos para los especialistas son de 209 coronas/hora (aprox. 20 euros). En perfiles no especializados sería de 188 coronas (18 euros). Y para los que no tienen experiencia anterior, 196 (19 euros). Depende de si son de obra civil o edificación y de proyecto a proyecto.
Según Pablo, por norma general, la jornada completa es de 37,5 h/semana. De lunes a viernes suelen ser de 8:00 a 16:00. También se pueden trabajar horas extra (con un valor mucho mayor que la hora normal). Algunos trabajan más de lunes a jueves. Según él, existe un sistema “12-9” (12 días consecutivos trabajando y 9 días libres) que está muy extendido en el país.
El motivo de estos sueldos es que no hay mano de obra, según él: “Hay dinero, pero no hay mano de obra cualificada de nacionalidad noruega”. Por ello se recurre a los trabajadores extranjeros.
Del sueldo anunciado a los mínimos oficiales
Vamos a ver los números. Pablo da el sueldo de los puestos de mayor responsabilidad: 62.000 coronas/mes. Su conversión equivale a 10 coronas = 1 euro. El tipo de cambio de Norges Bank (banco central noruego) el 26 de octubre de 2026 es de 10,4545 coronas/euro. Con este tipo de cambio, las 62.000 coronas equivalen a unos 5.930 euros brutos. Es decir, 270 euros menos que los que declara Pablo.
Lo más importante es el sueldo mínimo por hora. Noruega no tiene un salario mínimo por ley que abarque a todos los sectores. Pero sí que en el sector de obras existe un salario mínimo, que es el que se aplica. Según la respuesta de la Inspección de Trabajo (Arbeidstilsynet) del 16 de marzo de 2026, el salario mínimo por hora en vigor desde el 15 de junio de 2025 es de 264,32 coronas para el fagarbeider (trabajador cualificado).
Los no cualificados sin experiencia en el sector tienen un salario mínimo de 239,61 coronas/hora. Este mismo perfil, pero con al menos 1 año de experiencia, tienen un salario mínimo de 249,00 coronas/hora. Esto es para cualquier persona que trabaje en una obra (sin importar la antigüedad).
A la misma cotización en euros (con el mismo tipo de cambio), esto supondría 25,28 euros/hora para el cualificado y 22,92 euros/hora para el no cualificado sin experiencia. Y 23,82 euros/hora para el no cualificado con un año. Los valores que declara Pablo (209, 188 o 196) están por debajo incluso del mínimo más bajo (239,61).
Existe un escalón adicional. La patronal NHO Byggenæringen y el sindicato Fellesforbundet han evitado en abril el paro mediante una mediación. Han llegado a un nuevo convenio de la construcción. Desde el 1 de abril de 2026, el salario mínimo para el fagarbeider es de 276,48 coronas/hora (unos 26,45 euros/hora). El aumento general es de 6,50 coronas/hora.
El neto y el contrato
También hay que tener en cuenta el neto. En otro caso de una pareja de españoles en Noruega que hemos contado, explicábamos que el sistema de retención de trabajadores extranjeros es voluntario (PAYE), con un tipo general del 25 %. Con algunas condiciones y excepciones. Si no tienes tarjeta de retención fiscal, el empleador te retiene un 50 % de tu salario (como anticipo).
Es importante recordar que todo trabajador debe tener contrato por escrito (firmado en un plazo máximo de 7 días desde el comienzo del mismo si es superior al mes). Para buscar ofertas tenemos EURES y el buscador de Nav (servicio público de empleo noruego) Arbeidsplassen. En este último podemos filtrar por idioma de trabajo (por ejemplo, inglés).
Con estos datos es poco lo que se puede sacar de un sueldo anunciado en un vídeo mensualmente. Sería interesante comparar el salario por hora del contrato con los salarios mínimos (264,32 coronas por ley -tabla marzo 2026- o 276,48 por convenio desde abril 2026). Además de la jornada acordada y de la retención correspondiente.

articles.title: La Fiat Grande Panda passe à 400 km d'autonomie sans faire exploser son prix
articles.text:
Une batterie de 53 kWh
La Fiat Grande Panda repose sur la plateforme Smart Car de Stellantis, destinée aux modèles électriques les plus abordables, en attendant les E-Car qui se placeront prochainement en dessous. Cette plateforme accueille plusieurs modèles, comme les Citroën ë-C3 et Fiat Grande Panda pour les citadines, mais aussi les Citroën ë-C3 Aircross et Opel Frontera pour les SUV.
Plusieurs batteries sont proposées, mais la Fiat Grande Panda utilisait pour l’instant seulement l’accumulateur LFP de 44 kWh, pour une autonomie de 327 km WLTP. Ce qui n’est plus suffisant pour séduire quand les Renault 5, Volkswagen ID. Polo et Cupra Raval proposent plus de 430 km.
Fiat annonce donc l’arrivée d’une batterie LFP de 53 kWh dans la Fiat Grande Panda, pour une autonomie atteignant désormais 400 km en cycle mixte WLTP. Cette batterie provient des versions à grande autonomie des Citroën ë-C3 Aircross et Opel Frontera.
Une voiture qui reste abordable
Malgré cette nouvelle batterie plus importante, qui offre une polyvalence renforcée à la Fiat Grande Panda, le prix n’explose pas ! Elle est proposée à partir de 25 900 euros et reste éligible au bonus écologique. À ce prix, il s’agit de la finition d’entrée de gamme Pop, qui comprend une climatisation, un compteur numérique ou encore des radars de recul, mais pas d’écran d’infodivertissement à bord. Tout passe par le téléphone du conducteur, qui est connecté à la voiture en NFC.
Concernant la recharge, elle accepte une puissance de 100 kW, ce qui lui permet de passer de 20 à 80 % en une trentaine de minutes. Le moteur ne gagne pas en puissance : il s’agit toujours de la machine de 113 chevaux sur le train avant, commune à tous les véhicules commercialisés sur la plateforme Smart Car.
Cette nouvelle batterie lui permet de paraître plus sérieuse face aux Renault 5 E-Tech, Volkswagen ID. Polo et Cupra Raval, tout en conservant un argument : celui du prix. Ces modèles sont effectivement vendus à plus de 30 000 euros au catalogue, avant l’aide du bonus écologique. En débutant à 25 900 euros, la Fiat Grande Panda reste donc plus abordable. Certes, l’équipement est plus modeste, tout comme la puissance de son moteur, mais l’écart de prix est bien réel.
